News.title: Bull rider, 35, killed after being thrown from beast’s back and stomped on in front of horrified crowd during rodeo show
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FATAL STOMPING Bull rider, 35, killed after being thrown from beast’s back and stomped on in front of horrified crowd during rodeo show







Next

A BULL rider has been killed after being thrown from the animal’s back and stomped on in front of horrified spectators during a rodeo show.

Jason Blake Saylor, 35, suffered severe traumatic chest injuries after he was kicked by the beast in Ohio on Saturday.



He sustained fatal wounds despite wearing chest protection, authorities said.

Emergency services rushed to the scene at the Fox Hollow Stables in Clearcreek Township around 7.41pm.



The rider was pronounced dead less than an hour later at the Atrium Medical Center.

The rodeo company said on Facebook: “Our hearts are absolutely broken following the tragic loss of one of our bull riders and brothers in Christ last night at Fox Hollow Rodeo.



“There are no words to express the sadness we are feeling.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with his family, friends, and everyone affected by this heartbreaking tragedy.”

A probe has been launched to investigate the full circumstances of the ordeal.

Dylan was competing in the Xtreme Bulls event when tragedy struck.



He was reportedly thrown off the bull and then trampled by the beast as he was on the ground, according to PRCA.

Dylan was then airlifted to a medical center in Houston where he was later pronounced dead, local officials said.

In a social media post shared by the Wharton Country Youth Fair, Kendra Santos wrote: “Our rodeo family lost a talented young cowboy last night.

“There are no worthy words of sympathy at a time of such profound shock and sadness.”

Dylan had competed in various rodeo events throughout his successful career, amassing a whopping $15,000 in career earnings since beginning the sport.



He obtained his PRCA permit in 2018 before buying his PRCA card on February 14, 2024.

Dylan competed on the University of Wyoming Rodeo Team where he won the Mountain States Circuit Finals Rodeo.

In April 2025, a cowboy, 24, was trampled to death after being thrown from a rampaging bull at a youth rodeo in Texas.

News.title: ‘Dishonest’ architect struck off after accusing neighbour of ‘gender violence’ for using car as ‘phallic symbol’
News.content:
NEIGHBOUR WARS ‘Dishonest’ architect struck off after accusing neighbour of ‘gender violence’ for using car as ‘phallic symbol’







Next

AN ARCHITECT was struck off after accusing a male neighbour of “gender violence” as she claimed he used his car as a “phallic symbol”.

Karin Elliott made a long-running string of false and misleading allegations of racism and threatening behaviour against her neighbours, a tribunal heard.



Elliott was previously fined in 2021 for accusing neighbours in Norfolk of building “Nazi concentration camps” after they knocked down a garden wall to build a carport.

Elliott, who had run several university courses, started the long-running dispute between her and three neighbours when she made a planning application for CCTV.



She wanted to mount the CCTV on her £720,000 grade II-listed property she bought with her partner in 2016.

In the letter to residents in February 2024 asking for help with the application, she made some questionable claims about her neighbours found to be false.



She had claimed they had threatened her with a hammer, and attempted to build a President Trump-style wall for immigrants.

She wrote about one neighbour: “He threatened to hit one of us over the head with a hammer at one stage, after he was asked to desist.

“He had been starting to build a wall on our property illegally on a Sunday, following Trump’s declaration that he would ‘build a big wall’ to keep out immigrants. It is very upsetting. We are Irish/American and French.”

She also accused another neighbour of loudly singing “Tragedy” by the BeeGees from their balcony after Elliott’s father had died.



One series of false allegations to Norwich city council included a neighbour’s use of a chainsaw – which she considered to be racial harassment.

She allegedly believed that from “a psychoanalytic perspective,” her neighbour parking the “phallic symbol” of his white Nissan Navara pick-up truck across her driveway represented gender violence.

The tribunal found this claim “underscored how tenuously she constructed serious accusations against other people, and how casually she dispensed them”.

She also claimed her neighbours had “smashed down several of our historic walls, chopped down many of our historic trees, and built on our property, all without our consent”.

During her letter she further wrote: “We hope that the CCTV might deter them all from further trespassing and further destroying our listed garden, and from any further gender violence and racial harassment.”



During cross-examination in the hearing, she admitted: “I think I’d give this letter a serious editing if I did it again.”

Elliott’s partner, Francois Girardin, admitted none of the neighbours has said “anything directly racist”.

He did claim, however, that the couple implied racial discrimination by cheering for England during a sport event and flying the occasional Union Flag.

One neighbour on the end of the claims told the tribunal Elliott was an “absolute disgrace to her profession”.

The neighbour also felt that they could not spend time in their garden due to the couple constantly staring at them.



She also told them: “The Nazis didn’t get away with it and neither will you.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Architects Registration Board struck the architect off for a minimum of two years.

They labelled her guilty this month of unacceptable professional conduct because of her inappropriate communications.

News.title: Lula, 80, re-elected as Brazil president as vocal Trump critic fends off right-wing Bolsonaro to win knife-edge election
News.content:
LULA REMAINS Lula, 80, re-elected as Brazil president as vocal Trump critic fends off right-wing Bolsonaro to win knife-edge election







Next

BRAZIL’S left-wing president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has been re-elected for a historic fourth term after a narrow win at the polls.

The long-serving leader, 80, won a tight majority over Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of infamous ex-president Jair Bolsonaro who was jailed last year for plotting a coup.



Lula – a vocal Donald Trump critic – defied the odds as polls had shown he was trailing his opponent in the run-up to the ballot.

Bolsonaro had beaten Lula by more than 2.2 million votes in the first round of elections earlier this month.



Reports said voting was neck and neck for much of the count on Sunday evening.

But Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, managed to defy the predictions and hold onto power.

No leader since the country returned to democracy in 1988 has failed to take the presidency after winning the first round.

Lula had said the election was a matter of “sovereignty” and argued people faced a choice between the US and Brazil.



In his first speech after the result, Lula said all Brazilians voted to “guarantee democracy” on Sunday.

The re-elected president also promised better regulation of big tech platforms after alleged “interference” throughout the campaign.

Extraordinary photos showed Brazilians celebrating on the streets across major cities.

Some let off flares while others were pictured hugging in joy following the seismic result.

Sunday’s elections were marred by complications – as voting was extended in several regions because of disruptions, including bad weather and transport problems.



Lula secured 51.76 per cent of the vote while Bolsonaro had 48.24 per cent.

Lula, who has been president three times and is now set for a fourth term, was the candidate for the left-wing Workers’ Party (PT).

The veteran politician previously led the country between 2003 and 2010.



His social welfare programmes were praised for lifting millions out of poverty.

But his ride hasn’t been all smooth sailing – in 2018 he was jailed for 18 months after being found guilty of corruption and money laundering.

The convictions were cancelled in 2021, allowing him to run for presidency in 2022.

That year, he beat Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Lula’s main voter base is in Brazil’s poorer northeast regions.



Experts say he is also popular among low-income voters, Catholics and women.

News.title: Yobs who repeatedly terrorise neighbourhoods could be BANNED from town centres under new powers
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HELP ON YOBS

HELP ON YOBS Yobs who repeatedly terrorise neighbourhoods could be BANNED from town centres under new powers







Next

YOBS who repeatedly terrorise neighbourhoods could be banned from town centres under new powers to crack down on anti-social behaviour.

Persistent troublemakers could be slapped with curfews and banned from boozing in public hotspots including high streets and parks.



New Respect Orders coming into force today will give police and councils stronger powers to tackle repeat offenders.

Anyone caught flouting an order could face up to two years behind bars.



Housing associations and transport networks will also be able to apply for the orders, which only apply to adults.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: “Unchecked, anti-social behaviour blights our communities.



“But it is not inevitable and I won’t accept it.

“For too long, we have lacked the powers we need to deal with this problem properly.

“From today, that changes: authorities will be able to take tough action against these offenders.

Police chiefs welcomed the move, saying it would help officers clamp down on prolific troublemakers while offering support to stop them reoffending.



Under-18s will not face Respect Orders but can still be handed existing Youth Injunctions.

News.title: Senior ISIS-linked terrorist, 43, who plotted to kidnap British ambassador ‘smuggled himself into UK on back of lorry’
News.content:
TERROR TRAVEL Senior ISIS-linked terrorist, 43, who plotted to kidnap British ambassador ‘smuggled himself into UK on back of lorry’







Next

A TERRORIST who plotted to kidnap a British diplomat managed to smuggle himself into the UK on the back of a lorry.

Zana Abdul Rahman Rahim, 43, arrived in Dover in June despite being subject to a UK-wide ban over his chilling links to an ISIS-affiliated terror cell.



Rahim was discovered after being pulled over by West Yorkshire police for a broken light on his car.

After running a background check, officers discovered the man’s disturbing history.



In 2015 the man was jailed for seven and a half years in Italy for his role as a spokesman and strategist for an Isis-affiliated terror cell.

He was part of a larger terror network that plotted to attack and kidnap British and Norwegian ambassadors.

They also discussed smuggling missiles amongst other weapons into Europe.

Rahim worked as a second-in-command for the founder of the Rawti Shax network found – Najmadin Faraj Ahmad – while he was behind bars in Norway.

Ahmad, also known as Mullah Krekar, was closely connected to al-Qaeda and had hoped to overthrow the government of Kurdistan to make way for an Islamic State.

According to Italian court documents, the group planned to kidnap diplomats and barter for their release.



Rahim worked to keep the cell running while Krekar was locked up, coordinating finances and communications.

While living in Derby and working as a car washer, Rahim was arrested in part of a larger police sting across Europe in 2015.

He was sent to Italy with his accomplices and jailed.

In May of this year, Rahim travelled to France having completed his sentence.

He made a number of attempts to cross into the UK, before eventually succeeding in June.



As he was subject to an exclusion order banning him from Britain, he is currently in custody and will be sentenced on October 30.

The Home Office has confirmed his deportation will be sought at the earliest opportunity.

News.title: Villagers will hold Piddington-style referendum to leave UK over plans to move 930 refugees into RAF base
News.content:
Next

VILLAGERS will hold a Piddington-style poll over plans to move nearly 1,000 asylum seekers to a nearby RAF base.

Barnham in Suffolk, with a population of 611, is set to follow in the footsteps of Piddington, in Oxfordshire, which voted to leave the UK in July over similar plans.



Residents have agreed overwhelmingly to hold a symbolic independence ballot in opposition to the Home Office proposals to house 930 migrants at RAF Barnham.

The Home Office originally earmarked the site for 1,250 asylum seekers but the proposed figure is now 930.



A working group will meet today to set the timeline for Barnham’s vote.

The ballot will have no legal standing.



Mr Bauer said: “The villagers of Barnham will decide on Saturday what action they wish to take to continue to oppose the imposition of the asylum seeker accommodation on the village.

“A Piddington-style referendum is one of those options.

“I believe that a symbolic declaration of the desire to secede from the UK would show the strength of sentiment within the village and send a powerful message to Westminster.

“A Barnham referendum would show that Piddington’s was not an isolated event, but potentially the start of a powerful movement.”



Earlier this month, the Eastern Daily Press revealed the base currently has just 320 beds, and that public money was being spent on surveys and renovation work before the plans had been given the go-ahead.

No final decision has been made, but the Home Office has previously said it hopes to move the first asylum seekers in before Christmas.

A date has not been set for Barnham’s referendum, but a working group will meet on Monday to set out the timeline for the vote.

News.title: Tories demand John Healey RESIGNS unless Budget fully meets 3% defence spending target
News.content:
Next

THE Tories have demanded that John Healey resigns unless his Budget fully meets his three per cent defence spending target.

The Chancellor will unveil billions of pounds of new defence funds in a surprise announcement in his first Budget on Wednesday.



Money is also expected to be pumped into two giant investment funds which will then be invested in UK defence companies including drone manufacturers.

Mr Healey had called for defence spending to rise to 3 per cent by 2030 – and had quit as defence secretary in June when ex-PM refused to commit to a substantial rise.



Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith on Saturday demanded Mr Healey resign if he fails to set out how it will reach the target he himself set.

He said: “By the end of his Budget statement, John Healey must have fully funded 3 per cent defence spending, or resign.

“We are living in an era of extraordinary threats.

“And yet the Chancellor is dithering over finding the money to pay the country’s insurance premium.”

He said he would lay out a path to hitting his target at the 2027 spending review.

The Conservatives have said they would fund defence by cutting benefits.



The UK has just signed up to hit Nato’s target of spending 3.5 per cent of GDP on defence by 2035.

But the UK Government currently only spends around 2.6 per cent of GDP.

News.title: Angela Rayner hints tough reforms for foreigners seeking permanent residence in Britain face being watered down
News.content:
Next

TOUGH reforms for foreigners seeking permanent residence in Britain face being watered down, Angela Rayner has hinted.

The cabinet minister signalled a climb-down saying any shake-up “will be fair to the people who come to the country and contribute” following a Labour rebellion.



Proposals from Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood include foreign care workers waiting 15 years instead of the current five years for indefinite leave to remain.

Ministers and officials are now going through 200,000 responses to a public consultation.



But Ms Rayner told Sky News: “Shabana will be coming forward with the plans and they will be fair to the British taxpayers.

She added that they will be “fair to the people that come to this country that contribute and will give confidence in the British people that our system works for them”.

Ms Rayner said: “And I’ve got every confidence in Shabana being able to do that.”

This follows Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh facing questions after a deleted online post emerged in which she criticised making migrants wait longer for permanent settlement.

She repeatedly refused last week to back the plans during a TV interview before joking that her pledge never to lie had landed her in “awkward moments”.

But she later clarified her remarks saying she “fully” supported the Home Secretary and the Government’s position on migration reform.



Permanent residency gives an individual the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like.

They can also claim benefits if they are deemed eligible.

Mahmood had been looking to double the time needed for most migrants to qualify from five to ten years.

Under the plans, anyone who came here for health and social care visas could have to wait up to 15 years.

News.title: Two men killed by falling trees as Storm Boelo leaves 90,000 properties without power
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police were called to Dollis Road in Finchley at around 12:40 GMT to reports a tree had fallen onto a moving car, and the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Chief Inspector Guy Ellwood, from the North West Command Unit, said: "This is a deeply tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the young man who lost his life."

A London Ambulance Service spokesperson said it sent incident response officers, paramedics from its hazardous area response team, and a trauma team from London's Air Ambulance to the scene.

Earlier, Police Scotland said a man died after being hit by a falling tree at at Mid Kelton near Castle Douglas. Meanwhile, two women were also taken to hospital after being hit by a another falling tree in Aberfeldy.

During Storm Boelo and the earlier Storm Austen, which hit the UK on Friday, 838,700 properties across the country faced power cuts, according to the ENA.

Wind gusts peaked on Sunday morning at 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, and 84mph in both Stornoway in the Outer Hebrides, and Capel Curig in north Wales.

An amber wind warning issued by the Met Office was in place until 21:00 on Sunday across Scotland and parts of northern England.

A yellow warning that also covered other areas of the north of England, including Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds, Sheffield and Newcastle-upon-Tyne, as well as parts of the East and West Midlands and North Wales, also expired at 21:00.

The Met Office urged people to "stay indoors as much as possible", adding: "If you do go out, try not to walk, or shelter, close to buildings and trees."

The strongest gusts have continued to spread eastwards across the UK on Sunday.

News.title: Faisal Islam: Healey's Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds
News.content:
There have been almost no Budget leaks.

The chancellor's aides are using intelligence-style security measures to guard its secrets: the Budget has been split into "compartments" with very few given access to all of them. There are codenames. The IT has been locked down and ministers viewing the plans have to sign a digital promise not to brief media.

Such security is a response to the feeling that speculation around the last Budget, sometimes informed by insiders, was economically destabilising.

As a recent former defence secretary, Chancellor John Healey has embraced such strict procedures, and has approached most of his public engagements and interviews with a sturdy refusal to break the Budget omertÃ , akin to his fellow Yorkshireman Geoffrey Boycott's at times ultra-defensive stance on a cricket pitch.

The economic news has been good - growth has been better than expected and the International Monetary Fund has endorsed the UK for "standing out" among the G7 countries for at least planning to cut borrowing.

News.title: Funding set to double for plan to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas
News.content:
Funding is set to double to support a pledge by the prime minister to give every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas.

Ending rough sleeping was one of Andy Burnham's first promises when he entered Downing Street, announcing a Â£442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support.

On the eve of the first Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street on Monday, No 10 has indicated a further Â£432m will be added to the initiative in Wednesday's Budget.

Shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said rough sleeping had hit "record highs under Labour" and criticised Burnham for failing to end rough sleeping when he was the Mayor of Greater Manchester.

The BBC understands the government's commitment is that every rough sleeper will be able to physically move into accommodation by Christmas and/or they will be offered support as a way to prevent them sleeping rough.

Some people may choose not to accept accommodation, but ministers say support will still be offered to them.

The government said initial funding had seen specialist outreach teams and new bed spaces operating in Coventry, with further provision being rolled out in places including Plymouth and Camden in north London over the coming weeks.

Money being added to the pot this week will extend support beyond March 2027 to the end of this Parliament, taking total investment to Â£874m.

Ahead of hosting the summit, Burnham said: "Rough sleeping isn't a fact of life. It's a thing governments either choose to accept or don't.

"Well I don't accept it. That's why we're doubling funding so that people aren't just offered a safe route off the streets this winter but have that same support right through the rest of this Parliament too.

"But we can't do it alone. If we're going to end rough sleeping, we need every part of society behind us on this. So today we're bringing together businesses, charities and local leaders in Downing Street to make sure this is a solution that lasts."

More than 30 organisations have pledged support for the plan with new partnerships, including commercial businesses and charities.

News.title: Sharon Osbourne: 'I visit Ozzy's grave every day'
News.content:
It's been 15 months since Ozzy Osbourne died, at the age of 76, at his home in Buckinghamshire.

Although he had suffered from health problems for years, including Parkinson's disease and a fractured vertebra, his death was a shock.

Less than three weeks beforehand, he had been on stage in Birmingham, playing a triumphant farewell concert.

After the show, he was on a high.

"He was just so, so happy," recalls his wife Sharon.

"He was online, going through the reviews and saying, 'There's something terribly wrong', and I'm like, 'Why?'

"He goes, 'I didn't get slagged by anybody. Why are people being nice to me?'

"And I'm like, 'Because they like you'."

On the morning he died, Ozzy had woken up early and gone downstairs for his usual morning workout. Shortly afterwards, he had a heart attack. An air ambulance was called and paramedics tried to save him. But it was too late.

"I was asleep," says Sharon.

"We'd spoken in the night. Ozzy had woken in the night and he asked me to kiss him twice, and I did.

"And then he said, 'Hold me, hold me tight,' and I did.

"And then the next thing I know, it's early in the morning, and someone comes rushing into the room saying, 'Come down now'.

"I ran down, and that was it."

News.title: Letter making claims about Meghan's father written by his first wife, BBC understands
News.content:
A letter sent to the Metropolitan Police making a number of claims relating to the Duchess of Sussex's father was written by his ex-wife Roslyn Loveless, the BBC understands.

Meghan confirmed on Friday she had previously been informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father, Thomas Markle.

On Saturday, the Met confirmed it received a letter relating to Markle in 2019, and it was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

It has been reported that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Markle, 82, had been found in his former home in the Philippines. Markle, who is based in the US, denies all such allegations.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's half-siblings Samantha Markle and Thomas Markle Jr. Loveless divorced Markle in 1975 before he married the Duchess' mother Doria Ragland in 1979.

Meghan was born in 1981 and is the only daughter of Markle and Ragland.

In a statement shared on Friday, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Sources close to the duchess said Meghan warned Markle in a letter - sent while he was in hospital in the Philippines after having his leg amputated - that he would never meet his grandchildren.

News.title: Rapper Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
News.content:
Rapper Nicki Minaj said US President Donald Trump has "changed the energy of the country" as she joined him at a Michigan rally to stump for Republicans ahead of the nationwide midterm elections.

"He's given us a future to look forward to," she said, after Trump praised her figure and called her on stage to speak.

Minaj has called herself Trump's "number one fan" despite criticising some of his policies in his first term.

In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is locked in a tight race with Republican Mike Rogers with just over a week to go before the midterms. Former President Barack Obama held a rally - one of the first in this cycle - with the Democrat on Saturday.

Democrats are also aggressively hitting the campaign trail, with close elections taking place on 3 November which will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's presidency.

In his remarks on Sunday, Trump focused on El-Sayed's Muslim faith and background, alleging that he will "invite jihadists" into America if he wins.

El-Sayed has criticised similar remarks by Trump as Islamophobic, saying in an ad to voters last week that the US president "thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor's office".

In Port Huron on Sunday, Minaj, wearing a gold-coloured Gucci-branded suit, led the crowd in chanting Trump's name, and the names of Republican candidates in Michigan.

"We really need all these great people to be elected, because this is a major turning point for our country," she said.

"She never looked more beautiful," Trump said as she left the stage. "She gets it. She's smart," he added.

Earlier in his speech, Trump praised the rear end of one male Republican candidate before turning the crowd's attention to Minaj.

"By the way, I looked at a beautiful ass before," he segued. "Nicki Minaj. That's hard to miss."

He then asked her to "stand up" as the crowd cheered, and added that he hoped she was not "insulted" by his remark.

News.title: End approaching for Carrick but Man Utd fans make clear who they blame
News.content:
There was an air of inevitability about Michael Carrick's walk around Old Trafford after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.

It is not unusual for Carrick to applaud the Manchester United fans. If anything, his acknowledgements were not as pronounced as they were in Como after the equally devastating loss.

But after eight games without a win, the worst run since 2015-16 and two horrific defeats in a week, the end is approaching for Carrick, with his bosses in serious talks about his future.

However, if anyone in a senior position at the club thinks the issues at Old Trafford will be solved simply by changing the head coach and, more importantly, the fans will be appeased by a new face in the dugout, the reaction from the stands on an awful day on and off the pitch would have very clearly told them otherwise.

On Friday, as he looked back on that 4-1 loss to Como and ahead to Bournemouth, Carrick said: "We'll be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team on Sunday."

Sadly, they weren't.

Carrick could not answer if he will still be in charge for next Saturday's trip to Chelsea. He does not know.

"The responsibility is mine," he said. "What else can I say really right now? I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. I love this place and I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club."

News.title: Is 'ferritin face' a real thing - and can you really spot low iron from looks?
News.content:
"Do you have ferritin face?" a young woman asks on TikTok, pointing to dark circles, washed-out skin and brittle hair, alongside before-and-after style photographs. The content creator puts these features down to her iron levels.

It is one of a growing number of videos and posts on TikTok and Instagram claiming that low ferritin - a protein which stores iron in the body - can leave visible clues on your face.

Users list pale or grey-looking skin, dark under-eye circles, dry or cracked lips, hair shedding and weak nails, while others share portraits claiming stark visual differences.

The phrase "ferritin face" has spread widely across social media, with videos attracting millions of views.

But doctors say appearance alone cannot diagnose iron deficiency.

"Ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis," said GP Dr Aziza Sesay, who is based in the West Midlands. "However, it may be a clue to tell us that something is going on."

Pale skin, hair shedding or brittle nails can accompany low iron, but can also be signs of other conditions, she told BBC News.

News.title: Couple were celebrating anniversary before Bahamas tragedy
News.content:
He said both boys had been so excited and been snorkelling in shallow water as they sorted out their towels and bags on the beach when the boys got into difficulties.

Both parents went into the sea and tried to save them as they were swept out by the current, he added, and the whole ordeal happened in less than 10 minutes.

Nathan said the loss of his 36-year-old "childhood sweetheart" was "unimaginable", but she was a "hero... in life and in death" as she helped to rescue the two boys.

"I've known her since infant school," he told the BBC. "We first got together when we were 14... so 22 years."

"There are no words I can use to describe Leanne, same as anyone she has ever known.

"She was the purest of people, the most generous kind and beautiful person who ever walked the Earth.

"Our relationship was perfect. She was the perfect mother, the perfect wife, the foundation of our entire family."

Nathan added: "Royal Caribbean and Virgin Airlines were absolutely incredible to us and made an impossible journey home so much easier."

Now, as he "keeps strong for his boys", a fundraising page has generated nearly Â£9,000 in donations to support the family.

News.title: Board of Deputies of British Jews declares Greens to be racist party
News.content:
The Green Party of England and Wales has been declared a racist organisation by the Board of Deputies of British Jews.

The Jewish body, which is the largest in the UK, was responding to the "Zionism is racism" policy motion passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.

Board of Deputies president Phil Rosenberg said a vote passed by 118 votes to one to declare that the Greens had, "by adopting an antisemitic platform, become a racist party".

A spokesman for the Greens insisted the party does not discriminate against people who hold Zionist views and said it rejected the Board of Deputies' "characterisation of this motion and our party".

They added the decision "will not stop us from speaking out against the genocide in Gaza and pushing for stronger sanctions against the Israeli government and its leaders". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

The motion passed by the Board of Deputies urged other parties not to do deals with the Greens unless they rejected the policy.

Forming coalition deals with Greens at local or national level would be "failing to take antisemitism with the requisite seriousness", it said, unless the party's local leadership have rejected the policy and committed to overturn it.

Labour has already issued an ultimatum to local Green groups it is currently in coalition with, telling them to disown the motion or lose the party's support.

Rosenberg said: "By adopting an antisemitic platform, the Green Party of England and Wales has become a racist party. We will treat it accordingly.

"No political party has the right to tell Jews that a central part of our identity, rooted in thousands of years of history, faith and peoplehood, is racist.

"The Green Party's policy brands much of our community, including our synagogues and communal organisations, with that slur. It gives prejudice against Jews a political licence.

"The Green Party's leadership must now take responsibility for reversing this policy and confronting the antisemitism it has legitimised."

The motion backed by Green members at its party conference earlier this month said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/ or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It was criticised by Jewish groups, as well as four Green MPs and two former leaders, and opposition political parties.

Responding when the Green motion was passed, the Board of Deputies and Jewish Leadership Council said in a joint statement that "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, did not take part in the vote on the motion as he left the conference early to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election which was held days later.

He has since told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, he would not overturn the motion, which would be party policy until 2028.

News.title: Body found in search for man who fell overboard from ferry
News.content:
The body of a missing ferry passenger who fell overboard has been found on a beach in North Ayrshire.

HM Coastguard responded to a report of a man going overboard from the MV Caledonian Isles near Arran about 20:30 on Sunday 18 October.

The man was later named as 82-year-old Jim Wither, who was reported missing from Johnstone, Renfrewshire.

Police Scotland earlier received a report that the body of a man had been found in the Largs beach area on Sunday. Formal identification has yet to take place, but the family of Jim Wither has been informed.

Two helicopters, a coastguard aircraft, Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) lifeboats and rescue teams from the surrounding area were sent to find the passenger, but the search was called off at 16:55 on Monday.

Officers said the death was not being treated as suspicious and a report would be submitted to the procurator fiscal in due course.

News.title: Long queues after power surge at Stansted Airport
News.content:
Passengers arriving at Stansted Airport have described waiting in long queues to reach immigration control after a power surge shut down its systems.

Traveller Jill Stakem reported the airport's internal tram system had failed earlier and people were "being held in a corridor for over 90 minutes".

Stakem added: "It's horrendous. No communication, no seating for people, no-one offering watering."

In a statement, a spokesperson for Stansted Airport said: "Due to a power surge earlier today that affected the airport and local area, a number of airport systems were temporarily impacted."

They added: "All systems are now back in service with operational teams working hard to provide support to passengers on their journeys through the airport."

Another airport spokesperson confirmed the shuttle service "remained out-of-service due to a technical fault and contingency bussing is in operation to transfer passengers between the terminal and gates".

News.title: Dead whale found washed up on beach in storm
News.content:
People have been warned to keep away from a dead whale which has washed up on a shoreline.

Maryport Coastguard Rescue Team said it was called to Flimby beach where a juvenile northern bottlenose whale was found on Saturday, after Storm Austen and Storm Boelo battered the UK.

Northern bottlenose whales are most commonly found in the North Atlantic Ocean, where they can dive to more than 1,400m (4,593ft) deep and stay submerged for up to two hours, according to the charity Whale and Dolphin Conservation.

The Coastguard urged people to not touch the carcass as it "may have toxins that can pass to humans" and advised people to take care as Storm Boelo was "still going strong".

The Coastguard asked people to report any sightings of stranded whales as soon as possible, even if they might be dead, to keep clear from the mammal and to wait for help.

"Gathering round the animal will intensify their distress, and it is possible for disease to be passed to humans," it added.

News.title: Four-year-old girl dies after fall from tower block
News.content:
A four-year-old girl has died after falling from a tower block in east London.

The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to the scene at an address in St Paul's Road, Barking, at about 11:00 BST on Saturday morning, following reports that a child had fallen from height.

Paramedics from the London Ambulance Service gave first aid and the child was taken to hospital, but later died from her injuries.

A Met spokesperson said the incident was not believed to be suspicious.

"Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with the child's family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time," they said.

"An investigation into the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident is ongoing. However, at this time, the incident is not believed to be suspicious.

"We urge anyone with information about the incident to contact police on 101, quoting CAD 2424/24OCT."
