News.title: Spotify uploads lyrics for Dolly Parton's Welsh version of Jolene in Irish
News.content:
The lyrics to Dolly Parton's Welsh version of her hit Jolene were uploaded mistakenly to Spotify in Irish.

The song was recorded before her death on 25 August, and is a collaboration with Welsh singer-songwriter Bronwen Lewis as well as Parton's niece, Jada Star.

The version has parts of the song sung in English and Welsh - but the lyrics presented on the digital audio streaming service Spotify actually showed the language as Irish.

Spotify removed the Irish lyrics after the BBC approached it for comment.

The BBC asked Spotify when the single and lyrics were uploaded, when the error was noticed and when it will be replaced, but did not receive a response.

News.title: Burnham open to 'honest discussion' on EU free movement
News.content:
The prime minister says he would welcome an "honest discussion" about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and European Union.

Speaking to the Sunday Times, Andy Burnham said a new relationship with Brussels could include full EU membership or joining the single market, requiring free movement.

Asked about Burnham's remarks, Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg "you can't take anything off the table", adding the prime minister was saying "we've got to be pragmatic to get the best deal for Britain and he wants to have the conversation."

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch responded that the prime minister "hasn't thought this through", while Reform UK's Robert Jenrick dismissed the idea as "mad".

Migration dominated debate during the 2016 Brexit campaign, with the Leave campaign raising issues about rules allowing any EU citizen to move to the UK.

Burnham has previously committed to Labour's 2024 election manifesto which ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

He has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, would is due by 2029.

"I think you have to have a very factual, quite evidence-based debate about this," he told the Sunday Times, external, adding he believed the type of migration had changed from revolving door movement of young people.

"Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different," he said. "The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we've just got to have an honest discussion about those things."

But he stressed: "I can't see myself ever recommending anything that would involve joining the euro or Schengen."

The Schengen Agreement allows passport-free travel across EU countries. The UK was able to keep the pound when it was an EU member, but the bloc has pushed new members to adopt the Euro.

His remarks were made ahead of an EU summit on 20 November in Brussels, where the prime minister is expected to pitch options for a reset of relations with the bloc.

On Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Rayner said she wanted to see the best possible deal with the European Union, which may well involve concessions.

"What the prime minister is saying now, and what I want, is that we have an honest conversation about the facts of what the trade-offs are to get the best deal for Britain going forward," she said.

"The frustration for me in the previous debate we had when we had the referendum is that a lot of those facts didn't get the airtime... So I would like us to have an honest conversation about what the trade-offs could be and then put that to the people at a general election."

Writing on X, Badenoch dismissed it as "yet another example of Burnham's foot in mouth syndrome".

She added: "Most people who voted for Brexit did so because they didn't want free movement. Too many politicians have failed to understand the significance and impact of immigration on communities."

Conservative MP and former chancellor Jeremy Hunt, who backed Remain, warned the Brexit debate was "incredibly divisive" and insisted the current Brexit deal can still be made to work.

"I was at the top of a government that was paralysed for several years while we were trying to wrestle with the implications of that vote and I think, having made the decision, we should stick with it and make the most of it - I think we can make it a success," he told Kuenssberg.

Pointing to the one million young people not in work or training, he added: "Surely our priority in that situation is to get those jobs filled by the young people we have here instead of parking them on welfare.

"Which is why I think it's astonishing to lead on the issue of free movement... Something that is actually going to stop young people here getting jobs."

But Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper told Kuenssberg she believed allowing freedom of movement would be "a really good thing for growth" and pushed for the UK to rejoin the single market, the customs union, and also be involved in the bloc's defence pact.

The UK currently has "the worst of both worlds" on immigration, she said, as it was excluded from the EU's "new asylum pact with biometric data" that could be used to "tackle the small boats crisis".

Reform UK's economy spokesperson Robert Jenrick told Kuenssberg he had never believed freedom of movement "was a good thing", despite supporting the Remain position before the 2016 referendum when he was a Conservative MP.

"I think it's completely mad, the idea that this country needs more immigration," he said, claiming data shows mass migration "has been a disaster for working people, for Brits".

"The last thing they want is their wages being undercut by a load of low wage, low-skilled migrants from overseas," he added.

News.title: Elizabeth Holmes doc You Can See Everything rivals Clayface at box office with huge takings
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything gave DC Universe’s Clayface a run for its money at the box office this weekend.

Clayface, a horror movie about the Batman villain of the same name, sat comfortably at No. 1 on its debut weekend, taking in $24 million from 3,458 North American theaters. But You Can See Everything wasn’t far behind – again defying box office expectations.

The documentary about the disgraced Theranos founder, by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, collected an impressive $19.5 million while expanding to 2,655 venues on its second weekend, according to Rentrak, which compiles box office data. So far, the movie has made $45 million in total domestically.

The film begins 34 days before Holmes surrenders herself at the Federal Prison Camp in Bryan, Texas, where she’s serving an 11-year sentence after being convicted on four counts of fraud and conspiracy for lying about the capabilities of her biotech company’s blood testing technology.

The movie has been such a success that A24 expanded the film to 2,655 theaters, which makes it an exceptionally wide release for a documentary and more than triple its opening-weekend footprint.

open image in gallery The documentary about the disgraced Theranos founder, by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, collected an impressive $19.5 million while expanding to 2,655 venues on its second weekend.‘ ( A24 )

You Can See Everything is the highest-grossing nonmusical documentary since Michael Moore’s Fahrenheit 9/11 in 2004, and reviews have been overwhelmingly positive across the board.

Some commentators are predicting that it could become the first documentary to ever score a best picture nomination at the Oscars.

Clayface was a modest opening for a comic-book adaptation, but it was probably a relief for DC, since the studio has struggled with success at the box office this year.

The studio’s Supergirl was a box office flop in July, taking in $126 million worldwide against production marketing costs of at least $270 million.

open image in gallery Clayface’, a horror movie about the Batman villain of the same name, sat comfortably at No. 1 on its debut weekend ( Warner Bros )

In third place in the weekend box office rankings was Wildwood, a stop-motion animation about a teenage girl who searches an enchanted forest for her kidnapped brother. The movie debuted at $11 million this weekend and received rave reviews, but was expensive to make at about $100 million.

Following behind was the romantic fantasy movie Wicker, starring Olivia Colman as a lonely fisherwoman who commissions a basket maker to create her a husband (Alexander Skarsgard), taking in a solid $6 million.

Klara and the Sun, the adaptation of the sci-fi novel of the same name, didn’t have much success on its opening weekend, collecting just $725,000 from 880 theaters. It stars Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams.

News.title: Sylvester Stallone defends casting daughter in Tulsa King: ‘Of course it’s nepotism, you idiot’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Sylvester Stallone has defended the casting of his daughter in the TV series Tulsa King, while admitting that the hire was a case of “nepotism”.

The Rocky star, 80, plays the lead in the Taylor Sheridan-created crime drama on Paramount+, and serves as one of the show’s executive producers.

Scarlet Rose Stallone, one of three daughters from Stallone’s third marriage (to model Jennifer Flavin), appears in a recurring role in the series as Spencer, who is hired as a bartender by Stallone’s character, Dwight.

While the prevalence of so-called “nepo babies” – a term often used to refer to children of celebrities who themselves enter show business – remains a somewhat criticised trend in modern Hollywood, Stallone was defiant as he explained his reasoning for the hire.

open image in gallery Sylvester Stallone, Scarlet Rose Stallone, Sophia Rose Stallone and Sistine Rose Stallone attend the 2017 Golden Globes afterparty ( Getty Images for InStyle )

“First they go, ‘Nepotism is terrible,’” said Stallone in a recent interview with USA Today. “I said, ‘Oh please, you’re not a good parent if you haven’t performed a little nepotism. Then obviously you don’t care about your kids, because they come first.’

“Of course it’s nepotism, you idiot. That’s why we’re parents. We want the best for our children. So obviously, we let them have every advantage.”

He went on to say, however, that there are limits to the influence a famous parent can have over their children’s success, and that longevity in the industry ultimately comes down to talent.

open image in gallery Stallone in ‘Tulsa King’ ( PA )

Can they maintain that level of excellence?,” he asks. “That’s out of our hands. But if you can open the door, we’ll see if they have the ability to go through it.

“People will say, ‘She got that job, it’s too easy.’ You’re right. Perhaps it could be. But to maintain that, to be in front of millions of people, you either got it or you don’t.”

Tulsa King debuted on Paramount’s streaming service back in 2022, and is currently partway through its fourth season.

A spin-off series, titled Frisco King and starring Samuel L Jackson, is currently in development.

Stallone had three children with Flavin, whom he married in 1997: Sophia, Sistine, and Scarlet.

He also had two sons from his first marriage, to Sasha Czack: Seargeoh and Sage Moonblood Stallone, who died of heart disease in 2012 at the age of 36.

News.title: How to help your body adjust after the clocks changed last night
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An extra hour in bed sounds like a good deal. But while our phones may update to the autumn time change automatically, our body clock isn’t quite so quick.

You may even find yourself waking up earlier than normal and ready for bed before your evening has properly begun.

The reason for this partly lies in our circadian system: the roughly 24-hour internal timing system that helps organise tiredness and alertness. Changing the time on a clock does not instantly reset that system.

But there are some things you can do to support your body clock in adapting to the time change.

While these strategies won’t offer a guaranteed overnight reset, they will help you get back on track.

1. Dim the lights before bedtime

Your body doesn’t judge whether it’s day or night by using the numbers on a clock.

Rather, a tiny region in the brain called the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) – which acts as the body’s master clock – uses light signals from the eyes to help keep our circadian rhythm on track.

Bright evening light can suppress melatonin, a hormone that signals biological night, and shift your internal clock later.

This can help explain why some people feel less sleepy at their usual bedtime during the long, bright evenings of summer.

But even the light from electronic devices such as phones or e-readers can contribute to melatonin suppression.

open image in gallery The autumn time change often means we’re tired before our usual bedtime as the early nights draw in ( Getty/iStock )

So as your intended bedtime approaches, switch to lower, softer lighting and reduce screen brightness. It’s recommended you keep light exposure low in the hours before bed and make the bedroom as dark as practical during sleep.

Of course, the autumn time change often means we’re tired before our usual bedtime as the early nights draw in.

Shifting your body clock a little later can be helpful if you’re becoming sleepy and waking too early.

To do this, only start winding down before the bedtime you want. Don’t spend the entire evening in darkness as soon as the sun sets.

2. Get daylight

A walk, an outdoor lunch break or simply spending more of the day outside can strengthen the contrast between bright days and dim evenings.

That contrast helps synchronise the circadian system, which evolved under a much stronger daily light–dark cycle than many indoor lifestyles provide.

When you get this daylight is important, however.

Morning light generally moves the body clock earlier, while evening light generally pushes it later.

Ronan Lordan is a Postdoctoral Researcher in Circadian Biology at the FutureNeuro Research Ireland Centre and the School of Pharmacy and Biomolecular Sciences at RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

That distinction matters when the clocks go back, because someone waking too early doesn’t necessarily need another signal to wake earlier.

After the clocks change, try to get daylight during your normal waking day rather than deliberately seeking bright light at an unusually early hour. A lunchtime walk is one practical option.

If early-evening sleepiness is the problem, spending time outdoors later in the afternoon, while daylight remains, may be better than prioritising first-thing morning light.

In fact, a 2024 modelling study predicted that later-day light exposure could speed the autumn adjustment. However, the authors emphasised that these proposed interventions still need experimental verification.

Think of daylight as a useful daily cue – not a precisely proven clock-change prescription.

3. Stick to a regular sleep schedule

It’s tempting to treat the extra hour of sleep as permission to overhaul your weekend. But a regular routine is key.

Sleep depends on both the pressure that builds while you’re awake and the circadian signals that determine when you feel sleepy or alert. These processes interact, which is why sleep can’t always be summoned simply by deciding to go to bed.

Aim for reasonably consistent bedtimes and waking times according to the time change. Avoid swinging between very early nights, long lie-ins and late bedtimes. Keeping weekday and weekend schedules similar can support healthy sleep.

open image in gallery A walk, an outdoor lunch break or simply spending more of the day outside can strengthen the contrast between bright days and dim evenings ( Getty/iStock )

If you find that even with a consistent sleep schedule you’re struggling to fall asleep, choose a quiet activity done in low light until you feel ready for bed.

Dark autumn mornings can also make waking up feel harder.

Keeping a broadly consistent waking time, getting morning daylight when possible and allowing enough time for sleep may help maintain a stable sleep–wake rhythm – although some grogginess immediately after waking is normal.

4. Re-think your afternoon coffee

The earlier nights that accompany the winter months can make it harder to get through the afternoon.

When you feel groggy, coffee can look like the obvious solution. But as much as it pains me to give this advice as a coffee lover, you might want to skip that midday coffee.

Caffeine interferes with sleep long after its effects have worn off. A recent, small study found that a 400mg dose of caffeine (equivalent to around 3-5 cups of coffee) affected sleep even when consumed eight hours before bedtime.

That’s quite a substantial dose, of course – and not one many of us are consuming in the mid-afternoon.

Fortunately, the study also found that when a 100 mg dose of caffeine (equivalent to a single cup of coffee) was consumed four hours before bedtime, it had no effect on sleep compared to a placebo.

open image in gallery When you feel groggy, coffee can look like the obvious solution ( Getty/iStock )

If sleep is difficult, moving your last caffeinated drink earlier and reducing the amount you drink are sensible things to try.

Evening caffeine can also push the body clock later, so avoiding it may help when you’re trying to keep an earlier sleep schedule.

The autumn time change is a useful reminder that sleep depends on more than the number displayed on your phone’s clock.

Most people adjust to the time change within a few days to about a week, although some can take longer. But if you’re still struggling a month later, the clock change may not be the whole story.

News.title: North Korean howitzers seen at border with South Korea amid escalating tensions
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Tensions between North Korea and South Korea are running high this week after Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council, repeating accusations ⁠that Seoul fabricated a September landmine incident.

A Reuters witness at an observatory in South Korea overlooking the heavily armed border on Monday confirmed the presence of a North Korean artillery piece positioned in clear view near the frontier.

South Korea's Yonhap news agency on Sunday identified the weapon as a self-propelled 122mm howitzer, saying its deployment near the border marked a rare public display of ⁠such artillery.

Reuters also observed three North Korean armoured vehicles with their gun barrels pointed south, as well as about 20 to 30 North Korean soldiers carrying out fencing work inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ).

open image in gallery A North Korean guard post is seen in this picture taken from an observation deck in Gimpo, South Korea, 26 October 2026 ( Reuters )

"It is highly unusual (for North Korea) to expose its self-propelled artillery so conspicuously,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University ⁠in Seoul.

"By deliberately displaying it, North Korea is signalling through action, not words, that it intends to enforce its border policy through force `rather than dialogue or negotiation."

It is also warning ‌South Korea to exercise caution about escalating border friction, with the intention to prevent an accidental clash, he added.

North Korean state media KCNA reported that in the letter sent on Sunday, the country's UN representative said Seoul was using the landmine incident to depict Pyongyang's border construction as a military incursion.

North Korea warned in the letter ‌that violations of its sovereignty could trigger self-defence measures and that South Korea would be "wholly accountable for all the ensuing consequences."

The letter is a response to a South Korean letter to the Security Council last week, which said a 21 September blast in the DMZ was planted by North Korean troops ⁠and constituted a violation of the Korean War Armistice Agreement.

The UN Command, which oversees the DMZ, has said a North Korean mine across the line violated the armistice. Pyongyang has denied responsibility.

A spokesperson for South Korea's Unification Ministry said on Monday that the North Korean letter appears to repeat North Korea's existing position and seeks to justify its so-called border line marking work.

The ministry had no separate comment on the placement of the howitzer.

open image in gallery North Korean self-propelled 122-mm howitzers are deployed at their border as seen from an observation deck in Gimpo, South Korea, 26 October 2026 ( Reuters )

Seoul has proposed dialogue with North Korea to defuse border tensions. North Korea's letter also repeated accusations that South Korea had opened fire on North Korean personnel, calling that a violation of the UN Charter, which bars the threat ‌or use of force against another state's territorial integrity.

Seoul has said its military issues warning broadcasts and fires warning shots to send North Korean soldiers back across the line when they cross the military demarcation line (MDL), which bisects the DMZ.

North Korean troops have been building tactical roads and ⁠fences and laying mines near the MDL in recent years.

The Yonhap report cited photographs taken from an observatory in the South Korean border city of Gimpo that appeared to show the howitzer as well as North Korean troops conducting drills on the coast of Kaepung county, about 1.5km (1 mile) from the observatory.

In ​2015, there was a similar incident in which South Korean troops ‌were injured by North Korean mines. Then, Seoul resumed anti-North ​Korea loudspeaker broadcasts across the DMZ, triggering a military standoff. After North Korea expressed regret, the standoff ended with a high-level inter-Korean agreement.

News.title: The top habit that leads to a break-up — and ways to prevent it
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

At the end of a relationship, it’s normal to wonder where it all went wrong: When did this person become a stranger? How could our love story have turned into a psychological horror?

But while the breakdown of a partnership rarely happens overnight, it can begin with something as seemingly small as a sarcastic comment, relationship experts say.

A pointed dig is just one behavior that points to the underlying issue of contempt, which world-renowned relationship coach Dr. John Gottman identifies as the most destructive of the “four horsemen” predictors of an impending breakup.

Gottman’s research led him to classify contempt, criticism, defensiveness and stonewalling as the communication styles that often lead a relationship to fail, with contempt being the number one sign that a marriage is heading for divorce.

Below, we explore how contempt sneaks into a relationship and how it can be reversed with intentional efforts.

open image in gallery Contempt in a relationship is the biggest indicator of a breakup approaching ( Focus Features )

What is contempt and why is it so dangerous?

Contempt is considering someone inferior or unworthy of respect. It’s an emotion that can breed disgust, anger and a feeling of moral superiority over a partner — which is why clinical therapist Blythe Landry, who has more than 27 years of experience working with trauma and relationship dynamics, is adamant about how dangerous it can be for couples.

“Contempt is the death knell of romantic relationships,” Landry told The Independent. “It indicates extensive, built up resentments that have gone unaddressed, sometimes because the differences are so great they are not able to be adequately resolved. Over time, contempt changes the way we see our partner and can cause us to filter nearly everything they do through a negative lens, even when their behavior was not intended to hurt us.”

This is the real trouble with contempt: it affects every aspect of a relationship. Resentment over imbalanced household responsibilities or jealousy in the workplace can bleed into a casual conversation about an unrelated topic, causing unaddressed problems to pile up until the tension is overwhelming.

Couples therapist Marc Zola said that contempt often prompts a person to view a shortcoming in their partner as a character judgment or morality issue rather than a mistake or accident.

“In some ways, the expression of contempt is a function of a person's inability to manage uncertainty and instead to choose a definitive or black and white way of explaining a partner's disagreeable behavior,” Zola explained.

If these character judgments are left unchecked, the assumptions can deepen into negative feelings like resentment that make it impossible for support and trust in a relationship to grow, resulting in a downward spiral for the relationship.

How does it start?

open image in gallery ‘Over time, contempt changes the way we see our partner and can cause us to filter nearly everything they do through a negative lens, even when their behavior was not intended to hurt us,’ one relationship expert said ( Getty/iStock )

As marriage and family therapist Jamelia Knox told The Independent, contempt in a relationship can start as easily as teasing and body language like rolling eyes or sighing.

“It can escalate to be more overtly disrespectful: name calling, mimicking behaviors and superiority where you don't see your partner as your equal, but you see yourself as better than them, or they see themselves as better than you,” Knox explained.

Licensed psychologist and couples therapist Dr. Timothy Nguyen listed off early signs of contempt as “sarcasm, crassness, sharp humor, teasing, passive-aggressive comments, demeaning comments, and minimizing remarks.” Nonverbal clues might include eye rolling, sneering and laughing whenever a partner speaks.”

Zola, who described the behavior as “criticism on steroids,” agreed on the eye rolling and also warned against “all or nothing language,” saying: “It starts based on real experiences of disappointment in the relationship; often quite ‘normal' disappointments.’”

For example, statements like, “You never do XYZ for me,” and “That’s what you always say,” treat a character judgment as an impossible personality trait to fix, rather than a symptom of a broken relationship cycle.

How can contempt be prevented?

open image in gallery ‘When anxiety is present, couples must learn to separate the symptom from the partner while also recognizing that anxious questioning is more about an internal struggle with safety instead of an attack on each other’s worth or the relationship’s worth,’ one expert said ( Getty/iStock )

Although the bitterness of contempt is a surefire sign of underlying issues in a relationship, Nguyen said that it doesn’t have to be an “automatic dealbreaker.” “Rather,” he said, “it is often a desperate and distorted survival mechanism within a relationship.”

The most important thing that a couple feeling negative thoughts about each other can do is go to therapy. It might seem obvious, but talking through issues with a clear third party can help foster healthy communication in order to avoid small hurts that pile up.

Knox said that preventing contempt includes “being intentional about showing appreciation to your partner, just making sure you treat them as your equal, that they are just as valuable in a relationship as you are.” She recommended using “I” statements to communicate during arguments.

“When anxiety is present, couples must learn to separate the symptom from the partner while also recognizing that anxious questioning is more about an internal struggle with safety instead of an attack on each other’s worth or the relationship’s worth,” Knox explained. “This reframe, it can help to prevent the defensive shutdown that leads to more contempt from both partners.”

News.title: India preparing to evacuate thousands as Cyclone Arnab approaches Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Two states along India's eastern coast were preparing to evacuate thousands of people ahead of Cyclone Arnab, which is expected to make landfall on Wednesday.

One of the states said it would also close schools in some districts for two days.

Arnab, which formed over the Bay of Bengal before intensifying into a ⁠cyclonic storm, is expected ​to ⁠make landfall in Andhra Pradesh state by Wednesday morning, with gusts of as much ⁠as 140kmph (87mph), India's weather office ​said.

The cyclone will probably intensify further, it added.

The weather system is expected to bring heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to ‌Andhra Pradesh's northern and central ‌coastal districts, and southern regions of neighbouring Odisha.

Andhra Pradesh has called for boats at sea to return ashore and ordered speedy restoration of power in case of disruptions.

A senior Andhra Pradesh disaster management official told Reuters on Monday the state government had identified 570,000 people as vulnerable and evacuations would start on Monday evening.

Odisha's government announced the closure of schools and colleges in five districts for Tuesday and Wednesday, and said it was preparing to move residents of low-lying areas to cyclone shelters.

The Bay of Bengal is one of the world's ‌major regions ​for tropical cyclones.

News.title: Jordanian security forces arrest 3 men for a deadly attack on a church
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jordanian security forces arrested three men Monday for an attack on a Greek Orthodox Church that killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen.

The Public Security Directorate said the three suspects were arrested following a dawn shootout and that all three were wounded. No members of the security forces were injured in the dawn operation in Karak, south of Jordan’s capital, Amman. Karak is home to a minority Christian population.

The attack on the Greek Orthodox Church in Karak took place Friday during a funeral. Three men were reported to have taken part in the attack.

There was still no claim of responsibility, and no armed group has been accused of the attack.

Jordan's Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya identified the three men as those responsible for the attack.

“The security services have fulfilled their duties, resulting in the capture of those who carried out this terrorist act,” he said in a phone interview with state TV Al-Mamlaka. “They put up fierce resistance against the security forces, but were ultimately subdued and taken into custody, having sustained severe injuries.”

He added that there “are three individuals involved; they were identified early on in the wake of the terrorist incident, and the security services employed all the means at their disposal to apprehend them.”

King Abdullah II directed authorities to respond with “an iron fist” against what he called the outlaws of Islam and anyone attempting to undermine the unity of the Jordanian people.

News.title: Salah-mania grips Turkey after soccer star joins Trabzonspor club
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ever since soccer star Mohamed Salah posted a photo of himself last month sitting on a small boulder in a remote highland more than an hour from the city of Trabzon in northeastern Turkey, fans have flocked to the spot to pose in the same position.

The unlikely tourist attraction is not the only sign of the Salah-mania sweeping Turkey since the Egyptian star signed with the Trabzonspor club in August after leaving England’s iconic Liverpool club.

His arrival came as a much-needed boost to Turkish soccer fans’ spirits, which had been dashed months earlier when Turkey’s national team played in its first World Cup in 24 years only to exit the tournament without scoring any goals.

“God willing, we will win the championship title with him this year,” said Sinan Mor, who attended a match hosted by Trabzonspor Monday against Besiktas, one of Turkey’s most popular football clubs, which was in talks to sign Salah before he went to Trabzonspor. Mor wore a traditional thobe and a shemagh head wrap in the team's colors with sunglasses that had “MO SALAH” written on them.

Ahead of the match, Associated Press journalists who visited the “Salah rock” counted 46 visitors within two hours.

“If you can bring a global superstar to one of the most remote highland villages in Trabzon, that means something to us,” said Mustafa Bektas, a 44-year-old Trabzon supporter who travelled from Sakarya in western Turkey for the game and made the trek to pose on the boulder.

In the city, Salah-themed merchandise and art have popped up everywhere. Muralist Yildiray Yildirim said he's received multiple requests for Salah-themed murals outside local businesses after he painted an image of him wearing his Trabzonspor jersey on a wall outside a park.

On Google Maps, the club’s stadium is already marked as Mohamed Salah Camii — or mosque — in a nod to his fans’ almost religious fervor.

A new dawn for Salah

The move of a world record-breaking football star from the English Premier League to a lower tier European league team would usually mark the twilight of their career.

But for Salah, transferring from Liverpool to Turkey’s Trabzonspor at the age of 34 marked a new dawn.

Salah made a name as the third-highest goal scorer in Liverpool’s history and the world record holder for the most left-footed Premier League goals, but his latest campaign was disappointing. He scored only 12 goals, had a public falling out with coach Arne Slot, and in March announced he would leave.

Since his transfer to Trabzonspor, fans and commentators say Salah rediscovered his scoring touch, with teammates who bolster his strengths and an entire city that is turning into a fan club.

Nearly all the seats in Trabzonspor’s stadium, with capacity for more than 41,000 people, were full Monday. The stands roared every time Salah touched the ball. In the 71st minute, Salah scored one of the goals that won his team the derby and made him the leading scorer in the Turkish Super League.

The chants “Allah Allah Allah, Mohamed Salah” and “Trabzonlu (from Trabzon) Mohamed Salah” rose from the stands following the goal.

“He is a top player and a very good guy," Nigerian defender Chibuike Nwaiwu, Trabzonspor’s centre-back, told reporters. "He brings a lot of quality to the team.”

Representatives of Salah did not respond to requests for comment for this story.

Star brings economic benefits to Turkish city

Trabzon, a city of nearly a million people on Turkey’s Black Sea coast, is known for its green valleys, steep hills, a Byzantine-era monastery and head-strong locals with punchy accents.

The local economy runs on agriculture and tourism, and its team, where Istanbul’s jailed Mayor Ekrem İmamoglu was a board member before stepping into politics, is the city’s crown jewel.

Trabzonspor’s social media accounts gained a million new followers after signing Salah, according to local news reports, and new direct flights were launched between Cairo and Trabzon in August, anticipating a demand from Egyptian tourists.

Travel agent Ibrahim Eyupoglu said he has been selling packages with a ticket to a Trabzonspor match, a trip to the rock, and team merchandise.

“Before Salah, even derby games were played with empty stands. Now they’re always full,” he said.

Mustapha Sabbagh has been following Salah for 15 years from Lebanon. He signed up for the package and flew to Trabzon for two days. Then the 73-year-old jumped through a small river to sit on the “Salah rock.”

“Salah is the love of my heart. He has the magic touch,” Sabbagh said as he looked at his soaking-wet shoes and trousers with a big smile. “It’s worth it.”

Even Besiktas fans admitted their admiration. Salah’s talks with Besiktas collapsed over disagreements about his agent’s commission fee, according to Besiktas President Serdar Adalı.

“Unfortunately, I like his football a lot. The man is a star,” says Muhammed Mert Murat, 22, a Besiktas fan from Trabzon. He believes that Besiktas, which ranks fifth, just under Trabzon, would be leading Turkey’s Super League if Salah was playing for them.

Murat works in a tea shop next to a housing complex where locals believe Salah lives, and dreams about asking him why he didn’t choose Besiktas.

Still, he acknowledged, “There is a beautiful love for him here.”

News.title: Wolff puts ‘tequila on ice’ with Antonelli two points away from title
News.content:
Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Ferrari’s Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs. Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

A late virtual safety car after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac ground to a halt by the side of the track made the final laps rather processional, denying the huge crowds at COTA the opportunity of seeing the fast-closing Hamilton take on Verstappen for the final podium spot.

That might have been fun, with Verstappen having lost his cool with his team midway through the race, furious that they didn’t order team-mate Hadjar out of the way when he came up behind him after stopping: “Thanks guys. Really good strategy there. Stuck in the dirty air.”

Incredibly, his third place finish in Austin means is the first time since the final race of 2020 that Verstappen has been out of title contention.

But it hardly mattered. The day belonged once again to Antonelli who should be champion by the end of next week. Not that he was getting carried away. “It was the result we needed,” he said. “The whole team deserved it so much, bringing this [upgrade] package. It was also the perfect execution with the strategy to do the one stop.”

Asked about the title, he added: “We’re very close, we try to finish on a high and hopefully we can finish it very soon. I mean, the perfect way will be to finish in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season. I’m very aware that it’s very close, but the mindset doesn’t change. I want to finish on a high to go into 2027 with momentum.”

“Yeah, what a boy, no?” Wolff said, admiringly. “I was just saying before, I got a question about whether he was nervous before the race, and I said, ‘Oh, he just sneaked into my office before getting ready and said, ‘I’m just going to enjoy this right now, and it’s weird, I’m not thinking about the championship at all. Isn’t that funny?’”

Wolff added that there would “definitely be a lot of tequila on ice” in Mexico. In hindsight it was always going to be a more appropriate venue to crown the sport’s youngest ever champion. Antonelli is not, after all, old enough to drink yet in the state of Texas.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1
News.content:
Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

News.title: Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off
News.content:
This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Sports.title: Inside growing tensions at BBC ‘behind’ Mark Chapman’s deadpan delivery on Match Of The Day
Sports.content:
Next

MATCH of the Day host Mark Chapman’s dull presentation on Saturday night was blamed on growing tensions within BBC Sport.

Fans blasted the deadpan delivery of usually-upbeat Chappers, 53.



One wrote online: “Is Mark Chapman having a massive sulk or did he have a row with someone just before going on air?”

Another added: “Pretty sure the host is usually a lot more cheerful.”



Chapman, said to be dating co-star Kelly Cates, is believed to be unhappy about cuts being introduced by department chief Alex Kay-Jelski.

A TV insider said: “All the whispers are that whether this was deliberate or not his demeanour was all down to being enraged by the changes.



“It is a deeply unhappy ship at the moment.

“Fingers are inevitably pointed at the captain, Jelski.”



The show has seen a dip in viewing figures since long-time host Gary Lineker left last year.

Just over 1.86millon watched on Saturday.

That figure compares to 2.24million the same time in 2025 and 2.44million in 2024.

The BBC and Mark were asked for comment.

Sports.title: Ben White desperate for England recall after impressing Thomas Tuchel during Arsenal win over Everton
Sports.content:
Next

BEN WHITE once looked like he may never play for England again — now he is desperate to get back in the squad.

And the defender boosted his chances on Saturday by setting up Arsenal’s second goal in their 2-0 win over Everton, with Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel watching on at the Emirates Stadium.



White, 29, returned to the England fold in the spring after a four-year absence that began when he left the 2022 World Cup finals in Qatar for personal reasons.

The right-back missed this summer’s tournament and the most recent squad due to injury but is eager to play for his country again.



Asked if he hoped to be in the England squad for next month’s Nations League games with Croatia and Spain, the Gunners star said: “Yeah, definitely.

“It is an amazing feeling playing for England. It’s like nothing else.

“If that does happen, I’ll be absolutely over the moon.” White was booed by some England supporters at Wembley as he made a rollercoaster return to the international stage in March.

The defender scored — but then gave away a penalty which enabled opponents Uruguay to snatch a last-minute 1-1 friendly draw.

It was claimed White’s 2022 exit followed a bust-up with Steve Holland, who was the long-term assistant of then England manager Gareth Southgate.

And White only made himself available for selection again after holding talks with German chief Tuchel when he took charge at the start of 2025.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The road back to an England international recall has not been easy, with White struggling for form and fitness.

And the worst of a series of injuries came in May, just two months after Tuchel had decided to pick White for the first time.

He damaged a knee during a 1-0 win at West Ham, which forced him to miss the Champions League final with Paris Saint—Germain and the World Cup finals.

White said: “It was tough. As soon as I did it, I knew. I have had little things like that before and I kind of digested it walking around the pitch.

“It was that quick, really. I knew that was going to be me for the season — and I had a little cry on the way round.



“That was it, once I got in the dressing room, I was focused on trying to recover and get back.

“I literally trained every day over the summer. I didn’t really have a break — that was my aim.”

The work over the break has paid off for White.

And he continued his good start to the season on Saturday — by helping Arsenal move level on 21 points with Premier League leaders Manchester City with this victory over David Moyes’ Merseysiders.

Summer signing Ezri Konsa put the Gunners ahead after seven minutes, when the former Aston Villa centre-back bundled the ball home from a corner.



The scruffy strike was in contrast to the slick move that White helped create for Arsenal’s second goal on 68 minutes.

The right-back’s dinked cross found Gabriel unmarked at the back post. White now has three assists this season, starting in seven of the Gunners’ eight Prem games.

Only Greek winger Christos Tzolis and Declan Rice can better that tally for Arsenal — and it was the ideal way for White to mark his 200th appearance for the club.



White said: “It’s really creeped up, creeped up slowly. It’s amazing to play 200 games for this club.

“I wouldn’t want to be anywhere else. I had four years on the bounce at different teams.

“So to come here and be here this long, and play that many games, is a really nice feeling.”

White may be on the bench tomorrow when Arsenal head to Fleetwood in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta also has Jurrien Timber as back-up at right-back.



White believes he and the Dutchman are benefiting from being fit at the same time.

He said: “It’s always been — you have to play, you have to play. Now, it’s a different moment.

“We can actually get some rest. I am sure you will see the best versions of each of us.

“It’s really nice to share the load with me and JT.”

Sports.title: Man Utd need to sack Michael Carrick after Bournemouth but buck can’t stop with him – Jason Wilcox must go as well
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED supporters know the manager has to go but the buck cannot stop with Michael Carrick.

United matchgoers have booed the manager before. On Sunday, they turned on the players as soon as Carrick disappeared down the tunnel.



Diogo Dalot had dozily lingered longer on the pitch than teammates, so was the last player left on it. The boos grew louder for a United player who has outstayed his welcome.

United have lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth three times within three years under three different managers. That is ample evidence that Carrick cannot be the only one who goes.



There was gallows humour on the Stretford End as they told Sir Jim Ratcliffe to shove his new stadium up his backside.

There were sinister songs about kissing Ratcliffe and the Glazers on a bonfire. Ousting the Glazers is wishful thinking but jettisoning director of football Jason Wilcox is not just doable but advisable.



Ratcliffe said last year he would not have “tolerated” Ed Woodward. Wilcox has mimicked Woodward by promoting a former player from interim to permanent head coach only for United to spiral.

It has been sooner and more spectacular than under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Carrick is cut from the same cloth as his colleague and friend, who was also in the running to replace Ruben Amorim in January.



That Wilcox considered Solskjaer was a red flag. Wilcox’s treatment of Amorim in their infamous Wolves debrief last season convinced the Portuguese to engineer his own sacking.

Wilcox does not control the purse strings but he has made dire decisions, dodges questions and was underqualified for the DoF role he was promoted to in June 2025.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Man Utd ratings vs Bournemouth MANCHESTER United hit a new low for the season, if that's possible, with the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Michael Carrick stuck Bruno Fernandes on the bench – supposedly for ‘football reasons only’ – and kept him there for the whole game. So how did those who did play get on – and were there any shining lights on another stormy afternoon in Manchester? Find out how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated and slated United’s flops right here.

His past with Leeds United and Manchester City makes him an easy target. An image of Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada was captioned “Agent Leeds and Agent Sham,” the latter a reference to Berrada’s 14 years at City.

In this era where managers or coaches answer to sporting directors, it can’t be just Carrick’s head who rolls. Wilcox is at United on the strength of his time as Berrada’s colleague at City. Jobs for the boys.

Carrick went past the point of no return last month. United did not have the courage to dismiss him during the elongated international break.



The heat was turned up on City amid their guilty verdict, so those upstairs at United crossed their fingers and covered their own backsides.

They have since had them spanked by Atletico Madrid, Como and Bournemouth.

Sports.title: Barcelona 1 Real Madrid 2: Mbappe rains on Lamine Yamal’s parade to claim El Clasico win after Bellingham brilliance
Sports.content:
Next

KYLIAN MBAPPE will not win the Ballon d’Or – but he heads to London having firmly wiped the smile from Lamine Yamal’s face.

Mbappe’s double, a comical opener and a shock late winner, ended Barcelona’s perfect LaLiga start.



This is why Jose Mourinho was brought back.

Ahead of the Ballon d’Or showdown between Yamal and Harry Kane tonight, Barca’s teenage terror was, in prime Mourinho fashion, booted to the Clasico fringes by Real.



Mbappe has touted himself for football’s top individual prize, but surely cannot top either Kane or his LaLiga rival tomorrow night.

But in cutting the gap to the top a from six to three points, he and Real remain in the title hunt, Raphinha’s goal irrelevant and Barca hearts broken.



Mourinho had said there was to be no specific plan to stop Barcelona’s young phenom.

He may not have altered his tactics, but Marc Cucurella had certainly been given clear guidance: make his life hell.

Whether he was walloping his Spain teammate into the air, trying to relieve him of his shirt or just snapping at his heels the frizzy-haired full-back was sticking to his task with gusto and causing clear frustration.

LaLiga’s two grandest clubs have been freescoring this season but both were struggling to create clear openings.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Raphinha fired high and then, after a fine back-heel layoff from Anthony Gordon, sent another wide.

Mbappe attempted some acrobatics but was closer to the building site of a top-tier than Joan Garcia’s goal.

Perhaps then it was inevitable that, with the eyes of the world on the Nou Camp, the opener would be more by accident than design.

Taking a break from shamelessly kicking lumps out of Yamal, Cucurella fed Yan Diomande down the left.



The winger drove forward and guided a low cross with the outside of his boot, which is where the quality ended and the slapstick took over.

Gerard Martin arrived on the scene to clear, but thumped the ball straight into Mbappe, who was flinching instead of finishing but still ended up celebrating as it cannoned in off of his knee.

Yamal had the chance to hit back almost immediately, fed on the edge of the six-yard box by Fermin Lopez but duffed his finish entirely.



A superb Bellingham run five minutes after the restart opened the door for Real to double their lead.

Two-on-one with Mbappe all the Englishman had to do was square the ball, but he opted to go alone and made a mess of it.

There was much better to come, however.



After Raphinha’s leveller looked to have this Clasico on course for a point-a-piece, Bellingham, belatedly, rose to the moment.

Some stunning skill, sidestepping one Barca shirt and rolling another, sent Eduardo Camavinga haring down the right.

The French sub squared for his compatriot to prod home and seal a first Real Madrid win here in three years.

Mourinho dropped to his knees and pumped his fist as bottles rained down on his players who celebrated in front of the Barca fans.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A bit more of that and this time next year, the Ballon d’Or and a bit more may be in the hands of Mbappe.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker and Harry Kane’s old bosses on why striker should be England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE is the bookies’ favourite to win the Ballon d’Or tonight — as it comes to London for the first time.

The 70th anniversary ceremony is being held at the London Palladium Theatre, in tribute to its first winner, England great Stanley Matthews.



Three Lions captain Kane bagged an astonishing 73 GOALS for club and country last season — only ­bettered by Lionel Messi’s 82 in 2011-12.

Kane, a league winner with Bayern Munich, faces fierce competition from the likes of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.



Gary Lineker and Kane’s former bosses Harry Redknapp and Tim Sherwood told SunSport’s Jack Rosser and Isabelle Barker why Kane should be the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

GARY LINEKER

I’ve got a feeling it will be Harry. What he’s done has been amazing.

There are a lot of really, really good players in the world at the moment.

The Ballon d’Or is the Ballon d’Or. It’s way more important than it was in my day. I should have won it. I was robbed in 1986!

It’s between Harry and Lamine Yamal, if you look at the bookmakers — and you could make a case for both, obviously.

Kylian Mbappe and Yamal have made cases for themselves, as has Harry in a way — he’s done all the interviews.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

I’ve never seen him appear so much all over the place. And that’s great.

That’s how it is nowadays.

So you put yourself out there without quite saying it to everybody, classically British in his modesty, I suppose.

But he’s absolutely deserving if he wins it. And I hope he does, it would be great to see an English player win it.



He’s also a really good bloke, as well as a magnificent all-round centre-forward.

And to score that many goals this season, he totally merits it.

If you’re talking about the best footballer, it’s hard to look past Yamal. But I’d actually say this year’s Lionel Messi is still the world’s best player.

He was easily the best player at the World Cup. He really was. Spain won it, so therefore, Rodri won it. And he deserved it, too.



But Messi was unbelievable. He’s won enough. I think it’ll come down to Harry, I’ve got a feeling it’ll be him.

There are certain things that those voting have to weigh up about the success of your season.

But Harry won a double for Bayern Munich and hit a multitude of goals.

He won the European Golden Boot. He scored six goals at the World Cup.



Didn’t quite manage it at the end.

Will not winning a World Cup or Champions League count against him in some people’s eyes?

Because Spain won the World Cup and the World Cup is generally the big thing of the year.

Someone like Mbappe would have been running him close.



But Real Madrid didn’t win anything either — and France didn’t quite make it.

Kane was also brilliant at the World Cup. So you’re in among the game’s absolute elite.

I think it’s 50-50 between Harry and Yamal, ultimately — and it’s in London!

HARRY REDKNAPP

I have a funny story about Harry Kane, who I worked with when I was Tottenham manager.



I loaned him out when he was 17 to Barry Hearn, who was the chairman of Leyton Orient.

Hearn rang me and said ‘We’re going to get relegated. Have you got any players at Tottenham you could loan me?’

So I said, ‘Yeah, I’ve got three kids here you can have, take them, it will do them the world of good to go and play’.

So I loaned him three players, and I was at a function the other week where he spoke.



He said, ‘Harry loaned me three players — and at the end of the season we stayed up’.

Hearn recalled saying at the time ‘Andros Townsend, he could go back and play for Tottenham’, which he did, he played for England.

‘Stephen Caulker, he could go back and play for Tottenham’, he did — and he played for England, too.

He said, ‘Kane, no, he’ll never be good enough to play for Tottenham’, but he said at the function, ‘Shows you what I knew about football!’



To be fair, I don’t think any of us saw him going on to become the best centre-forward in the world, which he is.

And he should now win the Ballon d’Or.

He was a boy, like Frank Lampard, who would practise after training for an hour, every day, with Jermain Defoe, shooting, finishing, practising, wanting to be a success.

“I gave him his senior debut at Spurs in a Europa League qualifier in 2011 against Hearts.



Last 10 Ballon d'Or winners 2025 – Ousmane Dembele

2024 – Rodri

2023 – Lionel Messi

2022 – Karim Benzema

2021 – Lionel Messi

2019 – Lionel Messi

2018 – Luka Modric

2017 – Cristiano Ronaldo

2016 – Cristiano Ronaldo

2015 – Lionel Messi

2014 – Cristiano Ronaldo

“Our progression to the group stage was all but secure following a 5-0 victory in the first leg in Edinburgh.

“We got a penalty, and he’s only a kid, and he grabbed the ball and he wanted to take it, but he actually missed it!

“That shows what he was like — you had all those fantastic players in that team — but he didn’t care.

“He has remained humble, and he’s got time for everybody. He’s a fantastic human being. Really genuine.”

TIM SHERWOOD

Didn’t hesitate to give Harry Kane his first ­Premier League start.



Emmanuel Adebayor was a big player on big money — who we had signed from Manchester City.

Roberto Soldado, the top goalscorer in Spain, had come to Tottenham for a record fee.

He had a lot of traffic in his way. We know how many goals Jermain Defoe scored in the Prem.



But I judged everyone on a level playing field.

I watched Harry every day in training and decided the time was right to give him the opportunity.

I knew he wouldn’t be fazed by it.

He almost looked at me when I told him he was going to play against ­Sunderland on a Monday as if to say, ‘about time!’

I knew there wasn’t any danger of him going home and not ­sleeping properly.



He backed his ability and needed someone to back him too. I gave him that little bit of love he needed.

He took his opportunity with both hands.

A lot of people talk to me about Harry Kane’s failed loans. I don’t see any of them as failures.

They were better development pathways than playing with the Under-21s.



I always felt we needed him to go out and play competitive football.

It was the environment of meaning something.

The boys he played with at Orient needed to pay their mortgages.

He’s about the team before himself. That’s why everyone loves him.

If I asked him, he would pick winning the Champions League this season with Bayern Munich over the Ballon d’Or.



He’s just a model ­professional and that is why Alan Shearer is ­quaking in his boots.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

I think he will eventually look for a team that might win trophies in England.

He wants to come back to beat that Shearer’s Prem goalscoring record.

Because of his professionalism and durability, I think he would be able to.

Sports.title: Sean Dyche ‘lined up for Premier League return’ after eight months out as manager on brink of being sacked
Sports.content:
Next

SEAN DYCHE could be handed a surprise Premier League lifeline as Crystal Palace consider making a change in the dugout.

The 55-year-old has been without a club since being axed by Nottingham Forest in February but is now being tipped to make a comeback in South London.



According to The Telegraph, Dyche is high on Palace’s list of potential replacements for Pierre Sage, who is facing an uncertain future following another miserable result.

The Eagles were booed off by their own fans after Newcastle cruised to a 2-0 victory at Selhurst Park.



Will Osula broke the deadlock just two minutes after the restart before Harvey Barnes doubled the visitors’ lead.

It was another afternoon to forget for Sage, whose side were battered 5-0 by bitter rivals Brighton the previous weekend.



And the Frenchman’s troubles are mounting, with Palace sitting just one point above the drop zone after winning only two of their opening eight league games.

The Eagles have also shipped a staggering 19 goals in those matches, giving them the worst defensive record in the division.

Sage, 47, only arrived in the summer to replace Oliver Glasner, who had guided Palace to FA Cup and Europa Conference League glory.

Dyche also faces competition from former Tottenham and Brentford boss Thomas Frank, while ex-Ipswich boss Kieran McKenna could also contend for the Eagles job.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Dyche, meanwhile, could offer some much-needed experience after spending almost a decade at Burnley, where he earned two promotions and even secured European football on a shoestring budget.

He also helped Everton beat the drop before his brief spell at Forest ended after just 114 days.

But Sage remains in charge for now and faces a huge test against Tottenham next weekend, with Liverpool also on the horizon before the international break.

Sports.title: Incredible moment goalkeeper steps up and scores late free-kick as subs pour onto pitch to celebrate
Sports.content:
Next

A RUSSIAN goalkeeper scored a worldie free-kick in the dying minutes of normal time to give his team an incredible lead.

Ural’s Aleksandr Selikhov stepped up to the mark in his yellow jersey with a whole 23.3 metres in the way between him and the Chelyabinsk goalposts.



In the 87th minute, the 32-year-old plucked up the courage to boot it like a dart to the bullseye with an almighty kick.

The Chelyabinsk goalkeeper never had a chance, needing to stretch all the way to the near post and still missing it.





He tumbled to the ground as one of Selikhov’s team-mates booted the ball into the back of the Chelyabinsk net for good measure.

Celebrations erupted from the visiting fans with a flurry of orange players sprinting towards the electric party.

While some of Ural’s stars tried their best to collect the shotstopper for a hug, he was unstoppable in making it to the fans.

Selikhov jumped one barrier and then another, before lifting two arms in the air in a roar of elation.



The team’s classic orange and green colours were all over the place as fans swung their scarfs and waved their flags.

Even the stewards looked to be clapping the stunning moment – along with the substitutes.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But the game did not end there.

Four minutes into injury time, Brazilian centre-back Italo netted again leaving the blockbuster clash at 3-1.

The three points sent Ural into the top four of the Russian First League but they still trail leaders Nizhny Novgorod by a huge 12 points.



Meanwhile, Chelyabinsk sink firmly into the middle of the table in 12th.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick future LIVE: Board hold crisis talks as Man Utd boss on verge of sack
Sports.content:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick could be facing the sack following Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford

Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United is hanging by a thread after the Reds suffered a humiliating 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

Carrick, 45, had come into the game against the Cherries under huge pressure following a dismal start to the season, with the Reds winning just TWO in 11 fixtures across all competitions.

But United were humiliated on home soil with Bournemouth running out comfortable winners. Rayan put the Cherries ahead in the 38th minute before Marcus Tavernier capitalised on a defensive error from Leny Yoro to double the visitors' lead.

Despite an improved start to the second half, Bournemouth made it three in the 71st minute with Evanilson rounding Senne Lammens before curling the ball home from a tight angle.

That is how it remained with Carrick now facing the sack after United extended their winless run to seven matches. They have dropped to 16th in the Premier League table on just seven points from a possible 24.

Sports.content:
Fabian Hurzeler aims thinly-veiled dig at Liverpool after Brighton lose at Anfield

Brighton suffered just their second defeat in 13 games this season as Liverpool's first half double did the damage at Anfield, much to the annoyance of Fabian Hurzeler

View 2 Images Fabian Hurzeler had a dig at Liverpool post-match (Image: Getty Images)

Fabian Hurzeler believes Brighton were the only side "who really tried to create and win", despite suffering a 2-0 defeat by Liverpool.

‌



‌



Quickfire first-half goals from Andoni Iraola's side settled the Premier League clash at Anfield on Sunday. Florian Wirtz's effort went in off Pascal Gross for an own goal before Alexander Isak tucked in Bradley Barcola's cross four minutes later.

‌



Yasin Ayari fired Brighton's best chance over the crossbar before striking the post with another attempt. The Seagulls could not respond to the early blitz and suffered just their second defeat in 13 games across all competitions this season.

‌



Hurzeler's side boasted 64 per cent possession and had 1.35 xG to Liverpool's 0.87 xG, but couldn't make it count, registering just one shot on target to the Reds' four. And there was more than just a hint of sour grapes in the Brighton boss' post-match press conference.
