Sports.title: The game is up for Michael Carrick - but Man Utd are a shambles of a football club
Sports.content:
The game is up for Michael Carrick - but Man Utd are a shambles of a football club

MANCHESTER UNITED 0-3 BOURNEMOUTH: Michael Carrick will be the fall guy but Red Devils fans know where the blame lies for this latest malaise

View 2 Images Carrick appeared to wave goodbye to United fans after the game (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

A huge banner unfurled in the Stretford End said it all in one word. The message simply said: “Standards” written alongside pictures of Bryan Robson, Roy Keane and Eric Cantona.

‌



‌



How this great club has fallen. From the glory days of those Manchester United legends to this utter shambles at Old Trafford. Sadly, this must be the last rites for Michael Carrick’s reign because there is simply no way that he can survive this abject humiliation.

‌



At the final whistle, Carrick went to each corner of the ground as if he was saying goodbye. The game is up. It is always the manager who ends up paying.

‌



This will go down as one of the worst, most damaging and shocking defeats United have ever suffered at Old Trafford. You actually felt sorry for Carrick as he looked lost on the touchline.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Carrick’s attempt to stir some of reaction with his emotional, heartfelt five-minute and 25 second monologue followed by the bold decision to drop Bruno Fernandes did not work.

Instead, yet another manager has been left heading for the scrapheap as Old Trafford should be renamed the Theatre of Nightmares.

‌



Carrick was clearly calling out United’s current generation when he said they should follow the example of there likes of Wayne Rooney and Sir Bobby Charlton by showing “sacrifice and hard work.”

But United were meek, spineless and pathetic. They showed no fight for the manager, no passion for the fans and were an absolute disorganised mess.

‌



Bournemouth played United off the pitch. They were sensational. But United were as bad as Bournemouth were good. By the end, Old Trafford had turned toxic.

The Stretford End was chanting: “Sell United, now f*** off home.” They turned on the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Then they saved the encore with a chorus of abuse for director of football Jason Wilcox.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox watch on at Old Trafford (Image: Getty Images)

Old Trafford was half empty by the final whistle and when United fans - some of the best and most loyal in the country - have given up then you know it is all over.

‌



This has descended into an ugly civil war. The club has lost its way thanks to bad ownership, bad recruitment and too many players who are not fit to wear this famous old shirt.

These days, the loudest rumbling from the Old Trafford crowd comes when Harry Maguire ventures forward. At least he showed some heart. But that is not enough.

‌



The real surprise was that it took Bournemouth so long to score. Ayden Heaven was booked for a mindless two-footed challenge. Justin Kluivert swung over a free kick and there was Brazil star Rayan completely unmarked to fire home at the back post after 38 minutes.

The second goal was comically bad. Lenny Yoro chased down a long ball, slipped and let in Adrien Truffert. His cross was turned home by Marcus Tavernier. That is when the United fans unfurled their Standards banner.

‌



United were just lucky that Bournemouth were so wasteful. It could have been five or six. The third goal came after 71 minutes.

Man Utd next manager odds as clear favourite emerges to replace Michael Carrick READ MORE :

‌



Lewis Cook’s long ball forward was chased down by Evanilson. The Bournemouth striker rounded keeper Senne Lammens and then showed fabulous skill to curl a shot into the top corner.

We used to expect those sort of great moments of magic from United. Now the opponents come to Old Trafford to showcase their talent and humiliate this once great club.

‌



Tellingly, Fernandes - the player dropped days after questioning Carrick’s tactics - never came off the bench. But no-one could really question that decision. He has been so poor this season. Yet another player blaming everyone but himself.

Even more revealing, the United fans chanted Carrick’s name just before the final whistle. At the end, Carrick was actually cheered as he went round the ground to thank the fans while thumping his chest to show the club is in his heart.

Article continues below

But those same fans let Carrick leave the pitch - and then turn their anger on the players who were roundly booed as they went down the tunnel. The Old Trafford faithful have decided who is to blame. And it is certainly not Carrick.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick is a scapegoat - the Old Trafford faithful know who is to blame at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is a scapegoat - the Old Trafford faithful know who is to blame at Man Utd

Michael Carrick is on the brink of being sacked after Manchester United were thrashed 3-0 by Bournemouth, but the real culprits for the club's mess were sat in the stands at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is the lightning rod for criticism at Old Trafford (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick was the man standing in the eye of the storm on the Old Trafford touchline, but the chant from the stands made clear the feelings of the Manchester United supporters.

‌



‌



After being taunted by the jubilant Bournemouth fans with shouts of "you're getting sacked in the morning", the United faithful issued their response. It was unequivocal support for their beleaguered boss.

‌



The Sky Sports cameras then honed in on two of the other architects of the current mess at United: Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox. The United chiefs are responsible for the decision to hire Carrick as the full-time manager in the summer and they were also behind the lopsided transfer window which saw £155million spent on midfielders and nothing elsewhere.

‌



United's malaise is nothing new. Yet the nature of the past two games has made a managerial sacking feel all but inevitable. After the shambolic display in Como came the disjointed thrashing by Bournemouth.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The build-up to the game was dominated by Bruno Fernandes. Carrick made the correct call in leaving the United skipper on the bench after his subordination in Como. But it didn't have the desired effect and two wins from 12 games this season, with an extremely daunting fixture list on the horizon, means the writing is on the wall.

"It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," Gary Neville said on co-commentary for Sky Sports.

‌



"It is horrible to say that. I did think that last season that the club should have gone for the best manager they could have got and not given the job to Michael Carrick. Because I felt this might happen this quickly but this has gone very, very sour very quickly and the club is a mess."

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada will likely sack Michael Carrick for their own mistakes (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

It was a neat summation of the current situation at United, where it is now nigh-on impossible to identify a glimmer of hope. The way they conceded the second and third goals spoke of a team completely bereft of confidence - and of one sorely lacking in quality.

‌



Leny Yoro fell over to allow Marcus Tavernier to score. Senne Lammens lost his bearings and left his goal unguarded for Evanilson to help himself. They were mistakes more befitting of pub football in the local park.

The neglect the club's hierarchy have shown to the defence is ridiculous. And, what's worse, it was completely foreseeable. The failure to sign a left-back left an obvious Achilles' heel, while there is no chance any serious club would still be relying on over-the-hill players like Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt.

‌



That is there for all to see this season, and the Stretford End's focus as the game meandered to its close showed they know where the blame lies. Just as former executive Ed Woodward was previously, director of football Wilcox is now the lightning rod for their ire.

"They have badly let this football club down," Neville said as Wilcox and Berrada came into view after the full-time whistle.

Article continues below

He's not wrong. But their jobs are not up for discussions. They will be the ones to throw Carrick to the wolves after another another toxic performance.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick on brink as Man Utd fans make voices heard in Bournemouth hammering
Sports.content:
Manchester United's season plumbed new depths on Saturday as Bournemouth secured a comfortable victory on an afternoon where Old Trafford turned toxic.

A Bruno Fernandes-less Red Devils side lacked any spark with Michael Carrick now surely on the brink of losing his job as the Cherries won 3-0 at United for the third time in four years.

The hosts were two goals down by half-time with Rayan and Marcus Tavernier putting the Cherries on course for another success in Manchester. Evanilson capped the afternoon with a sensational third 20 minutes from time.

The two opening goals coming inside five minutes of the first half - Rayan finishing from a free-kick before Tavernier benefited from a defensive slip.

‌



United showed nothing by way of a fightback in the second-half and Evanilson was able to round Senne Lammens before finishing brilliant from out wide in front of the travelling fans.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Bournemouth had the better of the early exchanges and found themselves bearing down on goal, but Rayan could not make the most of a three-on-one opportunity as his effort was blocked. United gradually got themselves back into the contest without posing any major threat.

‌



The deadlock was finally broken come the 37th minute as Rayan's side-footed finish at the back post opened the scoring. His goal coming from a free-kick that owed to a poor Ayden Heaven two-footed challenge, which only earned him a yellow card.

The travelling faithful quickly erupted into chants of 'you're getting sacked in the morning' as Carrick watched his side fall behind yet again. But things would get worse before the interval as Leny Yoro, being chased down by Adrien Truffert, slipped and that allowed the left-back to square the ball for Tavernier, who slotted into an empty net.

View 5 Images Michael Carrick is now without a win in eight with his job in major doubt

Matheus Cunha, not Fernandes, was the man called upon to change United's direction of travel as the hosts ran out for the second half, but only the offside flag prevented Bournemouth from going three goals up inside 30 seconds of the restart.

‌



Evanilson was deserving of his strike after 70 minutes as he curled home from far out after rounding the United goalkeeper, but come the dying stages Old Trafford had rafts of empty seats. The home fans had seen enough.

Those that remained at the Theatre of Dreams defiantly sung Carrick's name at full-time, instead reserving their ire for the players and ownership.

IS CARRICK'S BRUNO STATEMENT FINAL ACT?

With Fernandes, without Fernandes. There doesn't seem to be much of a difference when it comes to this United side. Carrick had little option but to drop his captain in light of the comments he made during the week. Was that going to be an example of self harm? Or did he have to show some authority?

In all honesty it probably didn't make much difference. United were seven games without a win with Fernandes in the team. That was extended to eight without him, and even with the Red Devils three goals down and needing a goal, the Portugal international remained glued to the bench with Carrick happy to go down without him. Cunha, Joshua Zirkzee and Shea Lacey all called upon instead.

‌



View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes was dropped to the bench and was forced to watch on

It would be remiss to claim that having Fernandes in the team would've changed the course of the afternoon. The Portuguese playmaker has not been replicating the form that made him the PFA Player of the Year last season.

His recent demise has mirrored that of his team, who were on a wave of momentum under Carrick last season as they rose up to third. This result now leaves them one point off being third from bottom as the Bournemouth fans sang that United were going down with City.

It isn't that bed, yet, but Carrick's latest and boldest roll of the dice has done nothing to change his fortunes, with time desperately running out.

‌



OLD TRAFFORD'S SEEN ENOUGH

When fans walk out before the half-time whistle you know you're in the midst of a low ebb. For all the dire afternoons at Old Trafford since 2013, the fans have showed more patience and staying power than the players, the managers and the hierarchy have deserved.

View 5 Images Evanilson capped Bournemouth's stellar outing with a third goal in the second-half (Image: Getty Images)

But in the midst of a seven game winless run, which was extended to eight, it was after Tavernier's goal that doubled Bournemouth lead that the camera panned to fans walking up the concourse and for the exit. That was only 42 minutes in, but they'd seen enough.

Even the boos, which have been more regular than ever this season, have been kept under wraps for the last decade considering the results and performances, but this feels like a real tipping point, and one that could see a major change, likely in the dugout.

‌



There was a huge black banner in the stands that read "standards". It had a images of those from yesteryear, when United were the dominant force. Nowadays they're a million miles from that, and things only seem to be getting worse.

View 5 Images Ayden Heaven was lucky to avoid a red card in the first-half

HEAVEN DODGES RED, BUT PAYS PRICE

Gary Neville remarked that we "don't see tackles like that anymore", half joking that the last time he saw a player fly in with two feet was in the 1980s when United great Bryan Robson was still playing.

The young defender is still very much a player learning his trade, but his poor tackle was lucky to escape a dismissal. VAR checked the challenge and claimed he stayed on the pitch only because he made no contact with Evanilson, who himself looked stunned that Heaven had even attempted such a tackle.

‌



To add insult to injury, it was from the resulting free-kick that Bournemouth scored their opening goal as Rayan volleyed home at the back post. Heaven himself was complaining for a foul as the delivery came in, but his complaint was surely born out of hope and not expectation. He and United simply got what they deserved.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola puts limit on Florian Wirtz as Liverpool boss defends goalless run
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola puts limit on Florian Wirtz as Liverpool boss defends goalless run

Florian Wirtz remains without a goal in the Premier League this season and Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola admits his position will not lend itself to him scoring regularly

View 2 Images Liverpool star Florian Wirtz has found himself under the spotlight for months (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola admits that Florian Wirtz is "not going to score 15 goals a season" as he launched another defence of the Liverpool playmaker.

‌



‌



Now into his second season at Anfield, more is being expected of the German, who cost a British record £116million when he moved to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen.

‌



He was part of a hugely underwhelming Liverpool team that finished fifth last season, which resulted in Arne Slot's sacking, and now Iraola is tasked with getting the most out of Wirtz. He has been regularly criticised with the Reds yet to find a position that routinely gets the best out of him.

‌



Wirtz has been hauled off after 70 minutes or earlier in three of Liverpool's seven games, but Iraola has claimed that the role that the German plays means he's never going to be regularly scoring.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“I’m delighted with Florian,” Iraola told the El Boro podcast. “He’s coming off three very good performances and I trust this is the start of finding his confidence again. We believe in him a lot. He is judged a lot in terms of goals and assists, but he is a player for whom that won’t be his strength.

“He’s not a No.10 or a second striker who is going to score 15 goals this year. No. I mean if he can do that, even better, but he’s a player who gives us a lot of control over the matches. He has a lot of confidence on the ball. Ultimately, we have to make him feel comfortable but he’s probably feeling more comfortable in Champions League matches.

‌



“In the Premier League, he has to get used to those duels. Here, duels are really hard to win. He’s in that process. It’s true he’s been here a year but he’s still acclimatising to this competition. But in terms of talent I have no doubt about him and in terms of attitude either. He is a player who works a lot.”

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola has continued to back his German playmaker

‌



Wirtz's performance in the Champions League win over LASK recently was arguably his best performance in a Liverpool shirt. The German was hugely creative with Bradley Barcola among the beneficiaries.

The Premier League has been a different story and he's come up with just the two assists domestically so far, and remains without a goal. Last term Wirtz equally found it difficult to regularly influence games in the final third.

Article continues below

Fitting the ex-Leverkusen man into the line-up is also having notable knock on affects. If he plays as the No 10 then only two midfield slots are available, leaving big names missing out. Equally if he were to play from out wide, which is an option, then he is playing instead of one of the number of wingers in the Liverpool squad.

Sports.title: Smith beats Schindler in Dortmund thriller after Littler's QF exit
Sports.content:
Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund.

The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen.

Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw.

Schindler was broken in the next but offered a four-leg burst - including finishes of 116 and 127 - to cut the deficit to 9-7 and threaten a famous comeback, but the next three legs went with throw as Smith closed out victory and the £150,000 first prize.

Victory sees Smith join Michael van Gerwen, Phil Taylor, Rob Cross and Peter Wright as the only players to win multiple European Championship titles, with his latest success following his World Series of Darts title in September and lifting him to world No 6.

Machineseeker European Championship results Quarter-Finals: Ross Smith 10-6 Luke Woodhouse, Gerwyn Price 10-3 Stephen Bunting, Martin Schindler 10-1 Jonny Clayton, Krzysztof Ratajski 10-6 Luke Littler Semi-Finals: Ross Smith 11-7 Gerwyn Price, Martin Schindler 11-6 Krzysztof Ratajski Final: Ross Smith 11-8 Martin Schindler

"I'm not going to lie, I was a bit sweaty there going to that end with Martin - he wouldn't let up, would he!" Smith said. "Full credit to him. To have this trophy in my hands, to win another major - I'm absolutely over the moon and drained, but I'm buzzing!"

Luke Littler was the pre-tournament favourite to claim the only missing ranked major from his glittering CV, only for the world No 1 to suffer a shock quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajaski.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler failed to win a maiden European Championship as he suffered a surprise defeat at the hands of Krzysztof Ratajski (Credit: ITV)

How Smith secured Dortmund title

Schindler thrashed Jonny Clayton 10-1 and despatched Ratajaski - who eliminated Littler 11-6 in the previous round - to reach his maiden ranked TV final, with the German missing chances to grab the early lead against Smith.

He wasted multiple opportunities to break in the third leg but responded with a 14-dart hold in the next, levelling the match, before Smith quickly pulled away.

Image: Smith came into the event as No 1 seed after a strong season on the PDC European Tour

Smith took out an 86 finish to break and kept the German crowd quiet by sweeping all five legs in the next mini session, with Schindler only allowed back in when his opponent squandered five darts at double to open a seven-leg lead.

The pair traded breaks of throw before Schindler followed a 15-dart hold by firing successive ton-plus checkouts, with Smith stuttering over the closing legs before wrapping up victory with his fifth match dart.

"It's a strange one. I really don't think I played great this week," Smith added. "I think a lot of players let me off as well, but sometimes you have to win ugly. I'm proud of doing that because you have got to dig deep. You have to really fight hard and I think I've done that this weekend."

Despite just falling short of a first Premier title, Schindler made history in reaching the European Championship final on home soil and becoming the first German to reach a televised final.

"When I started playing darts ten years ago, I didn't expect anything and now I made a major final," said an emotional Schindler.

"I tried everything to win this one, but fair play to Ross, he played well. I lost but I'm still very happy! I'm going to be in the Grand Slam now. That's probably the best part of it!

Sports.title: 'The pace was rubbish' - Russell in blunt admission after Austin struggle
Sports.content:
George Russell admitted his pace in the United States Grand Prix was "rubbish", with the Mercedes driver at a loss to why he trailed race-winning team-mate Kimi Antonelli by such a large margin,

Russell finished 54 seconds behind the sister Mercedes in the 56-lap race in an eighth place that only just kept him in mathematical championship contention heading to this week's race in Mexico, where Antonelli is set to clinch the crown.

Russell had held his grid position of sixth through the race's first stint but dropped to eighth after serving a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop for an incident with Oscar Piastri in the opening lap, when he was judged to have gained an advantage over the McLaren by running off track and retaining position.

Russell subsequently spent the final 26 laps on the similarly one-stopping Piastri's tail but was unable to find a way back past the Australian driver.

Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The pace was rubbish. That's the long and short of it.

"The five-second [penalty] didn't help things and probably cost me two or three positions but the pace wasn't good enough when it needed to be."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty.

Russell made no excuse for his lack of competitiveness and said he had no immediate answer for why his Austin weekend was such a struggle.

"Just not been quick enough," he added.

"I need to try and understand why that is. It's strange when you're so far off.

"Hopefully there are some answers somewhere but at the moment I don't have them."

What went wrong for Russell?

Antonelli's win was his ninth of the year and represented what Toto Wolff, Mercedes' team principal, believes was "the best race that he's delivered so far".

It was the first win for Mercedes upgraded car, which has taken time for the world championship leaders to get the best out of since the aerodynamic revisions debuted at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of October.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix.

The team have said, however, that the changes have narrowed the car's optimum set-up window.

On Russell's weekend, Wolff said: "George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult.

"In Q2 he was there and thereabouts. Q3, it didn't work. He said, 'that goes on me'.

"And today in the race, I don't know, we got stuck behind Piastri, which looks a bit unfair why he didn't get past. It's the same engine, it's the same electric charging and deployment. But I'm going to see him now."

'He's not 54 seconds slower over a race distance'

Analysis from Sky Sports F1's Jenson Button:

"George has had a lot of tough races but also some great races and that's the thing that's really difficult to understand - how he's able to get the maximum out of that car on some tracks but not at others.

"Austin was difficult as he started so far down. He was in the pack and when you're in the pack, sometimes it's difficult to move forward. You're in the dirty air. You try to do something different with strategy but then you get a five-second penalty which puts you back further.

"I don't believe his pace is that far off. He's not 54 seconds slower over a race distance."

Sports.title: Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for world title
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix.

Antonelli had an outside chance of clinching the 2026 title as early as Sunday's Austin race provided he won, Lewis Hamilton finished outside the top four and George Russell was ninth or lower.

And while he held up his side of the bargain by brilliantly claiming a ninth win of the season on a one-stop strategy to his nearest rivals' two, Hamilton took fourth and Russell eighth to stay in mathematical contention.

But Antonelli has moved 123 points clear of Russell, and 124 points clear of Hamilton, with just a maximum of 125 left to play for this season to make a coronation at next Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix all but inevitable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty

Antonelli, who only turned 20 in August and is in his second season of F1, will definitely clinch the title with four rounds to spare in Mexico if he finishes anywhere in the top nine.

"We are very close," said the Italian, who will also be assured of the title at the next round if neither Russell nor Hamilton win the race.

"We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."

Antonelli won at the Circuit of The Americas by 13 seconds with Charles Leclerc finishing a fine second for Ferrari after winning out against Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the battle of the two-stop strategies. Leclerc overtook Verstappen at Turn 12 after an entertaining battle with seven laps to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

Hamilton was fourth, crossing the line just one second behind Verstappen after also fast-catching the Red Bull late on, with Lando Norris fifth on a one-stop strategy ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar.

While Antonelli was peerless up front, team-mate Russell's difficult Austin weekend, and indeed season, was summed up by his disappointing eighth-place finish.

Russell, who had started sixth, dropped behind the McLarens after having to serve a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop after being judged to have gained an advantage by going off track in battle with Oscar Piastri on the first lap.

United States GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Lando Norris, McLaren



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) George Russell, Mercedes



9) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



10) Pierre Gasly, Alpine

The elongated pit stop dropped Russell behind Piastri, whom he was then unable to pass despite following closely for almost half the race. He described his race pace as "rubbish".

Liam Lawson continued his relentless points-scoring form with ninth for Racing Bulls, while Pierre Gasly was 10th for Alpine.

Faultless Antonelli returns to winning ways - and verge of history - in style

Despite his inexperience in just his second year of F1 and the fast-looming spectre of achieving his lifelong dream of becoming world champion, Antonelli had already barely put a foot wrong across the title run-in during a period when Mercedes have rarely had the fastest car.

The Italian had not won a race since his fortuitous triumph at the Spanish Grand Prix in mid-September and Mercedes' most recent upgrade, first brought to the car two races ago in Malaysia, had initially not delivered the results the team had expected.

But any suggestion that the season's world championship-leading team and driver might have to take a defensive approach to the final rounds of this season to get over the title-winning line was firmly put to bed in Austin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli looks ahead to Mexico as he moves to brink of a title win

Antonelli's pole position - his first in eight races since the Belgian Grand Prix since July - had been perhaps his most unexpected of the season and had led Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to play down the Italian's prospects of victory.

On Sunday, the Italian was alone among the top five on the grid to opt for the medium tyres for the race start and yet, despite his rivals behind having the grippier softs for the crucial uphill run to COTA's wide first corner, Antonelli had a dream getaway and easily converted his starting advantage into a lap-one lead.

It was instead second-placed Verstappen who came under pressure from behind, the Dutchman initially overtaken by Leclerc through the Esses before getting back ahead of the Ferrari into Turn 13 later round the opening lap.

But Antonelli had soon opened an early lead of four seconds and, struggling to keep up, Red Bull pitted Verstappen surprisingly early on lap 13. He took on a second set of soft tyres, locking him into a two-stop race given the requirement to run two different tyre compounds.

Ferrari soon followed suit with their drivers but Mercedes stuck to their guns on a projected one-stopper and did not pit Antonelli until the end of lap 24. When they did they switched him onto the more durable hard compound, ensuring he could go to the end of the race without stopping again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff says that Kimi Antonelli's performance at the United States Grand Prix was 'exceptional'

Antonelli rejoined in fourth place but was back in the lead by lap 32 by passing the long-running Leclerc.

Verstappen had by then pitted for a second time having run into a more problematic second stint on softs. And while the fresher tyres of the Red Bull and Ferrari into the closing laps meant Antonelli's lead over both came down, neither had sufficient speed to truly cause Mercedes alarm.

"It was the result we needed," said Antonelli. "The whole team deserve it so much.

"All this time putting so much work into bringing this new package and finally seeing the result is very pleasant.

"It was also perfect execution from strategy to call the one-stop. Really happy we made it stick. Today was a great team effort."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen reflects on the United States GP, in which he finished third

Verstappen had looked the most likely to challenge Antonelli on his two-stopper but, in the end, it was Leclerc who got closest.

Ferrari's soft-medium-medium tyre strategy allowed the Monegasque to display impressive turn of speed from his first stop onwards, eventually fighting back from his final stop to pass the long-running Norris and then Verstappen during his final stint.

"It was quite a good race," said Leclerc. "Unfortunately we came short of the victory which was our target.

"At the end of the day, a positive race. We had good pace. The first stint was more difficult."

Sports.title: Mbappe's late strike earns Mourinho and Real Clasico glory at Barca
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe's double took Real Madrid to a famous 2-1 Clasico win, which had Jose Mourinho sliding on his knees in celebration in Barcelona.

It was the 87th minute when Mbappe tucked in from Eduardo Camavinga's cutback following some sublime skill from Jude Bellingham. The celebrations from Real Madrid were wild, with their head coach unable to contain himself, his staff on the pitch, and his players clashing with Barcelona fans.

Real had been on the defensive after Raphinha's snapshot had levelled a pulsating clash, with Lamine Yamal narrowly clipping wide as LaLiga's defending champions pushed for a winner. Instead Real have closed to within three points of their great rivals. Atletico are second just two off Barca now.

Image: Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe celebrates after scoring against Barcelona

It's been a bad week for Hansi Flick's side, whose 11-game winning streak at the start of this season was halted with defeat in the Champions League at Paris St-Germain. This loss will sting far more - it's Real's first win in Barcelona in three years.

Mbappe's opener had been fortuitous, Gerard Martin slamming a clearance in off him. But Real's move to get to that point had been excellent and throughout the contest they showed they were willing to go toe-to-toe with their more favoured hosts.

There was controversy before Raphinha's equaliser, with Joao Cancelo not punished for putting his studs into Yan Diomande's calf. But Mourinho and Real Madrid will leave Spotify Camp Nou celebrating.

Key moments at Spotify Camp Nou...

18: SHOT! It's end-to-end as Guler steps in off the right and forces Garcia into a save moments after Gordon tested Lunin.

Image: Barcelona's Anthony Gordon, right, is challenged by Real Madrid's Arda Guler

24: SHOTS! Raphinha whacks one over the bar from 16 yards and then links up brilliantly with Gordon before bending a low effort just wide.

33: OVER! Mbappe scissor-kicks over the bar after a brilliant move featuring a big Bellingham tackle and Guler's gorgeous cross.

41: GOAL! Mbappe gives Real the lead when Gerard Martin whacks the ball against him from Diomande's cross into the box! A bizarre goal at the end of a fine team move from the visitors.

50: CHANCE! But Bellingham can't find the pass to Mbappe after skipping away on the counter to set up a two-on-one against Martin, who shuts him down.

57: CONTROVERSY! Cancelo puts his studs into Diomande's calf. The Real winger continues his attack before going to ground - but there's no retrospective punishment for the Barca defender.

61: GOAL! Pedri reverses a pass into Raphinha and his snapshot beats Lunin, who got a hand to the ball but couldn't keep the equaliser out.

Image: Barcelona's Raphinha celebrates after scoring against Real Madrid

66: SAVE! An amazing save from Lunin, as he claws away Martin's powerful header from a corner.

78: CLOSE! Lamine Yamal skips past a couple of challenges then clips a shot at goal - but the ball bounces just wide.

87: GOAL! Mbappe sensationally wins it for Real, slotting in after Camavinga cuts the ball back to him following sublime skill from Bellingham.

Sports.title: City's perfect start ended in derby draw with Man Utd
Sports.content:
A late equaliser from Elisabeth Terland earned Manchester United a well-earned 1-1 draw that ended Manchester City's perfect start to the WSL campaign.

City looked set for victory as Khadija Shaw finally broke the deadlock with a little over 20 minutes to go. However, it was Shaw who inadvertently set up Terland for the equaliser in the last minute of normal time.

Both teams came into the contest in good spirits. City had made a perfect start in their opening six WSL games, while United had been starting to click under Eva Olid.

It was the hosts who appeared more likely to find the opener following a tense first half. They were on top after the break, with Jess Park ratting the crossbar on the hour mark as they looked to make their dominance count.

Shaw had been having an uncharacteristically quiet evening, being heckled by home fans and marked out of the game by Maya Le Tissier in the first 45. She targeted Dominique Janssen when the game resumed and the switch paid off.

The PFA Player of the Year backed into the Dutch defender before turning and firing through her legs to find the bottom corner and give City the lead against the run of play on her 100th WSL appearance.

It was a bitter blow for the Red Devils, whose hard work looked set to be unrewarded. That was until Shaw's tame clearance from a deep Le Tissier cross fell to the feet of Terland, who dispatched perfectly to snatch a share of the spoils.

The result means that City only go level on points with Chelsea at the top, but fall behind Sonia Bompastor's side on goal difference following their come-from-behind win against Crystal Palace.

55: SAVE! Terland denied from close range by Yamashita.

60: OFF THE BAR! Park's dipping effort crashes off the woodwork.

63: SAVE! Shaw comes alive as she tests Tullis-Joyce.

68: GOAL! Shaw breaks the deadlock on her 100th WSL appearance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bunny Shaw opened the scoring for Man City

86: OFF THE LINE! Clinton fails to wrap up game against former side as Le Tissier clears on the line.

89: GOAL! Terland nets dramatic late equaliser.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Elisabeth Terland scored a very late equaliser for Man Utd

Jeglertz: Disappointed to concede so late

Man City boss Andree Jeglertz speaking with Sky Sports:

"You remember the last five minutes where you concede a goal and you feel disappointed.

"Overall, it's a fantastic football game. An intense game, a lot of emotions during the whole game. United is giving us a big fight. You can't say anything about the result but of course you are disappointing when you concede late and had a big chance before that.

"I'm so happy for her [Bunny Shaw]. A tough game for her. A lot of hits and knocks and then she's the one scoring for us. She has done it so many times. At the same time, we always want to win games."

Terland: We had the chances to win

Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland speaking with Sky Sports:

"I think with the way the game evolves we should be happy with a point. I'm really happy with the performance today. We could've come away with a win. We will take the point at the end of the day.

"We had the chances today to get the goals. Even in the first half, we should be up. There's a lot to take from this game and this is the standard going forward.

"It's a fun way to play football. If we can play like this every week, it is enjoyable. We are competing against a top team and should probably win. That just speaks for itself."

Sports.title: Rodgers backs 16-game 'NFL International week' after Paris history
Sports.content:
Aaron Rodgers endorsed the introduction of an international week to the NFL season as he led the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris on Sunday.

Rodgers and the Steelers made history last year when they beat the Minnesota Vikings in the NFL's Dublin debut at Croke Park, before travelling overseas again this week to deliver another milestone moment for the league in the French capital.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell revealed on Friday that the league has plans to play a game in Tokyo, Japan in either 2027 or 2028, with wider ambitions of reaching 16 international games per season.

"I really look forward to that. We know that soccer worldwide probably has the most amount of fans. If you watch the World Cup at all, you know how fanatical the people for their country teams are. But the NFL is still shown in a number of countries, the Super Bowl is shown in over 100 countries; the reach of the league is fantastic," said Rodgers.

"I think I always wanted to be a part of it. I remember the 2011 CBA, there was talk about expanding the amount of international games, didn't really a whole lot until the second CBA.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player NFL commissioner Roger Goodell explains how the league is following Formula 1's model with international games, but adds that they may explore creating an international franchise or division.

"And there was talk about doing an international week, where you had games in 16 different places and you just added an extra bye week. I think it would have been phenomenal for the game.

"Now that the owners want to push for 17 games for the extra revenue and because they care so much about player safety. But it would have been nice."

Sunday's game in Paris featured as part of a record nine international games being played during the 2026 campaign, joining Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro as the league's newest host territories.

The NFL will now head to Madrid, Munich and Mexico City over the next month amid what has taken shape as a Formula 1-style format.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron Rodgers passed Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history

"You could do obviously Canada, you could do Mexico," Rodgers continued. "There's been games in Brazil. You could probably open up another country in South America. Obviously there's a lot of opportunities in Europe, Ireland is fantastic, France, Spain, Germany, multiple games in England. And then who knows?

"There's Dubai, those areas really got into the sporting world in a number of ways, you got boxing and UFC, so I think there's great opportunities for expansion in those.

"It'd be awesome to see them have an international week because I think it's great for the game and the expansion of the game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rodgers gives his reaction after his side beat the New Orleans Saints

The Steelers arrived late into Paris this week as they landed on Friday morning before heading straight into media availability at their hotel. Rodgers said at the time he wished the team had flown in at the beginning of the week as the Saints had.

Arrival time has become a prominent talking point surrounding the NFL's international games, the Rams landing in Melbourne just a day before their defeat to the San Francisco 49ers. It came a year after Sean McVay's side dominated the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium having flown in on the eve of the game, a strategy that did not work in Australia.

"I wish there was a mandate from the league and they would have to open up their pocketbooks, too, which, you know, maybe a little tight on money and stuff," said Rodgers.

"But I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday to really enjoy the culture and the place you're going. And you can do events in those cities and outreach stuff and community work. But they won't because they're a little tight."

Sports.title: Manchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approach
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s hierarchy are in crisis talks over whether or not to sack Michael Carrick as head coach after he oversaw another torrid defeat, against Bournemouth at Old ­Trafford on Sunday, that left his job in the balance.

Carrick was defiant after the 3-0 humbling, insisting he was not expecting to be removed from his post. “I totally understand the situation,” Carrick said of his job prospects. “I’m not expecting anything in ­particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal and I love this place.”

But the United executive are actively ­considering his dismissal, the ­Guardian understands, with the expectation at the club being that Carrick will be sacked.

Eddie Howe remains the preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football, should there be a change in the dugout, with the former Newcastle manager’s extensive Premier League experience placing him ahead of other potential ­targets.

Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, given that Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.

Julian Nagelsmann, the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by Christopher ­Vivell, United’s head of ­recruitment, but Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim ­Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte is another who may be in the frame.

Carrick, who left Bruno Fernandes out of his starting lineup – insisting before kick-off that he did so for football reasons and not because of the captain’s criticism of his ­tactics after the midweek ­Champions League defeat at Como – said: “I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, ­whatever decision is made on anything really. So that’s kind of it. I’m not expecting anything either way.

“It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won’t change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see.”

United endured a sixth defeat in 12 games in all competitions after Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and ­Evanilson scored for Marco Rose’s side. They have won only once in the league this season and sit in 16th. Their last win was on 10 September, against Sabah in the Champions League.

The club cannot announce a sacking until they inform the New York Stock Exchange, which is closed at weekends. When Ruben Amorim was sacked in January, the decision was taken on the Sunday night after the coach’s explosive press conference following a draw at Leeds, but was not announced until the next day.

Carrick made a point of ­applauding the home supporters at the end of the match, pumping his hand to his chest as he walked past a supportive Stretford End. As soon as he disappeared down the tunnel, boos met Fernandes, who was following the manager, alongside other United players.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It wasn’t a farewell from me,” ­Carrick said. “I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way.

“To have that connection with the supporters, it’s mixed emotions, it’ll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support. The situation is where we are and we haven’t had results or performances that have been good enough.”

On his decision to omit Fernandes, who was an unused substitute, ­Carrick said: “There’s always times when you’re trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference, but those are the decisions we made today.”

Harry Maguire, United’s captain in Fernandes’ absence, insisted that the squad were “fully behind” ­Carrick. He said: “Coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season.

As individuals, we’re not ­playing well enough. We have to look at ­ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team. That’s every player that I’m talking about. When things aren’t going your way you have to do the basics well.”

Sports.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
Sports.content:
Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile.

There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.

Fabian Hürzeler praised the Brighton performance and the self-belief necessary to take the game to Liverpool when trailing to two quickfire goals. But he exaggerated the threat they displayed. Yasin Ayari missed a glorious chance to open the scoring and also struck a post, but Alisson was troubled more by his own distribution after Liverpool’s second goal than by anything the visitors engineered.

“I think everyone in the stadium saw there was one team who really tried to create and tried to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” claimed the Brighton head coach, prompting a mass raising of eyebrows in the post-match press conference. “The difference was that they scored and we didn’t. They blocked a lot of shots and defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes and lost some important personal duels but overall I saw a team with a lot of good things. It is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”

Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. Liverpool’s attacking force devastated the visitors’ hopes of a fifth straight win and clean sheet in succession in the Premier League. The hosts were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.

There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat the Brighton captain and Olivier Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross rebounded off two Brighton players before going to Wirtz, whose first-time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low-key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz’s shot was credited as an own goal by his fellow German, Pascal Gross. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

It should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.

Liverpool soon doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Brighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously extended. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.

Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second-half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.

Iraola said: “It is a very valuable win. The key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions, and we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last ones when we’ve conceded first.”

Sports.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
Sports.content:
At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby.

Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher.

However, Eva Olid’s ever-improving hosts fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually earned when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell kindly to her in the penalty area.

Olid, in fact, repeatedly said in her post-match press conference that her side had “deserved to win”.

United climbed to fourth in the table, while that late strike meant City dropped to ­second – now behind Chelsea on goal difference – and breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race. Perhaps more strikingly, if any United fans who saw their men’s team being humbled by Bournemouth earlier on Sunday managed to navigate the winds of Storm Boelo and get to Leigh for this 6pm kick-off, they will have seen a team with characteristics unrecognisable from those wearing red at Old Trafford; hard work, resilience, teamwork, running – real, hard running – and fighting spirit.

This United team markedly improved on last season’s league meetings with their local rivals, both of which ended in 3-0 victories for City. This time Andrée Jeglertz’s visitors were given a real test.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Show Chelsea came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 after Molly Bartrip’s shock opener. It was the first time Chelsea had trailed all season and they struck back in the second half with two Melvine Malard goals, before Sandy Baltimore converted from the penalty spot in the 90th minute. London City Lionesses stayed third after drawing 2-2 at Liverpool, with the visitors denied all three points by a stoppage-time own goal from Jana Fernández. Freya Godfrey and Kadidiatou Diani had earlier wiped out Beata Olsson’s penalty. Aston Villa moved level on points with Everton after winning 3-2 at Goodison Park. Amalie Vangsgaard’s double put Villa three up after Noelle Maritz’s early goal, before the hosts made it a nervy finish with two late goals. Birmingham won for the first time this season as Wilma Leidhammar’s effort midway through the second half saw off Charlton 1-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

For spells of the first half, City’s fluid pass-and-move football, their speed down the left-wing with ­Lauren Hemp, and the technical prowess of Yui Hasegawa and Aoba Fujino in particular, made it feel as though there was only one likely outcome, as Fujino fizzed an effort narrowly wide of the United goal.

United, though, proved a tough nut to crack and, against the run of play, created the better chances of the opening 45 minutes.

Terland was unable to reset her feet and ­connect properly with Andrea Medina’s ­cutback. Later Ella Toone and Jess Park both had efforts saved by Ayaka Yamashita.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw blasts Manchester City into the lead against United. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

Park’s powerful, driven shot clipped the top of the crossbar around the hour mark, after Yamashita had saved well from Terland one-on-one.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Not long later, though, last season’s WSL Golden Boot winner Shaw ­delivered the breakthrough with a ruthless, low strike that was hit with too much venom for Phallon ­Tullis-Joyce to react. Shaw, who had been booed by the home fans after exchanging robust challenges with Maya Le Tissier in the first half, ran across to celebrate in front of the City fans, many of whom were waving inflatable bananas in the air. She almost had a second goal moments later but whipped a close-range, rising shot just over the bar.

Shaw glanced a header wide from a City corner and Grace Clinton missed a huge chance to seal it for the ­visitors. Continuing to battle, United were eventually rewarded when Le Tissier’s hopeful, high ball into the box, after a free-kick was taken short, was met by a defensive header from Shaw, but that only dropped as far as Terland who lashed in first time to draw huge roars and clenched fists from the United technical area.

Jeglertz is staying calm, insisting: “Nothing has changed. We are absolutely on the right track, in everything we are doing. We are playing well in most of the games and getting the result in most of the games. But this league is challenging. [We are just going] to stay calm and focusing on the next task.”

As for United, this late goal felt like a pivotal moment for Olid, giving the club a lift. Her tenure began with chastening losses to London City and Chelsea but this rally against their neighbours showed they are rapidly improving. She said: “That was one of our best performances, in general, in terms of fight, hard work, how we were ­pressing and how we played with the ball.

“How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time – just two months and a half working together – the progression has been massive.”

Sports.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.”

Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said.

“My way, my idea, is that the best way to defend is to have the ball.” The problem with that is that only the three promoted sides have had less possession than Palace. “Here every mistake, every situation that is bad for the team will be a goal,” Sage said.

Palace conceded two goals against Besiktas on Thursday to the only shots on target they conceded. Newcastle similarly scored with both their shots on target. “We conceded fewer chances with our defending in open play today but it’s not enough,” the Palace manager said. “For the moment the pressure is always the same because I don’t find the solution. Today was not a tactical problem but a mental problem. When we came back from the dressing room we let our opponents have too many things. When you don’t control the ball you give the initiative to the opposition.”

Sage is sure he can improve ­Palace’s fortunes – they are 17th having lost back-to-back Premier League games, the other being a 5-0 thrashing by their rivals Brighton – and said that although he remains in regular contact with the Palace chair, Steve Parish, the issue of his future has never been raised. “Inside, we are just really focused on solutions,” Sage said. “How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work. There’s no noise inside, if you want.”

There was relief for Matthias Jaissle as he oversaw a first ­Newcastle win in three games. “It was a tough game especially in first half,” the ­German said. “We couldn’t get ourselves the reward for the intensity of our possession.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The first half out of possession was not that bad but we didn’t have our attacking mindset. The second half was much better. Even if you don’t play a fantastic game in possession, keeping a clean sheet is the fundamental of football.”

Sports.title: Ouattara rescues point for Brentford as Hull maintain unbeaten home record
Sports.content:
Hull’s unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after this draw with Brentford.

The opening goal came courtesy of a 24th-minute Oli McBurnie penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey flattened Tim Iroegbunam while trying to hook the ball away.

Although Brentford’s Caoimhín Kelleher guessed right, he could not stop McBurnie scoring his first Premier League goal for more than 900 days.

After the break, Hull were left to rue some inattentive defending as Igor Thiago found his way to Dango Ouattara, who slotted the ball home under very little pressure to make it 1-1 in the 63rd minute.

Jaidon Anthony pushed for a second Brentford goal and saw a shot land just wide before getting a second chance, which forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, but there was a quick counter as Mohamed Belloumi raced in the other direction before firing over from distance.

An 88th-minute chance was Hull’s last opportunity to find the winning goal, but Mohamed-Ali Cho’s cross to Joe Gelhardt resulted in an off‑target shot that ensured the Tigers took no more than a point.

Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, was pleased with the improved efforts of his side after the defeat by Fulham the previous weekend. “I think we played a good game, especially in the first half,” he said. “We were much more aggressive in duels, we won a lot of first and second balls. Maybe there were some cheap mistakes, bad passing, bad receiving, but you see how fast they are – in five seconds they were in our box. We should have scored one or maybe two more with better decisions.”

Both clubs were required to pick through the detritus of the pre-match display in the opening minutes as balloons and litter were carried by the strong winds of Storm Boelo on to the pitch.

The first chance of note fell to the visitors, with Hull faltering in midfield after 11 minutes and allowing Hickey to unleash a shot that was comfortably dealt with by Tzolakis.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie (left) hugs Mohamed Belloumi after putting Hull ahead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Ten minutes later Belloumi found McBurnie inside the box, but as the Scot was preparing to strike Mathias Jensen rushed in to foil the attempt.

After 22 minutes the visitors offered their hosts a golden chance when Hickey, having failed to collect a ball from Kelleher, lunged at the legs of Iroegbunam and floored him to give away a penalty. McBurnie stepped up and made no mistake.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Brentford had to wait until the 63rd minute to equalise, Ouattara made the most of lax Hull defending to collect an Igor Thiago ball and tap home.

Belloumi then reacted with a sprint towards the Brentford goal with Cho – on as a substitute – in pursuit as backup, but the long-range shot was too high and flew into the stand.

The final roll of the dice was Cho’s cross in to Gelhardt, but he was wide of the mark and the whistle blew on a 1-1 draw that maintains unbeaten records home and away. Jakirovic said: “I can regret the chance we had through Mohamed-Ali Cho and Gelhardt, maybe it should have been 2-1, but in the end I think it’s a fair result.”

Brentford’s head coach, Keith Andrews, who had a spell at Hull as a player, was happy to see the response from the players who were brought off the bench during the second half in the leadup to their equaliser. “It was a tough game and it was always going to be a tough game, “ he said.

“I’ve got a lot of respect for Sergej and the journey he’s taken this team on – I think it’s been remarkable. We reacted well at half-time, the impact from the bench was pretty good but it was a tough game.”

Sports.title: Roefs and Trafford stand firm as Sunderland and Leeds battle for point
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris can usually do impassive to perfection but, by the final whistle, even Sunderland’s ultra-balanced manager was looking more than a little fed up and frustrated.

His bottom-placed team had arguably just about deserved a second Premier League win of the season but, instead, had to settle for a draw on an afternoon when the hugely disruptive Storm Boelo proved the enemy of good football.

While Daniel Farke will doubtless regard his resilient side’s fifth league draw of the season as a fair return on the windblown road, much now hinges on Sunderland’s visit to Coventry on Saturday.

At least Le Bris’s side ended a run of four straight league defeats on a day when they could have done without meeting James Trafford’s goalkeeping excellence. “It’s so hard to win games,” said Sunderland’s manager. “But it’s a positive point; we played with intensity and togetherness. We were Sunderland today.

“It’s still a long journey but I think we’ve shown we’re embracing the challenge. We probably deserved more today. But there’s no drama, no panic.”

The wind was strong, and capricious enough, to bend the corner flags out of shape, send pieces of rubbish swirling around the pitch and turn passing calibration horribly awry but it would take a hurricane to throw Brian Brobbey off balance.

The good news for Sunderland was that their formidable centre-forward had recovered from a hamstring injury and seemed to be relishing the physicality of his duel with Jaka Bijol.

Along the way Brobbey had a ­couple of first-half chances. First came the connection with an Enzo Le Fée cross and the slightly deflected shot that prompted a decent save from Trafford.

Then there was the moment when Brobbey bullied Bijol into attempting a short back-pass before charging after it and ­getting there before Trafford. Hats off to Farke’s England goalkeeper for keeping his cool, bravely ­standing his ground and eventually saving cleverly with a leg.

Leeds possess a not-too shabby centre-forward of their own in ­Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He passed a late fitness test on a bruised foot and, although initially less involved than Brobbey, seemed on a mission to engage Luke O’Nien in a personal subplot.

View image in fullscreen James Trafford denies Brian Brobbey from close range. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

It soon became clear that Calvert-Lewin had little enthusiasm for being marked by O’Nien’s central defensive partner, Nordi Mukiele, and duly manoeuvred himself into cameos against the former at every ­opportunity. Yet although O’Nien endured a couple of wobbles he also made a vital, quite possibly goal-preventing tackle on Calvert-Lewin as half-time beckoned.

The second half had barely begun before fortune frowned on Sunderland. An attempted clearance ­concluded with O’Nien throwing out an elbow and accidentally catching Mukiele in the throat. T he former Paris Saint-Germain defender requiring lengthy treatment as Le Bris looked on anxiously.

Eventually it became apparent a distressed Mukiele – who, Le Bris reported, fully recovered – could not continue and the recently erratic Omar Alderete stepped off the bench.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

By now, a generally ­second-best Leeds were renascent and it took important interceptions from Alderete and Le Fée to break the ­dangerous stride of Jayden Bogle and Ao Tanaka respectively. Undeterred, Sunderland rallied. Nilson Angulo was in encouraging form and two shots from the Ecuadorian forced Trafford into a couple of smart saves.

Shortly after the hour mark the fading Brobbey was replaced by the inexperienced Ukrainian striker Timur Tutyerov as, simultaneously, Farke introduced fresh attacking legs of his own.

They belonged to Noah Okafor and Anton Stach who filled the spaces behind Calvert-Lewin from where Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson had struggled to ­destabilise Sunderland’s backline.

The game remained in the balance. Trafford did well to somehow scramble the ball to safety as Granit Xhaka’s corner very nearly curved beyond him but Robin Roefs was required to dive at Calvert-Lewin’s feet after spilling Tanaka’s shot. Calvert-Lewin wanted a penalty but Stuart Attwell disagreed and a video assistant referee check endorsed that viewpoint.

When the former Newcastle midfeilder Sean Longstaff, on as a Leeds substitute, unleashed a dangerous low, 20-yard shot, Stadium of Light regulars feared the worst but Roefs proved equal to it, making a superb one-handed save to turn the ball around a post.

There was still time for Longstaff to have another shot cleared off the line but Farke remained sanguine. “I’m not complaining about the draw,” said the Leeds manager. “It’s always good to have a clean sheet. It’s fair to say that, in weather like this, it wasn’t the nicest game.”

Inevitably, Farke was invited to praise Trafford and his concession of a mere six league goals in eight games. “He chose a good team,” he said smiling before turning serious. “He delivers, he has the potential to be England’s No 1.”

Sports.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
Sports.content:
Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written.

“The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again.

In the corner, Madrid’s players piled on. This was the Frenchman’s 10th goal against Barcelona but none felt quite like this. Not only was this the first time Barcelona failed to win in the league this season, their record-equalling run halted at nine; it was the first time they had failed to win any game since returning here a year ago.

“I’m not going to let them have their heads on the moon,” Mourinho said, but he knew what this meant. So much for a struggling side heading to an inevitable fall; so much for Barcelona going nine points clear, the title race run before November. There is life in Madrid and in this league. Life in their manager too: this was expertly planned and executed, the rivals who were running at 4.3 goals per game reduced to just one. Those certainties, misplaced, seemed a long way away now; a season starts here instead.

In the beginning, the ball was all Barcelona’s but no sooner had they lost it than the first shot was Madrid’s, Pedri’s startlingly loose pass allowing Arda Guler to break and fire over on four minutes. That felt like a pattern set, a portrait of the way both teams would likely approach this. So too did the way that Marc Cucurella went for Lamine Yamal, the Madrid full-back seeking a way under the winger’s skin – a task in which, it had to be ­concluded, he was successful.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha is congratulated by his teammates after scoring Barcelona’s equaliser. Photograph: Jose Breton/AP

The impression though was deceptive, Madrid willing to step on to the front foot and apply a pressure with which Barcelona were not comfortable, Pedri and Rodri unable to fully settle. Where they could they played too, Bernardo Silva included alongside Aurélien Tchouaméni.

They were also, naturally enough, ready to run. In those early phases, Fede Valverde was opening the pitch with long diagonals. From one, Mbappé went dashing up the left, leading to Joan García scooping away ­Guler’s shot. This was frantic and Madrid were finding it to their liking, Mbappé and Yan Diomandé a threat.

Quick Guide European football roundup Show Ballon d’Or contender Harry Kane failed to find the net on Sunday, but Bayern Munich won 3-1 away at Freiburg to regain top spot in the Bundesliga. The visitors took a 2-0 lead through Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry — his 100th goal in the Bundesliga — before an 82nd-minute Tom Bischof own goal brought Freiburg back into the contest, but Michael Olise secured victory for Bayern in the fifth minute of added time. Bayern remain without their head coach, Vincent Kompany, who collapsed during training on Friday, but lead the Bundesliga on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, who beat Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 on Saturday. Marcus Thuram scored and then earned the penalty that decided Inter’s late, come-from-behind 2-1 victory over visiting Fiorentina. Álex Jiménez had put Fiorentina ahead midway through the second half at San Siro. Thuram equalised in the first minute of added time with a low shot through traffic and was tugged down minutes later to set up a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the seventh minute of stoppage time. That late comeback moved Inter back to the top of the table, level on 22 points with Lazio but ahead on goal difference. Juventus eased past Lecce in Serie A, with first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz enough to secure a 2-0 victory. It was only Juve's second win in six league outings, an inconsistent run of early season form that sees Luciano Spalletti's just outside the European places in Italy. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The hosts tried to impose control but could not. That said, they too enjoy flying into space, and from a Pedri run Raphinha shot over. Then Anthony Gordon bombed through and produced a neat back-heel for Raphinha to curl wide. The Brazilian would have another shot wide soon after, although the openings were often lost to an insistence on playing (and ­wasting) one last pass or, conversely, to snatch at shots. The half’s best opportunity came when Guler’s gorgeous ball was volleyed over by Mbappé. Back and forth it went, Gordon drawing a sharp save from Andriy Lunin.

In the midst of it all the Camp Nou roared in indignation with each, increasingly intense Cucurella challenge on Lamine Yamal, before silence fell on 41 minutes. Cucurella released Diomandé, so often the destination, who pulled across low and hard. Gerard Martín got there first but could only hit it against Mbappé and in. There was fortune there, but it had been worked for, not simply found. And when Lamine Yamal had a wonderful chance to level he wasted the opportunity, scuffing wide at the near post, a picture of a night that wasn’t his.
