Barcelona came back at Madrid in the second half. The tackles around the box were racking up: Tchouaméni and Bellingham, Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté. The threat never went away, Martín ended one ­Bellingham break, but the match had tilted. On the hour Barcelona were level. Lamine Yamal took a corner short to Pedri who slipped a clever angled, reversed ball into Raphinha to strike low into the net.

The noise rose. Raphinha was denied at one end. García saved from Guler at the other. And, Barcelona back again, Lunin made an astonishing stop from Martín’s header. Barcelona had taken a grip but not entirely, leaving them exposed to every break and leaving the game, the players and the entire place on edge. Mbappé ran at Barcelona, Pedri ran back again, leading a move that concluded with some neat footwork and a shot just wide. Huijsen then dived in to stop Frenkie de Jong and stopped a Lamine Yamal shot with his face, laying him out. The chance had been laid on by Gordon.

Barcelona insisted. Madrid, tired now, resisted. But there was still some fight in them, and still some finish too.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
Sports.content:
Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road.

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.

It proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 win at Ibrox on Saturday. After dropping two points at Dundee, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

View image in fullscreen Rangers’ Kevin Kelsy scores the third goal against St Johnstone. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”

Cláudio Braga and Calvin Miller scored to help Hearts secure a 2-0 win over Motherwell at Fir Park on Sunday. A return to winning ways after last weekend’s humbling 7-1 defeat by Celtic leaves Hearts four points behind second-placed Rangers and eight off the leaders. Motherwell sit 10th after this sixth straight defeat, equalling a record from 2003. They were booed off the pitch at the interval and at full time.

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice on Saturday. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: Man United's players 'aren't professional, don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things and have CONNED Michael Carrick' - he will look at them 'in disgust', rages Gary Neville
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has accused Man United's players of 'conning' Michael Carrick and branded them 'unprofessional' in an eviscerating attack. Sunday's abject 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford followed the dire 4-1 embarrassment in Como and looks likely to spell the end of the manager's tenure. Carrick, 45, received a warm reaction from the Stretford End despite the latest miserable loss and the home faithful then turned on the squad, booing them off the pitch. Neville appears to agree with the sentiment shown by fans, saying he has 'no time for the players', some of whom he claims 'don't eat the right things' or 'go to bed at the right time'. 'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned him for a few months. They have they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast. 'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though. He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players. Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players 'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them. 'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should. 'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.' Carrick chose to leave Bruno Fernandes on the substitutes bench on Sunday after the club captain's scathing remarks about team tactics in midweek and did not turn to him, even with the team losing. It represented the first time Fernandes has been pulled from the line-up for non-fitness reasons since Carrick, again, took him out against Villarreal in November 2021. Jamie Carragher believes Carrick 'deliberately tried to embarrass' Fernandes by snubbing him on Sunday. For Neville, the simple fact that Fernandes was willing to break rank as he did and publicly take a swipe at Carrick shows that the players have turned on the manager. He went on: 'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes. 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.' United were beaten 3-0 at home by Bournemouth and the manager is hanging on by a thread United are 16th in the Premier League and some bookmakers have suspended betting on Carrick being axed. Eddie Howe remains the current betting favourite to take the helm if indeed United choose to pull the trigger just months after making Carrick permanent boss following his interim spell. Carrick put his hand to his chest and showed his appreciation for the support fans offered him after the Bournemouth defeat but insisted his gestures should not be interpreted as a farewell. Asked if he expects to be sacked, Carrick said: ‘I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. ‘I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. ‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see. ‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now? ‘I've tried to do everything I can to not be in this position, of course I have. For a number of reasons, we've not been able to stop that happening to the position we're in right now. ‘I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful lot to see us going through this at this moment in time. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough.’ ‘It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them. ‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. ‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. ‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’ READ: This was the end for Michael Carrick after his gang of the damned were relentlessly dismantled 3-0 by Bournemouth... he will be the next to walk into Man United's endless winter, writes OLIVER HOLT READ: Man United 0-3 Bournemouth PLAYER RATINGS: Which 3/10 star was totally off the pace in Old Trafford disaster? Sports.title: Betting SUSPENDED on Man United to sack Michael Carrick after humiliating 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth - with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann favourites to replace him
Sports.content:
Betting SUSPENDED on Man United to sack Michael Carrick after humiliating 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth - with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann favourites to replace him

Bookmakers have suspended betting on Michael Carrick being sacked by Manchester United.

The 45-year-old manager presided over yet another humiliating defeat on Sunday, watching his side go down 3-0 at home against Bournemouth.

His United future is hanging by a thread and almost all major betting companies are no longer offering a market on Carrick being dismissed.

Attention inevitably then turns to who might replace Carrick if indeed the axe does fall, with United languishing in 16th in the Premier League table.

Currently, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe (4/5) is the bookies' favourite, while Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are also in the running.

Nagelsmann (5/2) has been out of work since leaving his post as Germany boss after their disappointing World Cup campaign.

And ex-Premier League winner Conte (5/1) left Napoli by mutual consent at the conclusion of last season.

Other runners and riders, albeit with longer odds, include Unai Emery (17/2), though there is no indication he would want to abandon his post at Aston Villa and Thomas Tuchel (22/1), who remains under contract with England ahead of a home Euros in 2028.

Gareth Southgate, Diego Simeone, Kieran McKenna and Cesc Fabregas are all given the same outside shot of taking the helm as Tuchel.

There are a few more comedic offerings, with Gary Neville listed at 100/1 to take charge – as is sacked former manager Erik ten Hag.

For now, Carrick remains in his position at the crisis club and insisted his gestures to the United fans cheering him after the defeat on Sunday were not a goodbye.

‘It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them.

‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion.

‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair.

MAN UNITED NEXT MANAGER ODDS: Eddie Howe - 4/6 Julian Nagelsmann - 5/2 Antonio Conte - 5/1 Unai Emery - 17/2 Thomas Tuchel - 22/1 Gareth Southgate - 22/1 Diego Simeone - 22/1 Kieran McKenna - 22/1 Cesc Fabregas - 22/1 Darren Fletcher 33/1 Mauricio Pochettino - 33/1 Carlo Ancelotti - 33/1 Ole Gunnar Solskjaer - 33/1 Roberto Martinez - 33/1 Fabian Hurzeler - 40/1 Luis Enrique - 50/1 Daniel Farke - 50/1 Sebastian Hoeness 50/1 Brendan Rogers - 50/1 Ralf Rangnick - 66/1 Roberto Mancini - 66/1 David Moyes - 80/1 Ange Postecoglou - 80/1 Lionel Scaloni - 80/1 Erik ten Hag - 100/1 Wayne Rooney - 100/1 Gary Neville - 100/1 Sebastian Beccacece - 100/1 (Odds provided by Betfair, subject to change and correct at time of publication)

‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’

Asked if he expects to be sacked, Carrick said: ‘I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way.

‘I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made.

‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see.

‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now?'

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton says he 'loves' spending time with Kim Kardashian's kids as he gives rare insight into their romance
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with Kim Kardashian and admitted he 'loves' spending time with her four children.

The pair have been romantically linked since February, and have since gone Instagram official.

But the Formula One legend spoke about his relationship with the reality TV star in a rare moment at this week's US Grand Prix in Austin.

During a panel event at Circuit of the Americas, the Ferrari driver said: 'My niece and nephew always gave me a lot of happiness.

'My girlfriend's kids, I love spending time with them,' he added, referring to North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7.

'She's got four, so I'm getting to play with these kids. I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family.'

Lewis Hamilton has revealed he 'loves' spending time with Kim Kardashian's four children

Hamilton offered a rare glimpse into their romance during an event in Austin this weekend

Kardashian exuded glamour as she strutted out of the Bulgari Hotel in Rome on Friday night

Kardashian, who shares her four children with ex-husband Kanye West, has been to support Hamilton at some races this season but skipped Sunday's race in Austin because she's in Rome celebrating her 46th birthday with mom Kris Jenner.

It comes just days after Kardashian admitted she is 'really, really happy' with how their romance is going during an episode over her reality show.

Kim made the coy admission on The Kardashians and revealed the iconic driver meets every requirement on her famously demanding relationship checklist.

The star discussed a list of more than 50 qualities she wanted in her ideal partner, before suggesting she had finally found someone who fulfilled them all, while speaking to comedian Nikki Glaser, 42, on the set of their film The Fifth Wheel.

When producers pressed her to reveal more about the mystery man, Kim said: 'Oh, you guys are really trying to get this out of me.'

She added: 'Let me just say this – I am just really, really happy. That's all I'll say for now.'

Since going public with their romance, Kim has been seen supporting Lewis at his Formula One races across the globe.

The couple also took a trip to Japan earlier this year, and they are said to have spent a weekend at luxury hotel Estelle Manor in the Cotswolds, and visited Paris – the 'city of love' – in February too.

In the same month, they appeared publicly together at the Super Bowl, when they were shown on the stadium's big screen during the game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks.

Lewis – who has previously been linked romantically with singer Nicole Scherzinger, 48, and actress Sofía Vergara, 54 – and Kim had known each other for several years prior to their relationship.

Sports.title: Mourinho knee slide
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho accuses VAR of 'sleeping' in furious rant despite winning El Clasico - after Real Madrid boss rolled back the years with iconic knee slide to celebrate late winner

Jose Mourinho hit out at the VAR officials despite Real Madrid's late victory in Barcelona's back yard.

The Portuguese rolled back the years with an epic knee slide as Kylian Mbappe struck a late winner to cut the gap to three points behind Barcelona in La Liga.

His most iconic knee slide came 14 years ago when Cristiano Ronaldo sealed a 90th-minute comeback win against Manchester City in the Champions League.

And Mourinho - now 63 and sporting a grey beard - was on good form as Madrid won 2-1 thanks to Mbappe's double.

But his press conference was dominated with his frustrations and he said: 'The referee was great but the VAR was sleeping.

'There was a clear red card for Cancelo on Diomande that would have changed the game.'

Jose Mourinho won his first El Clasico back at Real Madrid - but still ranted about VAR

He was outraged at Jose Cancelo's apparent stamp on Yan Diomande - not long before Raphinha's equaliser for Barcelona

But Mourinho celebrated Kylian Mbappe's late winner with a knee slide, rolling back the years

Referee Juan Martínez Munuera had allowed play to continue but replays showed that Cancelo had effectively stamped on the forward. Minutes later, Raphinha equalised - and Barcelona had several chances to snatch a winner via him and Lamine Yamal.

Mourinho added: 'In my view, Real Madrid do not play to win at the Camp Nou. Real Madrid play to win La Liga.

'This must be the mentality. We need to continue like this and don’t go over the moon after this win.'

He is fast gaining momentum in his second spell in charge at the Santiago Bernabeu, with eight wins in their last nine games in all competitions.

Mbappe had put Madrid ahead going into half-time before Raphinha equalised, but the Ballon d'Or contender finished what he started in the 87th minute.

Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi was at fault twice, accidentally knocking the ball to Mbappe for the first before being skinned by Yan Diomande for the second.

Mourinho was a tempestuous presence on the touchline all night, and had to be calmed down at one point by the referee.

But at full time he was a happy man and crossed the pitch to embrace deputy goalkeeper Andriy Lunin, standing in for Thibaut Courtois, who was ruled out with the flu.

Mbappe struck twice, capitalising on defensive errors from the La Liga leaders

Anthony Gordon and Jude Bellingham faced off against each other and played well

Despite his ferocious activity throughout the game, and his wild celebrations for Mbappe's winner, he was a calm presence at the final whistle, sauntering around with his hands in his pockets.

Madrid have shattered Barcelona's flawless start to the league season and edged ahead in the all-time El Clasico ledger.

They have won 107 derby games to Barcelona's 106, having drawn 52.

Mourinho now has six wins, six draws, and six defeats in the fixture, which has been going since 1888.

England stars Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon both starred in Sunday night's edition and put in strong displays, with the latter teeing up Raphinha for a great chance with a beautiful backheel in the first half.

Former Manchester City stars Rodri and Bernardo Silva played for the first time in Spanish football's marquee fixture, while Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella, and Dean Huijsen joined the ex-Premier League contingent.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was introduced as a substitute deep into added time.

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick felt his side were simply too jaded after four matches in 12 days and did not appear overly troubled by the defeat.

'We were not playing at the highest level because of the (lack of) freshness,' he said.

'It's not top for us but we have to accept it and defeats is part of the game. It's the first defeat in 10 games.

'We have a whole week before the next game to prepare and disconnect.'

Sports.title: Kimi Antonelli WINS the US Grand Prix but is forced to wait for F1 title - as triumph in Texas puts Mercedes star on the brink of history
Sports.content:
It was a day of high stakes and Kimi Antonelli’s father Marco kissed him on the forehead on the grid at the Circuit of the Americas.

Antonelli, 20, was a little red in the face, nothing to do with any embarrassment at his dad’s tenderness, but perhaps a sign he was feeling the weight of history on this warm afternoon that yielded a huge win for him at the US Grand Prix, if not the total fulfilment of his world championship ambitions. Not yet. That will inevitably come.

‘Another small step,’ purred his Mercedes boss Toto Wolff in acclamation over the team radio.

Antonelli, trying to be as cool as possible, had indicated to his team-mates that he had enjoyed the ear-splitting flypast that had drowned out the last strains of the Star-Spangled Banner belted out in the pre-race rituals. The words, ‘Home of the brave,’ were not audible above the engine roar that rent the skies a second or two sooner than perfect choreography’s best-laid plans had dictated.

And then Antonelli spoke to his engineer Peter ‘Bono’ Bonnington, a couple of manly hugs between them, and he stepped into the car, aiming to become the youngest title-holder ever in just a couple of hours.

It was always going to be a tough task in Austin, where he was to go on to triumph by more than 13 seconds from Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, but at least he had started where he would have chosen to. On pole and best placed to set about steeple jacking the wonderful first turn up the hill, with a new hospitality confection overlooking it and punters on the deep grass bank beside it.

Kimi Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix to take another huge step towards the F1 title

After qualifying on pole, the Italian kept his nerve to storm to a convincing win in Austin, Texas

Charles Leclerc (left) and Max Verstappen (right) joined F1's runaway leader on the podium

That first left-hander, a tight one, was his principal challenge. He ruled danger out of the equation there, even with Verstappen, who came home third, sharing the front row of the grid. Antonelli was too fast away, and could take any line he chose, almost bang through the middle of the track as it turned out.

What a relief for Antonelli, for Max Verstappen has been a master here, a four-time winner at COTA, and now the Italian had an element of control over the race.

By then end of lap one, he was more than two seconds ahead of the Dutchman, who was passed by Ferrari’s Leclerc before repassing the Monegasque.

Briefly on the mathematics of the title contest, which are complicated.

This is owing to uncertainty over whether the scheduled final two races will go ahead in Qatar and Abu Dhabi at the end of November and beginning of December. Will they fall victim to war? Nobody can tell. How will Iran act over the next few months? Or the Houthis by proxy? Or The Donald after midterm elections on November 3 (a contest incidentally fighting with Big Pharma for advert airtime on TV networks here)?

So if the schedule were to play out as Formula One bosses hope it will, with the Middle Eastern rounds still on, he needed to leave here 125 points in front.

If they are yet to be called off, and Imola offered as the lone replacement, which is the stand-in option, reducing the existing schedule to just four rounds after Austin, he only needed to leave 100 points clear.

His lead at the start over his demoralised team-mate George Russell stood at 102. Over Lewis Hamilton 111. Over Verstappen 119. Russell was starting sixth, his mental tyres proverbially punctured. Hamilton started fifth, not the best scenario for him behind his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc on a track where he has won five times in a country where he has won six times, the first occasion being in Indianapolis in his debut year at McLaren, 19 years and 20 seasons ago.

To remain in the fight (based on the original roster of races) Russell had to finish eighth or better; Hamilton fourth. But, really, this was a case of them merely prolonging their agony. Their hopes were already destined for the morgue.

So this was the scene. And in brief flickers it looked as if Antonelli might pull off his dream. Hamilton, though, was largely running fourth, which is where he ended up. He had made a decent start and is now 124 points back.

It is inevitable that the Mercedes star will become F1's youngest ever champion very soon

His Mercedes team-mate George Russell endured a frustrating weekend, finishing in ninth

That means – and apologies for all these figures – to be certain of the title Antonelli now needs to finish ninth or higher in Mexico City next weekend, and only that is required if Russell or Hamilton were to win.

As for Russell, he finished eighth and, like Hamilton, only theoretically in the fight – 123 adrift, and even that yawning margin seemed in doubt after an eventful opening lap.

He ran off and then banged wheels with McLaren’s Oscar Piastri. He was punished with a five-second penalty for the latter. And when he had served it, he came out 10th, albeit behind two cars, the Alpine of Pierre Gasly and the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson, neither of which had stopped. He clambered his way to finish where he needed to stay in the contest, arithmetically. But it was a poor afternoon for him, one that summed up his miserable season, one that has seen him demoralised by Antonelli’s run to glory.

‘It was the result we needed,’ said the winner, celebrating his ninth victory in 18 races.

Despite his title glory being delayed, Antonelli’s father Marco could sip the champagne in the Mercedes hospitality area as dusk closed in here, well assured that his boy will be crowned champion in Mexico.

If it’s not there, it will be in Brazil seven days later. Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi/Imola are just spares, laps of honour for Kimi, the kid blowing everyone away.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick 'deliberately tried to embarrass' Bruno Fernandes by dropping him against Bournemouth, claims Jamie Carragher - as Gary Neville labels 'whingeing' Man United captain 'an excuse merchant'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick 'deliberately tried to embarrass' Bruno Fernandes by dropping him against Bournemouth, claims Jamie Carragher - as Gary Neville labels 'whingeing' Man United captain 'an excuse merchant'

Jamie Carragher has claimed Michael Carrick left Bruno Fernandes on the bench during Man United's defeat by Bournemouth to 'embarrass him in front of the supporters'.

Fernandes, 32, was dropped from the starting XI by the under pressure Carrick after his explosive outburst following United's shambolic 4-1 defeat away to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

That represented the first time Fernandes has been pulled from the line-up for non-fitness reasons since Carrick, again, took him out against Villarreal in November 2021.

The move didn't have the desired impact though as United were dominated by Bournemouth, yet Carrick refused to turn to his club captain.

Lisandro Martinez and Matheus Cunha were initially summoned from the bench, and even when United went 3-0 down after 71 minutes, Carrick brought on Joshua Zirkzee and youngster Shea Lacey instead as he only used four of his permitted five substitutes.

Fernandes looked subdued on the bench throughout the game, and Carragher felt Carrick never had any intention of using him.

Jamie Carragher claimed Michael Carrick 'tried to embarrass' Bruno Fernandes by leaving him on the bench against Bournemouth

Carrick dropped Fernandes after his midweek outburst in the media and refused to turn to him

'I don't think he was ever going to bring him on,' Carragher said on Sky Sports. 'It was a decision to just leave him on the bench and almost try and embarrass him a little bit in front of the supporters, I don't know.

'He brought him off in midweek and that's where the... what Bruno did after the game was on the back of him getting brought off.

'And I think Michael Carrick never had any intention of bringing him on at all today - that sub was never going to happen.'

Speaking after the defeat, which left Carrick on the brink of losing his job, the former midfielder refused to be drawn too much on the issue.

'He's fit and available but we decided to pick the team we did,' he said. 'Unfortunately for everyone, we didn't manage to get the right result.

'There's always times when you're trying to make decisions that make a difference.'

When the team news was announced earlier on Sunday, Carragher had claimed Fernandes' absence could be a positive for the side and also benefit several individual players.

Carragher explained: 'He's Man United's best player, PFA Player of the Year, but Michael Carrick had to make the stand. But, once you've put him there (on the bench) you need a result.

'You're hoping, could this (the benching) bring us together as a group because there's no doubt about it, even though he's the best player there will be a lot of people who don't like playing with him at Man United because he's permanently throwing his arms up at people.

'He's basically saying "you lot aren't good enough to play with me". That's what we see from Fernandes a lot when things aren't going right for Man United, so hopefully the players in the dressing room will stick together and that's what they'll need today.'

Gary Neville told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast after Sunday's defeat.

Gary Neville called Fernandes an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast after the defeat

Carragher claimed that Carrick never had any intention of using Fernandes in Sunday's defeat

'Eric Cantona was very unorthodox as a captain. Roy Keane could sometimes be explosive in his interviews after matches, but they weren't whingers about the tactics, about pressing, or excuse merchants.

'Bruno can't press. To come out and whinge after the game about the manager's tactics, when you've just lost 4-1, and a few thousand fans have paid thousands of pounds to travel over in that far corner and get wet through. I'm sorry, read the room, Bruno.

'This is not a time for whingeing, throwing your arms up in the air. This is a time for you to stand up and say, that's not good enough. Be positive. Do something with a positive influence as a captain. But he's not.

'He's gone and basically thrown his manager under the bus the week after [Lisandro] Martinez did the same.'

Nevilled added: 'They weren't singing for Bruno Fernandez to come on today. They're backing Michael Carrick.

'So get in your box. You know where you stand. Michael Carrick's won things for the football club on a constant basis, and proven that he can have the humility, the resilience. And Bruno has got that. Bruno has delivered for Manchester United in more ways than any other player in the last 13 years.

'He's massively talented but he let himself down this week. He didn't need to do that because he's basically stuck the knife into his manager.'

Pre-match, Carrick had said: 'When you're picking the starting XI and you've got options to choose from, it's always a difficult decision. We've got to make what we feel is the right one for today and the team to get the performance that we want.'

On whether Fernandes was dropped after his explosive outburst, he replied: '(The decision was for) pure footballing reasons.'

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

Sports.title: Sunderland stop the rot in atrocious Storm Boelo conditions - but Leeds boss Daniel Farke is left grateful to £45m James Trafford
Sports.content:
Sunderland stop the rot in atrocious Storm Boelo conditions - but Leeds boss Daniel Farke is left grateful to £45m James Trafford

Well at least Sunderland stopped the rot, even if they remain rock-bottom. And Leeds United departed with a point, not something to be sniffed at in the Premier League.

But this was a tough watch on a bleak day when neither side could beat each other – or the elements – and find the quality required for a breakthrough.

In atrocious conditions caused by Storm Boelo which saw winds of 50mph batter Wearside earlier in the day, that was perhaps understandable.

Half-chances proliferated at both ends but really it needed a touch of class from somewhere to break the deadlock and warm the cockles of over 46,000 frozen spectators.

Or a mistake perhaps. Neither came.

Two of the division's leading marksmen – fit-again Brian Brobbey of Sunderland and Leeds' Dominic Calvert-Lewin – were left to feed off scraps.

Leeds were left grateful to goalkeeper James Trafford as they claimed a point at Sunderland

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was left to feed off scraps before he was withdrawn

Leeds might have pilfered the points late on through former Newcastle man Sean Longstaff

Both were withdrawn during the second half, which in many ways summed things up, although Leeds might have pilfered the points late on through former Newcastle man Sean Longstaff.

That would have been harsh on Sunderland, who showed undeniable spirit in ending a run of four straight Premier League defeats.

For all Leeds' progress this season – they have lost just once – wins are proving hard to come by and this stalemate marked their fifth draw of the campaign and left them in seventh.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke said: 'First of all, I think it's fair to say that this was not the nicest piece of football.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 6, Mukiele 6 (Alderete 52, 6), O'Nien 6, Reinildo 6; Xhaka 6, Sadiki 6; Rigg 6, Le Fee 6 (Diarra 79), Angulo 7 (Talbi 79); Brobbey 6.5 (Tutierov 65, 6) Booked: Mandava Manager: Regis Le Bris 6 LEEDS UNITED: (3-4-2-1): TRAFFORD 7.5; Bijol 6, Muharemovic 6, Justin 6; Bogle 6, Ampadu 6, Tanaka 6 (Longstaff 89), Gudmundsson 6; Aaronson 5.5 (Okafor 65, 6), Wilson 5.5 (Stach 66, 6); Calvert-Lewin 6 (Nmecha 85) Booked: Ampadu, Bogle Manager: Daniel Farke 6 Referee: Stuart Attwell 6 Attendance: 46,182

'But these games also belong to the Premier League and we came here to a difficult ground where not many teams have won.

'With the weather conditions, you could hardly predict the curve of the ball, so you have to dig in and show steel.

'This is what we did and to get a clean sheet away from home is always pleasing. Overall a draw was a fair outcome.'

Farke pointed to the disruption which saw defender Nico Elvedi miss out through illness and Calvert-Lewin, Noah Okafor and Anton Stach struggle with knocks during the week.

The Leeds boss was also left grateful to his £45million club-record signing James Trafford who made a number of saves to keep the Black Cats at bay.

Farke added: 'I wouldn't say there was one world-class save but several good saves and James showed why we were desperate to sign him. To be honest, I expect this from him.'

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris was happy to take the positives after his side's abject 2-0 surrender at Bournemouth last weekend.

The manner of that loss prompted defender Nordi Mukiele to brand his team 'arrogant' and 'not good enough'.

After fighting tooth and nail against Leeds, this was another step in the right direction following the 1-1 draw at Lech Poznan in the Europa League.

Le Bris reflected: 'It was a tight game against a good team.

'We are struggling a bit, so the most important thing was to be Sunderland.

'We showed togetherness, intensity, consistency and avoided the unforced errors that we've committed in recent games.

'The weather wasn't easy to manage, but we created some small chances, although not enough to win it.'

Farke flatly rejected suggestions last week that Leeds could mount a serious challenge for European qualification this season.

He claimed such talk is 'unrealistic' and his side certainly struggled to impose themselves on Sunderland during the first half.

Brobbey went closest with a 20-yard strike that Trafford kept out and the England goalkeeper cut an assured presence all afternoon.

Sunderland's commitment was clear to see and typified by Trai Hume's crunching challenge on Leeds left-back Gabriel Gudmundsson as half-time approached.

Leeds began to turn the screw after the break and Tarik Muharemovic headed straight at Robin Roefs from a corner.

But as the hour mark approached, Trafford proved his worth again when turning Nilson Angulo's low curling shot away for a corner.

Calvert-Lewin saw appeals for a penalty ignored before Leeds substitute Longstaff hit a low, left-foot shot in the 90th minute which Roefs turned round a post.

Longstaff went close again moments later but could not find the net as both sides settled for a point from a game they will be happy to move on from quickly.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace feel numbered as clinical Newcastle triumph 2-0 to ease pressure on Matthias Jaissle, writes BOBBY MANZI
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace feel numbered as clinical Newcastle triumph 2-0 to ease pressure on Matthias Jaissle, writes BOBBY MANZI

Two managers were desperate to alleviate the pressure on their jobs at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

For 45 minutes, it looked as though both Matthias Jaissle and Pierre Sage would achieve that - with defences on top in a tame affair.

But an 11-minute Magpies masterclass saw Palace implode, leaving the Newcastle boss in a much more secure job than the man in the opposite dugout.

Newcastle sliced through Palace as William Osula roamed free of Chris Richards to poke Jacob Murphy’s cross home from close range. Harvey Barnes added the second, capping off a slick passing move with a neat finish inside the box.

Daily Mail Sport’s Bobby Manzi unpacks a consequential afternoon in south London.

Harvey Barnes and William Osula scored within 11 minutes of each other as Newcastle climbed to seventh in the Premier League

Defensive improvement

This was a monumental defensive performance from Jaissle’s side, who kept only their second clean sheet of the season.

Confidence in the Newcastle backline was low after conceding eight goals in their previous two away matches.

But a change in personnel at centre-back, bringing experienced heads Dan Burn and Fabian Schar in from the start, gave Newcastle much more stability.

Schar made 15 defensive contributions, 10 clearances and was not dribbled past once. Similar can be said of Burn alongside him.

Besides a good chance inside the six-yard box for Jean-Philippe Mateta inside the first five minutes, Palace did not create much of note.

There were some scruffy penalty area scrambles in the first half but Burn and Schar consistently found ways to deal with it.

Newcastle had greater defensive organisation, giving a stable platform to win for the first time since mid-September.

‘It’s important to mention Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw have done a good job in the last weeks,’ Jaissle said. ‘But we went for more experience and leadership to give stability to a young group who have been shaking a bit with the defeats. We’re really glad it worked out.’

The midfield pair were pivotal, too. Nico Gonzalez and Joelinton grafted defensively.

Every player knew their role in a dogged showing, and that will encourage Jaissle moving forward.

Matthias Jaissle's side were better at both ends of the pitch against struggling Crystal Palace

MATCH FACTS Crystal Palace (3-4-3): Benitez 5; Richards 4, Disasi 6, Canvot 6; Khalaili 6, Wharton 4, Kamada 6, Mitchell 6; McNeil 6 (Osorio 62min 6), Mateta 5 (Nketiah 62min 6), Pino 6 Booked: Canvot, Khalaili, Pino Manager: Pierre Sage 5 Newcastle United (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 8; Dedic 7 (Thiaw 90min), Schar 8, Burn 7, Hall 7; Gonzalez 8, Joelinton 7 (Steur 85min); Murphy 7, Willock 6 (Ramsey 77min 6), Barnes 7 (Elanga 77min 6); Osula 7 (Wissa 77min 6) Booked: Gonzalez, Schar Manager: Matthias Jaissle 8 Referee: Paul Tierney 7

Clinical Magpies

At the opposite end of the pitch, it was a clinical Newcastle performance. They did not have many chances, amassing less than one expected goal but lethally punished Palace’s mistakes to climb to seventh in the league.

Osula's goal came from nowhere after the break. Newcastle had created very little in the first half but Jaissle's team talk seemingly sparked them into life - moving the ball quicker and with more purpose.

It was a simple goal, a neat cross in and some clever movement. A perfect response to their dull first half where they did not manage a shot on target.

Again, their second goal was another rapid move. Adam Wharton’s sloppiness in midfield was punished as Newcastle quickly shifted the ball to the right, crossed low into the box before laying off to Barnes.

Moving forward, Newcastle must create more chances because, aside from the goals, they crafted very little.

But the clinical display – alongside the defensive strength – marked a step in the right direction.

Sage’s time to go

The season’s first managerial sacking is imminent. Will it be Palace manager Sage or Michael Carrick at Manchester United?

At this rate, both clubs could release their statements at the same time. If at least one hasn’t posted the traditional corner flag picture alongside an official statement by Monday afternoon, something has gone seriously wrong.

Palace have the worst defence in the Premier League, conceding 19 goals in eight games, with only Oliver Glasner’s Nottingham Forest keeping them outside of the relegation zone.

There were signs of improvement in the first half against Newcastle. Palace defended as a solid unit and did not offer Newcastle a shot on target.

However, they imploded straight after half time, shipping two cheap goals. Soft goals have been a hallmark of Sage’s side, as have lapses of concentration and inconsistent performances within games.

An 11-minute spell straight after the break killed all the positive work Palace had done.

It feels like Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace are numbered after another disapponting loss

Meanwhile, this was the second game in a row they conceded less than one xG but shipped two goals.

It can be argued that they have been unlucky with every mistake punished. But that is a product of the defensive structure, where they are asked to be aggressive and come unstuck when they don’t have the ball.

Sage believes possession is the best form of defence, which is slightly worrying considering only three teams have had less possession than Palace this season.

Palace have won just one of their last six, and Sage’s defensive record is alarming decision-makers. It is difficult to see him fighting on much longer. Palace play again on Wednesday, and the quick succession of games may be Sage’s saving grace.

But supporters are growing restless, booing the team and manager off the pitch on Sunday.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua told change for Tyson Fury fight won't be enough
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua told change for Tyson Fury fight won't be enough

Anthony Joshua will be eager to topple Tyson Fury in their highly-anticipated all-British heavyweight showdown later this year

View Image Tyson Fury will take on Anthony Joshua

Amir Khan insists Anthony Joshua reuniting with Ben Davison won't be enough in the Tyson Fury showdown.

‌



‌



Joshua and Fury are expected to finally end their decade-long feud in Cardiff on December 11. And ahead of the all-British clash, 'AJ' dropped a major bombshell after revealing that he would be reuniting with Fury's old trainer Davison.

‌



The Brit left the trainer after he was brutally knocked out by Daniel Dubois back in 2024.. The Brit joined forces with Oleksandr Usyk's team for his two recent wins - back-to-back knockout victories over Jake Paul and Kristian Prenga. But just months after knocking out Prenga, the 37-year-old has changed trainers once agin.

‌



But Khan believes the switch back to Davison still won't be enough. "He knows Tyson Fury well, but still, a trainer, it’s not enough. A trainer can’t tell him how to fight. You might tell him the fundamentals, that’s about it, really, but a trainer really isn’t going to make a difference," Khan told Hard Rock Bet.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: 'Internal moaning' emerges as star told he will '100% be sold'
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: 'Internal moaning' emerges as star told he will '100% be sold'

Arsenal are level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table and have two tough tests coming up this week

View 3 Images Arsenal are targeting another unbeaten week in all competitions (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal are ready for trips to Highbury Stadium and Anfield as Mikel Arteta targets another unbeaten week for his Gunners. The club have the Carabao Cup to contend with as well as a tough Premier League test against Liverpool on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



However, Fleetwood Town are up first as the fourth round of the League Cup arrives for the north London outfit. Arteta's side climbed level on points with Manchester City on Saturday after Enzo Maresca's side stumbled at Villa Park.

‌



City's 2-1 loss early in the day was followed by Arsenal's 2-0 win over Everton just a few hours later. It was a double from the backline as Ezri Konsa and Gabriel secured the three points at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Now, Arteta will aim to continue in the Carabao Cup as they travel to the League Two side on Tuesday night. Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the red side of north London.

Arsenal rocked by Riccardo Calafiori injury as Mikel Arteta confirms latest blow READ MORE :

Bukayo Saka injury update as Arsenal fear losing star for two months READ MORE :

'Internal moaning' emerges

Former Aston Villa chief executive Keith Wyness claims there'll be some internal complaining at Arsenal over staff cuts coinciding with Arteta's new contract extension. The Scot believes the club have created a "bad look" after announcing the redundancies around the same time as the Spaniard's fresh terms.

Arteta's new deal, which runs until June 2030, was made public on October 7 and has seen an increase on his £10million salary alongside bonuses of £5m a year. A week later, Arsenal announced up to 60 job cuts following a review carried out by an external company.

‌



Speaking on the Inside Track podcast, Wyness states that announcing these two pieces of news so close together has caused 'internal moaning' and is overall a "disastrous" way to handle things.

View 3 Images Some 'internal moaning' has been touted as a result of Mikel Arteta's contract extension (Image: Henry NICHOLLS / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He said: "It is a bad look, and I think it could have been avoided. I think it was all about timing. Look, they've obviously been in discussions with Mikel and his team for quite a while. They've obviously also been handling these redundancies and looking at the cost reductions for a while.

‌



"So they've had time to think about this and to bring them out so close together. While they're not related, it's just a very bad look. There'll be a lot of moaning internally about the way it's done. And clubs exist very, very much on the staff. People don't understand just how valuable these people are within the clubs.

"We had this whole discussion about Man United and what a disastrous way they've handled it, and I must admit I would have expected a little bit better from Arsenal. Had it been two or three months apart, the whole thing wouldn't have looked connected."

‌



Star told he will '100% be sold'

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres has been told he will definitely be sold in the next year (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Gabriel Agbonlahor insists that Viktor Gyokeres will "100% be sold" before next season after failing to make an impact this year. The Sweden international started the win over Everton and grabbed the slightest of assists for Konsa's opener.

‌



However, Agbonlahor slaughtered the striker on talkSPORT as he claimed the 28-year-old was "running in slow motion." He said: "Jesus Christ, Jesus Christ. Looks like he’s like running in slow motion, isn’t he? Looks like he can’t run.

"Can he hold the ball up? Yes, he can, but he will be one that won’t be at the club next season. Yeah, 100%. They would have got rid of him this season if they could have for [Julian] Alvarez. If Alvarez wanted to come and hadn’t turned Arsenal down, they would have said, 'I would give you Gyokeres and money.'"

‌



In the Premier League, Gyokeres has made the starting XI just once this season and has managed 148 minutes so far. He is yet to find the net across 10 appearances in all competitions.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Brighton boss throws shade at Iraola as fans break golden rule
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Brighton boss throws shade at Iraola as fans break golden rule

After Liverpool overcame Brighton and Hove Albion, Seagulls boss Fabian Hurzeler had plenty to get off his chest at Anfield

View 2 Images Fabian Hurzeler was not too gracious after Brighton and Hove Albion's defeat to Liverpool (Image: 2026 MB Media)

It was a perfect weekend of football for Andoni Iraola and his Liverpool side. On a weekend Manchester City and Chelsea both suffered defeats, the Reds capitalised by overcoming third-placed Brighton and Hove Albion to climb into the top four.

‌



‌



Alexander Isak's sixth Premier League strike of the campaign and an own goal from Pascal Gross saw Iraola secure his first league victory at Anfield. He's endured an inconsistent start on Merseyside, but the triumph ensured they moved within arm's reach of table-toppers City and second-placed Arsenal, who moved level on points with a 2-0 victory over Everton.

‌



There were some low moments, including the sight of an improved Florian Wirtz going off injured, but it appeared to be more of a precaution. There was also a moment for one of Iraola's summer signings to secure his hero status at the club - Mirror Football takes a look at some key moments from the weekend.

‌



Hurzeler throws shade at Iraola

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was anything but gracious in defeat when he offered his verdict on the match. In his press conference, after being asked for his view, he replied: "I think everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players.

"I think everyone in the stadium, and you as well, felt there was a missed opportunity for us, because it's not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Also, before they scored, we had one, two big chances and today I think it was just the difference that they scored, we didn't score.

‌



"They kept a clean sheet because they defended well with their centre-backs, with full-back [Ronald] Araujo and with [Milos] Kerkez. I think they blocked a lot of shots. They really defended the box well. We didn't have that efficiency. We couldn't keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes, we lost some important personal duels."

Liverpool fans break golden rule

View 2 Images Araujo is winning over Liverpool fans with every performance (Image: 2026 MB Media)

‌



Liverpool fans in awe of Ronald Araujo have broken a famous golden rule in football - never fall in love with a loan player.

It's an adage as old as time, yet the home fans could not help but cheer when Araujo put his head in harm's way, from point-blank range, to block a shooting opportunity, despite there being a real risk of serious injury. While he had one near miss, he took a kick to the face from Malick Yalcouye in the final knockings of the match to halt a counterattack.

‌



Araujo arrived on loan from Barcelona this summer. The club does hold the option to buy him for around £47m at the end of the season, but it's too early to tell if they will fork out the money to sign him permanently.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Sir Jim Ratcliffe 'accelerates' Carrick sack plan as club legend blamed
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Sir Jim Ratcliffe 'accelerates' Carrick sack plan as club legend blamed

Manchester United insiders have their own theory

View Image Michael Carrick cut a dejected figure after Manchester United's defeat to Bournemouth (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick's Manchester United future is hanging in the balance following his side's 3-0 drubbing against Bournemouth on Sunday. Goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson condemned the Reds to a third defeat in four and extended their winless run to eight matches in all competitions.

‌



‌



It has increased the pressure on Carrick, who could face the sack with United winning just two of their 12 games this season. They have dropped down to 16th in the Premier League table, having picked up seven points from a possible 24 available, and haven't won in the top-flight since beating Ipswich Town in August.

‌



Speaking post-match, Carrick cut a dejected figure and didn't seem sure if he'll be the man in the dugout for United's trip to Chelsea next Saturday. Meanwhile, Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have both called for United to sack Carrick after the club slumped to another defeat and dropped to within one point of the relegation zone.

‌



Following the defeat to Bournemouth, Mirror Football has rounded up the latest news from Old Trafford...

‌



United bosses to accelerate sack plan

Manchester United's board are now expected to accelerate the process of appointing a new head coach, with the expectation from insiders at the club that Michael Carrick will be relieved of his duties, according to Sky Sports.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe and United bosses feel that a change is needed to improve the club's fortunes, with former Bayern Munich manager Julian Nagelsmann and ex-Newcastle United head coach Eddie Howe the leading candidates.

‌



But the decision on who is going to replace Carrick is poised to come down to director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada, who will make a recommendation to co-owner Ratcliffe.

Giggs' attack on Neville

Rhodri Giggs, the brother of Manchester United legend Ryan, has launched an X-rated attack on Gary Neville amid the club's growing crisis. After the Reds were beaten against Bournemouth, Rhodri, 49, turned on Neville and United's ownership, accusing the former England defender of failing to hold Sir Jim Ratcliffe accountable.

‌



In an explosive post on X, he wrote: "Gary Neville you’re an absolute w****r. Prime Pep couldn't get a tune out of this lot. Call your mate Jim [Ratcliffe] out who got us into this mess further.

"The owners are parasites and don't have a clue."

Sports.title: 7 managers Man Utd can appoint immediately with Michael Carrick under immense pressure
Sports.content:
7 managers Man Utd can appoint immediately with Michael Carrick under immense pressure

Michael Carrick is edging closer to a Manchester United exit and the club could turn to a pool of experienced free-agent managers to replace him

View 7 Images Michael Carrick could soon have his Manchester United tenure ended (Image: Getty)

It now seems inevitable that Michael Carrick will imminently be relieved of his duties at Manchester United. So, who are some big free-agent coaches who could step in to replace him?

‌



‌



After guiding United to third in last year's Premier League, Carrick was handed the reins permanently in the summer. But only £153million was thrown his way transfer-wise and this was almost exclusively spent on midfielders.

‌



To start the current season, United have been dismal and after a 4-1 thrashing by Como in the Champions League, they hosted Bournemouth on Sunday, needing to turn up. They did not. Carrick's side were dominated from the word go and fell to a 3-0 defeat, leaving them near the foot of the table. Chants of "sacked in the morning" rang out from the Cherries' away end.

‌



Although the fans inside Old Trafford applauded Carrick down the tunnel, the consensus seems to be amongst pundits and supporters alike that we've seen the last of the 45-year-old in the United dugout. So what next?

Gary Neville sends blunt Michael Carrick sack message and points finger of blame at Man Utd READ MORE :

Harry Maguire points finger for Man Utd loss and speaks out on Michael Carrick's future READ MORE :

Well, an interim like Darren Fletcher could be shuffled out once more if Carrick does get the boot and then the club could turn their attention to one of many top-class free-agent managers. Here at Mirror Football, we've singled out seven prospective Carrick supplanters who are currently unemployed.

Eddie Howe

Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe has emerged as a frontrunner for the role. He stepped down as Magpies manager in July after nearly five years at the helm and is currently on a break from coaching.

‌



During his time at St James' Park, Howe guided Newcastle to the Champions League and lifted the Carabao Cup in 2025. His previous spell with Bournemouth was equally historic, as he won the Championship with them in 2015, earning promotion to the Premier League.

View 7 Images Howe is the bookies' favourite to take over (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Antonio Conte

Former Chelsea and Spurs manager Antonio Conte has actually addressed the possibility of taking over at United. He most recently managed Napoli and is a five-time Serie A-winning coach, but left Naples in June after winning the 2024/25 title.

‌



His stint at Stamford Bridge also saw him lift the Premier League and FA Cup. In a lengthy statement released earlier this month, the Italian claimed he is open to future projects but is not in any negotiations with United or any other club.

View 7 Images Conte has touched on the possibility of joining United (Image: Getty)

‌



Julian Nagelsmann

Julian Nagelsmann stepped down from his role as Germany manager after their disappointing World Cup 2026 campaign and he remains unattached.

He previously managed Hoffenheim, where he became the youngest manager in Bundesliga history, before taking over at RB Leipzig, whom he helped reach the Champions League semi-finals. He then endured a stint at Bayern Munich and has previously been of interest to top English clubs.

‌



View 7 Images Nagelsmann disappointed at the World Cup (Image: Getty)

Kieran McKenna

Former United coach Kieran McKenna is familiar with what it takes to work at the club - though that has seemingly meant very little for Carrick. McKenna managed United's Under-18s and worked under Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer with the first team.

‌



He then left to manage Ipswich Town, where he achieved back-to-back promotions to the Premier League. He has been on a planned sabbatical since leaving the Tractor Boys in June, but he is a lifelong United fan. However, it has been claimed that a hefty compensation fee would stand in the way of any club wanting to hire him.

View 7 Images McKenna worked under Solskjaer (Image: Getty)

‌



Gareth Southgate

We enter cloud cuckoo land slightly with these suggestions, but Gareth Southgate's name has been linked with United since he stepped down as England boss in July 2024. With Southgate at the helm, the Three Lions made a World Cup semi-final and consecutive Euros finals.

Southgate's only stint in club management with Middlesbrough from 2006 to 2009 was forgettable. Still, he has previously stated that he would reconsider returning to a club if the project was the right fit.

‌



View 7 Images Southgate is a wildcard option (Image: Getty)

Roberto Martinez

Another former international coach without a job, Roberto Martinez, has always been highly thought of. The Spaniard enjoyed spells with Swansea City, Wigan - where he won the FA Cup - and Everton before guiding Belgium to a third-place finish at the 2018 World Cup.

‌



His latest job came with Portugal, where he won the Nations League. His bond with stars like Bruno Fernandes and Diogo Dalot could put him on the list, though he remains an unlikely option.

View 7 Images Martinez is without a club (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer

Finally, perhaps United bite the bullet and give club legend Solskjaer another try. Many fans grew fond of the Norwegian during his stint as boss from 2018 to 2021 and his name came up after Ruben Amorim's exit.

The top brass may not want to admit they made a mistake sacking him five years ago by bringing him back, but he is on the market after being dismissed by Besiktas in August 2025.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire points finger for Man Utd loss and speaks out on Michael Carrick's future
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire points finger for Man Utd loss and speaks out on Michael Carrick's future

Manchester United were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford by Bournemouth, putting even more pressure on struggling boss Michael Carrick

View 2 Images Harry Maguire has given his verdict on Michael Carrick (Image: https://www.youtube.com/@manutd)

Harry Maguire has voiced his support for Michael Carrick amid mounting calls for the Manchester United manager to be sacked. The Red Devils fell to yet another Premier League defeat at the hands of Bournemouth, with their last win in the league coming in August against Ipswich Town.

‌



‌



The Cherries ran out emphatic 3-0 winners at Old Trafford, with goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson putting the seal on a miserable afternoon for the home side. Despite this representing Carrick's third Premier League defeat in eight games, Maguire remains firmly in his manager's corner and believes the players themselves must shoulder the blame for their recent poor form.

‌



Reacting to the game on BBC MOTD, he said: "We're fully behind Michael [Carrick], coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season. As individuals, we're not playing well enough."

‌



Maguire also gave a scathing overview of their Old Trafford display, stating that there was a crisis of confidence within the dressing room. He said: "Very disappointed. Coming to the game we wanted to get a win for our fans and to concede another set play for the first goal is not good enough.

Michael Carrick on brink as Man Utd fans make voices heard in Bournemouth hammering READ MORE :

"We have to remain focused and when things aren't going your way you can't be giving away set plays. The second goal is a mistake and then we're 2-0 down at half time and we couldn't react. There's a lack of confidence at the moment - the results, the performances we have to look at ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team.

‌



"That's every player that I'm talking about. When things aren't going your way you have to do the basics well and conceding set plays, a simple set play is just nowhere near good enough.

"It's an individual thing - we have to stick together as a team. So early on in the season - we can still have a good season but something has got to change quick. It's been disappointing, that has to change."

‌



Carrick shouldered his share of the blame for the woeful result, conceding he feels a sense of "responsibility" for the way things are currently unfolding at United. He told Sky Sports: "It was a strange, mixed of emotions at the end of the game. It wasn't a nice way to end the game.

View 2 Images Maguire backs Carrick all the way (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"It was a tough day for the players. We went into the game having been rocked. You can feel that. They're really hurting and disappointed in there. It's not a nice feeling. You have to accept it, we're in that situation."

‌



He added: "It's really difficult to have a day like this at this football club and feel the emotion and dynamics of what it was like today. Not for me personally but for Manchester United.

"It was really mixed. I feel responsibility with the position I'm in. I've been at the club a long time. It hurts a lot going through this."

‌



Manchester United have a challenging fixture ahead against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, followed by a home Champions League clash with Roma.

Sports.title: F1 star hit with 80-place grid penalty as he's given biggest ever punishment
Sports.content:
F1 star hit with 80-place grid penalty as he's given biggest ever punishment

The Formula 1 driver has been hit with the biggest-ever grid penalty in history at the US Grand Prix

View 2 Images Gabriel Bortoleto is now a record-holder for all the wrong reasons (Image: Kym Illman/Getty Images)

Gabriel Bortoleto has been hit with an 80-place grid penalty following an investigation ahead of the United States Grand Prix. The Audi driver is now a victim of the worst-ever penalty in Formula 1 history after stewards found an issue with the fitting of new engine components.

‌



‌



Bortoleto had originally qualified in 13th place for Sunday's race, one spot behind teammate Nico Hulkenberg. He had gone into qualifying already carrying a 20-place grid penalty after being given a fourth control electronics unit and a fourth energy store by Audi.

‌



Regulations state that only three are allowed per season, meaning he was handed a sanction. Ahead of the final practice session, it was confirmed that more power unit changes were being made to Bortoleto's R26, including: a new exhaust set, turbocharger, ICE, MGU-K and ancillary components.

‌



Each of these additions carried a 10-place penalty and another five-place punishment was doled out for control electronics and energy store fittings. Overall, Bortoleto has been hit with an 80-place drop since arriving in Texas for the United States Grand Prix.

Jeremy Clarkson criticised for suggesting F1 driver deserved grid penalty because of his nationality READ MORE :

Previously, Jenson Button held the record for the most places dropped with a 70-place punishment given in 2015 while driving for McLaren. In a full statement, the stewards said: "Infringement: Breaches of Articles B8.2.2 (read with B8.2.3) of the FIA F1 Regulations. Decision: Drop of 60 grid positions for the next Race in which the driver participates. Reason: The penalty is imposed in accordance with Articles B8.2. 8a and B8.2.8b of the FIA F1 Regulations.

"The use of Energy Store (ES) and Control Electronics Unit (PU-CE) additional element(s) carries a 5 grid place penalty by virtue of Article B8.2. 8b of the FIA F1 Regulations and the use of Engine (ICE), Turbocharger (TC), Exhaust Set (EXH), MGU-K and Power Unit Ancillary Component (PU-ANC) additional elements carries a 10 grid place penalty by virtue of Article B8.2.8a of the FIA F1 Regulations.

‌



View 2 Images The Formula 1 star has been hit with an 80-place penalty (Image: Simon Galloway/LAT Images)

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Therefore there is an accumulation of 60 places. Subject to Car 5 being classified in the results of Qualifying, Car 5 will be allocated a grid position in the Race in accordance with Article B2.5.4b.iv of the FIA F1 Regulations."

Despite these major penalties, Bortoleto is remaining upbeat about his performance over the weekend. He told Globo: "It was one of the best laps I've done this season. I felt it was an incredible lap, and in the last corner I think I lost about three tenths, and without those three tenths lost, maybe even a top-3 or top-4 finish in Q1 would have worked.

Article continues below

"But we knew that in Q2 it was purely about helping Nico (Hulkenberg). I wasn't going to have any laps available. I did have one lap, but with completely worn-out tires, no way to turn. I knew I was going to help him by giving him a tow, I tried my best, unfortunately he couldn't get through to Q3. But that was the objective. I felt confident in the car, I felt we were fast, I felt we had potential."

Sports.title: Liverpool blunt free-scoring Brighton as star man proves his worth in impressive win
Sports.content:
Liverpool produced a clinical first-half display to see off high-flying Brighton at a breezy Anfield.

Pascal Gross inadvertently turned into his own net to give the Reds the lead before Alexander Isak doubled their advantage in a four-minute burst to clip the Seagulls' wins.

Brighton huffed and puffed but could not find their scoring boots despite plundering 23 goals in their previous seven Premier League matches.

It was the visitors who had the first big chance as Yasin Arayi squandered a golden opportunity. Diego Gomez played in Pascal Gross whose pull-back fell perfectly into the path of Ayari, but he blazed over the bar with the goal at his mercy.

‌



Liverpool hit the front just three minutes later. Ronald Araujo showed grit and tenacity to jump up after being fouled, then fed Florian Wirtz whose wayward strike hit Gross and deflected past Bart Verbruggen.

The lead was soon doubled as Bradley Barcola pressed full-back Olivier Boscagli to win the ball high up the pitch. He crossed to Alexander Isak who finished exquisitely.

Alisson was almost punished for a careless pass out from the back 10 minutes before the break, Ayari striking the post. Araujo then went close for Liverpool but was thwarted by Verbruggen.

Brighton had the better of the second half but couldn't find a way through as Liverpool saw out the closing stages with relative ease.

‌



It's a result that takes the Reds back into the top four, a point behind the Seagulls and six off pace setters Manchester City and Arsenal.

Ron they got right

Some of Liverpool's recruitment has been questioned in the last couple of seasons, but Ronald Araujo has had an immediate positive impact at Anfield.

‌



The 27-year-old arrived from Barcelona in the summer on an initial season-long loan deal with an option to buy next summer for around £47million. On current form, that looks a bargain.

He was imperious here, especially in the first half. Araujo played a pivotal role in the first goal, driving forward and refusing to be stopped despite being fouled to provide Wirtz whose drive was deflected into the Brighton net.

And he could have had his first Premier League goal just before the break, bursting on to the ball and striking crisply on the angle, only to see his effort saved by Verbruggen.

While eyebrows have been raised in other quarters, Araujo is definitely one Liverpool got right.

‌



The Holy Trinity Version 2.0

View 2 Images Barcola set Isak up for Liverpool's second (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Barcola was always likely to prove himself a pivotal signing for Liverpool for years to come, and there are already signs of a new, exciting front three emerging at Anfield.

Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mane and Roberto Firmino established themselves as the Reds' holy trinity and fired them to success at home and on the continent.

Now Cody Gakpo, Isak and Barcola are bidding to follow in their footsteps. It's early days and, let's face it, they're unlikely to reach the heights of their predecessors.

‌



But there were encouraging moments from all three here, with Barcola setting up Isak for Liverpool's second goal and Gakpo a constant threat on the left.

Gakpo, of course, was the subject of interest from Manchester City in the summer and things could have worked out very differently. Now he looks a key cog in Andoni Iraola's side.

The Hurz could be yet to come

While this was a disappointing afternoon for Brighton, more pressing developments for their future might just have taken place 30 miles along the East Lancs Road.

Manchester United were humbled 3-0 by Bournemouth in a result that piles the pressure on Michael Carrick and may well see him sacked as Red Devils boss.

‌



There will of course be a clutch of candidates to succeed him if he does depart Old Trafford, and one of those looks likely to be Fabian Hurzeler.

The 33-year-old has made a huge impact at Brighton and they are still the division's top scorers despite failing to find the net today. The Seagulls sit third and this result in isolation will not worry them.

But an approach from United, despite their problems, would surely be difficult for Hurzeler to ignore. Brighton are experts in succession planning, but it would doubtless be a huge blow if the German was to jump ship.
