Sports.title: The maths behind Antonelli becoming F1 world champion at Mexico GP
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has taken another giant step towards becoming Formula 1 world champion by dominating the United States Grand Prix from pole on Sunday.

The Mercedes driver consequently took his ninth victory of the 2026 season and it leaves him with one hand on the championship trophy - though it has been for a while.

So, when will he do it and become F1’s youngest ever world champion?

How many drivers can still win the F1 2026 title?

There were six mathematical contenders heading into Austin - Antonelli, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris - as 139 points separated the drivers with 150 left available pre-Texas.

Three of those - Verstappen, Leclerc and Norris - have now dropped out of contention though, due to them finishing third, second and fifth respectively. All solid results, but it just shows how unlikely world championship glory was for them as it meant their hopes had ended.

For Antonelli to become champion at Circuit of the Americas, he needed to win with Russell finishing ninth or below and Hamilton taking fifth. But as his Mercedes team-mate took eighth and the Ferrari driver, who he succeeded at the Silver Arrows, finished fourth, the fight goes on to next weekend.

How Antonelli becomes world champion at Mexico GP

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

There are now 125 points left available in the 2026 campaign with five rounds remaining - Mexico, Sao Paulo, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - provided the Middle Eastern grands prix go ahead amid the conflict.

Russell is now 123 points behind Antonelli and Hamilton is 124, so the 20-year-old Italian is all-but certain to take the crown at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. After that race there will be 100 points left on the table, but the other two must be behind Antonelli by 99 or fewer, due to the championship leader having the most wins this season by a comfortable margin - so he would win it on countback.

This means both must outscore Antonelli by 24 and 25 points respectively. So for Russell, that entails him winning and his team-mate finishing no higher than 10th, while for Hamilton, he must also take victory but Antonelli not take any points.

Sports.title: F1 United States GP: Antonelli dominates from pole - but forced to wait for title
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has taken another step towards an inevitable Formula 1 title with a sovereign United States Grand Prix win, defeating Charles Leclerc at Austin's Circuit of the Americas.

From pole, the Mercedes driver warded off a challenge from the Ferrari man and Max Verstappen as he stuck to the Silver Arrows’ masterplan and executed a clean one-stop race.

Antonelli's ninth grand prix win of 2026 wasn't quite enough to secure the title just yet, but the 20-year-old Italian now looks set to become F1's youngest ever world champion at next weekend's Mexico Grand Prix.

Antonelli held onto his lead at the start of the 56-lap race as second-placed Verstappen suffered a poor getaway. That left the Red Bull driver vulnerable to Leclerc, who had picked off Isack Hadjar and then swept past Verstappen with a high commitment move through the Esses.

Lewis Hamilton, starting on used softs, also worked his way past Hadjar. Behind him, George Russell was handed a five-second time penalty for going off the track on lap one while defending his position. As the top of the order settled down, Oscar Piastri was told to let quicker Lando Norris past on lap eight for seventh.

At the front, Antonelli controlled a narrow but sovereign three-second lead on Verstappen. That prompted Red Bull to roll the dice and call the Dutchman in on lap 14 for a second set of soft tyres, putting him on a two-stop race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Mercedes didn't take the bait and kept Antonelli out as it looked determined to stay on a one-stop strategy. Struggling for grip on used softs, Hamilton came in for mediums next, as did his team-mate Leclerc and the two McLarens.

That left a temporary top three of Antonelli, Hadjar and Russell until all came in for what was supposed to be their only pitstop, with Antonelli eschewing the soft tyres entirely to go from mediums to hards on lap 25.

Verstappen didn't enjoy his new-found lead all that long as he started struggling with engine braking issues, calling his Red Bull "undriveable". It forced him into the pits on lap 32 for a second stop for mediums, dropping down to fifth, 18 seconds behind new leader Antonelli.

On the slower hard tyres Antonelli faced a challenge from Leclerc, but both he and Ferrari team-mate Hamilton were yet to stop again as Verstappen remained Antonelli's real challenger. The two Ferraris both moved to hard tyres in the final third, which droppèd them behind Verstappen.

To get to Antonelli, though, Verstappen first had to clear second-placed Norris, who also banked on a one-stop strategy. Verstappen's battle with Norris allowed Leclerc to exploit his fresher tyres and close the gap, with the three cars converging with 10 laps to go.

At the start of lap 47, Verstappen made a late lunge on Norris to the inside of COTA's steep Turn 1 hairpin, snatching second away before Leclerc also found a way through. On much fresher tyres, Leclerc then picked off Verstappen on the back straight on lap 49 to take second.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alex Slitz / Getty Images

Antonelli's win never came under real threat as he led Leclerc by 13 seconds, with Verstappen another four seconds behind in third.

Norris also fell into the clutches of Hamilton as the latter secured fourth from the reigning world champion on lap 51, which also meant the seven-time world champion remained in mathematical title contention until next week.

Hadjar finished sixth ahead of Piastri, who held off Russell for a distant seventh. With Russell needing to avoid finishing ninth or lower to prolong his theoretical title chances, he only just managed to do so after a frustrating weekend.

Liam Lawson continued Racing Bulls' canter to fifth in the constructors' championship by finishing ninth, with the final point going to Alpine's Pierre Gasly. Antonelli is now all but certain to wrap up the championship in Mexico, needing just two points to become the youngest ever title winner aged 20.

Haas driver Oliver Bearman was one of three retirements, the eventual result of first-lap damage from contact with Gasly, which the Briton was handed a 10-second penalty for and provoked a brief VSC period.

Alpine's Franco Colapinto also disappeared from the race, while Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas retired late on with engine trouble, causing the second brief virtual safety car period of the race.

Sports.title: Inside COTA's Turn 1 clubhouse and its plans to build a second track
Sports.content:
For spectators and TV viewers tuning into coverage of Formula 1's United States Grand Prix, it's been hard to miss. Turn 1 of the Circuit of the Americas has a distinctly different look to it this year with the addition of a mammoth multi-storey clubhouse.

Connected to the main paddock area via a cable car that crosses the track, this weekend the new hospitality structure serves as an extension of F1's swanky Paddock Club. From 2 January it becomes a year-round members-only club, dubbed 'The Circuit', as the venue turns private at the start of next year.

"It isn’t an annual membership in the traditional sense," said Parris Mullins, COTA’s Senior Vice President of Motorsports. "It’s much more like a country club. There are annual dues to maintain the facilities and cover staffing, but the initiation fee is a one-time payment that essentially provides a lifetime membership.

"We’ve had more than 50 additional submissions in the past 24 hours, and that was before this race weekend. Before this race weekend, around 600 people had reached out. We’ve had one-to-one conversations with approximately 140 of them, and many have started putting down deposits and signing contracts.

"There will never be more than 300 members. We’re limiting North American membership to 250. The remaining 50 places will be a mix of international and corporate memberships."

A view from COTA's new Turn 1 clubhouse. Photo by: Filip Cleeren

The new facility isn't just COTA president Bobby Epstein's brainchild alone, though. It fits a calendar-wide push by F1 management for races to significantly ramp up their hospitality offerings.

"A lot of our contract renewal was dependent on this as well," Mullins added. "We needed to improve both the members’ experience and the experience for the Paddock Club guests. F1 has made a big commitment to it. The sport has grown, and certain markets demand these kinds of amenities. They have to keep improving what they offer."

Why COTA is building a second circuit

COTA's decision to go private has some side effects, with the venue now no longer available for track days or for regional driving clubs. But there's a solution on the horizon. On an empty plot of land to the north of the existing F1 track, COTA has crafted advanced plans to build a second, shorter circuit designed for both cars and motorcycles.

"A second track will be built, primarily because we recognise that we’re displacing a number of people and organisations that have been partners of ours since the circuit opened," Mullins explained.

"Growing motorsport, particularly in the local area, is very important to us. We’re not going to build another FIA Grade 1 facility because there’s no need for one. Instead, we want to build something that suits the local motorsport community, allows them to continue using a circuit and gives them access at a much lower price point.

"There’s obviously prestige associated with COTA. I know people love being able to say they’ve driven their car on the grand prix circuit, and we’re sorry that this won’t always be possible unless they’re members. But we want to give people somewhere they can drive, enjoy motorsport and continue participating at a grassroots level."

While details remain sparse, the circuit's undisclosed layout has already been defined. COTA is also open to the new circuit, built to FIA Grade 3 standards suitable for touring cars, sportscars and entry-level single-seaters, hosting smaller motorsports series. But by not having to cater to F1 cars, Mullins feels there is an opportunity to come up with a track more suited to high-performance sports cars and the people who drive them.

"We want to create something fun with a different personality from the grand prix circuit," he said. "COTA was built around the requirements of a single major race weekend. I’d like it to have corners we don’t have here. We don’t have a banked corner, for example, so I think the new circuit should have one. It should also have an iconic chicane. We want features that people can enjoy in the kinds of cars they bring to the track. The layout should suit them much better."

Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

When asked about the timelines for the secondary track, Mullins didn't want to commit to a firm date, but there is a sense of urgency not to leave local driving and car clubs without a track for too long.

"We still need to finalise everything and work through the process with the city," he said. "We’re far enough along that we’re comfortable saying we want to get it done sooner rather than later. We don’t want the local motorsport community to go without a facility for too long, but we also need to get the project right."

COTA still sees itself as the "people's race" with its enormous spectator numbers of up to 440,000 across the F1 weekend, and by gradually turning the entire venue into one giant theme park the organisers want to lean into F1's changed demographic in the post-Netflix era. Some of that can be taken quite literally, with the rollercoaster rides of the new COTALAND amusement running alongside the circuit's third sector. But the grand prix also continues its tradition of big-name end-of-day concerts, roping in Austin's popular college sports and food culture.

Earning a new F1 deal to 2034 gives COTA the long-term stability to write off those investments, and turn them into ways to make the circuit a year-round source of revenue alongside hosting the likes of F1, MotoGP, WEC and - from 2027 - Formula E. COTALAND fits into that picture, and so does the exclusive members club and the secondary track.

But COTA hasn't forgotten that its core business is to keep the hordes of F1 fans entertained over a weekend. "Formula 1 provides the on-track action. Our job is to complement that between sessions," Mullins said. "The concerts were the first step. What Bobby did with those was really groundbreaking.

"At the end of the day, this is sport, but it’s also entertainment. We want to entertain people."

Sports.title: Red Bull no longer falls away on difficult days: What Austin qualifying reveals about its progress
Sports.content:
In Austin, the battle for pole position looked for a long time as though it would be between Max Verstappen and Ferrari. By the end of qualifying, however, the Scuderia had failed to get either car into the top three, while Kimi Antonelli emerged as a surprise contender.

Verstappen had to settle for second place, making his conclusion during the Dutch media session in the paddock clear: yes, the Red Bull driver could certainly live with that starting position, but there was still more potential to be unlocked.

That was especially evident from the Q2 lap with which Verstappen impressed his rivals. On a set of scrubbed tyres, the Dutchman was faster than some drivers from the other top teams on fresh rubber, making a third consecutive pole position seem within reach.

When Autosport asked Verstappen why the picture in Q3 was so different from the second qualifying segment, the four-time world champion explained: "I just didn't have the same grip anymore. It's as simple as that.

"I simply couldn't carry the speed that I wanted through the slow corners anymore. That's something we obviously need to understand, because there was for sure more in it. I just couldn't get it out of the car in Q3."

The wind appears to have been an important factor in that story. In the closing minutes of Q3, many drivers were caught out by gusts of wind, explaining why there were only three improvements on the second runs. Lando Norris spoke of the worst gusts of wind he had ever experienced behind the wheel, which caused him to lock up despite braking earlier as a precaution.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Ronaldo Schemidt / AFP via Getty Images

Verstappen clarified, however, that this could not explain the whole story of Q3.

"On the final run, the wind was really bad, but not on the first run. So I don't really understand why it was so disappointing. But anyway, if that's still good enough for second place, then that's okay."

Ferrari's pace also dropped away in Q3, with Charles Leclerc – like George Russell, incidentally – pointing to the increased cloud cover and falling track temperature, which pushed the Pirelli tyres slightly outside the ideal operating window for them.

Red Bull no longer falls away on challenging days

Qualifying in Austin was nevertheless revealing about the progress Red Bull has made in recent weeks, particularly since the Baku upgrade. On a day when neither driver was particularly happy with the feeling in the car, the team still managed to secure second and third places on the grid.

That marks a considerable contrast with the first half of this season, when Red Bull would often slip towards seventh and eighth on a difficult day – right at the back of the group comprising the four leading teams.

Verstappen acknowledged this too and recognised that qualifying in Austin was, in that sense, representative of the team's recent resurgence.

"Yes, absolutely. The car has been a lot better over the last few weekends, that's clear. And as I've said over the past few weekends as well, some circuits will simply suit us a little better than others. I think this one is still okay, but I think Singapore and Malaysia were clearly better for our car."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

Nevertheless, Verstappen's race pace in Austin looked more than respectable on Friday, giving him confidence heading into Sunday.

"Normally, yes. It's a bit difficult to judge who's really the fastest in race pace, but over the last few weekends it's been pretty good for us. I hope the set-up we have on the car is the right direction for the race."

The start remains a major question mark for Red Bull, although second place on the inside of the grid offers opportunities if Verstappen manages to get away well.

"Yes, but I don't think about that too much. If an overtake happens in the first corner, then it happens. And if it doesn't, then it's still such a long race in which so many things can go right or wrong. If you have a good balance and enough speed in the car, you can race here through strategy or even by overtaking someone on track."

Sports.title: Verstappen responds to COTA boss and proposes drastic measures to tackle bumps
Sports.content:
It is one of the main talking points in the Formula 1 paddock this weekend: the extreme bumps at the Circuit of the Americas. Drivers raised their concerns during Friday evening's drivers' briefing, after which Verstappen stayed behind for some time to speak further with representatives of the FIA and the circuit.

Because the track was built on Texas' infamous high-plasticity clay, it suffers from a severe shrink-swell effect. Two years ago, it was completely resurfaced, while two further interventions were carried out ahead of this year's event. The section between Turns 9 and 11 was resurfaced again, while efforts were made to remove the worst bumps between Turns 12 and 19.

According to the drivers, however, that is not enough. Verstappen already described the track conditions as "unacceptable" and "out of control" on Thursday, adding on Saturday that he is taking painkillers every day in Austin, just as Lando Norris needs headache tablets for every session.

When the bumps came up again after qualifying during Verstappen’s Dutch media round in the paddock, he said: "There are a few corners here that are simply really unacceptable."

That appears to refer primarily to the enormous bump under braking for Turn 1 and a rather dangerous one at Turn 19, but when Autosport put that to Verstappen, he explained that there are more problem areas.

"Turns 1 and 19 are indeed really bad, but also that whole fast section between Turns 4 and 5, there are such big bumps there... Of course I understand that the ground here is a problem, but that's something you should have looked at beforehand. That really shouldn't be an excuse."

Besides placing considerable physical strain on the drivers, the bumps through the Esses are also potentially dangerous. Several drivers have already come close to losing control of their cars at that point during the practice sessions in Austin, and if things actually go wrong through the sequence of high-speed corners, the consequences could be immense.

"Yes, those are things that really shouldn't happen at such high speeds, when the car bottoms out like that", Verstappen said.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

Verstappen proposes far-reaching measures

Bobby Epstein, chairman of the Circuit of the Americas, responded to Verstappen's initial comments by suggesting that the situation was not as bad in practice as the Dutchman had made it sound.

"We don't feel good that there's a bump at the bottom of Turn 1. We didn't know about it until this week. We would have fixed it. But the other things Max spoke about, all the bumps around the track, we've fixed them. The track is in really good shape", Epstein told ESPN.

He even expressed the expectation that Verstappen would change his mind after Friday practice.

"Max doesn't say I'm wrong a lot, but he's also right a lot. He's usually very frank, and I appreciate that about him. I had no problem with him saying what he said, but I think he might be surprised in some areas that bumps he thought were here aren't [there] anymore."

However, when those comments were put to Verstappen during the Dutch media session, that proved to be anything but the case. The four-time world champion is still far from impressed with the condition of the circuit and believes Epstein would say the same if he were to drive the RB22.

"I invite him to drive my car", Verstappen said. "I think he'd have to get out after five laps and wouldn't be able to walk anymore."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

According to Verstappen, far-reaching measures will be needed in the coming years. On Thursday, he had already said that F1 drivers should no longer have to accept such conditions because of the damage to their spines, and after qualifying the Dutchman put forward a concrete proposal for the years ahead.

"You can put down a new layer of asphalt again, but a year or two later you'll have the same problem, so you need to look deeper.

"I think the FIA and Formula 1 should also be stricter about that. I understand that it all costs a lot of money, but this is really just putting a plaster over the problem. You need to dig the whole thing up and put in a proper foundation if you know the ground underneath is moving."

Sports.title: Antonelli pole shows Mercedes is 'finally seeing the results' of car upgrades
Sports.content:
Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli reckons his United States Grand Prix pole is the reward for Mercedes' efforts to finetune its comprehensive but troubled Malaysia upgrade.

Antonelli held off Red Bull tandem Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar on Austin's Circuit of the Americas as Ferrari flattered to deceive in Saturday's qualifying shootout by taking fourth and fifth.

With the gusty conditions only getting worse throughout Q3, nailing the first of two qualifying runs proved to be pivotal. And following a weekend that had been building up as a battle between Verstappen and Ferrari duo Charles Leclerc plus Lewis Hamilton, Antonelli sprung somewhat of a surprise by taking his first pole since July's Belgian Grand Prix.

It was a reward for Mercedes' efforts to exploit its big Malaysia upgrade, which has made the W17 faster but also more difficult to set up. That struggle looked set to continue in Austin's first practice session, but the team gradually chipped away to improve the balance. A new front wing for Austin, which was trialled in Singapore practice, was intended to further improve the package.

"I'm happy because we've been working really hard on this package, and we're still trying to understand it fully," said Antonelli, after denying Verstappen a third consecutive pole.

"Since Singapore, we've taken a big step further, and now we've just got to keep working on it, keep understanding. But it's a good result for the team because they've done a tremendous job on bringing this package. Finally, we're seeing the results.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

"It was surprising, but also one of the biggest achievements for me today is that I didn't do track limits! That also made our life a little bit easier. I didn't put myself in a difficult situation, and we were able to just progress throughout the session and build from there."

Antonelli gets a first, if remote, opportunity to tie up the championship on Sunday if he wins the race and team-mate George Russell finishes ninth or lower, and Hamilton is no higher than fifth.

With Hamilton and Russell only starting fifth and sixth respectively, the chances of Antonelli celebrating a maiden title in Texas may still be small, but they are not negligible either.

"I'm just going to try to do the best race I can. I'm going to try to win, and then we'll see what happens," said the 20-year-old Italian.

"It does feel a little bit different, but the goal stays the same. I just need to keep doing my job, and actually, I feel like I can enjoy the driving and everything more because I'm in a very good position. But still, the mindset is always the same."

Sports.title: Leclerc and Hamilton's differing theories behind Ferrari's Austin qualifying disappointment
Sports.content:
Ferrari had been pegged as the team to beat after practice at the United States Grand Prix, but ultimately found itself wanting when it came to qualifying and failed to find enough progression through Q3.

Charles Leclerc had headlined both Friday practice sessions, while Lewis Hamilton took the honours in FP3 after Leclerc's best lap was deleted, and it looked as though the team was primed to battle against Red Bull's Max Verstappen for pole position.

As the session unfolded, Mercedes entered the fray; Kimi Antonelli then reeled off a strong first effort in Q3 which proved good enough to clinch pole over Verstappen. Leclerc could only manage fourth, with Hamilton fifth on Sunday's Formula 1 grid as its pace appeared to plateau at the business end of qualifying.

There were two strands to this: Ferrari's straightline speed, and its difficulty in getting the tyres sufficiently prepared for the final part of qualifying.

The Ferrari demonstrated strong performance in the low-speed corners, and through practice had also been able to find time between Turns 6-10 at the end of the esses section, and through the high-speed Turns 16-19. But as the pace ratcheted up through the qualifying session, the Ferraris couldn't quite respond.

Leclerc reckons the source of Ferrari's flat end to Q3 was partly down to the change in track temperature. The Ferrari chassis manages to maintain reasonably cool tyre temperatures in race trim, but this comes at the expense of single-lap pace in qualifying as it becomes much harder to load them with the right level of heat. When the track dropped in temperature, it made the right tyre window more difficult to find.

"It's very disappointing because I think there are some other weekends where we've been strong in free practice, but then coming to quali it's very clear that the others are just having a lot more in the straights and it's very difficult for us to match that," the Monegasque explained.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"I feel like today it's a qualifying where we had the potential in the car, but the car also includes tyres and in Q3 unfortunately we were not in the right place. It was like one or two degrees less in Q3 and for me it was a huge difference; I just really struggled in the out-lap, I was sliding quite a lot already from the out-lap and that made it very difficult after that.

"There are reasons for [the plateau] and so at the same time I think we just need to work harder and try and understand those tyres even better than what we are doing now. The others I think normally have a bit more, it's a bit easier for them to extract the lap time in Q3 than it is for us and as soon as we are a tiny bit outside the window, we pay a lot the price, so this is something that we need to look into.

"Our car for some reason, it's very difficult to put some heat in those tyres which is a good thing for us on a Sunday, but in qualifying it makes it very tricky when the track temp goes down."

Hamilton, on the other hand, didn't experience the same issues as Leclerc; conversely, he felt that he'd had a "really good" out-lap to prepare the tyres and had enjoyed a relatively clean run with his final lap of the session.

Instead, he theorised that it was simply a matter of how Ferrari was running its power unit - partly due to overall power, and partly due to the cut-off in power from the electrical systems.

"I haven't looked at the data," said Hamilton, "but we know through the weekend we look at the straight, like just up to Turn 1 [compared to] Max, when we cut power they just keep pulling. That's similar in other places like going into Turn 11.

"I think we might be similar in maybe Turn 12 within the rest of the lap. You see it on the overlay. I don't know what happened, my car felt really good. Lap was solid, so they were just quicker.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Angela Weiss / AFP via Getty Images

"I think [power unit is] the only place we lose. I think our car is really solid: at least as good, maybe slightly better than the others, but I think they have closed up on chassis.

"We've seen the Red Bull closed up on their downforce. Mercedes took a three-tenths step of upgrade at least from a couple of races ago. I think they're starting to figure out how to utilise that.

"They're now matching us through the corners, we're not able to take that step in this season to close that speed on the straight."

Putting a number to that powertrain deficit to the Red Bull-Ford unit, Hamilton's assessment was that the practice pace suggested a swing of around three to four tenths of a second on the straights, and that Ferrari simply couldn't match up to that through its cornering speed alone.

If the situation is indeed tyre-related, then Ferrari will be confident that it can manage temperatures through the course of the grand prix - but engine power, especially on the lengthy back straight, will be harder to compensate for.

Sports.title: Alonso says F1 has ‘very low quality drivers’ at back of grid after Albon collision | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso believes Aston Martin failed to score points despite their strongest showing this year because of his first-lap collision with Alexander Albon.

The pair made contact when Albon tried to pass Alonso on the inside of turn 11. The clash damaged Alonso’s car and he finished the race 16th, four places lower than he started.

“Albon forgot that corner 11 was there and he had to turn left,” said Alonso after the race. “But we need to get better and start a little bit higher up because I think the bottom third of the grid, the quality of the drivers is very low at the moment.”

The two-times world champion believes he could have finished as high as ninth place without the damage he picked up on the first lap.

“I think it was the best race of the year by far for us in terms of competitiveness,” he said. “The car was very strong in the race good tyre management.

“We got a lot of damage on lap one with Albon incident, despite that the car was still competitive. So I think we today we could have had maybe a P9, P10 on merit.

“So the best and the strongest race of the year, but ruined in the first lap with the turn 11 incident.”

Sports.title: Hadjar urges Red Bull to redesign clutch after another poor start | Formula 1
Sports.content:
A frustrated Isack Hadjar blamed Red Bull’s clutch design for his poor start in the United States Grand Prix.

Hadjar fell from third place to fifth at the start of the race. He went on to finish sixth.

“The clutch needs a redesign because at the moment it’s too fragile, it’s not coping well with temperatures,” he told Sky. “It is a real struggle.”

“I do everything perfect in terms of procedure and then I just have clutch over-delivery,” he added. “These things that are just out of my control, it’s starting to piss me off.”

However Hadjar said the clutch wasn’t the only problem he had to cope with. He complained about the team’s decision to switch him to the hard tyre compound for his second stint.

“I have poor radio coverage, I can’t hear what’s happening like in the pits,” he said. “Then I leave the pits with the wrong [settings] map and then I’m losing a second a lap every lap on that hard tyre.”

Hadjar’s team mate Max Verstappen, who finished third, also had a list of problems after his race, including a poor start.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It was just the same always in the start, the problem that we have,” he said. “But then the pace is just probably not where we wanted it to be.

“Also I think, for whatever reason, the softer compounds this weekend didn’t really seem to work that well in the race for the first time in a long time. So we were just on the wrong tyres.

“Also I think the way that we used the tyres in the races was the wrong way around, so very quickly it gave away that we had to do a two-stop.

“Then the whole weekend already the power unit has not been consistent, so lap after lap, corner after corner, I’m having different kinds of problems with my engine braking or shifts as well, so I cannot be consistent. That makes it of course very difficult.”

But having won the two grands prix prior to this weekend, Verstappen does not think his car was quick enough to take three in a row.

“Even if we would have done the tyres in the right order or chosen the right compounds, I don’t think we had the pace of Kimi [Antonelli],” he said, “but maybe we could have been second.”

Sports.title: Bearman disagrees with penalty for Gasly collision: ‘I don’t regret going for it’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman disputed the stewards’ decision to penalise him for his collision with Pierre Gasly during the United States Grand Prix.

The pair made contact as Bearman tried to pass Gasly for 10th place. The incident left him with damage which led Haas to retire his car after Bearman served his 10-second time penalty.

“After the [Virtual Safety Car] I managed to get a good launch and [had] good battery level,” Bearman explained. “I caught the two in front of me very quickly and managed to make the Pierre go defensive into turn 12 and then into 13 I sent one up the inside.

“To be honest, yeah I went up his inside, he saw me because he left space, but for me it didn’t really feel like enough. It was a bit of space but only half a car and by the time I was committed, I wasn’t disappearing. So we made a bit of contact.

“I picked up a huge amount of damage on my car. I probably damaged Pierre’s car as well. It was a shame because I felt like I was massively penalised for it anyway. It actually ruined my race, to have that amount of damaged. I was losing a second a lap due to downforce.

“Then on top of that, I picked up a penalty. In my view, it was a racing incident. I sent a move, okay, but I felt like I was entitled to a bit more space than I got. I didn’t lose control. I had to even climb up onto the kerb to try and avoid contact, because I didn’t feel like I was given enough space. So one of those things. The main thing was that I picked up a heck of a lot of damage, and the car was terrible after that, so it was a shame.”

The stewards ruled Bearman was not close enough to Gasly to be entitled to space. “The front axle of car 87 [Bearman] was not ahead of the mirror of car 10 [Gasly] at the apex where a collision occurred

between the two cars,” they noted.

“The stewards determined that the driver of Car 87 was wholly to blame for the collision and imposed a 10-second penalty accordingly.”

Bearman was surprised to learn of his penalty, replying “you’re kidding me?” when told on his radio.

Gasly went on to finish in 10th place. Bearman said “I don’t regret going for the move” despite the penalty and damage. “At this stage if we don’t do something special and get a bit lucky and be aggressive and go for it, then we’re not going to score points because we’re fast enough to do that on merit.

“Looking where he is now, I’m happy that he’s likely going to score points after the contact that we had, but I feel like that could have been me and of course that was what I was going for.”

Sports.title: Stewards explain reason for Russell’s “mitigated” US GP penalty | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell received a five-second time penalty for a first-lap incident in the United States Grand Prix but the stewards considered a harsher sanction.

The Mercedes driver was penalised for leaving the track at turn 12 and gaining an advantage while fighting for position with Oscar Piastri . Russell stayed ahead of the McLaren.

“I was on the inside, he was overtaking on the outside, that’s his risk,” said Russell when his race engineer Marcus Dudley warned him he was under investigation.

The stewards decided that because Russell was also fighting Isack Hadjar at the time, and the incident happened on the first lap, a harsher penalty was not deserved.

“The driver of car 63 [Russell] was defending position from car 81 [Piastri], into turn 12 and left the track, then proceeded to rejoin in front of car 81, prior to turn 13. He retained that position. Accordingly he is determined by the stewards to have left the track, rejoined it and gained a lasting advantage.

“The normal penalty for this is a 10-second penalty, however the stewards considered that the driver of car 63 had previously been pressuring car six [Hadjar] and that put car 81 into an attacking position (and therefore car 63 into a defending position). Further, this was a first lap incident and in our determination, the penalty should be mitigated to five seconds.”

The stewards chose not to penalised Gabriel Bortoleto for a similar incident on the first lap of the race when he tried to pass Franco Colapinto. They said this was because they could not determine which driver was ahead at the apex.

“At the entry to turn 11, car five (Gabriel Bortoleto) moved to overtake car 43 (Franco Colapinto) on the outside. Car 43 stayed alongside and in that battle car five left the edge of the track and rejoined ahead of car 43.

“Under the Driving Standards Guidelines, had the front axle of car five been ahead at the apex, car five would have been entitled to racing room on the inside. There was no racing room on the inside which explained why car five left the edge of the track. Had the front axle of car 43 been ahead of the front axle of car five at the apex, car 43 was not obliged to leave racing room on the outside.

“The stewards were unable, by reference to the available evidence, to reach a level of comfortable satisfaction as to which of the two cars was ahead at the apex and in these circumstances determined to take no further action.”

Sports.title: Antonelli poised to claim F1 title after victory in Austin and penalty for Russell | 2026 United States Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was never seriously threatened as he scored his ninth victory of the season in Austin.

The Mercedes driver will go to next week’s race in Mexico with a strong chance of clinching the title after team mate George Russell picked up a five-second time penalty.

Antonelli only lost the lead after making his single pit stop, which dropped him behind Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc. But the Red Bull driver’s second pit stop dropped him behind and Leclerc didn’t waste time trying to defend his position when Antonelli caught him.

Verstappen attempted to use a two-stop strategy to attack the Mercedes driver. But despite starting on softer tyres than his rival he was unable to get ahead at the start and spent the first lap yo-yoing for position with Leclerc.

He made steady progress after his early first pit stop on lap 14 but was frustrated by how long his team took to move Isack Hadjar out of his way when he caught his team mate. “Thank you guys, really good strategy there stuck in dirty air,” Verstappen remarked sarcastically on his radio.

Verstappen had further cause for complaint as his car’s handling deteriorated after half-distance. “I must have a problem with my car, it’s un-driveable,” he said.

Leclerc delayed his second pit stop, running nine laps longer than Verstappen, and emerging with a set of hard tyres on lap 40. While he closed on Verstappen, the Red Bull driver moved within range of Lando Norris, who held second place after only pitting once.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

By lap 47 Norris had Verstappen and Leclerc breathing down his neck. Both passed him with little difficulty, dropping the McLaren driver out of the podium places. Two laps later Leclerc picked off Verstappen with similar ease.

Antonelli was never in danger, however, and comfortably claimed victory by over 16 seconds.

Leclerc and Verstappen completed the podium, while Norris fell into the clutches of Hamilton. The Ferrari driver passed him easily, but his slim chances of catching Verstappen ended when Valtteri Bottas retired, triggering a Virtual Safety Car period.

Norris hung on to fifth place ahead of Hadjar. The Red Bull driver ran a strong first stint on softs and was puzzled by his team’s decision to put him on hards instead of mediums at his sole pit stop.

McLaren told Oscar Piastri to let Norris past him early in the race. He held on to seventh ahead of Russell.

The Mercedes driver came in a frustrated eighth after collecting a five-second time penalty for an incident on lap one. The stewards ruled he left the track and gained an advantage at turn 12 while fighting the McLaren drivers.

Liam Lawson and Pierre Gasly took the final points in ninth and tenth respectively.

Antonelli’s win gives him a 123-point lead over team mate Russell, with Hamilton another point behind. With 125 points available, they are the only drivers left who can beat him to the title, but a coronation at the Mexican Grand Prix next week is now a near certainty.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora’s Inside Game Covers Poor Distance Control
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora’s towering stature is frequently billed as a nightmare puzzle for Jaron “Boots” Ennis. His gritty scrap against Ermal Hadribeaj exposed a deeper issue: height means little if you lack the hand speed and sharp timing to protect it.

Shawn Porter zeroed in on those deficiencies while breaking down Fundora’s October 17 win alongside Hadribeaj. The unheralded challenger slipped past the WBC junior middleweight champion’s reach all night, causing chaos until Fundora finally halted him with one tick remaining in round 12.

“He couldn’t time you last night,” Porter told Hadribeaj Porter’s channel. “You were coming after him, and there was not one moment where he saw you coming.”

Porter mentioned Timothy Bradley’s note that Fundora’s father deliberately schooled him in phone-booth infighting, knowing shorter foes would inevitably crowd him. Preparing for the trenches makes tactical sense. It does nothing to develop range control or a punishing perimeter game.

“You don’t have natural speed with the jab. You don’t have natural timing with the one-two,” Porter pointed out.

That gap undermines Fundora’s physical gifts. An 80-inch reach should turn the outside into a minefield, yet Hadribeaj walked into chest range round after round.

Labeling Fundora an inside specialist lets him off the hook. Smothering a foe by choice after dictating terms from the outside is one thing. Living on the inside because you lack the tools to keep opponents off your chest is entirely different. Porter’s critique puts Fundora squarely in that second camp.

Hadribeaj also smothered Fundora so effectively that the champion lost leverage on his trademark uppercuts. Porter observed that while a few broke through, the challenger took away the arc and velocity that crushed earlier rivals.

That pattern should set off alarm bells for Fundora’s camp ahead of a clash with Ennis.

Hadribeaj was an overlooked mandatory, not a pound-for-pound technician, yet he repeatedly forced the champion into disorganized exchanges.

Ennis would not have to wage a simple war of attrition. Boots could exploit those same entry lanes with explosive combinations, fluid stance switches, and evasive angles before Fundora resets his feet. Breaching Fundora’s perimeter would simply trigger a much heavier assault.

Hadribeaj maintains that Fundora’s rare height might still trouble Ennis. His own 12 rounds offered the opposite verdict: a modest puncher penetrated Fundora’s defenses at will.

Boots would still have to respect the champion’s durability, heavy inside clubs, and unrelenting output. Fundora eventually broke Hadribeaj through pure grit, and absorbing that type of heat drains any gas tank.

Fundora cannot gamble on elite punchers gassing out before his defensive gaps catch up to him. Halting Hadribeaj protected his belt, but it never answered Porter’s questions about how effortlessly he was reached.

Sports.title: Lindolfo Delgado Off Saudi Card Amid Safety Concerns
Sports.content:
Lindolfo Delgado is off the October 31 Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli undercard in Riyadh, according to Lance Pugmire, after trainer Robert Garcia publicly questioned the safety of traveling to Saudi Arabia.

“Told definitively that Delgado is off the Saudi card,” Lance Pugmire posted on X.

Delgado was scheduled to face Arthur Biyarslanov for the vacant IBF light welterweight title. His absence follows days of uncertainty over travel arrangements against a backdrop of attacks on Saudi airports.

An October 21 U.S. Embassy security alert reported that operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remained suspended. A separate travel advisory urged Americans to reconsider visiting Saudi Arabia because of drone and missile threats. Those warnings provide substantial context for the concerns Garcia raised before Delgado’s removal.

Garcia had spoken about his worries over taking Delgado and his team into the country while they still lacked travel arrangements. NY Fights reported those comments on October 22, several days before Pugmire’s update.

That makes this more serious than an ordinary fight-week cancellation. A boxer can spend months preparing for a championship opportunity and still face a decision that has little to do with the opponent across the ring. The importance of the belt does not remove the risks involved in reaching the venue.

Robert Garcia made the only sensible move a trainer can make in that spot. When a fighter enters title contention, the camp has to deal with enough variables inside the ropes without having to worry about closed airports, missile alerts, and basic travel logistics falling apart on fight week.

Pushing a fighter onto a plane under those conditions, especially with the U.S. Embassy issuing formal warnings in Riyadh, would have been reckless.

Biyarslanov has already arrived in Saudi Arabia, according to BoxingScene’s earlier reporting. He now faces uncertainty over whether he will fight Saturday and whether the vacant championship will remain available to him on this card.

Pugmire’s brief post does not specify the final decision-making process within Delgado’s camp or establish what happens to his IBF opportunity.

The organizers now have a missing title challenger days before the event. Finding another boxer may fill the slot, but it would not answer the travel and safety questions Garcia raised before Delgado was ruled out.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Didn’t Deserve Fighter Of The Year
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford’s win over Canelo Alvarez secured him 2025 Fighter of the Year honors from The Ring and the BWAA. It belonged in the Performance of the Year discussion instead. Beating an aging champion in a lone appearance was simply not enough to capture the sport’s top annual award.

Mike Coppinger raised that point on X, agreeing with Stephen “Breadman” Edwards that boxing needs a recognized Performance of the Year category. Coppinger argued Fighter of the Year should require at least two bouts, noting he backed Naoya Inoue for that reason. One spectacular night does not equal a complete twelve-month campaign.

Crawford’s backers cite the climb from 154 to 168 pounds to claim undisputed status in a third division. Those accomplishments carry historical weight, but the state of the opponent cannot be ignored. Canelo was 35, well past his physical prime, and later had surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. How much the joint limited him remains up for debate, yet it belongs in any honest assessment of the night.

The win also failed to answer key questions about Crawford at super middleweight. Taking on a dangerous contender like Osleys Iglesias would have tested him against prime physical power rather than an older, damaged champion. Crawford walked away and retired instead, leaving the Canelo bout as his sole 2025 appearance.

A factual detail also got lost in the online back-and-forth. Crawford did not capture the Ring or BWAA awards in 2023. Inoue swept both honors after stopping Stephen Fulton and Marlon Tapales, delivering two elite victories while Crawford fought just once against Errol Spence Jr.

Crawford earned recognition for beating Canelo, but Fighter of the Year went too far. Proving himself against an active, dangerous contender at 168 would have built a real case instead of relying strictly on the star value of a single name.

Sports.title: Zuffa Boxing Faces Expensive Gamble Rebuilding Conor Benn
Sports.content:
Conor Benn’s search for another massive payday puts him in treacherous territory after Ryan Garcia destroyed him in just two rounds. Eddie Hearn insists Chris Eubank Jr. stands as Benn’s lone viable move, openly wondering how Zuffa Boxing navigates this mess.

Benn commands enormous paydays, which makes soft matchmaking nearly impossible. Zuffa needs major events to justify its financial backing. Staging an uncompetitive tune-up becomes a brutal sell coming off an early knockout loss. Paying Benn top-tier money to beat up overmatched opponents turns into a fast way to burn through cash.

“The only fight for Conor Benn now is Chris Eubank. That’s it,” Hearn said to iFL TV. “Chris Eubank, ironically, holds the keys to Conor Benn’s next payday.”

A domestic clash with Eubank carries built-in nostalgia and guaranteed UK attention. In contrast, grinding out a rebuild at 147 pounds demands heavy lifting, since cruising past an overmatched opponent won’t erase the image of Garcia dropping him.

Benn must topple legitimate welterweight contenders to prove he belongs among the elite. His outings against Regis Prograis and Garcia offer plenty of reasons to doubt he can pull that off. Those bouts laid bare technical flaws that a soft touch can only paper over.

Zuffa might purchase some breathing room with careful matchmaking, yet Benn eventually has to face punchers capable of targeting those exact holes. That reality makes a gradual comeback an expensive gamble with zero guarantee of a payoff.

Hearn floated the idea that Zuffa could present Benn with lethal fights like Shakur Stevenson or Jaron Ennis, triggering immediate salary disputes.

“He’ll go, ‘I’m not fighting those guys for that kind of money,’ and they’ll go, ‘See you.’ He may never even fight again,” Hearn claimed.

Hearn didn’t quote Benn’s contract or point to a concrete offer Benn turned down. His forecast leans on speculation, though the underlying business logic holds up. Exactly how many setup bouts will Zuffa finance before demanding a dangerous matchup?

Old grievances clearly color Hearn’s comments. He still resents the way Benn walked out on Matchroom without picking up the phone after years of promotional loyalty.

“You can’t knock Conor Benn for taking the deal,” Hearn admitted. “What you can knock him for is the way that he treated me in terms of not even having a conversation with me.”

Personal bitterness aside, Hearn pinpoints a genuine dilemma. Benn’s price tag creates immediate pressure to deliver marquee fights, while his recent tape gives prospective rivals a clear roadmap to beat him.

Settling the score with Eubank delivers the quick cash grab Benn wants. Attempting to rebuild at welterweight forces Benn to take on dangerous contenders to restore his standing, which is precisely where the entire operation could unravel.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Could Abandon WBO Title Over Raymond Muratalla
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson could soon face a tough business call if the WBO installs Raymond Muratalla as his mandatory challenger at 140 pounds. Taking that fight means accepting real physical risk without the massive financial windfall tied to bouts against Devin Haney, Ryan Garcia, or Gervonta Davis.

Top Rank took the first step by petitioning the sanctioning body to elevate their top-ranked contender. A petition doesn’t make the fight a done deal, yet it instantly forces the question of whether Shakur actually wants the matchup if it gets ordered.

Nobody can say Shakur is running just yet. At the same time, wanting to wear a world title strap and wanting the specific challenger standing behind it are completely separate things.

Muratalla brings zero box office power compared to the superstars Shakur keeps calling out. The challenger hits hard enough to turn lights out, but that kind of heavy-handed grit rarely guarantees a huge network budget or career-best purse. Without any clear financial guarantees on the table, Stevenson would effectively be asked to accept a discounted payday for a fight that could destroy his road to far bigger money.

That threat doesn’t mean Muratalla has to outbox the champion for twelve rounds. Stevenson could easily control long stretches with his southpaw jab, footwork, and outside defense. Still, he would need to stay locked in every second Muratalla steps inside to plant his feet. One slip against a true puncher wipes out entire rounds of clean boxing.

Defending the belt carries obvious perks for Shakur. He retains his hardware, adds a legitimate scalp to his resume, and silences critics who would otherwise claim he ducked the division’s toughest boogeyman. Chasing mega-fights with Haney, Garcia, or Tank always involves tricky promotional hurdles and clashing timelines. A hypothetical super-fight puts no cash in the bank until ink hits paper.

If a genuine blockbuster offer surfaces right as the WBO issues a firm order, dropping the title becomes a very real temptation. Shakur would take heat from fans for walking away from an elite challenger, but boxing remains a business first.

Holding that WBO belt helps Stevenson sell himself as the top dog at light welterweight. If Muratalla gets named mandatory, holding onto the hardware means taking a fight where the physical risk completely outweighs the financial reward. Until Shakur puts his signature on a bout agreement, nobody should be shocked if that belt suddenly loses its shine.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Runs His Own Fighter Of The Year Campaign
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is out here campaigning for Fighter of the Year like an actor chasing an Oscar. He put together the kind of year that lands him in the conversation, yet he talks like the engraver already finished carving his name onto the plaque.

The WBC welterweight champion took to X to laugh off his detractors, already picturing their meltdown if he takes the hardware.

“I wish I can screenshot peoples faces when I am picked as fighter of the year.

They think comments and their opinion matter

HILLARIOUS”

Ryan builds his case around a February decision over Mario Barrios and a wild second-round blitz of Conor Benn in September. Grabbing a belt and immediately defending it with a highlight-reel knockout gives him a loud pitch to make to the public.

Still, do those two names really justify that kind of swagger?

Barrios and Benn ring bells with casual fans. That definitely juices his campaign, because everyone remembers the violent finish. But star power alone cannot carry the day when stack-ranking his resume against elite runs across the sport.

Voters have to dig into the actual depth of the competition, what each challenger brought to the ring, and how those nights stack up against the best wins in boxing this year.

That brings us right back to the Hollywood analogy. Ryan stays in everyone’s face, feeding his base fresh talking points and using every single critique as fuel to dominate the timeline. Every debate over whether he deserves the trophy simply keeps him front and center.

There is nothing wrong with wanting recognition. Fighters have short careers, and an award can help sell their next appearance. Ryan also understands how to get a reaction without throwing a punch.

Still, he is getting ahead of the voting. His post treats disagreement as something he will eventually laugh at, when the reasonable question is whether beating Barrios and Benn amounts to the best year in the sport.

If Ryan gets his wish and steps into the ring with a 49-year-old Floyd Mayweather Jr. before December wraps up, what does that actually show the ballot casters? Mayweather’s brand still sells pay-per-views by the truckload, but Ryan would be sharing a ring with a man staring down his fiftieth birthday, nearly a decade removed from actual world-class prize fighting.

Beating up a retired legend does not tell voters a single thing about how Ryan handles the elite, prime talent ruling today’s welterweight division.

A third outing would certainly give Ryan an active calendar year. Still, the quality of the man in the opposite corner has to justify the accolades Ryan demands. Mayweather earned his legendary status decades ago; Ryan cannot simply inherit those accolades by beating on a senior citizen.

That kind of booking makes the Oscar campaign comparison dead accurate. Ryan would have a massive box office spectacle to push during voting season, leaving the panel to figure out whether there is any genuine substance behind the marquee name.

Sports.title: Nearly Three Years Out, Vasily Lomachenko Bypasses Tuneup For O’Shaquie Foster Clash
Sports.content:
Vasiliy Lomachenko wants to make his comeback at super featherweight in 2027, eyeing an immediate collision with O’Shaquie Foster for three world titles. Stepping directly into a fight of that magnitude following a layoff of over two years represents a massive gamble.

In an interview with DAZN, Lomachenko revealed plans to end his retirement and target the victor of the unification clash. Foster then took care of business, outpointing Emanuel Navarrete to collect the WBC, IBF, and WBO belts at 130 pounds.

Lomachenko (18-3, 12 KOs) long maintained that 135 pounds was north of his natural fighting weight. Returning to super featherweight pits him against men his own physical dimensions. Yet, the calendar tells a harsh story: Lomachenko has not made 130 pounds since forcing Guillermo Rigondeaux to retire on his stool in December 2017. He was 29 years old on that night. He turns 39 this coming February.

“During the preparation, it looks very good, but nobody knows what will happen after another month or two of preparation,” Lomachenko admitted.

That physical reality demands scrutiny before any title clash gets finalized. Lomachenko built his legendary status on dazzling footwork, laser reflexes, and suffocating punch volume. Dropping five pounds will not magically restore those physical gifts after such an extensive absence from competition.

Foster presents a nightmare stylistic exam for an aging ring master. His victory over Navarrete showcased frustrating defensive elusiveness, slick counterpunching, and lateral movement. Lomachenko cannot afford his trademark reconnaissance rounds against a mobile champion who racks up points from distance.

The championship math matters as well. Foster currently holds three titles rather than the full undisputed collection, with the WBA strap still elsewhere. How the division shakes out over the coming months will dictate exactly what sits on the table when Lomachenko officially makes his move.

Lomachenko has not boxed since May 2024, when he broke down George Kambosos Jr. in Australia to capture the IBF lightweight crown. The desire to compete remains potent. Taking an interim tune-up bout before stepping directly into Foster’s sights would tell boxing, and Lomachenko, whether his reflexes can still match his ambitions.

When an elite fighter sits out from May 2024 until 2027, the biological clock does not pause. Lomachenko dropping back down to 130 pounds after a decade away from the division introduces extreme physical stress on an aging body.

Bypassing a tune-up saves wear in the gym, but walking straight into a unification against a rangy, prime champion after years of inactivity leaves zero margin for error.

Sports.title: Arthur Biyarslanov Lands In Saudi Arabia While Lindolfo Delgado Remains Stranded Stateside
Sports.content:
Lindolfo Delgado’s chance at a world title could vanish from the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli card before either junior welterweight laces up the gloves. Arthur Biyarslanov is already on the ground in Riyadh, yet Delgado’s trip remains entirely up in the air ahead of their scheduled October 31 vacant IBF title bout.

According to BoxingScene, Biyarslanov touched down alongside promotional teammate Mbilli after the pair took an alternate route into the Saudi capital. Meanwhile, Delgado’s trainer, Robert Garcia, chose not to address his fighter’s travel status while heading back from Albert Gonzalez’s win in San Antonio. That report stopped short of an official pullout, but the clock is ticking fast.

Right now, Biyarslanov is getting acclimated in the host city while nobody knows if his challenger will ever show up. With less than a week remaining, the delay wipes out the essential window Delgado needs to shake off jet lag, adjust to the local clock, and put the finishing touches on his camp.

Dan Rafael added more fuel to the fire, reporting that Delgado, Garcia, and the rest of the crew are still stateside without flight itineraries in hand. When pressed on whether the matchup actually takes place, Rafael noted that an insider gave it a flat “probably not.” While not a formal scrap just yet, that level of skepticism speaks volumes.

A vacant world championship is usually all the motivation a boxer needs to cross an ocean. At the same time, elite fighters require reliable logistics, smooth transit, and a clear setup they can trust. Dealing with travel chaos during peak fight week is the last thing any contender needs before stepping inside the ropes.

Having Biyarslanov in town gives organizers half the equation. It does nothing to solve the other side, and neither man gains anything from sitting through fight week wondering if the opening bell will ever ring.

The marquee event will march on behind the headliners, but undercard contenders are putting their health, records, and livelihoods on the line. Even the brightest championship belt loses its shine when the simple act of getting to the arena turns into a nightmare.

Unless Delgado’s team solidifies an itinerary immediately, this clash stays trapped in limbo, leaving one fighter waiting in the desert and the other stuck thousands of miles away.

Ghana News.title: Kwadaso NCCE educates SHS students on constitutional values
Ghana News.content:
The Kwadaso Municipal Directorate of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) has engaged students of two senior high schools in the municipality to promote constitutional awareness and responsible citizenship among the youth.

The schools were Prempeh College and Methodist Technical School.

The engagement brought together students, teachers, and NCCE officials to discuss the relevance of the 1992 Constitution and citizens' role in safeguarding Ghana’s democracy.

Ms Mavis Achiaa, the Kwadaso Municipal Director of NCCE, addressed the students and described the Constitution as the supreme law of the land and the foundation of the country’s democratic governance.

Speaking on the theme, “Upholding Our Constitution in the Digital Age: Our Collective Responsibility,” she urged the students to demonstrate responsible behaviour both online and offline.

She said the 1992 Constitution guarantees citizens' fundamental human rights and freedoms while outlining their civic duties and responsibilities.

Ms Opoku noted that the Constitution remained relevant in guiding national conduct and governance, particularly in an era of rapid technological advancement that had transformed communication, access to information, and civic engagement.

She said that although digital platforms had expanded access to information and improved communication, they had also created challenges, including misinformation, cybercrime, online abuse, identity theft, and digital fraud.

She warned that the irresponsible use of digital platforms, particularly social media, could threaten national cohesion and democratic stability.

Students actively participated in the interactive session, raising questions about online safety, cyberbullying, and responsible use of digital platforms.

Facilitators provided practical guidance on how young people could protect themselves online while contributing to good governance and national development.

Some teachers who attended the programme commended the NCCE for the initiative and urged the Commission to sustain such educational engagements in schools. At the end of the programme,

The schools established Civic Education Clubs to promote continuous civic learning and encourage students to become responsible citizens.

The students thanked the NCCE for the engagement and pledged to apply what they learned in their academic and personal lives.

Ghana News.title: NCCE engages women’s groups on rule of law and anti-corruption
Ghana News.content:
The National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) in the Krachi East Municipality has organised a follow-up civic engagement with women's groups to strengthen public understanding of the rule of law, accountability and the fight against corruption.

The engagement forms part of the Commission’s Civic Engagements on the Rule of Law and the Fight Against Corruption project, which seeks to promote civic awareness and encourage citizens to uphold the principles of good governance.

The initiative builds on earlier awareness campaigns conducted in the 60 project districts, which equipped women’s groups with knowledge of the rule of law, corruption, accountability, civic responsibilities, legal protections and available reporting mechanisms.

According to the NCCE, initial engagements have shown the importance of sustained civic education in translating knowledge into practical action.

It said continuous engagement, reinforcement of key messages and opportunities for participants to share their experiences and challenges were essential to promoting lasting behavioural change.

The Commission observed that women continued to encounter corruption in their daily interactions with public institutions, markets and service providers.

It noted that barriers such as fear of victimisation, limited knowledge of reporting procedures and cultural norms that discouraged speaking out against wrongdoing could prevent some women from reporting corrupt practices.

The follow-up engagement is therefore intended to assess how participants have applied the knowledge gained during the initial sessions, reinforce positive attitudes and behaviours, address misconceptions and strengthen their capacity to promote integrity and accountability within their families, workplaces and communities.

The initiative also seeks to empower women to become active advocates for transparency, accountability and the rule of law.

The NCCE Krachi East Municipal Office has invited participants from the initial engagement to attend the follow-up session at the Church of Pentecost, Dambai Central Assembly.

The engagement forms part of broader efforts to deepen civic participation and promote responsible citizenship in the fight against corruption.

The engagement featured over 60 women who reflected on their first engagement, success, challenges and lessons learned from the Krachi East Municipal Director, NCCE, under the auspices of Mr Clement Kwesi Mamadu,

Participants came from across the municipality, where facilitators reminded them of previous engagements and asked whether they were applying them in their daily activities.

Chief Inspector Mr Charles Adams of Dambai Division Command led the participants through a reflection on their previous encounters, successes, challenges, and lessons learned.

He then guided them in applying the Rule of Law in everyday life and reminded them of practical experiences in identifying and responding to corruption.

Mr Samuel Annan (ADO1), of the Krachi East Municipal Fire Command, also engaged participants on overcoming barriers to reporting corruption and building community integrity through women's association.

He again said that personal and collective commitment to promote transparency must be treated fairly.

Ghana News.title: Sandra Amarquaye wins PR Professional Practitioner of the Year at IPR Excellence Awards 2025
Ghana News.content:
Sandra Amarquaye, Corporate Communications Manager at Karpowership Ghana Company Limited (KGCL), was named PR Professional Practitioner of the Year at the 2025 Institute of Public Relations (IPR) Ghana Excellence Awards.

This recognises her contributions to strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and reputation management.

The award adds to her impressive record of professional achievements, including being named Internal Communicator of the Year at the 2024 IPR Ghana Excellence Awards, recognised among the Top 10 Women in PR in Ghana in 2024, and receiving the Community Development and Relations Leadership Impact Award at the Sustainability and Social Investment Awards.

In 2021, she was named Sustainability and External Relations Champion at the Women in Mining and Energy Awards. She also received Karpowership’s Ace of Initiative award in 2018 for her innovative contributions to the organisation.

At Karpowership Ghana, Sandra contributes to corporate communications, media relations, stakeholder engagement and CSR initiatives, helping strengthen the company’s reputation and relationships with employees, institutional stakeholders and communities.

Her work reflects communication's strategic role in building trust, supporting partnerships, and communicating corporate responsibility and sustainability initiatives.

At the award ceremony, Karpowership was also recognised for Best in Crisis Communications, highlighting the company’s work in crisis communication and reputation management.

Sandra credits her achievement to teamwork and the support of colleagues in Ghana and at Karpowership’s headquarters.

“This award is not just a personal achievement; it is a recognition I share with the entire Karpowership team. I am grateful to my supportive colleagues in Ghana and at our headquarters, whose collaboration and commitment make my work easier and contribute to our collective success.

"I remain committed to using strategic communication to build trust, strengthen partnerships and create meaningful value for our stakeholders and communities,” she said.

Before moving into corporate communications, Sandra worked as an energy reporter and producer at TV3 Network Limited.

She is an accredited member of the Institute of Public Relations Ghana and holds two Master of Arts degrees in Public Relations and Media Management.

Her latest recognition marks another milestone in a career defined by professional growth, purposeful communication, stakeholder relationships and a commitment to excellence

Ghana News.title: NDC cancels constituency election in Amenfi East
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has cancelled its constituency-level election in Amenfi East in the Western Region following challenges during the party’s nationwide internal polls.

The cancellation was one of the difficulties encountered during the exercise, which also saw delays in some constituencies, partly due to problems distributing ballot papers.

Despite the setbacks, the party has expressed satisfaction with the overall conduct of the elections, describing the process as an improvement on the previous exercise.

The NDC says it will assess the challenges encountered and draw lessons from the exercise to strengthen preparations for the upcoming regional elections.

The party’s Acting Director of Elections and IT, Mahdi Jibril, disclosed the cancellation in an interview with Channel One TV on Sunday, October 25, while reviewing the conduct of the polls.

“I would say so far, it is an improvement from the last election. I think the party is happy with the process,” he said, adding that, apart from the cancellation in Amenfi East and other logistical challenges, the exercise had been satisfactory.

Ghana News.title: Jerry Ahmed Shaib urges safe contraflow, seeks Metro Mass buses for Weija-Gbawe
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Minority Whip, Jerry Ahmed Shaib

The Member of Parliament for Weija-Gbawe, Jerry Ahmed Shaib, has urged the Ministry of Transport to extend Metro Mass Transit buses to his constituency to help address persistent transport challenges.

He welcomed the introduction of contraflow on the Kasoa-Accra road as a potential measure to ease congestion but cautioned that road safety must be the priority.

“My expectation is that we should do it in a manner that would not end up actually causing accidents,” he said in an interview on Channel One Newsroom on Sunday, October 26.

Mr Shaib said commuters in Weija-Gbawe and surrounding communities, including Tetegu, face high transport costs and often have to board multiple vehicles to reach their destinations. He appealed to the Transport Minister to provide at least four to six Metro Mass Transit buses to serve the area.

“I’m praying that the Minister of Transport would also hear our cry and also furnish us with at least four or six Metro buses so that they can ply both Weija and Gbawe, Tetegu, all of these places,” he said.

According to the MP, some commuters who normally spend between GH¢15 and GH¢20 on a journey now pay as much as GH¢60 to GH¢70 because of the transport difficulties. He said additional buses would help reduce fares and ease the daily burden on residents.

Ghana News.title: Gender advocate urges sustained breast cancer education in rural Ghana
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian media personality and US-based healthcare professional, Josephine Oppong-Yeboah has urged the Ghana Health Service (GHS) to intensify breast cancer education and outreach programmes, particularly among women in rural communities.

She said myths and misconceptions about the disease had contributed to delays in seeking medical care, resulting in preventable deaths.

Ms Oppong-Yeboah, who is a gender and disability advocate, said sustained public education, led by the GHS, could help dispel these misconceptions and encourage more women to seek medical attention early.

She also commended non-governmental organisations supporting the health service to promote breast cancer awareness across the country.

In an interview, she said breast cancer awareness should not be limited to October, when the disease is highlighted globally, but should be maintained throughout the year to reach more women and girls.

“Many women are still under the impression that once breast cancer is detected, they are going to die. Such myths can only be corrected through sustained educational outreach,” she said.

She noted that some women were afraid they would die if their affected breast had to be removed, prompting them to delay seeking treatment until the disease had progressed and become more difficult to manage.

“We need to educate our women and girls about breast cancer. There is life after breast cancer detection. It only becomes a problem when the condition is detected late,” she said.

While acknowledging the global campaign to raise breast cancer awareness in October, Ms Oppong-Yeboah said Ghana needed to sustain its education efforts beyond the month.

“As a nation, we need not to wait for October to do this education. We have to adopt any means to reach our women, especially those in the remotest parts of the country,” she said.

She added that misconceptions about breast cancer were particularly prevalent in remote communities, where access to healthcare remained a major challenge.

“We should not be losing our women to breast cancer. We need to do whatever we need to do to get the awareness message to our women,” she said.

Ms Oppong-Yeboah also encouraged women and girls to visit health facilities for breast health checks and seek medical advice when they noticed any unusual changes, emphasising the importance of early detection.

Ghana News.title: Roads Ministry wins PR Organisation of the Year for the second time
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Roads and Highways has won the Public Sector PR Organisation of the Year award for the second consecutive time at the Institute of Public Relations (IPR) Ghana Excellence Awards.

The award recognises the Ministry’s efforts to improve public communication, stakeholder engagement and access to information on road infrastructure development.

The IPR Ghana citation said the Ministry had distinguished itself through timely dissemination of information on road projects and the use of innovative communication tools to engage the public.

This year’s awards ceremony, held in Koforidua in the Eastern Region, recognised public institutions that demonstrated leadership in communication and applied public relations best practices to promote public trust.

The Institute commended the Ministry’s Public Relations Unit, led by Alhaji Nasir Ahmad Yartey, a public relations practitioner and development communication professional with more than 17 years of experience in Ghana’s public sector, for its strategic and professional work.

It said the Unit had strengthened proactive media engagement, community outreach programmes and relationships with key stakeholders to keep the public informed about road infrastructure projects across the country.

The Ministry had also introduced digital communication tools to improve access to road development updates, enhanced social media reporting, used visual storytelling to showcase infrastructure progress and strengthened crisis communication systems, it said.

In 2022, the Ministry received the Best Social Media PR Unit award at the Government PROs Excellence Awards, while Mr Yartey was named second runner-up in the PRO of the Year category.

The Ministry reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining communication reforms, deepening citizen engagement, and supporting the delivery of safe, resilient, and modern road infrastructure.

The IPR Ghana Excellence Awards are a major event that recognises individuals and institutions for outstanding performance, accountability, and innovation in public relations practice and professional communication.
