World.title: Kenya: Police Rescue 59 Ethiopians, Including Four-Year-Old Child, in Marsabit Smuggling Operation
World.content:
Nairobi — Police have rescued 59 Ethiopian nationals, including a four-year-old child, in a multi-agency operation targeting suspected human smuggling in Marsabit County.

The operation, conducted on Saturday, also resulted in the arrest of a caretaker suspected of harbouring the victims at a residential house in Jirime Location, Marsabit Central Sub-County.

According to a police report, officers from the Counter Intelligence and Operations Team (COICT) in Moyale, Kenya Police Service (KPS) Marsabit, Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) Marsabit and Administration Police Service (APS) Marsabit conducted the operation following a tip-off.

The officers first raided a residence belonging to a man identified as Aden Lama, where they rescued 30 Ethiopian nationals comprising 23 males and seven females.



A suspect identified as Halkano Guyo Galgalo, who was reportedly the caretaker of the residential property, was arrested on suspicion of harbouring the victims.

Police said the suspect was detained to assist with investigations into the suspected human smuggling operation.

Further intelligence gathered during the operation indicated that additional victims had been moved to another location, prompting officers to pursue them.

The multi-agency team subsequently rescued another 29 people, comprising 28 adults and a four-year-old child, approximately 14 kilometres towards Shegel area along the Marsabit-North Horr Road.

The second group included 20 male and eight female adults, alongside the minor.

The rescue brought the total number of Ethiopian nationals recovered during the operation to 59 adults and one child.

Police said the operation was led by the Sub-County Police Commander (SCPC) for Marsabit Central, while COICT Moyale was tasked with investigations.

The arrested caretaker was taken into custody as investigators sought to establish the circumstances under which the Ethiopian nationals were being accommodated and whether other individuals were involved in the suspected smuggling network.

Police did not immediately disclose the intended destination of the victims or how long they had been held at the locations.

The authorities also did not provide details regarding the condition of the rescued individuals or whether additional suspects were being pursued.

Close 

The operation comes amid continued efforts by security agencies to combat human trafficking and smuggling networks operating across Kenya's northern border regions.

Marsabit County's proximity to Ethiopia and other countries in the Horn of Africa makes it a strategic area for cross-border security operations.

The rescued Ethiopian nationals and the arrested suspect were expected to assist investigators as police continued inquiries into the incident.

Authorities have not yet announced whether the suspect will face formal charges.

The investigation is ongoing.

World.title: Kenya: Ruto Mourns 23 Killed in Kanga Road Crash
World.content:
Nairobi — President William Ruto has mourned the 23 people killed in a road accident at Kanga near Mtito Andei along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, calling for greater caution among motorists and stricter safety inspections for public service vehicles (PSVs).

In a condolence message shared on social media, Ruto expressed sympathy with the families and friends of the victims, describing the incident as a devastating loss for the affected families and the country.

"I convey my heartfelt condolences to the families and friends of the 23 people who lost their lives in the tragic road accident," the President said, adding that the country shared in their grief.

He also wished those injured in the crash a quick recovery.



The President urged all motorists, particularly drivers operating public service vehicles, to exercise caution and observe traffic regulations to prevent further loss of life on Kenyan roads.

Ruto further directed relevant authorities to conduct thorough inspections of public service vehicles to ensure they comply with the required safety standards.

The directive comes amid renewed concerns over road safety following the fatal collision at Kanga, near Mtito Andei, on the busy Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.

The President said vehicle inspections should help ensure that public service vehicles meet the required safety standards, as part of efforts to prevent road accidents.

The accident has renewed calls for motorists to adhere to traffic rules and for authorities to strengthen enforcement of road safety regulations.

The Nairobi-Mombasa Highway is a key transport corridor connecting the capital to the Coast, carrying passenger buses, commercial vehicles and private motorists.

Ruto's call places renewed emphasis on responsible driving, compliance with traffic regulations and regular inspections of public service vehicles.

The President's message did not provide further details on the cause of the crash or the condition of those injured.

World.title: Sudan: 'Sudan Drone Strikes Killed 306 in Three Weeks' - UN Human Rights Chief
World.content:
Amsterdam / Geneva / Sudan — The UN Human Rights Office documented hundreds of deaths and injuries in October, with attacks attributed to both sides hitting displacement sites, markets, hospitals, and vital infrastructure. The UN Security Council has separately condemned deadly drone strikes in Abyei.

The UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, has condemned a sharp escalation in drone strikes across Sudan after the UN Human Rights Office documented at least 306 deaths and hundreds of injuries during the first three weeks of October.

The strikes, attributed to both the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), hit civilian sites and infrastructure, including homes, markets, hospitals, displacement sites, power stations, and water sources.

Türk said the increasing use of drones, which have already accounted for the majority of conflict-related civilian deaths in Sudan this year, was deeply disturbing and exacting a horrifying toll.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Scores of civilians have been killed and vital infrastructure and services on which they depend eviscerated, driving further displacement and deepening the already severe humanitarian crisis," he said.

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights renewed his call on the warring parties to comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law, including the prohibition on directing attacks against civilians and civilian objects.

Displacement sites and gold mines targeted

The UN Human Rights Office has documented numerous drone strikes on displacement sites where people who had fled fighting had sought shelter, resulting in a sharp increase in casualties among internally displaced people.

Between 6 and 10 October, alleged drone strikes attributed to the Sudanese Armed Forces on shelters in Ghubeish and El Nuhud in West Kordofan killed at least 25 civilians and injured 31 others, including women and children.

In Abu Shendi, in Blue Nile state, an alleged RSF drone strike on 9 October hit a gathering of displaced people engaged in traditional gold mining near a displacement site. At least 31 people were killed, most of them women and children.

Further attacks targeted the Bajoun gold-mining area in Gadeer locality, South Kordofan, on 9 and 16 October. Drone strikes attributed to the RSF killed 42 civilians and injured 25 others.

The UN Human Rights Office said attacks on gold-mining areas were linked to the war economy sustaining the conflict and raised serious concerns about the deliberate targeting of sites with economic value to the opposing side.

However, it stressed that an object's financial contribution to the war effort was not, by itself, sufficient to make it a legitimate military objective under the laws of war.

Transport, markets and hospitals hit

Civilians travelling by road have also come under attack. On 18 October, at least 139 people were killed and dozens more injured when a transport truck was struck in a repeated, or "double-tap", drone attack in Dibab, West Kordofan, an area controlled by the RSF.

Markets have continued to face drone strikes with alarming regularity. Attacks in Al Dabba in North Darfur, Nyala in South Darfur, and El Odaya in West Kordofan reportedly killed a total of 23 civilians.

Healthcare facilities have also been hit. An attack attributed to the RSF on Um Darfa hospital in Blue Nile state on 11 October seriously injured two health workers and forced the facility to stop operating.

The UN Human Rights Office also warned of an emerging pattern of retaliatory strikes. Drone attacks attributed to the RSF on Khartoum, including the airport area, were reportedly carried out in response to alleged Sudanese Armed Forces airstrikes on Nyala in South Darfur.

Türk said wider peace efforts must address the continued flow of weapons fuelling the conflict and press for an end to arms transfers used in flagrant disregard of international humanitarian law obligations to protect civilians.

"I urge both parties to the conflict, and their affiliates, to commit to a ceasefire," he said.

He stressed that a negotiated settlement placing human rights at its centre and backed by accountability for widespread violations and abuses was the only viable path to lasting peace in Sudan.

Security Council condemns drone strikes in Abyei

Separately, members of the UN Security Council have strongly condemned drone attacks in the disputed Abyei area on 19 October, near Amiet market and Todach, which killed and injured numerous people, including women and children.

Close 

The council expressed its condolences to the victims' families and communities in Abyei and wished those injured a full and speedy recovery. It also voiced grave concern that the death toll could rise as the UN Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) continued to verify the casualties.

Council members stressed that international humanitarian law prohibits attacks against civilians and civilian objects, warning that such attacks could amount to war crimes.

They called for a full, transparent, and prompt investigation and emphasised that those responsible must be held accountable.

The council reiterated that Abyei must remain demilitarised and free of all forces other than UNISFA. It called on all actors to halt military operations and withdraw from the area.

It also reaffirmed its support for UNISFA and urged all parties to cooperate with the mission to safeguard civilians, humanitarian workers, and peacekeepers.

World.title: Guinea: 'Go Green and Go Thirsty' - Guinea's Plastic Ban Clashes With Need for Safe Water
World.content:
Plastic water sachets are an essential way to provide people in Guinea with safe and affordable drinking water. But their use clashes with the government's objective of outlawing single-use plastics. Until a solution can be found, authorities have been forced to lift a ban, less than three weeks after implementing it.

The Republic of Guinea passed its law to ban single-use plastics two years ago, but only enforced it on 20 September.

However, in the face of mounting public anger, it was forced to do a U-turn and lifted the ban on 7 October, for the next six months.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"To govern is to foresee. The ban was a most reckless decision," said Emmanuel, who buys water sachets every day in the capital Conakry.

"How can you ban the population's only access to safe drinking water without having provided an alternative solution?" asked Oumou, also from Conakry. "You can't suddenly go green and make people go thirsty."

RFI also spoke to Faya Blaise, who said he would like government ministers to "come see how life goes in the poorer neighbourhoods".

"They should see how we live and the difficulties we face before making decisions that impact us directly."

Health issues

The World Bank describes Guinea as a country with poor infrastructure and widespread poverty, with â 3.7 million of its 15.1 million people living on less than $4.20 per day.

Emmanuel in Conakry described the lengths he has to go to for safe drinking water, given the expense of buying it bottled.

"I pay CFA 3,000 [around €4.50] for a small bottle of water and CFA 500 [€0.75] for a water sachet of 400ml. I decided to collect rainwater and bought a product at the pharmacy to kill the bacteria it might contain and purify it."

Jonas from Dabola, in central Guinea, told RFI that nobody in his small town drinks the tap water provided by the national water company.

"It is as filthy as water in a pig's wallow. It contains bits of clay, and I have to filter it to bathe."

Disappointment and anger after world fails to agree plastic pollution treaty

Ben Youssouf Keita, a doctor who runs a medical centre in Conakry, told RFI there had been a rise in the number of patients with water-borne diseases after the ban was enforced in September.

"A lot of patients were admitted for abdominal pain and diarrhoea. After talking to them, we found out that they have been drinking water from boreholes, or tap water."

He welcomed the temporary pause in the ban, saying it could avert cases of typhoid or dysentery, adding: "Meanwhile, the government should launch an awareness campaign on the need to boil water wherever it comes from - rain, river, wells - before drinking it."

Alternative solutions

Following the lifting of the ban, factories producing single-use plastic water sachets have resumed their activities - for the next six months, at least.

Abdoulaye Fofana heads a water sachet production plant and is the chairman of the Union of Mineral Water Producers. He told RFI that the sector needs to quickly find environmentally friendly solutions.

"We are challenging our suppliers to find biodegradable plastics. In order, hopefully, to set up small companies for collecting and recycling the plastic. That should ensure a healthy, unpolluted environment."

Abdoulaye heads up a small industrial sanitation company. He said that bags made of cassava fibre could replace plastic sachets.

"It is environmentally friendly because it is biodegradable and takes six months to disintegrate. Cassava is widely consumed in Guinea. This is an alternative that will give work to the farmers," he said.

However, the price of biodegradable sachets is far higher than that of plastic sachets.

Close 

In light of this, Mamady Aminata Touré, an environmental campaigner, is calling on the government to focus its efforts on developing the recycling sector.

"There aren't many companies involved in plastic processing and recycling in Guinea. We need to develop this sector and build confidence in these companies. And that's where the government has a role to play with incentives and subsidies."

For M'Bany Sidibé, head of the Union for the Defence of Consumers in Guinea, the best long-term solution is to develop the national water authority.

"It will take at least five to 10 years to get safe, drinking water across the whole of Guinea," he told RFI.

Sidibé warns that in the absence of an alternative that is as cheap as plastic water sachets, they will remain essential.

World.title: Kenya: Govt Targets Black Spots, Reckless Overtaking in New Road Safety Plan After 22 Die in Kanga Crash
World.content:
Nairobi — The government has outlined a three-pronged road safety intervention focusing on infrastructure funding, stricter traffic enforcement and improved driver training following a head-on collision that killed 22 people along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.

Transport Cabinet Secretary Davis Chirchir said the government would strengthen the management of accident black spots, intensify enforcement against dangerous driving and tighten training and oversight of commercial and public service vehicle drivers.

The measures were announced following Saturday's fatal crash at Kanga, approximately 10 kilometres east of Mtito Andei, involving a commercial cement tipper truck and a passenger bus belonging to Power of the Word Church International, Mombasa.

The accident occurred at approximately 7:45am, leaving 22 people dead and several others injured. Initial accounts indicated that improper overtaking may have contributed to the collision, although investigations into the cause remain ongoing.



In a statement dated October 25, Chirchir said "the government was pursuing coordinated and sustained interventions to address the country's road safety challenges, working with Parliament, the Judiciary, the National Police Service, county governments and other stakeholders."

"The first intervention will focus on structured funding for road safety infrastructure, with the government seeking to strengthen the black spot management programme," he stated.

He pointed out that the initiative is intended to identify high-risk road sections and implement targeted engineering and infrastructure improvements to reduce the likelihood and severity of crashes.

The latest accident has renewed scrutiny of the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, a major transport corridor used by passenger buses, commercial trucks and private motorists.

Chirchir cited the October 3 accident at Salama, near Mtito Andei, which claimed 17 lives, as another reminder of the urgency of addressing road safety risks.

The government said targeted infrastructure improvements would form part of broader efforts to prevent recurring accidents on dangerous road sections.

However, the statement did not specify the funding allocation, implementation timelines or the first locations to be prioritised under the strengthened programme.

The second intervention will involve intensified traffic enforcement against dangerous driving, reckless overtaking, speeding and other violations that put motorists and passengers at risk.

The government said enforcement agencies would also promote responsible road-user behaviour as part of efforts to reduce preventable road deaths.

The Kanga collision has brought renewed attention to overtaking on busy highways, particularly where heavy commercial vehicles and passenger buses share the same carriageways.

Although improper overtaking is among the suspected factors in Saturday's crash, authorities have yet to establish the definitive cause.

The National Transport and Safety Authority (NTSA), the National Police Service and other relevant agencies are investigating the incident to determine what happened and establish whether any violations contributed to the collision.

Chirchir said the government would work with the relevant institutions to strengthen compliance and accountability across the transport sector.

The third pillar of the plan will focus on stronger training and oversight of drivers, particularly those operating commercial vehicles and public service vehicles.

The government intends to pursue structured training and compliance measures aimed at improving driver competence, discipline and adherence to road safety requirements.

The intervention comes as questions emerge over the regulation of vehicles used to transport passengers, including buses operated by institutions and organisations, alongside trucks operated by commercial enterprises.

Both vehicles involved in the Kanga crash were commercial vehicles, highlighting the importance of effective regulation, vehicle compliance and enforcement regardless of ownership.

The government said improved driver oversight would form part of a wider effort to ensure that operators meet safety requirements and that drivers observe traffic rules.

The Ministry also plans to engage Parliament, the Senate and the Judiciary to address implementation challenges surrounding the Commercial Vehicle Regulations 2026, Vehicle Inspection Regulations 2026 and School Transport Regulations 2026.

Close 

The proposed regulatory frameworks are intended to strengthen vehicle roadworthiness, driver accountability and fatigue management.

The government said effective implementation would require cooperation among road agencies, law enforcement institutions, the health sector, county governments and other stakeholders.

The planned national approach will operate under clearer responsibilities, measurable targets and stronger accountability, according to the Ministry.

The government also commended emergency responders, medical personnel and security officers who participated in rescue efforts following the Kanga collision.

The injured victims were taken to Mtito Andei Sub-County Hospital and Kambu Level 4 Hospital for treatment.

Chirchir extended condolences to the bereaved families, friends and the affected church community, as investigations continued into one of the latest deadly crashes on the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway.

The government said sustained collaboration among public institutions and transport stakeholders would be necessary to reduce road deaths and improve safety across the country's road network.

World.title: Sudan: Famine Risk Is Rising in Sudan As 19.5 Million Face Acute Hunger - UK-Led Warning
World.content:
Amsterdam / London / Khartoum — A joint statement by the UK and 31 partners urges the warring parties to lift restrictions on aid, protect humanitarian workers, and allow air access into Darfur as food insecurity worsens. The Emergency Lawyers group has welcomed the joint ministerial statement, while the displaced people's coordination body calls for 90-day humanitarian truce in Sudan,

A UK-led international warning* has called for urgent action to avert famine in Sudan, where an estimated 19.5 million people are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, including 5 million facing emergency levels.

The joint ministerial statement, published on 23 October by the UK and 31 international partners, warns that Sudan's food security is deteriorating alarmingly and that the risk of famine in the coming months requires immediate action.

The statement says the number of children suffering from severe acute malnutrition could exceed the projected 825,000 unless the current trajectory is reversed. The number of areas affected by food insecurity, initially assessed at 14, is also expected to double.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Conflict remains the principal driver of Sudan's hunger crisis, according to the statement, which says fighting has displaced millions of people, damaged critical infrastructure, and disrupted healthcare, food production, supply chains, and markets.

The crisis is being compounded by what the signatories describe as systematic obstruction of humanitarian aid, alongside the effects of El Niño, which have reduced rainfall and increased drought across more than half of Sudan.

Call for unrestricted humanitarian access

The statement says the parties to the conflict bear primary responsibility for alleviating the suffering of Sudanese civilians. It urges them to remove all obstacles to humanitarian assistance and ensure full, safe, rapid, and unhindered access, while protecting humanitarian personnel.

The signatories call for humanitarian operations to be authorised across all front lines and through cross-border routes, including air access into Darfur. They say this would enable aid operations to be deployed rapidly and allow timely medical evacuations of humanitarian workers.

They also call for measures to reduce delays in visas and customs clearance, extend the validity of visas and travel permits, and remove additional permits, taxes, and other bureaucratic requirements that slow aid deliveries.

The parties are urged to refrain from attacks on civilian infrastructure, including agricultural and food systems essential to providing basic services. The statement also calls for stronger civil-military coordination to protect humanitarian workers and aid facilities.

International funding needed

The statement calls on the international community to increase humanitarian funding urgently in response to growing needs and to ensure assistance reaches those most in need.

It also urges development and financial institutions to adapt their programmes to the worsening food security situation and prioritise the areas facing the greatest need.

With the risk of famine looming, the signatories stress the importance of supporting Sudan's winter cropping season and strengthening locally led responses.

The statement concludes by expressing solidarity with the Sudanese people and humanitarian organisations continuing to provide life-saving assistance under extremely difficult conditions.

Displaced people's coordination body calls for 90-day humanitarian truce in Sudan

The General Coordination for Displaced Persons and Refugees has called for an immediate halt to fighting in Sudan and a humanitarian truce lasting at least 90 days, as a step towards a permanent ceasefire and an end to civilian suffering.

The body stressed the need to open all humanitarian routes without restrictions or obstacles and ensure food and medical aid reaches everyone affected, particularly displaced people, refugees, and communities at risk of famine.

It called for civilians to be protected and attacks on residential areas, markets, healthcare facilities, and water sources to stop, with those responsible for violations held accountable.

The coordination body also urged urgent and effective international action to increase humanitarian funding, halt the flow of weapons to both sides in the conflict, and support a serious political process leading to a just and lasting peace.

It appealed to the international community, the United Nations, the African Union, humanitarian organisations, and donors to intensify diplomatic and humanitarian efforts, provide the resources needed to meet growing needs, and exert serious pressure on the warring parties to stop fighting and ensure aid reaches all those affected, without discrimination or exception.

Emergency Lawyers warn of worsening humanitarian catastrophe

The Emergency Lawyers group has welcomed the joint ministerial statement on worsening hunger and food insecurity in Sudan, warning that the humanitarian catastrophe is deepening as the war continues and the basic conditions for survival deteriorate.

In a statement, the group said the crisis had been exacerbated by the failure of the agricultural season, water shortages, and declining vegetation cover. These conditions had forced many people to dispose of their livestock because they could no longer provide them with food and water.

Rising prices, restrictions imposed by the army and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian movement and the transport of goods, looting by armed groups, and the obstruction and targeting of humanitarian aid had further deepened food insecurity, the group said.

These conditions coincide with continued displacement in western and central Sudan, the absence of basic services, and ongoing military operations that put civilians' safety and needs at risk.

The group warned that the deliberate deprivation of civilians of food and water, obstruction of relief efforts, looting of property, attacks on objects indispensable to the survival of the population, and forced displacement could constitute war crimes or crimes against humanity, depending on the circumstances of each incident and its legal elements.

It also condemned the use of humanitarian aid as a tool in political conflict, or as a means of pressuring communities and denying them relief. Aid must reach those in need without discrimination or exploitation, it said.

Emergency Lawyers called for relief centres to be established in the worst-affected areas and communities at risk of becoming depopulated, providing food, drinking water, healthcare, and other essential supplies.

The group also urged both sides in the conflict to lift restrictions on civilian movement and the transport of goods, end looting and attacks that obstruct relief operations, ensure aid can reach people safely, and protect water sources and civilian infrastructure.

It called on the international community and donors to increase humanitarian funding and direct it towards the areas with the greatest needs.

World.title: Kenya: Kalonzo Claims People Are Being Paid to Divide Opposition, Defends Gachagua Visit
World.content:
Nairobi — Wiper Patriotic Front leader Stephen Kalonzo Musyoka has claimed that individuals are being paid to sow confusion and disunity within the opposition, reaffirming his commitment to bringing opposition leaders together ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Kalonzo said he was aware of efforts to undermine opposition unity, urging Kenyans to disregard what he described as baseless claims targeting opposition leaders.

Speaking during a church service at ACK Church of Faith in Ithareini, Kirinyaga County, alongside Democratic Party (DP) leader JB Muturi and other leaders, Kalonzo maintained that opposition cooperation remained essential in challenging President William Ruto's administration.

The Wiper leader also defended his recent visit to former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua at his Wamunyoro residence, dismissing suggestions that the meeting was unusual or intended to create divisions within the opposition.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Kalonzo said he and Gachagua had maintained a close friendship since the former Deputy President's impeachment, noting that Gachagua had previously visited his home in Tseikuru.

He explained that his visit to Wamunyoro was therefore a reciprocal engagement between friends and should not be interpreted as a source of political controversy.

The opposition leader reaffirmed his commitment to unity, insisting that he would continue engaging fellow opposition leaders as they prepare for the 2027 elections.

He said political differences should not be allowed to derail efforts to build a united opposition capable of addressing the country's challenges.

During the church service, Kalonzo led congregants in a moment of silence in honour of those who lost their lives following the collapse of a building in Eastleigh, Nairobi.

He also offered prayers for rescue teams and people who remained trapped beneath the rubble as emergency operations continued.

The Wiper leader called for compassion and solidarity with affected families, saying the tragedy had left the country mourning.

The opposition leaders joined the congregation in remembering the victims and praying for those still awaiting rescue.

Kalonzo also mourned the 22 people reported killed in a road accident along the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

He expressed concern over the continued loss of lives on the busy transport corridor, saying Kenyan families had suffered repeated tragedies involving road accidents.

The Wiper leader recalled that pilgrims had also died in an accident along the same highway last month, arguing that the recurring incidents highlighted the urgent need for improved road safety.

He said the country could no longer afford to lose so many lives on a highway that serves thousands of motorists and passengers travelling between Nairobi and the Coast.

Kalonzo renewed his pledge to transform the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway into a dual carriageway, saying expanding the road would help improve traffic flow and address safety concerns.

He maintained that the project should be prioritised to reduce congestion and minimise the risks associated with the increasing volume of traffic along the route.

The opposition leader said the loss of 22 lives in Sunday's accident underscored the urgency of addressing infrastructure challenges and improving road safety.

Kalonzo's remarks come amid ongoing efforts by opposition leaders to strengthen cooperation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The Wiper leader maintained that he remained committed to working with other opposition leaders, dismissing claims that his engagements were intended to undermine unity.

Close 

He urged Kenyans to reject attempts to create divisions among opposition leaders, saying their focus should remain on addressing the country's economic and governance challenges.

Kalonzo said he would continue engaging political leaders across the opposition as they seek to establish a common political direction ahead of the next election.

He reiterated that unity remained critical to the opposition's efforts to challenge President William Ruto and offer Kenyans an alternative leadership.

The Wiper leader's renewed commitment to dualing the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway also places infrastructure development and road safety among the issues he is highlighting as the country moves towards the 2027 election campaign.

World.title: Kenya: 15-Year-Old Girl, 16-Year-Old Brother Killed in Ordinance Explosion in Garissa
World.content:
Nairobi — Two siblings aged 15 and 16 have died after an unexploded explosive device detonated while they were herding cattle in Bura East Sub-County, Garissa County.

The incident occurred on Saturday, at approximately midday, leaving the two minors critically injured after they reportedly struck a strange object they had discovered while grazing livestock.

According to a police incident report, the explosion was reported by the Officer Commanding a Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) Forward Operating Base (FOB) camp in Bura East, who said a loud blast had been heard at around 1200 hours.

The military officer subsequently dispatched a drone to conduct aerial surveillance around the camp but did not immediately identify the source of the explosion.



A team was later deployed to patrol areas surrounding the military installation, where they discovered the two injured children.

The siblings were evacuated to the KDF camp for medical attention as efforts were made to stabilise their condition.

The police report identified the deceased girl as Malyun Ahmed Diriye, 15, and her brother as Abdi Ahmed Burale, 16.

Malyun reportedly told the military team that they had discovered a strange object while herding cattle.

According to her account, her brother began striking the object with a panga out of curiosity, triggering the explosion.

The girl succumbed to her injuries shortly after being evacuated to the military camp.

Her brother also died while medical personnel were attempting to stabilise him.

The two siblings were residents of Guyo Village in Nanighi Location, Bura East Sub-County.

The KDF team suspects that the object could have been a rocket-propelled grenade (RPG), which may have been abandoned or used during an earlier attempt by militants to target the military camp.

However, the police report did not confirm the exact type of explosive device involved in the incident.

The circumstances under which the object was left in the area were also not immediately established.

Investigations are expected to establish the origin of the explosive and whether it was linked to previous militant activity around the military installation.

The incident highlights the dangers posed by unexploded ordnance in areas where security operations have been conducted, particularly to children and residents engaging in routine activities such as herding livestock.

Close 

Authorities have not issued further details regarding the recovery or disposal of the explosive device.

The deaths of the two siblings have also raised concerns about the risks posed by abandoned explosives to civilians living in security-sensitive areas of northern Kenya.

World.title: Seattle Seahawks dominate Chiefs 20-3 as Sam Darnold silences critics in potential Super Bowl preview
World.content:
After a bizarre 2025 season, the Kansas City Chiefs are right back at the top of the NFL in 2026 and already well on their way toward yet another Chiefs-Bills AFC Championship game.

But last year's Super Bowl Champions, the Seattle Seahawks, have been far less convincing. After opening the season with two wins over the New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals, Seattle entered the weekend just 1-3 since. The surprising loss to the Commanders was followed by a win over the hapless LA Chargers, then two frustrating losses to the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos in overtime.

Last weekend's loss was ugly enough that speculation started immediately afterward that Sam Darnold might be in danger of losing his starting job to Drew Lock. From Super Bowl winner to backing up Drew Lock in six games? It sounds crazy, but that's what going 27/51 with no touchdowns and two interceptions, in a losing effort to a quarterback with 107 passing yards, does in the NFL.

DENVER BRONCOS SURVIVE UGLY OFFENSIVE NIGHT TO BEAT SEATTLE SEAHAWKS 17-14 IN OVERTIME

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was adamant, however, that he'd stick with Darnold.

"Sam's played great football for us this year the majority of the time," he said in an October 16 radio interview. "There's other times he needs to take care of the football, but I think these are solutions we can find with Sam as our QB. I believe that."

"I think we have a lot of faith in Sam," he added in a news conference that same day. "Sam’s played great football for us. He’s done a lot of great things this year. We’ve obviously turned the ball over more than we want to. I feel like there’s things on our end that can help him play better football. And I think he’s definitely part of the solution, rather than the opposite."

He, and Seahawks fans, are probably glad Macdonald stuck with him. Despite some further, back-breaking struggles with ball security.

After a punt-filled first quarter, the second provided a lot more action. While Patrick Mahomes uncharacteristically struggled, with an interception killing a Chiefs' drive, Darnold was on fire for Seattle. On the Seahawks' first scoring drive, he threw for 71 yards, including a 33-yard completion to Jaxson Smith-Njigba. The very next drive, after Mahomes' interception, Darnold found Smith-Njigba again, connecting on a 28-yard touchdown pass thanks to some impressive strength from the 24-year-old wideout to stay in bounds.

In the waning seconds of the second quarter, though, Darnold's ball security issues crept up again.

After yet another big 28-yard completion to Smith-Njigba to put the ball at the Kansas City 2-yard-line with 30 seconds left in the half, the Seahawks tried a George Holani run that went backwards. Darnold, under pressure, tried to find Rasheed Shaheed in the endzone, only to get picked off by Noah Williams.

Williams added a lengthy runback, seemingly setting up the Chiefs for an unlikely, last-second score.

But Harrison Butker, not off to his best start thus far, missed the 58-yard field goal to end the half.

In the third, Darnold was back at it again, completing passes of 17, 12, and 19 yards to help Seattle add three points and make it 13-0. And the typically dominant Chiefs offense just didn't ever get on track. Mahomes was frequently hurried, and with Rashee Rice once again out, there was little separation from the Kansas City receiving corps. Kenneth Walker couldn't get much going on the ground either.

Mahomes was far from his best either, nearly losing a fumble in the third quarter, and mostly dinking and dunking his way down the field. Even when the Chiefs finally put together a solid drive in the fourth, Butker missed his second kick of the game, just a 45-yard try, that would have narrowed the score to 13-6.

Seattle took advantage, putting the game away with a 21-yard touchdown run from Emanuel Wilson on third-and-4.

While Lumen Field is a tough place to play, the level to which Seattle dominated Sunday night's game was still surprising. Prior to garbage time, they had a 388 to 210 yardage advantage with 22 first downs to Kansas City's 11. The Seahawks went 11/15 on third downs too, compared to just 3/11 for Kansas City. Kenneth Walker, coming off a game in which he had 19 carries for 128 yards and two touchdowns, went just 14 for 36 against Seattle. And the three points for KC entering the fourth quarter was tied for the fewest of any game in Mahomes' storied career.



It was the type of suffocating defensive performance that's become a hallmark of the Seahawks' run the past few seasons. And perhaps even more encouraging, a much better outing from Darnold, awful second quarter interception aside.

World.title: Bruce Blakeman calls Kathy Hochul Zohran Mamdani's 'puppet' during New York campaign rally

Republican New York gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman blasted Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul as a "puppet" of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a campaign rally Sunday.

Speaking at the event in Yorktown Heights, New York, Blakeman, the current Nassau County executive, accused his opponent of embracing the democratic socialist mayor's agenda while failing to crack down on illegal immigration and crime.

"Kathy Hochul, she was out campaigning with Mamdani this week," Blakeman said, according to the New York Post. "And I say that’s great."

HOCHUL DEFLECTS WHEN PRESSED ON TIES TO 'ANTI-CHRISTIAN' MAMDANI IN FIERY DEBATE MOMENT: 'SHAME ON YOU'

Hochul has been campaigning alongside Mamdani, including at a recent rally in Brooklyn.

The political alliance between the mayor and the governor, who is seeking reelection to a second full term, comes as democratic socialists have gained greater influence in New York politics.

Along with Mamdani's victory in last year's mayoral election, candidates aligned with Mamdani and New York's democratic socialist movement scored major victories in congressional primaries this year, including the defeats of two Democratic incumbents.

FAR-LEFT SURGE: MAMDANI-BACKED CANDIDATES OUST DEM ESTABLISHMENT INCUMBENTS

World.title: Cam Skattebo takes aim at NFL after controversial call in Giants win: 'Guess I’m going to play for free'
World.content:
Cam Skattebo has lowered his shoulder numerous times in his early NFL career, delivering bone-rattling thuds into opponents to help his New York Giants.

In Sunday’s win over the Houston Texans, though, Skattebo was flagged for unnecessary roughness after officials deemed he crossed a line when he laid the boom on safety M.J. Stewart, sending him to the turf after a big gain on the ground.

Skattebo was livid at the call, as was head coach John Harbaugh , who had to hold his running back behind him on the sideline before displaying his own displeasure at the flag being thrown.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After the game, where Skattebo’s 42-yard run in overtime helped set up Devin Singletary’s 30-yard touchdown to seal victory for New York, the second-year running back didn’t mince words as he took a shot at the league as a whole.

"Yeah, I’ll keep that conversation between us," Skattebo said when asked what was said to the official following the unnecessary roughness call. "I will say, man, the NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that, but then also wants to take stuff from me. So, I mean, I’m going to run the ball like I want to run the ball, and if I’m going to continue to get flagged or it or fined for it, man, I guess I’m going to play for free.

"I’m going to do what I can to be on this team, to give everything I got. If they’re going to punish me for that, I’m just going to keep doing it and keep playing hard."

To Skattebo’s point, the NFL has enjoyed his bulldozing style of running that turns back the clock to old-school running through the tackles.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

At the same time, the league has been trying to crack down on helmet-to-helmet contact for years, and referees believed Skattebo led with the crown of his helmet in this case.

However, looking back at the video, Skattebo’s run here appeared no different than others he’s had in the past. It’s why many NFL fans were in an uproar along with Skattebo, calling the call "soft," "bizarre" and more on social media.

It is very rare for officials to throw flags on an offensive player in those situations, which made it seem bizarre in the moment. The video replay almost confirmed as such, but nonetheless, as Skattebo pointed out, a fine might be coming his way from the league due to the unnecessary roughness call.

Controversial penalty call aside, Skattebo’s play in Week 7 was redemption after he did not get a single carry the game prior, as Giants fans believed Harbaugh had him in the doghouse following a costly overtime fumble against the Washington Commanders. The Giants ended up with a tie in that contest, but if Skattebo hadn’t fumbled, New York could be 5-2 today, given it came in field goal range, where the next score won the game.

"It wasn’t by design for him not to carry the ball," Harbaugh said after the tie to Washington. "Just when he was in there, we didn’t call any runs. You’re not thinking about which back is in the game and how many runs they’re getting. It’s we were going to give them all an equal shot, give them a chance, see who got a hot hand maybe, see who could get going with it. We weren’t planning on being down by 24, that’s for sure."

World.title: College homecoming party turns to chaos as deck collapses, leaving at least 28 people injured
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A college homecoming party took a frightening turn Friday night when a back deck collapsed at a Virginia home, leaving at least 28 people injured and sending emergency crews rushing to the neighborhood.

William & Mary confirmed students were among those injured at the off-campus residence in Williamsburg. All reported injuries were non-life-threatening, according to city officials.

Dispatchers received a report of a structure collapse around 10:07 p.m. on the 200 block of Matoaka Court. Responding police and firefighters found the home’s back deck had collapsed, the city said.

TERRIFYING SCENE UNFOLDS AS METAL CABANA FRAME CRASHES INTO PACKED CASINO POOL AREA

Emergency crews took 13 people to hospitals, while another 15 reportedly sought treatment on their own, according to the city’s Saturday morning update.

Neighbors told WAVY that a homecoming party was underway when the deck gave way. One described emergency vehicles stretching through the neighborhood.

"All the way down the street and wrapped around just ambulances and fire trucks," the neighbor, who asked not to be named, told WAVY. "We saw a lot of hospital gurneys coming out of ambulances. At least nine ambulances kind of wrapped around the street."

WATCH: VIRGINIA COPS CRAWL THROUGH BURNING HOUSE TO SAVE MAN TRAPPED IN FIRE

Joshua Wise, who lives next to the home, told the outlet some of his classmates were involved. He returned after emergency crews had finished responding but learned his housemate had been helping people get home.

"Word was traveling pretty fast," Wise told WAVY. "By the time I got back here, the emergency response was over, but I had a housemate who was helping people, trying to help out as much as possible, drive people home, get people where they needed to be."

Wise credited neighbors with coming together after the frightening incident.

"We did everything we could to help each other out and I think that that’s beautiful," he said.

5 VICTIMS RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL AFTER FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING, 1 REMAINS CRITICAL

In a Saturday message to the campus community, William & Mary’s senior vice president for student affairs and public safety, Ginger Ambler, said the university was still gathering information. Additional students may have sought care beyond those initially counted, she noted.

"We are grateful that none of the injuries were life-threatening," Ambler wrote.

She said staff across the university’s health, academic and student support offices were working to assist affected students.

"We recognize that such an experience may affect our students deeply and in different ways," Ambler wrote.

Wise also praised the emergency response.

"Thank goodness for the emergency responders," he told WAVY. "They were great. The ambulances and everything got here pretty fast."

World.title: Ninth Circuit questions Trump DOJ's emergency request to set aside 20,000 California mail ballots
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A federal appeals court on Sunday scrutinized the Trump administration's emergency effort to force California to set aside thousands of mail-in ballots tied to people the Justice Department suspects are noncitizens ahead of the midterm elections.

The three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit raised questions about both the government's legal arguments and whether the court has jurisdiction to intervene during a hearing in which attorneys representing the Trump administration and California argued for nearly two hours, Fox News' Matt Finn reported.

The federal government asked the panel to rule immediately, arguing that hundreds of thousands of California ballots could be tabulated each day while the dispute remains unresolved.

The hearing comes after the Trump administration filed an emergency request involving roughly 20,000 mail-in ballots sent to people it suspects are noncitizens.

CALIFORNIA MUST RESPOND TO DOJ'S EMERGENCY REQUEST OVER BALLOTS MAILED TO ALLEGED NONCITIZENS, COURT RULES

The DOJ wants California election officials to set aside ballots associated with individuals on its list while their eligibility is reviewed, rather than allowing the ballots to be processed alongside other votes.

Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, questioned whether the administration's requested injunction could be reconciled with the Constitution's Elections Clause, which gives state legislatures authority over the times, places and manner of congressional elections, subject to congressional regulation.

"It seems to me that you want us to issue an injunction that is entirely inconsistent with the law that the California legislature has adopted pursuant to the Elections Clause," he told Justice Department attorney Matthew Donnelly.

BLANCHE WON'T RULE OUT DOJ BLOCKING ELECTION CERTIFICATION IN 'DOOMSDAY' SCENARIO

"How can we do that?"

The panel also questioned whether the Ninth Circuit has jurisdiction to intervene at this stage.

Judge Gabriel Sanchez, a Biden appointee, questioned why the Ninth Circuit should weigh in when the district court has yet to rule on the DOJ's request and a hearing before U.S. District Judge David Carter remains scheduled for Tuesday.

Judge Patrick Bumatay, another Trump appointee, focused more heavily on the government's concerns about potential noncitizen voting and questioned California's handling of challenges involving suspected ineligible voters.

The Justice Department sought emergency relief from the appeals court after Carter did not rule by a deadline previously requested by the department.

California, meanwhile, has argued that the Ninth Circuit should not intervene before the lower court has ruled.

The Justice Department initially filed the suit Oct. 15, roughly two weeks after California began mailing ballots.

TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN IN ELECTION INTEGRITY FIGHT AS STATES GAIN NEW VOTER ROLL TOOL

Before oral arguments, the Trump administration accused California of having a history of "mishandling voter rolls."

California has disputed the federal government's underlying data while emphasizing that it has robust safeguards against noncitizen voting. Los Angeles County officials have said a preliminary review of a portion of the federal government's list identified apparent discrepancies, including people who were born in the United States or were not registered to vote. In a filing this weekend, California argued that the federal government's theory would "turn the Constitution on its head."

"When it comes to rules of elections administration, the federal government has no power to interfere with the States unless Congress passes a law governing the time, place, or manner of elections," the state contended.

More than 3 million people have already cast ballots statewide, including more than 500,000 in Los Angeles County, according to figures cited during the litigation.

The Justice Department has emphasized the urgency of its request, arguing that each day without a ruling risks allowing additional ballots to be processed before the citizenship dispute can be resolved.

Bennett said the three-judge panel would try to issue a ruling as quickly as possible.

Reuters contributed to this report.

World.title: JD Vance sees Bengals making 'a run' but that's understandable because he's a fan, especially of Ja'Marr Chase

We know by now that Vice President JD Vance is a big fan of the Cincinnati Bengals so, of course, he had something to celebrate on Sunday when his team beat the Baltimore Ravens.

Vance did not attend Sunday in Baltimore, but the Bengals punished the Ravens by scoring all their 35 points in the second half, mostly thanks to four touchdown passes by quarterback Joe Burrow.

JD VANCE VISITS CINCINNATI BENGALS PRACTICE AND QUARTERBACK JOE BURROW IS CONVINCED IT WAS MOSTLY ABOUT HIM

It was the type of performance from the Bengals that everyone expected from a potential Super Bowl contender and particularly the offense.

And that had Vance feeling pretty good about his club.

Can you imagine? The second-most powerful man in the country posted on X about his NFL team. Let that sink in a second.

Anyway, the Veep continued ... "It's early, but I think the Bengals are going to make a run. Who Dey!"

The Bengals have won two consecutive games, but they do indeed need that run Vance is predicting.

They've been a roller coaster of a team, winning two in a row after losing two in a row after winning two in a row. If they continue that pattern, you know what comes next — some frustrating football.

Speaking of being a fan, Vance loves Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase.

JA'MARR CHASE THROWS HELMET AS FIGHT BREAKS OUT ON FIRST DAY OF BENGALS TRAINING CAMP

That got the VP's attention.

"Special shout out to Ja'Marr Chase, an amazing talent, who made my little six-year-old's year by noticing his football gloves," Vance posted.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

There were, by the way, "reports" that the Bengals were generally unmoved or even unfriendly during Vance's visit to their training facility. But, as Vance's boss would say, fake news.

Vance shook hands and talked with coach Zac Taylor and other players and assistant coaches.

Anyway, back to the "run" that Vance is predicting. The Bengals play four teams in their next five games with losing records. Two of those teams, the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans, have won only once each.

World.title: NFL fans put on brave face in Paris as Steelers beat Saints with chaos in the city
World.content:
The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints in the NFL’s first-ever game in France that went off surprisingly well despite the protests and civil unrest all week in Paris leading up to the matchup.

The NFL was questioned throughout the week after seeing violence, looting, vandalization and more occurring in Paris over widespread anger regarding public living costs, deteriorating public services and more. Even President Donald Trump admitted he was "worried about it," talking about the Steelers-Saints matchup.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

But the league, despite beloved soccer team Paris Saint-Germaine postponing its Saturday match to Monday due to the unrest, didn’t blink.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Neither did its fans.

OutKick caught up with several fans who braved the potential of being caught in the middle of the protests in Paris, and though there were some inconveniences, it didn’t go any further than that for these football goers.

"If I’m being honest, I have not seen enough. I’ve seen some graffiti everywhere, but I haven’t seen anything myself," one fan said outside Stade de France.

NFL OVERCOMES CIVIL UNREST, TRUMP CONCERNS AND CALLS TO POSTPONE AS STEELERS AND SAINTS KICK OFF IN PARIS

Another added: "For the most part, it hasn’t been a problem. There’s been a few delays and disturbances, but it hasn’t been that big of a problem."

One fan that caught up with OutKick came all the way from Mexico, where protests due to violent crime, working conditions, and housing costs are nothing new for him.

"[It] don’t matter. Mexico is almost the same," he said when asked about France’s widespread protests. "We have a bad government. I don’t care. I don’t care [about] the problems in France. It’s OK for me. I came for the game."

Fair enough.

There were, of course, heightened security measures, as the NFL worked closely with Parisian police, French national authorities and the U.S. State Department to ensure the safety of all attending the game and the surrounding area. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers owner Art Rooney II all met with President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace to go over safety plans as well before the game.

As for fans experiencing one of the most iconic cities around the globe, it wasn’t ideal to say the least.

"There are some stores I want to go to that are boarded up a little bit, or have cracks in their glass," one fan explained. "But other than that, the city seems great. It’s not as bad as I was expecting.

"There’s a lot of really beautiful things that they’re hurting for no reason. I understand they want to speak their voice, but they’re doing things that shouldn’t be done – vandalizing monuments and stuff. It’s not worth it."

Another fan believed that protesters have been going too far when it involves the destruction of property and more violent acts.

"Have they gone too far, the protestors? When they start tearing stuff up, yes sir. When they start burning vehicles and stuff, yeah, that’s too far."

Goodell said the game would go off without a hitch, Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed as much to OutKick, and that was the case in the end.

World.title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign events after car crash
World.content:
Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced Sunday.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement.

“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added.

Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign. A spokesperson for the campaign said they had no reason to believe the accident had been politically motivated.

The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.”

Police added that the incident is under investigation.

Peltola, a Democrat, is locked in a competitive Senate race against GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. She was elected to the House in 2022 but narrowly lost her re-election bid in 2024, the same year that President Donald Trump won the state by 13 percentage points.

Sullivan’s re-election race, in which he’s seeking a third term, is tighter than expected, with Alaska voters tying Trump to high gas and grocery prices resulting from the ongoing war with Iran.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance rallied voters in Alaska separately earlier this month.

Republicans have accused Democrats of recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan to run for the Senate, saying that voters may be confused by the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot if they plan to vote for the incumbent senator.

Democrats have not taken credit for recruiting the second Dan Sullivan into the race. He’ll appear on the ballot as Dan J. Sullivan, while the incumbent senator will be identified by his name, political party and a clear notation that he’s the incumbent.

Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska’s election officials, seeking to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It cited Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot as a point of “voter confusion.”

On Saturday, Democrats filed a motion urging a federal judge to dismiss the case.

World.title: Seahawks defense dominates Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III in big win
World.content:
The Kenneth Walker III revenge game didn’t go as planned.

The Seattle Seahawks’ defense dominated in a 20-3 win over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs in a Sunday nightcap, holding Patrick Mahomes and Walker, who won Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks in February — to their lowest passing and rushing totals of the season, respectively.

After having lost two straight games, Seattle got its best win of the season and is now only two games behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West.

“Really proud of our team,” Seahawks coach Mike MacDonald said postgame. “To stand steadfast in some adversity, that’s what we do. We find solutions.”

The Seahawks’ defense was the story. Mahomes was limited to only 165 yards through the air. He threw for no touchdowns and one interception. Meanwhile, Walker was limited even further.

He entered Sunday’s game leading the NFL in rushing yards and yards per carry (minimum 30 carries) and tied for the third-most rushing touchdowns. Against his former team, Walker ran only 14 times for 36 yards and no scores. He had run for at least 115 yards in four of the Chiefs’ first five games, and his previous lowest rushing total of the season was 70.

Walker walked off the field after the loss without greeting his former teammates.

The Seahawks ultimately held Kansas City to its fewest total yards, first downs and red-zone drives in any Mahomes start, while the Chiefs’ three points were also tied for their lowest output in any Mahomes start, per NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno.

“Our guys played great, man,” MacDonald said when he was asked about his defense. “They’re just a bunch of warriors.”

He added: “How do you not just tip your cap to those guys?”

Said Chiefs coach Andy Reid about his offense: “We’ll go back to the drawing board.”

The win was a much-needed breakthrough for Seattle, which has had an up-and-down season in defense of its Super Bowl win. The Seahawks won their first two games before they dropped three out of their last four. Their losses have been close, though, as all three came by a combined eight points.

Kansas City’s three points were the fewest by a Seattle opponent this season. And on the other side of the ball, quarterback Sam Darnold had one of his better performances of the year.

After having thrown two interceptions in three out of the last four weeks — all in losses — Darnold threw for 257 yards, one touchdown and only one pick Sunday night. He was aided greatly by receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had nine catches for 150 yards and a score.

And in an ironic twist, the Seahawks had one of their best rushing performances of the season. Seattle ran the ball 41 times for 153 yards, its second-highest total on the ground this season. Running back Emanuel Wilson ran for 100 yards, the first time a Seahawks player has reached the century mark since Walker did it in the Super Bowl.

Seattle is now 4-3 with two straight home games over the next two weeks.

The Chiefs fell to 5-1, scoring fewer than 22 points for the first time this year. Mahomes never looked in sync, while his receivers failed to create separation against one of the league’s best secondaries. Of Mahomes’ 19 completions, 11 went to Walker and tight ends.

“You gotta feel it. This sucks,” Mahomes said of the overall performance.

Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III is tackled by Leonard Williams, Uchenna Nwosu and Tyrice Knight of the Seahawks. Caleb Bowlin / Getty Images

Kicker Harrison Butker didn’t help the cause, missing two field-goal attempts, one of which would have made it a 13-6 game in the fourth quarter.

“All three phases, we gotta do better,” Reid said. “I take full responsibility for this.”

Kansas City’s offense will need to bounce back quickly, as it will face another great defense in the Denver Broncos in Week 8.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, will be tested again on Nov. 2 when they host the 5-2 Chicago Bears, who’ve averaged 30.8 points in quarterback Caleb Williams’ four starts.

World.title: Trump leans into Islamophobic rhetoric at Michigan rally
World.content:
President Donald Trump embraced Islamophobic rhetoric Sunday as he rallied in Port Huron, Michigan, in support of the state’s Republican candidates, including the GOP Senate nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers.

Trump alleged that Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee who is locked in a dead heat with Rogers, is a “jihadist,” calling him a “Muslim Brotherhood member” while saying Rogers is “apple pie.”

“Anyone with that record of support for jihadists would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane. They certainly should not give him a seat in the United States Senate,” Trump said about El-Sayed.

Throughout his comments Sunday, Trump offered no evidence for any of the claims about El-Sayed.

“He would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate. I want him to have a metal detector,” Trump said.

President Donald Trump has accused El-Sayed of having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an international Sunni Islamist organization founded in Egypt in 1928. Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty

Trump sought to draw a comparison between the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks and El-Sayed as he introduced speaker David Beamer, whose son, Todd Beamer, was a passenger who died on the hijacked United Flight 93.

“Twenty-five years later, Michigan needs to stand up and fight just like Todd did to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol,” Trump said.

Beamer went on to extend Trump’s comparison between the Senate race and 9/11.

“What has changed? Well, one thing is 9/11 was a surprise attack. What’s going on right now in our country and here in Michigan? It’s not a surprise. We can see the attack coming that culminates in this battleground state on Tuesday, November the 3rd,” Beamer said as Trump stood behind him onstage.

“What’s different this time is the enemy has not come from abroad. The enemy is right here among us, local terrorists, local citizens that want to demolish our country,” he added.

Beamer, who has been featured in Rogers’ campaign ads, compared the two men and claimed Rogers is “an American” while saying El-Sayed is not, going on to call him “anti-American.”

“Abdul has a birth certificate. The birth certificate says he’s a citizen of America. You know what? A birth certificate doesn’t make you an American,” Beamer said.

“He has blood that’s red. However, he has chosen to remove any strain of the white and blue part in his life. We cannot, cannot allow this man to invade and occupy our country,” he added.

Both Rogers and El-Sayed were born in Michigan.

Michigan Democrat senatorial candidate Abdul El-Sayed and former President Barack Obama appeared onstage together at a rally in Detroit on Saturday. Bill Pugliano / AFP via Getty

El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump’s and Beamer’s remarks.

El-Sayed went viral for a heated interaction last week with a town hall attendee who asked him to condemn the organization.

“You assume ... that because I am Muslim that somehow I would have some allegiance to something that is not our Constitution,” El-Sayed told the attendee last week.

Trump has accused El-Sayed of having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an international Sunni Islamist organization founded in Egypt in 1928. The Trump administration has designated certain chapters of the group in Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt as terrorist organizations. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied any ties to the group, which he has denounced.

Rogers was asked Sunday about Trump’s calling El-Sayed a “Muslim Brotherhood jihadist” and a “violent terrorist” in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press.” Pressed about whether he agreed with Trump’s characterizations, Rogers said the election is about “me versus Abdul,” adding, “I’ve never called him a terrorist.”

Rogers has previously questioned El-Sayed about his mother, Fatten Elkomy, over her work decades ago at a charity the U.S. government later labeled a supporter of terrorist groups, leading to its closure. Elkomy was not accused of wrongdoing at the time.

Trump helped popularize a false conspiracy theory about former President Barack Obama, claiming he was not a U.S. citizen and demanding to see his birth certificate. He has since repurposed “birther” attacks against other political rivals, including former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley, who was born in South Carolina.

Trump displayed content featuring El-Sayed at his rally in Port Huron, Mich., on Sunday. Brendan Sialowski / AFP via Getty

Trump on Sunday referred to Obama, who rallied in Detroit on Saturday on behalf of El-Sayed and other Michigan Democratic candidates.

“My competitor was here yesterday,” Trump, who is not running for office, said about Obama, who is also not running for office. “He didn’t have a crowd like this, I can tell you.”

World.title: Venezuela opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to country
World.content:
Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel laureate María Corina Machado is back in her home country after nearly a year in exile, her team confirmed to CBS News on Sunday.

"I am here. With you," Machado posted in Spanish on X.

Later Sunday night, she posted in Spanish, "Finally, Caracas, I'm here!!" along with video of supporters enthusiastically greeting her arrival.

Machado's senior adviser David Smoalnsky said in a statement to CBS that her return is "a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future."

"Machado returns to stand with Venezuelans in their pursuit of freedom, democracy, and justice, and to help advance a peaceful, inclusive, and sustainable transition leading to free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections, with guarantees for all," he said, thanking President Trump, the U.S. government and others for "their continued leadership and support."

Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado greets supporters at a church in Barquisimeto, Venezuela, on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Vente Venezuela Press Office via AP

Machado covertly snuck out of the South American country in December with a private U.S. rescue team to accept the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, her first public appearance in 11 months. The event was a month before the U.S. military deposed the country's then-President Nicolás Maduro.

Machado, who was barred by Maduro's government from exiting Venezuela, is considered a fugitive by the Venezuelan government, which accuses her of calling for military intervention against the country.

Edmundo Gonzalez, a former presidential candidate for Machado's movement who has been living in Spain, confirmed her return in his own social media post and said he would be next to her "very soon."

"Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" he wrote. "You know it, this is until the end."

After the news of her arrival, Machado was seen at a church in the state of Lara, west of Caracas. Dozens of supporters shook her hand and hugged her, with cellphones aloft to record her return, the Associated Press reported.

"María! María!" someone cried out, as another shouted, "Welcome to Venezuela!"

"Long live freedom, damn it!" a man yelled.

One woman wiped away tears and called it "a miracle" while another woman's hands flew to her face as she saw Machado enter the church.

Supporters of opposition leader Maria Corina Machado gather to demand that a date be set for presidential elections in Caracas, Venezuela, on Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Ariana Cubillos

Asked by reporters Sunday about Machado's return to Venezuela, President Trump said, "I don't know anything about it, but I think she's a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize. So how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe. She's a very nice woman. But we're doing really well in Venezuela."

Machado made several failed attempts to return to her home country, including during the aftermath of the devastating June 24 double earthquakes.

In September, the opposition leader was denied entry into Venezuela three times over 24 hours, Smoalnsky said in a statement shared with CBS News' Margaret Brennan and other journalists.

"She has attempted to enter the country by air and sea but has been turned away each time," he said at the time.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday the conditions that allowed for Machado's return to Venezuelan soil are "the direct result of the U.S. support reconciliation talks."

"The United States expects the freedoms of all sectors of Venezuelan politics to continue to be respected," he wrote on X. "Likewise, we expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy."

Machado's homecoming comes as doubts over Venezuela's democratic future — and the U.S.'s role in it — deepen.

Since Maduro's ouster, Venezuela has been run by acting President Delcy Rodríguez, a longtime Maduro ally who received the Trump administration's blessing to succeed him.

Rodríguez has exceeded the time she was authorized to serve as acting president following Maduro's capture and no election is scheduled.

Machado and her allies have been demanding a date for a presidential election in Venezuela, but U.S. officials have emphasized economic stabilization first.

World.title: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil's president
World.content:
Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of President Trump, was reelected Sunday in a result that provides relief to critics of Mr. Trump and keeps some distance between Latin America's biggest economy and Washington.

With 100% of the vote counted, Brazil's electoral court announced that the soon-to-be 81-year-old Lula had a lead of nearly 4.4 million votes — 51.8% of the total vote — over opponent Flávio Bolsonaro. The announcement capped an evening of chaos at polling places across Brazil, following a last-minute decision to extend voting by two hours. That decision by a Supreme Court justice may trigger legal action by Bolsonaro.

Lula's triumph bucks a trend in Latin America where increasing numbers of right-of-center presidential candidates allied with Mr. Trump have been winning, further extending the United States' influence in the region. Lula's victory leaves Mexico and Brazil, Latin America's two most populous nations, with left-of-center leaders. It also positions Latin America's largest economy, with a GDP of $2.6 trillion per year, to remain independent of the U.S., despite the pressure of increased tariffs imposed by Mr. Trump.

The announcement kicked off a celebration of supporters in and out of the Sao Paulo hotel where Lula watched the count with first lady Rosângela da Silva, allies, and friends.

A supporter of Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva celebrates after the results of the presidential runoff election in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on October 25, 2026. Juan BARRETO /AFP via Getty Images

Lula's victory, if confirmed by electoral authorities, will give him his non-consecutive fourth term as president. The next term begins on Jan. 5, 2027.

It is the first time since Brazil's military dictatorship ended in 1985 that the second-highest vote-getter in the first-round elections won the presidency. Bolsonaro had 47% of the vote in the first round to Lula's 45%, a difference of 2.2 million votes. However, more than 33 million voters out of nearly 160 million did not turn out in the first round.

A video published by Lula's campaign shows the veteran leader celebrating with first lady Rosângela da Silva and allies after his runoff victory was confirmed by Brazil's electoral court. Wearing star-shaped red glasses, he kissed his wife. Hundreds of his supporters began gathering on São Paulo's main artery to celebrate the victory.

In addressing supporters, Lula expressed his gratitude to the Brazilian people, and pledged to respect all Brazilians, regardless of gender or religion. He also attacked Bolsonaro."

"This was a defeat for denialism and lies. I must confess that every time I attended a debate, I felt embarrassed," he said.

He also doubled down on his commitment to Brazil's sovereignty.

"Either the homeland remains free, or we die for Brazil," he said. "This country will not accept being anyone's backyard."

In Rio de Janiero, cars beeped their horns and a woman dressed in red — the color of Lula supporters — shouted "You lost! Cry harder!" to four men in yellow and green sipping beers, Bolsonaro's signature colors. A huge roar echoed in the street as the result was confirmed.

Rodrigo Valentim, a 51-year-old businessman and supporter of Bolsonaro, said that another Lula government would harm the economy. He pointed to financial markets' positive reaction to the result of the first round, when Bolsonaro bested Lula.

"I don't understand how people can vote for Lula," he said. "The country is collapsing."

Sunday's victory will likely be the last of the veteran leader's political career. Lula began his political career in the 1970s as a union leader. He then helped found the Workers' Party, which he represented as a presidential candidate three times until he finally won it in 2002. He was reelected four years later and was succeeded by one of his cabinet ministers, Dilma Rousseff, in 2010. She was reelected in 2014.

Rousseff was impeached for accounting maneuvering in 2016 amid a sprawling corruption probe, which also ensnared Lula. He tried to run for president again in 2018 but was jailed in March after being convicted.

Lula was released from prison after 580 days and saw Brazil's Supreme Court annul his sentence after police found messages that showed the judge who convicted him was biased. He quickly became one of former President Jair Bolsonaro's biggest critics and narrowly beat him in 2022.

Lula admitted in 2024, two years into the job, that his administration had done little to earn the support of his voters.

Since he lost the first round, Lula reorganized his campaign, appealed to young voters, put millions of Brazilians on the streets to defend democratic values and his legacy, raised fears of another Bolsonaro administration and boosted several government initiatives.

Lula also defended Brazil's sovereignty and insisted that a Bolsonaro presidency would allow the U.S. to exert control over Brazil.
