World.title: Tallinn Zoo hosts annual Pumpkin Party
World.content:
Although Halloween is still a week away, the pumpkin-loving residents of Tallinn Zoo were presented with more than four tons of donated vegetables for their annual party this weekend.

The zoo's traditional Pumpkin Party took place on Saturday, with the residents being treated to carrots, beetroots, apples, turnips, potatoes, and cabbage alongside the seasonal gourds.

The elephants were one of the most popular attractions, and they were happy to demonstrate their pumpkin-handling skills to the crowds of excited children.

"They love pumpkins the most. The elephant eats the largest quantity of pumpkins – 600 kilograms a year," said Anita Tamm, a communications specialist at Tallinn Zoo.

"Many other animals at the zoo eat them too. The pygmy marmoset eats the least pumpkin at the zoo – just 120 grams a year. Other enthusiasts include hoofed animals, rhinos, apes and monkeys, and reptiles," Tamm said.

The only animals that do not like gourds are carnivores, such as the big cats.

The pumpkin party marks the end of the zoo's vegetable collection campaign. However, anyone can still bring their garden produce to the donation box at the zoo's north gate.

World.title: Police tackle underage drinking, illegal scooters in Tartu
World.content:
Police are cracking down on banned electric scooters and minors disturbing public order in Estonia's second-biggest city, Tartu, and carried out one of their largest recent operations targeting young people on Friday.

People out and about in Tartu in southern Estonia late on Friday night may have encountered an unusually large police presence.

Dozens of law enforcement officers were focused on light electric vehicle compliance in the Annelinn and Ülenurme areas. They identified two prohibited scooters, which can travel faster than the legal limit, and two cases of people riding two to a single electric scooter.

Officers also monitored helmet use and spoke with young people.

Kristo Kooskora, a senior inspector at the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), said that the weather had worked against them this time.

"It rained to some extent throughout the evening, and we saw very few scooters, but that does not mean the problem has disappeared. Various scooter gatherings have also become popular recently, and we have been dealing with those as well. Our work in this area is not over," she told ERR's evening news show "Aktuaalne kaamera."

There was more activity in the city center after midnight.

Nearly 50 police officers patrolled Küüni tänav, which leads from Kaubamaja shopping center to the main square, in an unprecedented operation.

"The checks were conducted by officers simply moving in from both ends and checking everyone caught between the police teams until the officers eventually met in the middle," Kooskora said.

According to preliminary information, police identified nearly 30 intoxicated minors, including some who were severely intoxicated. There were also minors using e-cigarettes and cases involving suspected drug use.

Handcuffs had to be used in several cases because the young people became aggressive. Some also attempted to flee, but their attempts were unsuccessful.

Officers said the operation confirmed the problem with minors is serious. Checks should be carried out more frequently, including on weekdays.

World.title: Justice chancellor: Wild boar cannot be made to suffer when training hunting dogs
World.content:
The Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish clear legal rules for training hunting dogs using live wild boars to ensure animal welfare and legal clarity, the Chancellor of Justice's Office says.

Four years ago in May, the regional affairs minister issued a regulation on measures to prevent and control African swine fever, introducing an exemption under which the ban on keeping pigs outdoors does not apply to wild boars kept for training hunting dogs.

The Estonian Union for the Protection of Animals asked the chancellor of justice to examine whether the regulation complies with the Animal Protection Act. The organization also pointed out that the law provides no legal basis for using wild boars kept in artificial environments to train hunting dogs and that no detailed requirements have been established for such training.

Deputy Chancellor of Justice-Adviser Olari Koppel said the ban on keeping pigs outdoors is a biosecurity measure and that the minister has the authority to introduce exemptions, provided they comply with EU law and do not undermine animal disease prevention. Koppel therefore sees no reason to believe that the exemption for training hunting dogs violates these conditions.

However, he noted that the regulation only provides an exemption from the ban on keeping pigs outdoors. It does not provide a legal basis for using wild boars to train hunting dogs or authorize activities prohibited under the Animal Protection Act.

"The absence of a specific legal provision does not, however, mean that such an activity is prohibited, provided other applicable rules are followed," Koppel said, adding that it must be possible to conduct training without endangering the animal's welfare.

The law does not establish a specific legal basis or detailed requirements for training hunting dogs using live wild boars. The activity is primarily governed by the Nature Conservation Act and the general animal welfare requirements arising from it.

Under the Animal Protection Act, animals must not be subjected to suffering or pain. According to Koppel, if hunting dog training cannot be conducted without causing such harm, the executive branch cannot make the activity permissible through regulations, guidelines or administrative practices.

"In that case, only the Riigikogu can decide through legislation whether the objective of the training and the benefits it provides justify making an exception to the prohibition established by law," Koppel said.

Koppel said the lack of clarity in the regulations is a problem. To address it, the Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish the conditions for training hunting dogs in legislation rather than merely in guidelines or explanatory memorandums. This would ensure compliance with animal welfare requirements and provide legal clarity.

World.title: Isamaa party promises to close the climate ministry and create scandals committee
World.content:
Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu said at the party's council meeting in Tallinn that the campaign for Estonia's parliamentary elections has begun and is intensifying.

"Those same three parties that, under SALK's leadership, have established a politics of lies under both Kaja Kallas' and Kristen Michal's governments are now maneuvering to escape political punishment and put up camouflage nets," Reinsalu said, referring to the coalition Reform Party and Eesti 200, as well as the opposition Social Democrats.

According to the Isamaa chairman, Eesti 200 is being pressured to withdraw from the elections so that its remaining voters will instead bolster the Reform Party and the Social Democrats.

"So much for political accountability," Reinsalu said. "With the prime minister's speech to the party council, the Reform Party has launched a new wave of fearmongering and lies. This is being dressed up in a marketing campaign whose underlying message is that, yes, we have failed, but we will do better in the future."

"The Reform Party is featuring a beloved actor in its campaign, while the Social Democrats have adopted a different tactic, attempting to conceal their complicity in the Kallas-Michal government by maneuvering to put forward the secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as their candidate for prime minister. This maneuver will not succeed!" the Isamaa chairman said.

Reinsalu summed up Isamaa's political plans following the 2027 Riigikogu elections with the words "Let the citizens decide."

The party plans to give citizens the right to initiate early elections, following the Latvian model, and to establish a commission of inquiry into scandals after the elections. Lying before the commission would be a criminal offense.

In the area of defense, the party plans to close the border with Russia.

Isamaa also pledged to introduce a supplementary budget that would cut spending.

"Cost-cutting starts at the top: parliamentary and ministerial salaries, closing the Ministry of Climate and a critical review of foundations and subsidies," the party pledged.

On taxes, Isamaa promised to abolish the motor vehicle tax and reduce value-added tax on basic foodstuffs (meat, fish, milk, fruit, vegetables and bread) to 13 percent starting July 1, 2027.

The party also promised to end what it described as the harassment of businesses. "The Climate Act will be thrown in the trash. Investment certainty and a stable operating environment will be restored for the resource-based economy."

The party pledged to carry out an artificial intelligence revolution with the same boldness that Estonia once demonstrated in building its digital state. "The goal is genuine productivity growth, exports and simpler government operations. Sovereignty risks will be taken into account."

Isamaa promised to protect fundamental freedoms and repeal unnecessary restrictions.

The party also pledged to ease the burden of raising children on families and protect teachers' incomes.

In the energy sector, the party will emphasize oil shale. "The energy sector will be provided with dispatchable generation capacity, domestic resources (including oil shale) and affordable prices. Efforts to render oil shale-based energy production unviable will be halted."

The party also promised stricter requirements for the use of Estonian in public spaces, a conservative immigration policy and the restoration of regional balance.

Parliamentary elections will take place in March 2027.

World.title: Iraq, US discuss prospects to strengthen joint cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Defense Nayef al-Shammari and Chargé d’Affaires at the US Embassy in Baghdad Steven Fagin discussed approaches to strengthen cooperation between Baghdad and Washington on Sunday.

During their meeting in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, the two sides discussed bilateral ties and strategies to enhance cooperation between the two countries, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting took place after the US-led international coalition formally completed its full withdrawal and ended Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Operation Inherent Resolve—the multinational military campaign formed in 2014 to fight ISIS—officially wrapped up after a 12-year presence.

The end of the combat mission shifts the relationship to a bilateral framework focused on non-combat intelligence sharing, targeted training, and security cooperation rather than active foreign military bases.

Iraqi security forces have assumed full operational control, and the government has set goals to bring remaining armed factions under state regulation.

World.title: Drone attack targets Iranian Kurdish base in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A drone attack carried out by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted on Saturday evening a base belonging to an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

According to reports, the strike hit the headquarters and a guard post of the Komala party. The base is located in the Alana Valley within the Balisan region, northeast of Erbil.

Local security and party officials confirmed the strike caused material damage to buildings but resulted in no casualties.

This attack is a part of Tehran’s intensified campaign against Iraqi-based Iranian Kurdish opposition groups.

Since the military conflict broke out in the region on February 28, Iran has launched over 1,000 drones and missiles into Iraqi Kurdistan, claiming that these groups are directly endangering its national security and have Israeli support.

In mid-August, two explosive-laden drones launched from Iranian territory targeted Iraqi Kurdistan Prime Minister Masrour Barzani’s private office and the home of a top intelligence official.

The strikes took place in Erbil province’s Pirmam area, which is around 30 kilometers north of the capital.

Security personnel recognized the drone as an Iranian-designed “Hadid-110” kamikaze drone carrying explosive payloads.

While Tehran and Iran-backed armed groups have previously accused Iraqi Kurdistan of hosting hostile Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, the authorities in the Kurdistan region of Iraq have always denied using their territory to threaten neighboring nations.

World.title: Iraq, KBR discuss oil sector development
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and a delegation from US-based KBR discussed on Thursday developing the country’s oil and gas sectors.

KBR’s delegation headed by the company’s president for sustainable technology solutions, Jay Ibrahim, discussed prospects for joint cooperation in the oil, gas, and energy sectors, as well as leveraging the firm’s expertise to develop infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of strategic projects, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting addressed the recovery of associated gas, the development of oil fields, the enhancement of production efficiency, and the modernization of oil facilities.

The two sides also discussed leveraging KBR’s cutting-edge technology solutions to help Iraq’s oil industry grow and to make it easier to carry out key projects that meet requirements for effectiveness, quality, and financial sustainability.

The Iraqi official stressed the importance of ongoing coordination among Iraqi authorities to identify potential areas for collaboration.

Al-Mandalawi noted that the government aims to develop actionable programs related to the Majnoon oil field, the recovery of associated gas at the West Qurna field, initiatives for ammonia production, and efforts to reduce gas flaring at oil fields.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of oil at discounts up to $28
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold 10 million barrels of oil via its southern ports at a discount ranging from $25 to $28 per barrel.

Sources told Attaqa News that most of these shipments were acquired by Indian companies and that the loading took place at the southern ports a few days ago.

Iraq has been unable to sell any oil at a price higher than $100 per barrel since the outbreak of the military conflict in the Middle East, according to two more sources, even though world prices have risen to almost $117 per barrel.

A source at the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) said that Iraq has not been able to sell oil for more than $85 per barrel.

About a month ago, the company sold some shipments of light crude at around $90 per barrel.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Oil, Salim al-Rikabi, said that oil sales are still being conducted via the southern ports, and there are variable discounts in place to cover transportation and insurance costs for the purchasing companies.

Recently, Iraq’s average oil exports have risen to approximately 3.2 million barrels per day, according to statements made by Oil Minister Basim Khudair to the official news agency.

Oil shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz account for roughly 3 million barrels per day.

Due to its inadequate tanker fleet, Iraq has resorted to giving substantial discounts on its oil since the start of the conflict in the region, often as much as $32 per barrel.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of crude at steep discounts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold approximately 10 million barrels of crude oil via its southern export terminals at steep discounts ranging between $25 and $28 per barrel against prevailing international benchmarks, according to industry sources cited by the energy platform Attaqa on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

Trade sources confirmed that Indian refining companies secured the bulk of the discounted shipments, which were loaded at southern offshore terminals in recent days.

Market participants highlighted that Baghdad has been unable to market its crude above $100 per barrel since the outbreak of regional hostilities involving Iran, even as international oil benchmarks surged toward $117 per barrel during recent trading sessions amid maritime risk and escalating conflict dynamics.

Confirming the pricing constraints, an official source at the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) disclosed that recent spot transactions have struggled to clear above $85 per barrel.

The source noted that approximately one month prior, SOMO managed to offload select Basrah Light cargoes at around $90 per barrel before market pressures widened discount spreads. The steep price differentials emerge as the economic observatory “Eco Iraq” reported on Saturday that Iraq’s aggregate crude oil export revenues totaled $37.39 billion from shipments of 533.46 million barrels across the first nine months of 2026.

World.title: Iraq increases port capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has announced that the country’s ports can now handle twice as much cargo as they could in the past.

The ministry’s media director, Hussein Ahmed, said on Sunday that the current capacity of Iraqi ports exceeds 79 million tons of cargo and more than 3.6 million containers.

Ahmed noted that Iraqi ports can now handle twice the cargo volume previously recorded, which was over 40 million tons, as reported by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The Iraqi official mentioned that improvements have been made to the ports, including the construction of new roads, upgrades to existing streets leading to the ports, and the establishment of marshaling yards to alleviate internal congestion.

Iraq’s State Company for Maritime Transport (SCMT), a government-owned maritime company operating under the Iraqi Ministry of Transport, announced on Sunday the reactivation of the Iraqi Line, marked by the arrival of the vessel Basra at the port of Umm Qasr.

SCMT’s director Ahmed Jassim said that the vessel arrived at the port of Umm Qasr carrying containers from the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, signaling the reactivation of the maritime route and the resumption of its commercial voyages after a hiatus that lasted for decades.

World.title: Iraq advances Japanese loan port projects as Grand Faw reach 98%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Transport is moving to activate two major maritime infrastructure projects—a new floating dock and an integrated shipyards city—financed under the Japanese official development assistance (ODA) loan framework.

The initiative is aimed at expanding vessel repair, maintenance, and auxiliary maritime services across Iraqi ports, coinciding with significant construction milestones at the strategic Grand Faw Port in Basra.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Hussein Ahmed, Director of Media and Government Communications at the Ministry of Transport, ministry officials held technical consultations with representatives of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) loan authority.

The discussions centered on selecting construction locations and addressing civil and logistical engineering requirements for both the floating dry dock and the specialized shipyard zone to modernize national maritime support capabilities.

The operational expansion coincides with near-completion across primary infrastructure phases at the Grand Faw Port. General Director of the General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Abdullah Aati Abdullah, announced that the port’s core breakwater works have reached 100% completion.

Additionally, the submerged immersed tunnel connecting the port to Umm Qasr has achieved a 98% execution rate, while foundational infrastructure across the facility stands at 94%.

Speaking at a press conference, Abdullah stated that technical teams are preparing to transition toward superstructure and terminal installation phases under the oversight of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Transport Minister Wahab Al-Hasani.

Abdullah confirmed that preliminary operational trials are scheduled to commence in the upcoming period. He noted that while broader regional shipping traffic has felt the ripple effects of security dynamics around the Strait of Hormuz, work remains focused on expanding container handling capacity, securing yard storage, and cementing Grand Faw’s position as a regional logistics hub connecting the Gulf to Europe.

World.title: Iraq to construct six dams with Turkey and 13 rainwater harvesting barriers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources revealed plans on Sunday, October 25, 2026, to construct six new dams under the bilateral framework agreement with Turkey, while advancing technical designs and assessments for 13 additional rainwater and seasonal flood harvesting barriers across several governorates to bolster strategic water reserves, support agriculture, and combat desertification.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Ministry Spokesperson and Director General of the General Authority for Irrigation and Reclamation Projects, Khaled Shamal, technical blueprints have been finalized for three dams under the first package of the Turkish framework agreement, preparing them for on-ground execution by Turkish contractors.

The three initial structures comprise the Kharaz Dam in Al-Muthanna Governorate, the Al-Abyad Dam in Ain Al-Tamr in Karbala Governorate, and the Abu Takiya Dam in Nineveh Governorate, with site evaluations underway for an additional three dams proposed under a secondary implementation package.

In parallel with the Turkish cooperation framework, Shamal detailed progress on domestic water harvesting infrastructure designed to capture torrential flash floods and surface runoffs. Technical engineering designs are complete for five submerged check dams in Nineveh Governorate—Sheikh Bakr 1 and 2, Ain Alaq, Ain Ba’shiqa, and Ain Bahzani—with active construction already launched at two sites.

An additional eight water barriers are undergoing hydrologic surveys and final design studies, distributed across Nineveh (3 dams), Najaf (2 dams), Al-Muthanna (2 dams), and Diyala (1 dam), providing vital localized water reserves to support nomadic resettlement, pastoral communities, and regional land reclamation initiatives.

World.content:
PM Narendra Modi congratulated Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election, pledging to deepen bilateral ties and advance shared Global South priorities

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday congratulated Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election, saying India and Brazil would work together to strengthen cooperation and advance the shared priorities of the Global South.In a post on X, Modi described Lula as his "dear friend" and said he looked forward to deepening and expanding the India-Brazil Strategic Partnership."Heartiest congratulations to my dear friend, President Lula, on his remarkable re-election victory. World.title: EAM to UN: Lead during global crises, don’t just be a spectator
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Urging

to show leadership, and not remain a mere spectator to global crises, external affairs minister

said Sunday large parts of the world cannot be left out from decision-making.

At an event on UN Day, he underlined the need for long-awaited reforms.

âWe live in an imperfect world but we all continuously strive towards greater perfection. Where UN is concerned, that means recognising its shortcomings and limitations and seeking its improvement. The case for reformed multilateralism gets stronger by the day,â he said.

Jaishankar spoke about how countries with little say were paying the price for conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine.

He also underscored the threat to peace from terrorism, saying its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable.

âIt can never be justified; it can never be rationalised. Yet, it continues because not all states really display zero-tolerance. Despite history holding so many lessons, some still allow political calculations to take precedence.â

âThe world must develop sharper awareness about this common threat.





And it must come together with stronger resolve and counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations,â he added.

He said the world cannot advance half-prosperous and half-denied and in an era of intricate supply chains, of globalised markets and of common resources, this is simply a prescription for continuous instability.

International economy must be urgently de-risked and nations provided with more diversified options. Market distortions through constriction and choke-points only add to suffering. A genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue,â the minister said.

World.title: Massive fire engulfs Shiv Market near Jammu Railway Station, 35-40 shops gutted
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Around 35 to 40 shops were completely gutted after a massive fire broke out at Shiv Market, opposite

Railway Station, in the early hours of Monday. No casualties or injuries have been reported so far, while fire and emergency services teams were working to bring the blaze under control.

The cause of the fire remains unknown.

BJP MLA Vikram Randhawa said the fire reportedly began due to a short circuit in one shop before spreading rapidly to adjoining establishments. Shiv Market is a major commercial hub with shops selling dry fruits and blankets, as well as eateries and dhabas.

âThe fire started with a short circuit in one shop and spread rapidly, engulfing surrounding shops. By the time the fire brigade arrived, the entire market had been consumed by the flames.

In my estimation, about 35 to 40 shops have been completely gutted,â Randhawa said.

Describing the firefighting efforts, the MLA said the blaze had engulfed the entire market by the time the situation could be brought under control. He added that police personnel and senior officers were actively involved in managing the situation.

âAs it kept growing, by the time the whole system came under control, it had already engulfed the entire market.





Right now, our police are completely alert and actively controlling the situation. You can see that from the SHO to our SP, everyone is personally involved, even holding and dragging pipes all the way to the shops,â Randhawa said.

A shopkeeper said at least 25 to 30 shops had suffered total losses and urged the administration to provide compensation to those affected.

We pray to God to grant everyone the strength to cope with this â the loss is immense, a total loss. I also urge the administration to step in as quickly as possible and ensure that compensation is provided without delay,â the shopkeeper said.

Randhawa said the full extent of the damage could be assessed only after the situation was completely under control. He said shopkeepers were cooperating with the administration, with the deputy commissioner, SP South, DSP, SHO and their teams present at the site. Members of civil society were also helping with relief efforts.

On compensation for affected shopkeepers, Randhawa said the matter would be discussed with the administration later, describing the damage as massive.

World.title: ‘Creamy layer case in SC won’t hit seniority of CSE-2025 batch’
World.content:
File photo: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: The pendency of the case regarding the OBC creamy layer in Supreme Court will not affect the seniority of successful candidates of 2025 batch even though their service allocation and foundation course are still to be finalised, official sources said on Sunday.DoPT officials said, âThe department and all training institutes are prepared to allocate services expeditiously to CSE- 2025 candidates and commence foundation course at the earliest. Delay in commencement of the foundation course will have no bearing on the seniority, gradation or other service conditions of the candidates.âThe clarification concerns the fate of successful candidates in the wake of SCâs Rohith Nathan judgement of March 11 in which it had said âsalaryâ cannot be added to âincomeâ for defining âcreamy layerâ criteria for any category of OBC candidates, including those whose parents are employed in PSUs/banks, etc. The judgement pertained to the case of candidates from PSU background being categorised over the years as âcreamy layerâ by including âsalaryâ in the âincomeâ of their parents.

World.title: CBSE makes AI a part of formal teaching, NCERT develops module
World.content:
NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII, which CBSE has earmarked for school-based assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From spotting deepfake to questioning a chatbotâs confident but incorrect answers, artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from being an optional subject towards becoming a basic skill for CBSE schoolchildren. Taking a step towards more formal AI teaching in schools, NCERT has developed a 20-hour introductory module for Classes IX-XII, which it has earmarked for school-based assessment. Separate AI textbooks are also being prepared for students pursuing the subject at a more advanced level.The move is part of a wider effort to make AI literacy accessible to students, irrespective of whether they study computers or choose AI as an elective. The idea is to first familiarise children with how the technology works, its uses and limitations, before moving towards more structured teaching through textbooks.NCERT developed the module on computational thinking (CT) and AI in consultation with IIT Madras and IIT Jodhpur.In an April-9 circular, CBSE had announced that NCERT would provide modules for Classes IX-XII for internal assessment during the 2026-27 academic session.Under the boardâs revised scheme, CT and AI modules are compulsory for Class IX, while Class X continues under the existing scheme.A senior education ministry official said AI had become an important part of everyday activities, from education and research to content writing and career guidance. âAI tools are being used for studies, research, content writing and even career advice. Students will be taught how to use AI tools correctly and fact-check information,â they said.

World.title: EC refuses to give details of SIR software, cites ‘trade secrets, IPR'
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has declined to disclose the name and version of the software it used to identify errors and anomalies in voter rolls during SIR, saying the information was related to âcommercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual propertyâ and, thus, exempt under RTI Act.

The reply, dated Oct 16, came in response to an RTI plea.

M A Mujeeb Ayyub, a social activist from Karimpur in Telangana, in his RTI plea dated July 27 had sought information regarding the software, application, algorithm or AI platform used by EC to identify errors, anomalies or inconsistencies in electoral rolls during SIR.

In response, EC said, âNo new software has been developed or procured for the SIR exercise. Further, EROs decide on the inclusion/exclusion of an elector on the basis of facts and records.â

An EC official said software and algorithm details were conventionally not shared under RTI requests. Even EVM manufacturers like Bharat Electronics Ltd and Electronics Corporation of India Ltd have earlier refused to share EVM source codes while replying to RTI queries.

He had asked whether any AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, or automated decision support system was used in any stage of the SIR exercise.

In response to the queries, EC simply said the information sought was a âclarification which does not come under the information as per Section 2(f) of RTI Actâ.

World.title: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to government than needed, says Justice Kaul
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to the govt than necessary in matters of judicial appointments, former SC judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has said in his forthcoming book âWithout Fear Or Favourâ, and claimed that he was prevented from hearing petitions for re-examination of the validity of provisions of PMLA.

Kaul also claimed Justice Chandrachud had, allegedly under pressure from govt, withdrawn a case from him in which a bench headed by him had questioned delays in implementation of the SC collegiumâs resolutions for appointment of judges. This, he said, âtroubled him the mostâ as the case was assigned years ago and was taken away all of a sudden.

Reacting to the claims, Justice Chandrachud said, âThere was never even a dissent by any member of the collegium over any name during discussions for appointments to the SC.â

âDYC asked if he should call government on collegium picksâ

Sources said resolutions passed by the collegium for appointments to the SC during Justice Chandrachudâs tenure were unanimous and signed by all members of the collegium without recording a single dissent.

In this case, a bench of Justices Kaul and Sudhanshu Dhulia had pulled up govt for its alleged pick-and-choose policy in clearing names sent by the collegium and had on Nov 20, 2023, asked why Centre was not transferring four judges from Gujarat HC and not appointing two Sikh lawyers for Punjab and Haryana HC as recommended by the collegium.





The case was thereafter taken away from his bench and it has not been listed in the last three years.

In an interview to Karan Thapar for The Wire, Justice Kaul claimed the former CJI took him aside during a collegium meeting and asked whether he should telephone govt to ascertain its views on the proposed appointments. Justice Kaul said pre-approval from govt before discussions in the collegium was a matter of concern.

âThis has unfortunately become a practice of names being discussed, and some kind of previous discussion with govt. That used to happen. It has been happening, I think before CJI Chandrachud and after. That is why it troubles me,â he said, adding that there was nothing wrong in holding consultations with govt, but it should happen only after the collegiumâs decision and not before.

Asked whether Justice Chandrachud was too deferential to govt, Justice Kaul said, âThere is a judicial side and there is an administrative side of the Chief Justice of India.

I wouldnât be concerned with the judicial side. I believe he had both the intellectual heft and the capacity and hard work to do so. But in consultations with govt and collaboration, I felt he was more deferential than necessary to carry it forward.

â

Justice Kaul said he tried to discourage Justice Chandrachud from discussing everything with govt beforehand as it could create its own problems. Asked whether Justice Chandrachud failed to live up to the high expectations from him, Justice Kaul said, âI would say that expectations were higher from him.â

TOI has reported how Justice Kaul had vigorously and successfully pushed many names for judgeship as part of the SC and HC collegiums and three of his proposals had met with resistance from other members of the panel. The then CJI had tactically refrained from holding collegium meetings to avoid embarrassing situations.

In reply to the TOI article, Justice Kaul had sent a rejoinder and said, âThere was no question of insistence of appointment of those suggested by me and all recommendations have been made by consensus. That other collegium members had reservations and I pushed the names, thus, seem to be a flight of your imagination.â

World.title: How far can a sitting judge speak outside the courtroom?
World.content:
In July 2018, Justice Ranjan Gogoi, months before becoming Chief Justice of India, said democracy sometimes needed “noisy judges”, alongside independent journalists. Eight years later, that judicial voice has become contentious.

On October 4, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, delivering the valedictory address at a moot court competition at NALSAR University of Law, said the right to vote was constitutional and integral to the basic structure. A process disenfranchising millions, he said, would be intrinsically arbitrary and violate Articles 14 and 326; Article 326 “cannot be tinkered with”, and “no court can condone” mass disenfranchisement. Citing Section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, he stressed the need for notice and a hearing before deletion, except in the case of death.

Former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai objected that “judicial propriety” did not permit a sitting judge to comment on a sub judice matter. Former Delhi High Court judges S.N. Dhingra and R.S. Sodhi expressed similar concerns, with Justice Sodhi stressing the statutory framework governing voting rights.

The day after Justice Bhuyan spoke, Justice Vikram Nath, the senior-most puisne judge in the Supreme Court, delivered a lecture in Delhi. “Impartiality and indifference are not the same thing,” he said. A judge must be impartial, but need not be insensible to the human consequences of law, he observed. Where is the line between an engaged judge and one who has said too much?

What does the Indian code require?

The starting point is the Restatement of Values of Judicial Life, adopted by the Full Court of the Supreme Court on May 7, 1997. Clause 8 says a judge shall neither enter public debate nor express views on political matters “or on matters that are pending or are likely to arise for judicial determination”. Clause 1 requires conduct sustaining public faith in judicial impartiality. The Restatement carries no sanction of its own, but has been reproduced and relied upon in judicial decisions.

When Justice Bhuyan addressed NALSAR, litigation arising from the West Bengal SIR remained before the Supreme Court. More than 22 lakh deleted voters had appealed for restoration, the Election Commission of India told the court, and related matters were due on October 5. Justice Bhuyan neither named the SIR nor sat on those Benches.

But did Justice Bhuyan state something the court had not already held?

Here the criticism requires qualification. On May 27, 2026, a Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant upheldthe Bihar SIR in Association for Democratic Reforms v Election Commission of India. The court described the right to vote as constitutional, though neither absolute nor unregulated, and said Articles 325 and 326 require inclusion of eligible electors and exclusion of ineligible persons. Rule 21A of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, it added, requires notice, inquiry, hearing and a reasoned determination before deletion.

Justice Bhuyan was therefore on established ground in describing voting as constitutional and stressing a hearing before deletion. The more debatable part was his proposition that a process disenfranchising millions would be intrinsically arbitrary and that no court could condone it. Yet the proposition was conditional and did not decide whether a particular SIR produces that result. The issue turns on how closely those words approached an answer to a live controversy.

Must judges remain silent on questions of public importance?

Comparative standards draw a more calibrated boundary. The commentary on the Bangalore Principles of Judicial Conduct recognises judicial freedom of expression on legal education, judicial independence and court administration. Principle 2.4 restrains comment that might reasonably affect a proceeding before, or capable of coming before, the judge, while Principle 4.11 allows judges to write, lecture and teach on law and the administration of justice.

The U.S. Supreme Court’s 2023 Code of Conduct permits Justices to speak, write, lecture and teach, but asks them to refrain from commenting on the merits of a pending or impending matter. For scholarly or educational purposes, they may describe the issues involved. The distinction is between explaining an issue and appearing to answer it.

Justice Antonin Scalia demonstrated the risk in 2003 when he criticised a lower-court ruling on the Pledge of Allegiance. The litigant sought his recusal, and Scalia took no part when the case reached the U.S. Supreme Court, although the Court gave no reason. In Britain, Lady Hale outlined competing arguments in the pending Brexit litigation in 2016, then stopped: “the case is destined for our Court, so I must say no more”. She later sat in Miller. Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg crossed a different boundary by criticising presidential candidate Donald Trump, then described her comments as “ill-advised”.

Indian practice also counsels against treating every public intervention as improper. At NALSAR in March 2024, Justice B.V. Nagarathna criticised Governors who withheld assent to Bills while related disputes were before the Court. Scholars Jasmin Moran and Christopher W. Schmidt recognise apparent-bias concerns without treating judicial silence as the answer.

Is Justice Bhuyan exceptionally outspoken?

Justice Bhuyan is an unusually visible judicial speaker. A conservative open-source audit found at least 25 public-facing engagements since he joined the Supreme Court on July 14, 2023. It covered institutional archives, Bar events and contemporaneous reports, excluding courtroom remarks, internal programmes and events where only scheduled participation could be established. At least nine addresses generated news reports, seven in 2026. The figure is a minimum.

In 2026, his speeches became more pointed. He questioned executive influence in judicial transfers, cited low conviction rates while discussing overuse of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, criticised restrictive bail conditions, sought greater transparency in collegium decisions and criticised frivolous prosecutions arising from food choices, poems, protests and slogans. Most generated headlines without a comparable propriety controversy.

Two episodes stand out. After Justice Bhuyan criticised the Supreme Court’s 2024 Delhi Metro arbitration ruling, retired Justice Indu Malhotra called the remarks an “indiscretion”. Former Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, by contrast, defended another July speech on dissent and criminalisation, while cautioning that sitting judges must exercise restraint because similar issues may later come before them. Their disagreement shows why controversy alone is a poor test.

Does his High Court record bear on this?

Justice Bhuyan’s Gauhati High Court record cautions against treating speeches as predictors of outcomes. In Monowara Bewa v Union of India (2017), his Bench upheld a Foreigners Tribunal finding and rejected a Gaon Panchayat Secretary’s certificate as an NRC linkage document. The Supreme Court later set aside that broader conclusion in Rupajan Begum v Union of India. In Sirajul Hoque v State of Assam (2019), it also reversed a 2017 decision of his Bench where variations in a family name had contributed to rejection of a citizenship claim. Yet in Md Anuwar Hussain v Union of India (2014), Justice Bhuyan set aside a Foreigners Tribunal order for lack of sound logic and cogent reasons, remanded the case and ordered the petitioner’s release from detention to argue it afresh. His record contains strict and claimant-protective strands. Extrajudicial language about citizenship, liberty or voting cannot safely predict how he would decide a properly argued case.

So, are Justice Bhuyan’s critics correct?

India’s Restatement uses broader language than the U.S. code. His propositions that voting is constitutional and deletion requires procedural safeguards largely track existing doctrine. The sentence that “no court can condone” mass disenfranchisement comes closer to stating a constitutional conclusion, although it was conditional and did not decide whether the SIR produces that result.

The criticism becomes weaker when enlarged into a claim that sitting judges should avoid public discussion of constitutional law, civil liberties, judicial appointments or court administration. Indian judges have long occupied that space, and international standards recognise its value. If a case presenting the precise issue on which Justice Bhuyan spoke were assigned to him, the Scalia episode shows why recusal could become a question.

Justice Gogoi’s “noisy judge” and Justice Nath’s formulation that impartiality need not mean indifference can coexist. The relevant measures are the subject of the speech, the specificity of the conclusion and its proximity to adjudication. Judicial speech can enrich constitutional conversation, but the lecture hall should not sound like a courtroom deciding a case before the parties are heard.

(V. Venkatesan is Contributing Editor at Supreme Court Observer. Views expressed are personal)

World.title: Stock markets decline in early trade; Sensex drops over 500 points
World.content:
Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty fell in early trade on Monday (October 26, 2026) amid elevated crude oil prices due to geopolitical uncertainties and caution ahead of the U.S Federal Reserve's policy decision later this week.

The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 536.30 points to 72,583.86 in early trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty fell 200.10 points to 22,402.80.

From the 30 Sensex firms, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance, Hindustan Unilever, Infosys, Bajaj Finserv and Reliance Industries were among the major laggards.

Kotak Mahindra Bank, Sun Pharma, Adani Ports and Axis Bank were the winners.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded 2.14% lower at $114.2 per barrel.

In Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi, Japan's 225 index and Shanghai's SSE Composite index quoted lower, while Hang Seng index traded in positive territory.

The U.S markets ended lower on Friday (October 23, 2026).

"Indian equities are likely to remain under pressure as elevated crude oil prices, escalating geopolitical tensions and uncertainty over the U.S Federal Reserve's policy outlook weigh on investor sentiment. The continuing stand-off in the Middle East, with the risk of further escalation, remains a key concern for domestic markets," Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, an online trading and wealth-tech firm, said.

The Federal Reserve's October 27–28 policy meeting will be a key event for global markets this week, he said.

"Although the central bank is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, investors will look for signals on the future policy path. Any hawkish shift in tone could keep U.S Treasury yields elevated, strengthen the dollar and constrain foreign portfolio flows into emerging markets. Conversely, a more measured outlook could offer some relief to risk assets," Mr. Ponmudi added.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹887.65 crore on Friday (October 23, 2026), according to exchange data.

On Friday (October 23, 2026), the Sensex settled at 73,123.83, down 125.56 points, or 0.17%. The Nifty dropped 87.65 points, or 0.39%, to close at 22,600.

World.title: An afternoon at artist Paul Fernandes’ gallery in Bengaluru
World.content:
As you walk into aPaulogy Gallery in Bengaluru, framed cartoons and paintings cover every wall. . Nestled in the quiet neighbourhood of Richards Town, artworks in this gallery are based on various key locations and landmarks in the city including MG Road, Cubbon Park, and India Coffee House.

Paul Fernandes was born in Bengaluru 68 years ago, and grew up watching the city evolve through his artistic lens. “This is a city I have always been very involved with at different levels. From a youngster who grew up in the old Bengaluru to today when things are quite different.” His water paint cartoons are a way to remember the old Bengaluru.

“There is Kempegowda, who founded Bengaluru. . The Mughals and the Marathas came here, followed by Tipu Sultan and Hyder Ali. The city also lived through 200 years of British rule. After Independence, a great number of people came here to work, and many of them have left much for us to appreciate,” says Paul, recalling the rich history of the city.

His journey as an artist has been “long and very pleasurable.” For Paul, it has been a process of learning in many different ways, “from not knowing what you’re going to do next to knowing what to do, it’s a beautiful journey of discovery.” He says even after 50 years of being an artist, he is still discovering interesting parts of drawing.

He developed his own style of painting with inspiration from the famed cartoonists such as Mario Miranda and RK Laxman. “The great Mario Miranda spent a lot of time drawing Goa, Mumbai, and many great cities across the world. He approached the subject with a happy light-heartedness, which is exactly what I’ve tried to do. And of course there’s RK Laxman who inspired millions including myself.”

In his gallery, a huge poster titled ‘One fine day on MG Road’ draws the eye. . With fine detailing and chaotic traffic spread across the canvas, it represents MG Road in 1993.

“I had an office there, right next to the Plaza Theatre. Now, there’s no Plaza left. Every few hours we’d go across the road and sit on a bench to take a break. This is what you saw when you looked out. There were no flyovers or metro lines, just a busy stream of people going up and down the road.”

To him the city has evolved like everything does, Paul believes that nothing is permanent and everything has to change. “Even when you look around the city, you’ll find the things that were believed to be permanent, have changed.” He mentions the Lal Bagh rock and the recent proposals to alter it. “There are monuments and structures that are centuries old, which are also changing.”

When asked if there is a particular aspect of the city that makes him nostalgic, he says “There are many, every road has a beautiful memory. There are no two roads in Bengaluru that are similar. Every road has its character, its beauty and it invites a memory from the past.”

Some of his paintings and cartoons are based on Mumbai. “I used to go there thrice a year to meet my wife. Everything about the city fascinated me, it was a busy buzzing place.” He has also painted series on Goa, Mangalore and Kerala.

“If you’re going to enjoy your work, you must let your work decide the pace of your life. Don’t go faster than your work and don’t speed it up. Art has to be slow and it has to be enjoyed and discovered. Every time you draw something, you are going to learn and from that learning you’ll make another drawing, which is more evolved than the last” Small things make up the big pictures for Paul.

aPaulogy Gallery at Richards Town is open on Monday to Saturday from 10am to 7:30pm. For more details visit apaulogy.com

World.title: Lula wins a record fourth presidential term as Brazil defeats far-right, defies Trump and Meta
World.content:
In an election campaign that may be recorded in history for countering far-right tactics, defying foreign interference and social media manipulation, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic fourth presidential term, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro of Liberal Party (PL) in Brazil’s runoff elections on Sunday (October 25, 2026). Mr. Lula secured 64 million votes, the highest total ever recorded in a Brazilian presidential election, surpassing his own record of 60 million votes he received in 2022. Declaring a “defeat for lies and denialism”, he pledged to govern for all Brazilians and protect the country’s sovereignty. “Brazil is nobody’s backyard,” Mr. Lula declared at a midnight rally, sending a clear message to U.S. president Donald Trump as he addressed hundreds of thousands of supporters gathered along São Paulo’s iconic Avenida Paulista.

In an emotional speech, Mr. Lula thanked women and older voters for their support and praised the mobilisation of young people on the streets and on social media. “People went out to vote because we managed to convince them that their votes were extremely important to safeguarding democracy in the country,” he said. He also said he had learned many lessons from the election and promised to change his approach to governing, ensure greater public participation in government decisions and give digital communication a more prominent role during his fourth term. “The future begins today, and its name is youth. I salute the women who made all the difference. I salute the older people who made sacrifices and made their way to the polling stations to vote,” he said.

Mr. Lula secured an unprecedented comeback in the election. He trailed in the first round, receiving 45.16% of valid votes against 47.03% for Mr. Flávio. As the prospect of a Bolsonaro presidency caused a major concern among the young, especially about public education, healthcare and transport, millions of people joined weekly rallies across the country, pledging support for Mr. Lula and demanding protection of public services. On Sunday (October 25, 2026), Mr. Lula told his young supporters that their voices have been heard. “We will make increasing investment in in the Unified Health System, develop a national artificial intelligence system, continue to expand public universities and support the digital and creative economies,” Mr. Lula told his supporters with massive rounds of applause.

The turnaround after the first round of election on October 4 was not only historic but also dramatic. Mr. Lula’s official campaign team almost took a back seat as millions of people came out on streets and joined the social media campaign. The online mobilisation was led by federal deputy André Janones, who is not a member of the Workers Party but created a WhatsApp channel called “Lula’s Army”, where he issued “missions” to more than 10 million subscribers every day. The campaign focused its efforts on persuading undecided voters and those who had abstained in the first round. Mr. Lula’s young supporters, many of them teenagers, went on door-to-door campaigns to win over voters who had backed other candidates in the first round. On Sunday (October 25, 2026), abstention rates fell to their lowest levels since 2002.

With most opinion polls predicting a neck-to-neck race and some even giving an edge to Mr. Flavio till a few days back, the Workers’ Party shifted its messaging from a comparison of the candidates’ personal records to a forward-looking agenda centred on concrete promises. Following the first-round results, Mr. Lula changed his campaign team’s leadership and began announcing measures such as an increase in direct cash transfer benefits, a new debt-relief programme, a package of benefits for small entrepreneurs and a pledge to make public transport free on weekends.

Even as Mr. Lula made these promises to the electorate, his campaign faced a big challenge: Big Tech firms – from Meta to X and Google – openly supported Mr. Flavio’s campaign while suppressing advertising by Mr. Lula’s team. In his speech on Sunday (October 25, 2026), Mr. Lula said he had to overcome “interference” by digital platforms and pledged to regulate big tech companies in Brazil. “This election was one in which we had to overcome interference coming from outside and through digital platforms. We will have to regulate them,” Mr. Lula said. On October 16 after an expose in the Brazilian media, Meta had admitted that its artificial intelligence tool had blocked the generation of campaign material supporting Mr. Lula while allowing the same technology to be used by the Flávio campaign.

With this historic mobilisation of people and a record victory, Mr. Lula also seems to have defeated Mr. Trump, who has repeatedly made clear that his preferred candidate in the race was Mr. Flávio. Now, Mr. Lula’s victory has applied brakes on the growing wave of right-wing leaders in the region. But Mr. Trump is not in a mood to throw in the towel. On Sunday (October 25, 2026) night, Mr. Trump questioned Mr. Lula’s victory, comparing it to the 2020 U.S. election which he lost to Joe Biden and alleged that Brazil had followed the “Joe Biden playbook.”

“Bolsonaro had a big lead in the first round and was the clear favourite to win the second. But the communists never give up power once they get it,” Mr. Trump said, echoing the far-right’s strategy of questioning election results which do not go in their favour.

Mr. Flávio was singing the same tune on Sunday (October 25, 2026) night as he refused to accept the election result, announcing that he would seek the annulment of the election. He accused the Federal Supreme Federal of “changing the rules midway” after a judge ordered voting across the country to be extended until 7 p.m. when Mr. Lula complained about many right-wing mayors curtailing the bus services in the poor areas many cities. “It is impossible to recognise the election result in the context in which these things happened,” Mr. Flavio said, adding that his legal team would challenge the outcome.

It is a complete misreading of the mood in Brazil. After Mr. Lula finished his speech on Sunday (October 25, 2026) night, the crowd broke into a rendition of Brazil’s national independence song, sending a message to the far-right, Mr. Trump and Meta.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi heads to U.P.’s Sultanpur for verdict in defamation case
World.content:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is set to appear before a special MP-MLA court in Sultanpur, which is set to pronounce its verdict in a defamation case against him on Monday (October 26, 2026).

Mr. Gandhi arrived at Lucknow's Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport this morning. Hundreds of Congress workers and local party leaders gathered at the airport to welcome the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Raebareli MP.

Mr. Gandhi did not speak to reporters before leaving for Sultanpur.

Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ told PTI Videos, "We have complete faith in the judiciary. Rahul Gandhi ji is going to Sultanpur for that case only."

Security arrangements have been strengthened in Sultanpur, particularly around the court complex, in view of the proceedings, police officials said.

The case relates to alleged objectionable remarks made by Mr. Gandhi against then BJP president Amit Shah at a rally in Bengaluru ahead of the 2018 Karnataka Assembly elections.

Local BJP politician Vijay Mishra, a former chairman of the District Cooperative Bank in Sultanpur, filed the defamation complaint against Gandhi on August 4, 2018.

Mr. Gandhi appeared before the court in 2023 and secured bail. The court had earlier fixed October 13 for pronouncing its verdict, which was subsequently scheduled for October 26.

World.title: Massive fire near Jammu Railway Station guts around 40 shops in market
World.content:
A massive fire ripped through a market near the Jammu Railway Station, gutting around 40 shops and reducing a bustling commercial stretch to rubble, officials said on Monday (October 26, 2026).

No casualties have been reported in the blaze, which broke out at around 10.30 p.m. in Shiv Market on Sunday (October 25, 2026).

The blaze continued to rage for nearly five hours, leaving behind a trail of destruction and dealing a major blow to shopkeepers whose livelihoods depended on the market.

The officials said around 40 shops, mostly dealing in food supplies, dry fruits, and blankets, were gutted in the devastating fire.

Preliminary investigations suggested that a short circuit in one of the shops triggered the blaze, which spread rapidly across the market, fuelled by winds, they said.

The narrow approach to the market posed a major challenge for firefighters, making it difficult to reach the affected shops directly, the officials said.

They said firefighting teams had to approach the blaze from the rear side of the market to tackle the flames and prevent the fire from spreading further.

Despite sustained efforts by the emergency services, the fire continued to consume merchandise and shop structures for hours before it was finally brought under control at around 3.15 a.m.

World.title: Panel formed to probe spurious liquor death claims in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas; report in 15 days
World.content:
The Madhya Pradesh Government has constituted a five-member committee to investigate claims that at least 10 persons died after consuming spurious liquor in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas district, officials said on Sunday (October 25, 2026).

The panel will submit its report within 15 days, they said.

Ujjain divisional Commissioner constituted the committee after conflicting claims over the deaths.

Some villagers have claimed that at least 10 persons died after consuming spurious liquor in Dewas district between September 27 and October 16.

The district administration had earlier dismissed the claims as false and misleading. It later said viscera samples of two deceased persons have been sent to a forensic science laboratory (FSL) for examination. The cause of death would become clear after the reports are received, it added.

The administration said 10 persons died in Chandana village between October 1 and 15, but denied that any of the deaths was caused by spurious liquor. It attributed the deaths to old age, common illnesses, brain haemorrhage and "deterioration of health due to excessive alcohol consumption".

Ujjain Additional District Magistrate Pratham Kaushik will head the probe committee, which includes Mandsaur Additional Superintendent of Police Ramsanehi Mishra, Ratlam Sub-Divisional Police Officer Lekhraj Meena, Ujjain divisional flying squad Deputy Excise Commissioner Harshvardhan Rai and Regional Director of Public Health and Medical Education Dr Deepak Kumar Pippal.

The panel will conduct a detailed and impartial inquiry into the causes and circumstances of the deaths, along with the related technical and administrative aspects, and submit a factual report within 15 days, according to the Ujjain divisional Commissioner's order.

Madhya Pradesh Congress president Jitu Patwari has claimed that 22 persons died after consuming spurious liquor in Chandana, Binjana and adjoining areas over the past month, while at least 40 people suffered damage to their eyesight.

The Opposition party leader has accused the administration of concealing the deaths and shielding the "liquor mafia".

World.title: Hyderabad’s Osmania General Hospital strengthens gender-affirming surgical care for transgender people
World.content:
The Osmania General Hospital (OGH) in Hyderabad has established a dedicated gender-affirming surgery service in the government healthcare sector in Telangana, marking a step towards improving access to specialised healthcare for transgender persons.

The Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery has introduced the service through a multidisciplinary team of specialists from plastic surgery, anaesthesiology, endocrinology, urology, gynaecology and psychiatry, along with nursing staff and other healthcare professionals. The initiative has been developed over the past eight months, said doctors.

The team has successfully performed several procedures for transgender people, including frontal bossing reduction, autologous fat grafting for breast augmentation, breast augmentation using implants, penile inversion vaginoplasty and bilateral nipple-areola complex-sparing mastectomy. Breast implants have also been facilitated through letters of credit under the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund (CMRF).

The initiative aims to provide safe, accessible and affordable gender-affirming surgical care within the public healthcare system, particularly for individuals who face financial and logistical barriers to accessing specialised procedures.

The service follows a multidisciplinary approach, with emphasis on patient evaluation, individualised surgical planning, perioperative care and post-operative follow-up. The hospital has also received support from the Queer Badhu Parents Association, whose president, Mukunda Mala, helped facilitate the renovation of a three-bed ward for transgender patients recovering from surgery, said Dr P. Lakshmi, Professor and Head of Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery.

The hospital plans to expand the range of gender-affirming procedures offered and further strengthen the multidisciplinary programme. The initiative is expected to help more transgender people access specialised surgical care through the government healthcare system while promoting inclusive, dignified and comprehensive healthcare.

World.title: Govt moves to establish new ‘umbrella’ privatisation entity
World.content:
• Proposed legislation aims to merge Public-Private Partnership Authority and Privatisation Commission

• Seeks to provide immunity to incumbent, former chairmen, secretaries and other officials

ISLAMABAD: The government has introduced a bill in the National Assembly, for the establishment of a Privatisation and Public-Private Part­nership Commission (PPPPC), by merging the existing Public-Private Partnership Authority (P3A) and Privatisation Commission, to prevent duplication of institutional functions and processes.

The proposed law that seeks amendments to both legal instruments — the Privatisation Commission Ordinance 2000 and Public Private Partnership Authority Act 2017 — also provides legal and investigation immunity to the current and all former chairmen, secretaries, board members, officials and consultants from any act of omission or commission in good faith and in personal capacity and commits public funds to contest any such cases.

The all-powerful commission will be led by the incumbent chairman Muhammad Ali and will comprise a majority of members from the private sector, including two women directors. It will collectively administer four public funds — privatisation fund, public contributory fund, viability gap fund and PPP project development funds — created through allocation in the federal budget, receipts from international lenders, income from investments or any other source.

The government claims that the PC Ordinance dealt with privatisation of SOEs under the government policy while P3A Act governed a separate body. Both frameworks were concerned with mobilising private sector capital and expertise in relation to public assets, infrastructure and services and their administration through two separate institutions entailed duplication of institutional functions and processes.

Therefore, the government’s pol­icy decision was needed for establishing a single institutional framework and mechanism for carrying out privatisation and public private partnership transactions in an efficient manner. For this, it seeks to reconstitute the Privatisation Commission as the Privatisation and Public-Private Partnership Commission, to repeal the Public Private Partnership Authority Act 2017 and dissolve the P3A.

The bill provides for the reconstitution of the board with a majority of independent members, including members with public private partnership experience and at least two women, fixed terms of office and clear grounds for disqualification and removal. The bill also empowers the proposed reconstituted commission to conduct functions of advising on, appraising, structuring, facilitating and monitoring public private partnership projects and the establishment of the viability gap fund, the PPP project development facility, and the public contribution fund.

The draft claims that it provides a comprehensive legal framework for public private partnerships, including the contractual framework for PPP agreements, a federal PPP pipeline, the approval process, the risk management unit and PPP transaction execution committees. It also empowers the commission to set up PPP nodes within government agencies, settlement of disputes and an alternative process for below-threshold projects.

The proposed law enables the commission to utilise public contribution fund to meet any government obligations with respect to PPP projects, including land acquisition, site handover, right of way and any such other enabling actions as may be required in connection with the project. All these funds would be non-lapsable.

The PPP agreement between the public and private parties shall be a public document and any interested person shall be entitled to obtain its copy subject to applicable laws, and the government or the commission or the government agency shall not be held liable for any claim of the private party for a risk which is not specified in the PPP agreement. All existing contracts signed by P3A would stand transferred to the new commission without any disadvantage to the private parties.

The proposed law empowers the commission to require in writing from any government agency to submit a complete list of its existing, proposed and planned projects, including projects under consideration or development, whether or not identified as PPP projects within fifteen days. The agencies shall be obligated to comply with such a requirement with full accuracy and completeness. Where a government agency fails to comply with any such requirement, the PC chairman may refer the matter to the ministry or division concerned for compliance.

There will be a committee to review potential PPP projects proposed for inclusion in the federal PPP pipeline and shall provide its recommendations, which shall be placed before the board for consideration and decision.

All officers, consultants, advisers, auditors, employees and other staff of the P3A shall upon the dissolution of the P3A be retained by the commission for a period of six months or until the expiration of their respective contracts, whichever is earlier, on terms and conditions not less favourable than those applicable to them immediately before the dissolution.
