In today’s AFL briefing: Max Gawn backs brutal list calls at Melbourne ahead of his own contract talks

Butters’ return to Adelaide highlights Gather Round program

Dean Solomon to join Damien Hardwick at Gold Coast Butters game to be a focus of Gather Round Greg Dundas Zak Butters will be bracing a fiery reception when he returns to Adelaide to play against the Power for the first time when the Western Bulldogs help draw a curtain on next year’s Gather Round. Look away, Port fans: Zak Butters in Western Bulldogs colours. Getty Images



The clash between Port Adelaide and Butters’ new club is the ninth game of the Gather Round fixture released by the AFL on Monday, and even has South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas – an avid Power fan – fired up. Revered at the Power after three best and fairest awards and three All-Australian guernseys from 156 games, Butters officially became a Bulldog earlier this month, signing the richest contract in AFL history. He stands to earn at least $17 million over the next nine years after crossing to the Dogs as a restricted free agent, aided by a complex side deal that convinced Port not to match the deal. Raised near Bacchus Marsh as a Bulldogs supporter, Butters’ future was the subject of conjecture throughout the 2026 season, with the Dogs pipping Geelong for his coveted signature.



It’s not yet clear, how Port’s passionate fan base will respond to Butters, but the AFL have capitalised on the appeal of his clash with his former teammates by making it a marquee match of Gather Round. It is one of three blockbuster games the league has scheduled at the Adelaide Oval to underpin the South Australian-based round - round four of the 2027 season. The festivities will open on Thursday April 8, with the Crows seeking revenge for their semi-final loss in 2026 to the Brisbane Lions, and close four days later with Butters facing his former side. Loading In between, the league has scheduled a humdinger of a Saturday-night match between leading premiership fancies Fremantle and Hawthorn.



There are two other games scheduled at the Adelaide Oval across the weekend – Sydney v Collingwood on the Friday night and an early Saturday game between Carlton and Melbourne, who met in a wildcard final in 2026. Gold Coast, GWS, Geelong and St Kilda are the four teams heading to the Barossa for their Gather Round games, while Richmond, West Coast, Essendon and North Melbourne are bound for Norwood Oval. Related Article Analysis

AFL 2026 Contending, rebuilding or stuck in limbo: What AFL trade period says about your team’s flag hopes Malinauskas – an avid Power fan – was quick to spruik the Gather Round program, which coincides with the Easter school holidays, and the inclusion of a players’ parade on the Friday. “The blockbuster weekend of footy will be boosted with the inaugural Players Parade on Friday, allowing fans to see their heroes from all 18 clubs in one spot,” he said.



“Personally, I’m looking forward to being at a packed Adelaide Oval to see Zak Butters take on his former teammates.” Gawn applauds ‘brutal’ Melbourne list calls Jon Pierik Melbourne captain Max Gawn has applauded the club’s “brutal” list-management calls which led to the departure of favourite son Jack Viney, but hopes he can finish his career as a one-club player. Melbourne captain Max Gawn cycles alongside Tour de France champion Cadel Evans ahead of the Great Ocean Road race. AAPIMAGE



Gawn is off contract in 2027, but at 33 is still playing some of the best football of his career, which he attributes, in part, to his punishing off-season cycling regime. The 2021 premiership skipper won All-Australian selection for the ninth time in 2026, and is keen to remain a Demon for life when contract discussions open. However, he understands the business of football, having watched his fellow premiership on-ball brigade of Clayton Oliver, Christian Petracca and Viney, along with key defender Steven May, depart over the past two seasons. “I’m pretty keen in Melbourne. I understand ‘Vines’ would have said the same thing 12 months ago. So, I’ve just applauded ‘Lamby’ [list boss Tim Lamb] and King [coach Steven King], and if I’m the one that has to move on next year, and I still think there’s footy ahead of me, then that conversation will come, but right now, it does look like my finish will be with the Demons,” Gawn said on Monday. Kicking on: Melbourne skipper Max Gawn is off contract in 2027, and wants to finish his career as a one-club player. Getty Images However, speaking as an ambassador at the launch of the Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Race, Gawn hinted he would be open to offers, should negotiations with the Demons not go as planned, and if new club Tasmania came calling.





“I applaud the list management team; they’ve made some brutal decisions,” Gawn said. “None more brutal than probably Jack this year, but you’ve seen with what we’re able to do this year, with most people tipping us [to finish] bottom four, and we come out and play some pretty good footy.” Gawn said he was delighted that Essendon and the Eagles showed interest in Viney, his former co-captain. Fresh start: Ex-Melbourne midfielder Jack Viney will continue his career with West Coast after being traded to the Eagles on the final day of the trade period. Getty Images “I went from a little bit of surprise [at his departure], and then I went a little bit of other clubs were making him feel generally loved,” Gawn said.



“And now, he’s like, once it got to a point where West Coast were interested, he’s like: ‘I want to get there so bad, I want to rejuvenate my career, I want to take my family over there’. So I’m really excited for him.” Gawn said the Demons had needed a substantial make-over, having seen how quickly Geelong transformed, even after winning the 2022 premiership. Only nine Demons players now remain from the 2021 premiership team. “I sat there and looked at that [2022 Geelong] team, I was like, OK, and then they play in the grand final three years later, and they had 10 or 15 new players in that team. And, at the same time, Melbourne was still running the round with the ’21 premiership team,” Gawn said. Related Article Live

AFLW AFLW ladder with one round to play; ‘Difficult decision’: Dons sack inaugural coach “It’s like, well, we haven’t changed or adapted or moved on. We’re still trying to win it again with the ’21 premiership team, and Geelong, at that very same time, had changed over 15 players. It’s like, OK, this is what’s needed in a way to stay in the modern game.”



A cycling enthusiast who now has his own podcast on the sport, Gawn’s pre-season training program has so far included “Everesting” South Australia’s exhausting Willunga Hill, riding the 3.7km climb 39.5 times in 21 hours, and another punishing ride on the island of Phuket in Thailand. He will soon head to Patagonia, at the southern end of South America, to ride in the wilderness. This program will also include running. Solomon gets Gold Coast gig After coaching Essendon through the second half of 2026, Dean Solomon will return to Gold Coast as an assistant coach to Damien Hardwick. Dean Solomon as coach of Essendon. Getty Images Solomon, now 46, was on the coaching staff at the Suns from the club’s inception in the AFL in 2011 to 2020, even serving three games as interim coach following the departure of Rodney Eade in 2017.



Solomon later joined the board at Essendon – the club where he made his name as a player and was part of the 2000 premiership team – but relinquished that position a year ago to return to a hands-on coaching role. He started the 2026 season as an assistant to Brad Scott, and became the club’s stop-gap coach when Scott was sacked mid-season. Despite holding some ambition to become the senior coach permanently, Solomon’s hopes were dented by a record of just one win from his 12 games in charge. After hiring Solomon’s former teammate Mark McVeigh as senior coach for 2027, Essendon announced last month that Solomon had declined their offer of another role in the football department and would return to live in NSW with his wife and children. On Monday, the Suns spruiked Solomon’s recruitment as a homecoming. “Dean played a significant role across our club’s first decade in the competition, and his expertise and industry experience will be instrumental in helping us take steps forward in the years ahead,” Gold Coast’s general manager of football Craig Cameron said.



Solomon said the Suns job aligned with his family circumstances . Related Article AFL 2026 ‘An A-plus character’: The prospect from a family of Essendon diehards who could kickstart the Dons “The opportunity to return to the Gold Coast Suns to work alongside and learn from Damien Hardwick and an experienced group of coaches is one I’m really excited by,” Solomon said. “The potential of the list that has been assembled is incredibly inviting and I see it as an exciting time to be part of the Suns. “The Gold Coast and Northern New South Wales has been home for my family and I for over 16 years now, so to be able to be with my wife and kids again and still coach at the highest level at a club where I’ve previously spent 10 years, is something I’m very grateful for.” Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: Shooters wary of surrendering firearms as confusion surrounds NSW gun buyback
World.content:
PoliticsNSWNSW State Parliament Shooters wary of surrendering firearms as confusion surrounds NSW gun buyback Jessica McSweeney October 26, 2026 — 4:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Doubts are mounting over how many people will participate in the first stage of NSW’s controversial gun buyback scheme as confusion lingers over which shooters qualify for exemptions to the caps. The first buyback appointments opened on Monday ahead of the November 2 start date for the scheme, but farming and shooting groups have questioned how many will willingly take part without knowing if they qualify for an exemption next year. NSW has opened the first appointments before the buy back starts next week. WA Police The government introduced a four-gun cap for most shooters, with farmers and sporting shooters granted a 10-gun cap, under legislation rushed through the parliament in the wake of the Bondi terror attack in which 15 people were killed and dozens of others injured. Under a draft regulation, a further exemption to the cap would be considered by the police commissioner on a case-by-case basis if gun owners have a genuine need for each additional firearm above the cap.



A NSW government statement said police will conduct “targeted consultation” on the regulation. Police Minister Yasmin Catley said circumstances that may qualify for an exemption include farmers with guns at multiple properties, or elite sporting shooters who need different guns for different sporting events. Related Article NSW State Parliament Women rush to firearms training ahead of NSW gun buyback “We’re just making sure people have all the right information, so they can make a decision about how they want to deal with the guns that they have and how they choose to participate in the buyback,” Catley said. Bookings opened at noon on Monday for gun owners to surrender their guns at six police stations: Narellan, Penrith, Sutherland, Griffith, Grafton and Dubbo. A further 34 stations will participate in the scheme in the coming months.



The first stage of the scheme will offer compensation of up to $1000 for each gun. Compensation for higher value firearms will come next year. NSW Farmers Association rural affairs committee vice chair Glen Andreazza said he would be surprised if any farmers participated in the buyback before knowing what the regulations for exemptions included. “There would be no reason for a farmer to surrender any weapons at this point in time,” he said. Sporting Shooters Association Australia is encouraging members to comply with the law. However, NSW chief executive Pete Szaak said the uncertainty around who would qualify for an exemption made it unlikely sporting shooters would voluntarily surrender guns in the first stage of the buyback.



Szaak said the looming regulations raised more questions than answers, leaving some sporting shooters confused. “Given there is no requirement to compulsorily hand guns in, you should think about all these things first … it’s not as if police are ripping doors down doing search warrants,” he said. Related Article Exclusive

Resolve Political Monitor Voters deliver verdict on guns as political division widens While the state Labor government has committed to taking the gun crackdown to the election, the Shooters Union is encouraging members to boycott the buyback. The Coalition and One Nation have called for the firearms caps to be repealed. Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane, who voted with the government to support the gun crackdown after the Bondi attack, has said the Liberals would scrap caps for farmers and sporting shooters.



A recent Resolve Political Monitor survey found voters were overwhelmingly in favour of caps on the number of firearms an individual can own and time limits on gun licences. In the survey of voters in August and September, 80 per cent said they supported restricting gun licences to Australian citizens, 73 per cent favoured the four-gun cap for individuals, and 75 per cent supported time limits on licences forcing owners to reapply every few years. A majority – 53 per cent – said they supported the government’s buyback, which has drawn criticism from gun owners, the Coalition and some independent MPs. Only 20 per cent opposed the scheme, with 27 per cent either neutral or undecided. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: ASX rebounds to end on a high; CSL names new chair
World.content:
Updated BusinessMarketsWorld markets ASX rebounds to end on a high; CSL names new chair Staff writers Updated October 26, 2026 — 4:51pm ,first published October 26, 2026 — 5:20am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. The Australian sharemarket has rebounded after an early fall to close in the green, with materials and energy stocks posting gains thanks to a rise in oil prices over the weekend. The S&P/ASX 200 gained 14.7 points or 0.17 per cent, to 8809 on Monday. The Australian dollar was trading at US70.33¢. Wall Street lost ground on Friday as oil prices hit their highest mark in four years. Bloomberg The gains were largely thanks to advancing energy and materials stocks off the back of a rise in oil prices. Earlier in the day, Brent crude advanced above $US116 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate rose above $US102 before retreating slightly in the afternoon. The gains were linked to fears the US would restart its war with Iran, with President Donald Trump telling Fox News it was “getting to be decision time” on whether he would make a deal with Tehran or “finish it off”. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said if rationality existed, the US would not attempt an attack.



Woodside Energy rose 1 per cent and Santos added 1.3 per cent. Among the refiners, Ampol advanced 0.3 per cent and Viva Energy surged 3.2 per cent. Meanwhile, miners BHP and Fortescue added 1.3 per cent and 2.4 per cent respectively. Related Article AI AI darling NextDC announces board and pay purge after Melbourne power disaster Gold miners also reported gains, with Northern Star gaining 2.1 per cent and Evolution rising 1.6 per cent as the gold price steadied at about $US4000 ($5690) per ounce. Technology stocks fell early, following their Wall Street peers, but rebounded as the day progressed. WiseTech grew 1.7 per cent, Xero rose 1.4 per cent and TechnologyOne added 1.7 per cent. Embattled AI company NextDC slumped 2.5 per cent as it announced its chairman, Douglas Flynn, would stand for re-election at its annual meeting with investors next month but retire once a replacement is in place, and chief executive Craig Scroggie will forfeit millions in bonuses. Pharmaceutical giant CSL has named its interim chief executive, Gordon Naylor, as its next chair, replacing Brian McNamee, who will end his decades-long association with the Australian pharmaceutical giant.



Naylor will take over as chair on March 31. He will hand over chief executive duties to Deborah Waterhouse in February. Related Article Exclusive

Retail ASIC won’t sue Super Retail board over scandal that led to CEO’s sacking, says company McNamee, as CEO, helped steer the company’s transformation from a government agency into one of Australia’s largest listed companies, but it has struggled with a string of downgrades over the past year which sent its shares sharply lower. CSL shares ended the day down 1.6 per cent. On Wall Street on Friday, the S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent as the index posted its second-straight weekly loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.2 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.2 per cent after giving up a modest gain. Several AI-related companies rallied, helping ease some of the impact from the broader market slide. Micron Technology rose 2.5 per cent, Intel gained 1.7 per cent, Microsoft added 0.7 per cent, and Advanced Micro Devices closed 1.7 per cent higher.



The tech sector’s influence is also capable of quickly switching over to a heavy weight. Stocks that have benefited from the frenzy over AI have been swinging over rising worries about their path ahead. Investors are worried about whether their high prices are justified. Many of those companies have been borrowing to fund investments in AI technology, and high interest rates are making those loans more expensive. “Investors appear increasingly focused on the economics of AI, particularly the substantial upfront costs required to build AI infrastructure and the uncertainty around the timing of returns on those investments,” said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones, in a research note. The latest round of corporate earnings is being closely watched to help get a better sense of whether those investments are paying off, or might pay off. Several influential AI-related companies report their latest financial results next week, including Google’s parent, Alphabet, along with Microsoft and Amazon. Industrial companies had some of the biggest losses. Caterpillar fell 2.4 per cent.



American Express slumped 3.7 per cent, one of several financial stocks that lost ground, despite reporting profits for its most recent quarter that beat analysts’ forecasts. The company did announce its first major job cuts in roughly a decade. Related Article Casinos Judgment day looms for Star casino as court decides size of fine JPMorganChase fell 1.5 per cent, Citigroup dropped 1.5 per cent and Capital One Financial slid 1 per cent. While higher oil prices weighed down much of the market, they helped boost energy companies. Chevron rose 2.9 per cent and ConocoPhillips gained 3.6 per cent. European markets closed mostly lower. France’s main index fell 0.4 per cent, though yields on French government bonds eased a bit.



Treasury yields in the US edged higher following sharp drops on Thursday. The yield on the 10-year Treasury edged up to 4.99 per cent from 4.96 per cent late on Thursday. Yields have been rising globally, partly over worries about governments taking on too much debt. Inflation also remains a concern and is stubbornly well above 3 per cent in the US. That prompted the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate at its last meeting in an effort to cool inflation. Wall Street expects the US central bank to hold rates steady at its meeting next week, but is leaning heavily towards another rate hike in December. Wall Street will also get several big economic updates next week, including the Fed’s preferred measure of inflation. The personal consumption expenditures index is expected to show that inflation rose at a 3.7 per cent rate in September, sharply above the Fed’s 2 per cent target. With AP, Bloomberg The Market Recap newsletter is a wrap of the day’s trading. Get it each weekday afternoon.

World.title: Gina Rinehart takes fight for Perth helipad at Hancock HQ to tribunal
World.content:
NationalWAGina Rinehart Gina Rinehart takes fight for Perth helipad at Hancock HQ to tribunal Heather McNeill October 26, 2026 — 4:49pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Gina Rinehart’s company Hancock Prospecting has taken its fight to build a helipad atop its West Perth headquarters to the State Administrative Tribunal after it was knocked back by the local council. The City of Perth grounded plans for the helipad at the Ord Street building in December, despite two councillors backing the idea of a helicopter landing in the city precinct, and the lord mayor describing Rinehart as an “amazing Australian”. Gina Rinehart is continuing to fight to put a helipad atop her new West Perth head office. Opposition to the helipad stemmed from concerns over noise, whether it was conducive with the area’s existing planning scheme, and whether allowing the CBD’s first private-use helipad would set an undesirable precedent. The area, in West Perth, is an office and residential precinct, with the City of Perth flagging nearby sites could accommodate more residents in the future.



But Ord Street Holdings counsel Grant Donaldson, KC, in his opening statement in SAT on Monday, argued the helipad would only be used in “daylight hours” between midday and 7pm up to 12 times a year for “occasional corporate transport”. “That’s 144 minutes per annum, that equates to the sound of an electric kettle boiling for six minutes, once every fortnight, between the hours of noon and 7pm,” he said. “This case boils down to what negative impact is this use going to have on the objects of the current or new scheme?” The mining giant has previously likened Perth to Tokyo and New York as a “global city”, saying “rooftop helipads are commonplace across the world’s leading cities, and our proposal would elevate Perth’s status”. But City of Perth barrister Tim Houweling said the fundamental issue in the case was noise.



Neighbouring buildings have also objected to the helipad. Related Article Planning and development Gina Rinehart circles around in fresh bid for helipad at Hancock headquarters The Child and Adolescent Health Service made a submission to the City of Perth stating that sudden, intermittent helicopter noise could interrupt testing of children with conditions including autism, sensory issues, ADHD or anxiety. The submission also raised concerns that its roof is old and made of asbestos, and helicopter downwash could disrupt the asbestos dust that has settled. After the council initially refused the helipad application, Hancock Prospecting lodged a revised development plan outlining a new flight path, in a bid to get the request over the line.



Previous plans had the helicopter approaching from the east or west of the eye-popping five-storey headquarters, in a route that would have seen it come down over the inner-city suburb of Subiaco or a mix of residential and office buildings in West Perth. Instead, the new flight path has the eight-seat Bell 429 helicopter approaching the building from the south-west, tracking Thomas Street on the outer fringe of Perth’s CBD botanic garden Kings Park, before turning and descending once it reaches Ord Street. A Hancock Prospecting spokesperson said the company’s original application was “developed with expert input and independent technical analysis which confirmed the helipad and flight path can operate safely and appropriately”. “However, as part of our extensive good faith efforts to reach agreement with the City of Perth, we have proposed an amended flight path and further reduced the proposed operating timeframes,” they said.



SAT judge Henry Jackson is presiding over the appeal, and will make a ruling on the helipad at the conclusion of the two-day trial which will hear from acoustic and planning experts. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: AFLW ladder with one round to play; ‘Difficult decision’: Dons sack inaugural coach
World.content:
Essendon will replace inaugural AFLW coach Natalie Wood next season after informing her that her contract would not be renewed for 2027 after the team’s 1-10 record this season.

Wood was informed on Tuesday about the decision, but players were only told after Sunday’s five-point loss to Hawthorn.

Bombers coach Natalie Wood leads her side on Sunday. AFL Photos

Wood is still planning to coach the final round game next Sunday against fellow strugglers Collingwood.

The Dons will be the third AFLW club seeking a coach, joining St Kilda and expansion club Tasmania Devils.

“The club is not offering me a contract as of next year,” Wood said post game on Sunday.

“It’s been a topic of conversation and a lot of questions with our poor performances this year

“It’s a disappointing end, as clearly I would have liked, like the last couple of years, to have better performances on the field.”

The Dons have struggled with injuries and form this season, but Wood was heartened by the club locking in several future leaders to new contracts but they will look for a new coach.

“We have fallen short of what we wanted on field. We believe a change is the right step,” Essendon chief executive Tim Roberts said.

“Natalie has handled this with real integrity, and her commitment to coaching out the season says a lot about her and how much she cares about the players.

“We thank Natalie for everything she has given the club over five seasons, and we wish her all the best for the next step in her football journey.”

Wood was the first female coach to reach 50 games while leading the team for five seasons since they entered the competition.

“[I] just continued on with the week as normal,” Wood said.

“We had two amazing players in Alex Morcom and Maddi Gay having their 50th and 75th game today, so really important celebrations, and we also had Amelia Radford announce her retirement.

Hayley McLaughlin of the Hawks kicks for goal against Essendon on Sunday. AFL Photos via Getty Images

“I would prefer no one ever knows, and I’d just disappear off into the sunset without any discussion or interview, but I was particularly aware this week of not wanting to get in the way of those three players.

“We really wanted to beat Hawthorn today. I thought we put up a really good fight, it was an ugly game of footy, tricky conditions. But always forefront of my mind is playing group first – so I thought it was best to hold off until today.

“Aysha (Ward, AFLW general manager) is heavily pregnant and is going on leave in two or three weeks, so I think the club is keen on getting a start in searching for their new coach.”

Wood said it was hard leading the AFLW side while Essendon as a club has faced so many leadership changes in recent seasons.

“Am I disappointed it’s fallen out this way? It depends how narrow of a view I have of it. Sometimes,” Wood said.

“I remember in my job interview, we were discussing about the wants of the role. [At the time], no female coach had lasted longer than two years, and I was not wanting to step into a senior coaching role without being well prepared and supported to have a career that’s longer than two years,” Wood said.

“To be the first female coach to coach 50 games, I’m really proud of that. To build a team from ground-up, as one of the last expansion teams and the season coming forward, it was a mad rush.

“At the same time, the club’s had a lot of instability. There’s been four CEOs, three presidents, three men’s senior captains and three senior coaches, so to build a culture within a program while the instability of the club – and it’s in a good spot now – it’s been hard at times while there’s been so much change in structure and leadership.

“When I look back to the start of the season and we had so many players sign long-term contracts, players who are really important to the program going forward - we’ve built a culture and place where players really want to be. I’ve done something right.”

The Hawks scored a vital win in their quest to make the top eight, winning by five points in rain-soaked conditions at the club’s new base in Dingley.

The Bombers were brave but couldn’t find the last goal they needed to get the win.

With AAP

World.content:

Dual-asset gold producer Kaiser Reef has wiped a key debt from its books after a solid September quarter, a move expected to unchain about $600,000 a month in operating cash flow. The company banked 6263 ounces of gold during the period, boosting its cash and bullion balance to a healthy $40 million and allowing it to fully repay the senior secured gold loan used to acquire its flagship Henty gold mine in Tasmania. Kaiser Reef is advancing a two-pronged strategy at its producing Henty gold mine in Tasmania (pictured) and the high-grade Maldon gold project in Victoria. Production from the company’s two Australian assets continued to build momentum during the period, with total gold output rising to 6263 ounces from 6000 ounces in the prior quarter. The cornerstone Henty mine churned out 5692 ounces of gold and a further 5259 ounces of silver, while its Maldon project in Victoria chipped in another 572 ounces of gold. Impressively, the Maldon operation has now lifted its output for three consecutive quarters, jumping 65 per cent since March. ‘We head into the December quarter with a fully funded balance sheet and clear operational priorities at both assets.’ Kaiser Reef managing director Brad Valiukas



Total production generated an underlying cash flow of $5.6 million for the quarter, which more than covered $2.8 million in debt and deferred payments, allowing Kaiser to increase its net cash and bullion position by a hefty $2.8 million. The strong financial position enabled the company to make a final delivery of 104 ounces of gold in October, wiping the slate clean on the 1872-ounce Auramet gold loan. With that facility retired, Kaiser’s only remaining gold delivery obligation is a deferred payment to Catalyst Metals as part of the Henty acquisition, requiring 50 ounces per month through to October 2030. However, the company says repaying the principal acquisition loan from the mine’s own cash flow is an important milestone. Kaiser Reef managing director Brad Valiukas said: “Kaiser delivered 6263oz of gold across Henty and Maldon during the quarter, while increasing cash and bullion to A$40 million, paying down debt and advancing Maldon. We have completely repaid the Auramet gold loan, on schedule, with the final delivery made in October. The gold loan helped us acquire Henty, and repaying it from Henty’s own cash flow is an important milestone for Kaiser.” The impressive quarterly report further underscores a remarkable full-year turnaround for Kaiser, which swung from a $20.24 million statutory loss in FY2025 to a $16.8 million after-tax profit in FY2026, backed by an impressive $44.7 million cash inflow from operations. The Henty mine, nestled in Tasmania’s richly endowed Mount Read Volcanics belt alongside the legendary Rosebery and Mount Lyell operations, remains the company’s gold-producing workhorse. A recent resource and reserve update effectively offset mining depletion, maintaining the mine’s ore reserve at 198,000 ounces of gold and its overall resource at 429,000 ounces. In a shrewd move to sweat its assets, the company is also working with fellow ASX-lister Flynn Gold to process its ore through Henty’s 300,000-tonne-per-annum processing plant. As part of the expansion plan, Kaiser has applied to increase its tailings capacity by two million tonnes.



While Henty provides the cash flow, Kaiser’s Maldon operation in Victoria’s fabled Golden Triangle offers a significant high-grade growth opportunity. The project, with a strong track record of producing 1.75 million ounces at a staggering 28 grams per tonne (g/t) gold, is anchored by the fully permitted 200,000-tonne-per-annum Porcupine Flats processing facility. Its Union Hill deposit hosts an inferred resource of 187,000 ounces grading a solid 4.44g/t gold, with site stockpiles adding a further 11,700 ounces. All up, the company’s global resource stands at 5.53 million tonnes grading 3.46g/t gold for 615,000 ounces. With FY27 total production targeted at around 32,000 ounces and no hedging in place, the gold producer appears well positioned to capture more upside should the bullion price remain steady. Another major milestone for the quarter was the start of underground development at the Union Hill mine. The new development will provide access for underground diamond drilling to test the northern extensions of existing workings at Maldon’s Eaglehawk, Linscott’s, Ladies and Sailors Reefs targets. The underground push adds another dimension to a busy surface exploration campaign aimed at building a pipeline of fresh drill targets. Recent infill soil sampling has outlined strong, continuous gold and arsenic anomalies across multiple structures, with some promising trends extending over 1.5 kilometres of strike. This work has been bolstered by a helicopter-borne magnetic and radiometric survey, providing a clearer picture of the structural architecture, with a surface diamond drilling campaign also ongoing. With the Henty operation humming along and paying the bills, Kaiser appears to be in an enviable position of being largely debt-free and sitting on a sizeable cash pile as it methodically advances exploration across one of Victoria’s most celebrated high-grade goldfields. With no hedging in place and a production target of 32,000 ounces for FY27, the company looks to be fully exposed to any upside in the gold price. As drill rods turn on both surface and underground hotspots at Maldon, punters will likely be watching closely for the results to start flowing. World.title: Push for early train times to get FIFO workers to Perth Airport
World.content:
PoliticsWAAirports Push for early train times to get FIFO workers to Perth Airport Hamish Hastie October 26, 2026 — 4:11pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Perth Airport boss Jason Waters is “confident” the state government will tinker with its train timetable to better cater the Airport Line for fly-in, fly-out workers. FIFO workers considering public transport for their flight days have long complained the Airport Line service does not run early enough to catch the morning peak of FIFO flights, which runs from about 4am to 8am. Perth Airport new terminal artist renders. The earliest train to the Airport Central station arrives at 5.27am, but for most intrastate flights, check in closes 30 minutes before the flight time – making it nearly impossible to catch a 6am flight using the train. Asked about a FIFO service at a press conference on Monday, Waters said he was in constant communication with the government in relation to both road and rail.



“I’m certain that as the airport grows and the needs of passengers become more clear and understood, I’m confident that we’ll see the availability of train follow suit,” he said. In the past, the WA government has been reluctant to extend train operating hours, because it would shorten maintenance windows on the city’s rail network. At the same press conference on Monday, Premier Roger Cook said Transport Minister Rita Saffioti was always reviewing timetables to make sure they served the community “That’s why you’ve seen millions of people shifting onto rail, taking part in the expansion of Metronet as paying passengers,” he said. According to the latest Public Transport Authority annual report, boardings on the Airport line increased 11 per cent from 2024-25 to 2025-26, rising from 5.62 million boardings to 6.23 million.



Airport transformation spurs warning for travellers Perth Airport will want to see as many people as possible coming to the airport on public transport as it gears up for one of the biggest transformations in the airport’s history. Construction will begin in the coming months on $5 billion worth of work, including a third runway and new terminal which will bring Qantas’ extensive Perth operations under the same roof as all other carriers at Terminal 1. Perth Airport new terminal artist renders. At the same time, another carpark and a new hotel will be built near Terminal 1, prompting a warning from Waters that “the journey ahead is going to be tricky.”



Related Article Traveller letters To catch an earlier flight, I asked for a downgrade. Qantas refused “We’re going to be bringing thousands of construction workers onto the terminal site, and that means there are going to be delays and challenges for passengers but we’re going to remain open 24/7 through the entire construction period,” he said. “Don’t get caught out last minute because from here on in, over the next five or six years, there’s going to be a lot happening at Perth Airport.” Waters revealed only 4 per cent of passengers to Perth Airport used the train to come or go from the airport, driven in part because there was no train servicing the Qantas terminals. However, he said once the airport was all under one roof the Airport Line would be a much more attractive option.



“The construction of the one airport model gives us the ability to really go to the people of Perth and Western Australia with a proposition that says use the train because we’re all in one place now,” he said. Speaking on the 40th anniversary of the opening of Terminal 1, Waters said the airport upgrades were expected to be completed by 2031 and the timing and cost was still on target, but work was still being done on the final time and cost. Perth Airport will be competing with mining, defence and the state government for materials and labour. More than $25 billion worth of work is under way at Henderson to prepare for AUKUS, billions are being spent on grid upgrades, and renewable energy projects and tens of thousands of homes are being built. Waters wasn’t worried about the competition in the state’s already hot construction sector.



“I think it’s actually exciting times for Western Australia. The AUKUS investment, the ongoing investment the state government’s making, as well as Perth Airport, it’s all part of what makes the package of Western Australia great,” he said. Perth Airport new terminal artist renders. “What is important is that in the background we are having conversations to ensure that we schedule things in a way that enable it all to be achieved in a sensible manner. So I’m not asking that anything be slowed down.” Cook said the Office of Major Infrastructure Delivery was working with big constructors to work out timings of project to avoid labor and materials constraints. “There’s timing around concrete, timing around rebar and other steel products to make sure that they can all work in concert with each other,” he said.

World.title: Sparks will fly when Bulldog Butters returns to Adelaide for Gather Round
World.content:
AFL briefing SportAFLAFL 2026 Sparks will fly when Bulldog Butters returns to Adelaide for Gather Round Jon Pierik and Greg Dundas Updated October 26, 2026 — 4:01pm ,first published 12:59pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. In today’s AFL briefing: Max Gawn backs brutal list calls at Melbourne ahead of his own contract talks

Butters’ return to Adelaide highlights Gather Round program

Dean Solomon to join Damien Hardwick at Gold Coast Butters game to be a focus of Gather Round Greg Dundas Zak Butters will be bracing a fiery reception when he returns to Adelaide to play against the Power for the first time when the Western Bulldogs help draw a curtain on next year’s Gather Round. Look away, Port fans: Zak Butters in Western Bulldogs colours. Getty Images



The clash between Port Adelaide and Butters’ new club is the ninth game of the Gather Round fixture released by the AFL on Monday, and even has South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas – an avid Power fan – fired up. Revered at the Power after three best and fairest awards and three All-Australian guernseys from 156 games, Butters officially became a Bulldog earlier this month, signing the richest contract in AFL history. He stands to earn at least $17 million over the next nine years after crossing to the Dogs as a restricted free agent, aided by a complex side deal that convinced Port not to match the deal. Raised near Bacchus Marsh as a Bulldogs supporter, Butters’ future was the subject of conjecture throughout the 2026 season, with the Dogs pipping Geelong for his coveted signature.



It’s not yet clear, how Port’s passionate fan base will respond to Butters, but the AFL have capitalised on the appeal of his clash with his former teammates by making it a marquee match of Gather Round. It is one of three blockbuster games the league has scheduled at the Adelaide Oval to underpin the South Australian-based round - round four of the 2027 season. The festivities will open on Thursday April 8, with the Crows seeking revenge for their semi-final loss in 2026 to the Brisbane Lions, and close four days later with Butters facing his former side. Loading In between, the league has scheduled a humdinger of a Saturday-night match between leading premiership fancies Fremantle and Hawthorn.



There are two other games scheduled at the Adelaide Oval across the weekend – Sydney v Collingwood on the Friday night and an early Saturday game between Carlton and Melbourne, who met in a wildcard final in 2026. Gold Coast, GWS, Geelong and St Kilda are the four teams heading to the Barossa for their Gather Round games, while Richmond, West Coast, Essendon and North Melbourne are bound for Norwood Oval. Related Article Analysis

AFL 2026 Contending, rebuilding or stuck in limbo: What AFL trade period says about your team’s flag hopes Malinauskas – an avid Power fan – was quick to spruik the Gather Round program, which coincides with the Easter school holidays, and the inclusion of a players’ parade on the Friday. “The blockbuster weekend of footy will be boosted with the inaugural Players Parade on Friday, allowing fans to see their heroes from all 18 clubs in one spot,” he said.



“Personally, I’m looking forward to being at a packed Adelaide Oval to see Zak Butters take on his former teammates.” Gawn applauds ‘brutal’ Melbourne list calls Jon Pierik Melbourne captain Max Gawn has applauded the club’s “brutal” list-management calls which led to the departure of favourite son Jack Viney, but hopes he can finish his career as a one-club player. Melbourne captain Max Gawn cycles alongside Tour de France champion Cadel Evans ahead of the Great Ocean Road race. AAPIMAGE



Gawn is off contract in 2027, but at 33 is still playing some of the best football of his career, which he attributes, in part, to his punishing off-season cycling regime. The 2021 premiership skipper won All-Australian selection for the ninth time in 2026, and is keen to remain a Demon for life when contract discussions open. However, he understands the business of football, having watched his fellow premiership on-ball brigade of Clayton Oliver, Christian Petracca and Viney, along with key defender Steven May, depart over the past two seasons. “I’m pretty keen in Melbourne. I understand ‘Vines’ would have said the same thing 12 months ago. So, I’ve just applauded ‘Lamby’ [list boss Tim Lamb] and King [coach Steven King], and if I’m the one that has to move on next year, and I still think there’s footy ahead of me, then that conversation will come, but right now, it does look like my finish will be with the Demons,” Gawn said on Monday. Kicking on: Melbourne skipper Max Gawn is off contract in 2027, and wants to finish his career as a one-club player. Getty Images However, speaking as an ambassador at the launch of the Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Race, Gawn hinted he would be open to offers, should negotiations with the Demons not go as planned, and if new club Tasmania came calling.





“I applaud the list management team; they’ve made some brutal decisions,” Gawn said. “None more brutal than probably Jack this year, but you’ve seen with what we’re able to do this year, with most people tipping us [to finish] bottom four, and we come out and play some pretty good footy.” Gawn said he was delighted that Essendon and the Eagles showed interest in Viney, his former co-captain. Fresh start: Ex-Melbourne midfielder Jack Viney will continue his career with West Coast after being traded to the Eagles on the final day of the trade period. Getty Images “I went from a little bit of surprise [at his departure], and then I went a little bit of other clubs were making him feel generally loved,” Gawn said.



“And now, he’s like, once it got to a point where West Coast were interested, he’s like: ‘I want to get there so bad, I want to rejuvenate my career, I want to take my family over there’. So I’m really excited for him.” Gawn said the Demons had needed a substantial make-over, having seen how quickly Geelong transformed, even after winning the 2022 premiership. Only nine Demons players now remain from the 2021 premiership team. “I sat there and looked at that [2022 Geelong] team, I was like, OK, and then they play in the grand final three years later, and they had 10 or 15 new players in that team. And, at the same time, Melbourne was still running the round with the ’21 premiership team,” Gawn said. Related Article Live

AFLW AFLW ladder with one round to play; ‘Difficult decision’: Dons sack inaugural coach “It’s like, well, we haven’t changed or adapted or moved on. We’re still trying to win it again with the ’21 premiership team, and Geelong, at that very same time, had changed over 15 players. It’s like, OK, this is what’s needed in a way to stay in the modern game.”



A cycling enthusiast who now has his own podcast on the sport, Gawn’s pre-season training program has so far included “Everesting” South Australia’s exhausting Willunga Hill, riding the 3.7km climb 39.5 times in 21 hours, and another punishing ride on the island of Phuket in Thailand. He will soon head to Patagonia, at the southern end of South America, to ride in the wilderness. This program will also include running. Solomon gets Gold Coast gig After coaching Essendon through the second half of 2026, Dean Solomon will return to Gold Coast as an assistant coach to Damien Hardwick. Dean Solomon as coach of Essendon. Getty Images Solomon, now 46, was on the coaching staff at the Suns from the club’s inception in the AFL in 2011 to 2020, even serving three games as interim coach following the departure of Rodney Eade in 2017.



Solomon later joined the board at Essendon – the club where he made his name as a player and was part of the 2000 premiership team – but relinquished that position a year ago to return to a hands-on coaching role. He started the 2026 season as an assistant to Brad Scott, and became the club’s stop-gap coach when Scott was sacked mid-season. Despite holding some ambition to become the senior coach permanently, Solomon’s hopes were dented by a record of just one win from his 12 games in charge. After hiring Solomon’s former teammate Mark McVeigh as senior coach for 2027, Essendon announced last month that Solomon had declined their offer of another role in the football department and would return to live in NSW with his wife and children. On Monday, the Suns spruiked Solomon’s recruitment as a homecoming. “Dean played a significant role across our club’s first decade in the competition, and his expertise and industry experience will be instrumental in helping us take steps forward in the years ahead,” Gold Coast’s general manager of football Craig Cameron said.



Solomon said the Suns job aligned with his family circumstances . Related Article AFL 2026 ‘An A-plus character’: The prospect from a family of Essendon diehards who could kickstart the Dons “The opportunity to return to the Gold Coast Suns to work alongside and learn from Damien Hardwick and an experienced group of coaches is one I’m really excited by,” Solomon said. “The potential of the list that has been assembled is incredibly inviting and I see it as an exciting time to be part of the Suns. “The Gold Coast and Northern New South Wales has been home for my family and I for over 16 years now, so to be able to be with my wife and kids again and still coach at the highest level at a club where I’ve previously spent 10 years, is something I’m very grateful for.” Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: Shooters wary of surrendering firearms as confusion surrounds NSW gun buyback
World.content:
PoliticsNSWNSW State Parliament Shooters wary of surrendering firearms as confusion surrounds NSW gun buyback Jessica McSweeney October 26, 2026 — 4:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Doubts are mounting over how many people will participate in the first stage of NSW’s controversial gun buyback scheme as confusion lingers over which shooters qualify for exemptions to the caps. The first buyback appointments opened on Monday ahead of the November 2 start date for the scheme, but farming and shooting groups have questioned how many will willingly take part without knowing if they qualify for an exemption next year. NSW has opened the first appointments before the buy back starts next week. WA Police The government introduced a four-gun cap for most shooters, with farmers and sporting shooters granted a 10-gun cap, under legislation rushed through the parliament in the wake of the Bondi terror attack in which 15 people were killed and dozens of others injured. Under a draft regulation, a further exemption to the cap would be considered by the police commissioner on a case-by-case basis if gun owners have a genuine need for each additional firearm above the cap.



A NSW government statement said police will conduct “targeted consultation” on the regulation. Police Minister Yasmin Catley said circumstances that may qualify for an exemption include farmers with guns at multiple properties, or elite sporting shooters who need different guns for different sporting events. Related Article NSW State Parliament Women rush to firearms training ahead of NSW gun buyback “We’re just making sure people have all the right information, so they can make a decision about how they want to deal with the guns that they have and how they choose to participate in the buyback,” Catley said. Bookings opened at noon on Monday for gun owners to surrender their guns at six police stations: Narellan, Penrith, Sutherland, Griffith, Grafton and Dubbo. A further 34 stations will participate in the scheme in the coming months.



The first stage of the scheme will offer compensation of up to $1000 for each gun. Compensation for higher value firearms will come next year. NSW Farmers Association rural affairs committee vice chair Glen Andreazza said he would be surprised if any farmers participated in the buyback before knowing what the regulations for exemptions included. “There would be no reason for a farmer to surrender any weapons at this point in time,” he said. Sporting Shooters Association Australia is encouraging members to comply with the law. However, NSW chief executive Pete Szaak said the uncertainty around who would qualify for an exemption made it unlikely sporting shooters would voluntarily surrender guns in the first stage of the buyback.



Szaak said the looming regulations raised more questions than answers, leaving some sporting shooters confused. “Given there is no requirement to compulsorily hand guns in, you should think about all these things first … it’s not as if police are ripping doors down doing search warrants,” he said. Related Article Exclusive

Resolve Political Monitor Voters deliver verdict on guns as political division widens While the state Labor government has committed to taking the gun crackdown to the election, the Shooters Union is encouraging members to boycott the buyback. The Coalition and One Nation have called for the firearms caps to be repealed. Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane, who voted with the government to support the gun crackdown after the Bondi attack, has said the Liberals would scrap caps for farmers and sporting shooters.



A recent Resolve Political Monitor survey found voters were overwhelmingly in favour of caps on the number of firearms an individual can own and time limits on gun licences. In the survey of voters in August and September, 80 per cent said they supported restricting gun licences to Australian citizens, 73 per cent favoured the four-gun cap for individuals, and 75 per cent supported time limits on licences forcing owners to reapply every few years. A majority – 53 per cent – said they supported the government’s buyback, which has drawn criticism from gun owners, the Coalition and some independent MPs. Only 20 per cent opposed the scheme, with 27 per cent either neutral or undecided. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: Flights disrupted in Wellington, wet and windy end to long weekend for South Island
World.content:
Gusty winds are causing delays and cancellations for flights coming into the capital.

An RNZ reporter said his plane from Auckland tried to land in Wellington twice, before returning to Auckland.

As of 2.30 pm at least seven arriving flights have either been cancelled or diverted, a Wellington Airport spokesperson said.

Multiple other flights appeared to be delayed, according to the airport website.

The spokesperson said passengers should check the status of their flights directly with the airline, as there may be more cancellations to come.

Earlier, police said they were closing a central road in Wellington due to high wind gusts.

A spokesperson said a stretch of Oriental Parade and Evans Bay Parade was being shut following reports of multiple people falling off bicycles and wing mirrors being blown off cars.

The road around the point is closed from Carlton Gore Road in Oriental Bay to Maida Vale Road at the intersection with Evans Bay Parade.

Fire and Emergency said crews have so far dealt with five wind-related callouts, including material falling from buildings and downed power lines.

Shift manager Becca Jennings said a piece of panelling had fallen off the ceiling of Jetts Fitness in Miramar, and glass had fallen onto the footpath and street from a balcony in Mount Victoria.

Crews in both areas were trying to keep the area safe, Becca said.

Meanwhile, parts of the South Island are being lashed by heavy rain and severe gales as an active front moves up the country.

MetService meteorologist Samkelo Magwala said a wind gust of about 200km/h was recorded at Mount Hutt, Canterbury, around 8am on Monday.

He advised people in affected areas to keep an eye on the weather and road conditions.

"Those people who are planning to travel after the long weekend ... should be vigilant when driving, especially in those areas where the weather won't be so pleasant," he said.

Weather warnings in place

Westland and Fiordland are under orange rain warnings, with up to 250 millimetres of rain expected about the ranges of Westland.

Metservice issued rain and wind warnings and watches for some of the South Island on Sunday, but more warnings are now in place for parts of the lower North Island.

New Zealand Transport Agency Waka Kotahi said heavy rain would make roads slippery, meaning drivers should think about adjusting their speed and travelling distances, avoiding sudden braking and staying visible.

"People are also urged to avoid driving through any floodwaters, especially where the depth is unclear and there may be hidden obstructions," the agency said.

"NZTA contractors will be monitoring the state highway network and will respond to any slips or obstructions that need clearing."

An orange strong wind warning is in place for Wellington, Wairarapa, the Canterbury High Country and Plains, Otago, Fiordland, Marlborough, Southland and Stewart Island, with gusts up to 120km/h possible in exposed places.

These warnings expire from 7pm Monday in the south and 9am Tuesday in Wellington.

A strong wind watch has also been issued for Christchurch from 6pm Monday, the Tararua District from 11pm Monday and in Horowhenua and Kāpiti from 3am Tuesday.

An orange heavy rain warning is in place for Grey and Buller districts, Westland, the headwaters of the Canterbury lakes and rivers about and south of Arthur's Pass, the headwaters of the Otago lakes and rivers, and Fiordland.

An orange heavy rain warning will go in place for the Tararua Range from 2am Tuesday.

There is a heavy rain watch for the Queenstown Lakes district away from the headwaters and Southland and Stewart Island, expiring from 11pm Monday in the south to 11am Tuesday in the north.

Westland can expect the heaviest falls, with 200 to 250mm forecast about the ranges and 300mm possible about isolated peaks.

Most of the warnings expire from Tuesday morning, with those in the lower South Island expiring on Monday.

MetService said there was a low to minimal chance of its orange wind and rain warnings being upgraded to red.

World.title: Firefighters battle blaze in Central Plateau military zone
World.content:
A large scrub fire near the Desert Road is continuing to grow, with helicopter crews and firefighters working to bring it under control in the Waiouru military zone.

Fire crews responded to the blaze on the Central Plateau about 10.15am on Monday, Fire and Emergency shift manager Becca Jennings said, and it appeared to be a continuation of a fire from the previous day that had escalated.

By mid-afternoon Monday the flames covered an area about 400x400 metres, but it had spread to 238 hectares by the evening.

Five helicopter crews and nine firefighting crews were working on the blaze.

Its original cause was unknown.

Supplied/ Sarah Moodie

The fire was in a fairly isolated area. There had been no reports of injuries and it did not pose a threat to the Desert Road or to buildings in the area, Jennings earlier said.

Motorists travelling on the Desert Road - State Highway 1 captured footage of large plumes of smoke just south and north of the Waiouru township.

World.title: Southland scrub fire still burning as wind hampers firefighting efforts
World.content:
High winds have prevented firefighters from working on a scrub fire burning in about 80 hectares of Southland land.

Six helicopters worked with monsoon buckets to protect two communications towers in the Centre Hill area, after emergency services were alerted to the blaze at about 4pm Sunday.

Fire and Emergency (FENZ) said high winds on Monday prevented helicopters from accessing the fire, while difficult terrain meant ground crews could not go on foot.

MetService issued a orange strong-wind warning for Southland on Monday, with gales forecast to reach up to 130 km/h in exposed places.

Fire and Emergency incident controller Hamish Angus said an assessment of the vegetation fire would be made as soon as conditions allowed.

While rain on Monday afternoon would help suppress any remaining fire in the open country, deep-seated areas of burning in mature beech forest would need checking, and any pockets of fire dug out and extinguished, he said.

The fire affected an area of about 80 hectares, mostly high country grazing and an area of native bush on adjoining public conservation land.

There were no reports of livestock being affected.

Fire crews from Southland volunteer brigades and the Department of Conservation were being arranged for Tuesday morning. FENZ said the crews were all experienced in arduous conditions.

World.title: Canterbury defend NPC title, ending Northland's dream run
World.content:
Canterbury have stormed back in the second half to claim the NPC rugby title, defeating the Northland Taniwha 43-24.

Trailing 21-10 at halftime, the defending champions turned the match around with five second-half tries to secure a convincing victory.

The win marks Canterbury's 16th NPC crown, with the red and blacks going back-to-back as champions.

"Yeah we had to dig deep there and I thought our bench was exceptional today to close out that game," Canterbury captain Brodie McAlister said after the match.

"The boys love coming back to play for their region, it's a proud region Canterbury.

"It's a good group and we're going to enjoy this one."

The Taniwha started strong, but were unable to maintain their momentum in the second spell. Despite their first-ever final ending in disappointment, their historic run will still be remembered as the province's finest season.

Taniwha captain Rivez Reihana remarked that Canterbury's marked increase in intensity after the break came as little surprise.

"We wanted to win the second half, especially the first five minutes," Reihana told SkySport.

"I think there was stuff we could fix all across the board, I'm not going to put it down to one thing.

"Canterbury just showed why they're the top team and have been for so long."

Far from defeated, Reihana said his players had gained confidence and plenty of belief after a breakout season that saw Northland hold the Ranfurly Shield for five weeks.

"It's just the beginning for this group, and we'll be back, trust me."

The game was played in front of a sold-out crowd at Te Kaha Stadium in Christchurch.

World.title: Man charged with attempted murder after child assaulted at Auckland park
World.content:
A man has been charged with attempted murder after an assault left a child critically injured at a central Auckland park, police say.

The attack happened about 4.45pm on Sunday at a play area in Myers Park, just off Queen Street, before a man was taken into custody. St John earlier said one person was taken to Auckland City Hospital in a serious condition, and the other to Starship Children's Hospital critically injured.

Police said the child and adult did not know each other.

On Monday afternoon, Auckland City District Commander Sunny Patel said: "The 20-year-old has been charged with attempted murder in relation to the assault".

"The child victim remains in Starship Hospital in a serious but stable condition, while the 20-year-old man remains in hospital in serious condition as a result of self-inflicted injuries."

The child's family had been notified and were being supported, Patel said.

Cordons around the playground have now been taken down.

A scene examination at the park had been completed, and police were continuing to investigate the incident.

"Police are not seeking anyone else in relation to the incident, nor do we believe there is any ongoing risk to the public," Patel said.

World.title: Tiaki Wai customers facing direct-debit delays on Wellington water bills
World.content:
Hundreds of direct-debit payments to Wellington's new water agency for residents' first bills are stuck in processing delays.

Tiaki Wai says the issue is mainly due to incomplete or incorrect information on forms, while a Wellington resident says the delay will impact her budget.

Sandra McCallum said she filled out a direct-debit form to the region's new water entity in August, so she could meet the first deadline of 1 September.

Now October, she'd been told the payments were highly unlikely to start in November.

"I think it is a real shortfall in planning," she said. "They must have known they were going to deal with tens of thousands of people who were going to set up direct debits.

"I imagine a lot of us haven't been paying, not for want of trying but because their systems haven't been set up well."

McCallum said she wasn't told her direct-debit form had any issues.

RNZ has received other messages from residents, who say they want to pay their bill, but have been unable, due to the delays.

McCallum said her total annual water bill was about $2500 and, as a pensioner, she wanted to spread that cost over a year. Now it would be a larger bill spread over 8-9 months.

"It impacts on my budget planning," she said. "There will be people who are absolutely unable to [manage] it."

Tiaki Wai's chief customer officer Liza Gunn said this was the first time residents had received a separate water services bill and many had chosen to do direct debits.

"While most direct debits are now in place, some hundreds are still in progress, mainly due to incomplete or incorrect information on their forms," she said. "We expect and understand there will be teething problems."

Direct-debit payments that had not yet been set up would be spread out across the remainder of the financial year.

Gunn said Tiaki Wai would pro-actively contact affected people to complete their direct-debit set-up. She urged anyone with concerns to contact the agency.

"No penalties will be applied for late payment of water charges for an initial period and no-one's water will be turned off because they have not paid their bill," she said. "This applies to all customers, whether they wish to pay by direct debit or otherwise."

Recently, RNZ reported about 30,000 people across the region had not paid their first bills. Second bills are due to arrive to Wellington, Lower and Upper Hutt, and Porirua residents and businesses from late October.

Wellington Mayor Andrew Little said Tiaki Wai faced a major job setting up their own independent billing, finance and customer management systems.

Under Wellington Water, much of that was managed through city councils in the region, because water charges were incorporated into council rates, he said.

World.title: Air New Zealand becomes first international airline to land in Sydney's new airport
World.content:
Air New Zealand has become the first international passenger airline to touch down at Sydney's new airport.

Flight NZ-165 from Auckland landed at Western Sydney International Airport at 7.28am on Monday morning, and left an hour and a half later.

Air New Zealand Captain Andrew McGuigan, who commanded the inaugural flight, said it wasn't every day that you get to be in charge of the first international flight to land at a brand-new airport.

"There was a real sense of excitement onboard as we made our approach into Western Sydney. It was a special moment for our crew and customers, but also for the many people on both sides of the Tasman who have spent months getting us ready for today."

The airline said the landing marked the start of a new service.

Air New Zealand will fly between Auckland and Western Sydney on Monday, Wednesday and Friday until the end of March 2027.

From April 2027, the three return services will run on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.

"More than 75 different teams across Air New Zealand and many partners have played a part in getting ready for today," Air New Zealand chief operations officer Kate Boyer said.

"From pilots and airport teams to engineering, digital, security, baggage, customer experience and operations, almost every part of the airline has been involved."

The airport is in Luddenham, about 45 kilometres west of the Sydney central business district.

World.title: 'Everything's pretty charred': Police seek cause of fire that gutted Napier church
World.content:
Police are investigating the cause of a fire that gutted St Paul's Presbyterian Church in central Napier on Monday morning.

"Everything's pretty charred," the parish's co-minister, Mark Johnston, says of the damage.

Emergency services were called to the blaze on Tennyson Street about 1am.

The building was well involved when crews arrived, and five fire trucks with two support vehicles fought the blaze.

The fire was extinguished shortly after 2am and there were no reports of injuries.

A fire has gutted St Paul's Presbyterian Church in central Napier. Paul Hatchard

Members of the church's community took to social media today to express their shock and sadness at the damage following a post of images from inside the building.

One described the building as a "treasure in the town" and said the church would be missed by multiple generations of people in the area.

Johnston, co-minister of the parish for the last two years alongside his wife, Carolyn Kelly, said a lot of the historic character of the church was destroyed.

"The body of the church has been pretty devastated by fire and water damage. The internals of the church [are] pretty much burnt out. The roof structure is still intact ... there was metal framing inside the structure ... but you can see the tin roof from inside now."

The fire was the third time a St Paul's Presbyterian Church had been destroyed since its establishment in Napier in the late 1800s, Johnston said.

No decision has been made yet on whether the church will be rebuilt on the site. Paul Hatchard

The original church was destroyed by fire in 1929, as was a rebuilt church, destroyed by fire months before it could be reopened after the Napier earthquake in 1931.

Pews from the earlier building, integrated into the Tennyson Street site, had been destroyed in the latest fire, Johnson said.

It was too early to tell whether the church would carry on at the Tennyson Street location, he said.

"We'll have to spend the next few months coming to terms with what's happened.

"A lot of our older members are going to be pretty devastated and they'll be grieving the loss of a building for which they've been a part of for a very long time.

"But churches are not just buildings and we are a people who will gather again as we have in the past."

Johnston said he was called about the fire about 2am and had been at the building greeting and comforting members of the church who were dropping in to see the damage.

"It's pretty upsetting. [I'm] feeling for the people in our congregation. Some are pretty upset ... it's upsetting for us ... it's mutual," he said.

He was grateful for the support of the community in the wake of the fire.

"People rally round and we've already felt that from the community and we'll feel that in the coming days.

World.title: RLWC quick hits: Big crowds and bigger scorelines in week two
World.content:
The second week of the Rugby League World Cup was short on genuine contests as the tournament's haves and have-nots collided.

Aside from Australia's win over Fiji, where the gallant Bati gave the Kangaroos a hell of a scare, it was big scorelines across the board.

But with fans across three Australian states and two other counties voting with their feet, there are still plenty of quick hits from the second round of matches.

1. Tongan wall holds yet again

Tonga took care of business in their win over Lebanon. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer )

For the second week in a row, Tonga's opponent enjoyed plenty of field position and for the second week in a row Tonga's scrambling defence proved more than up to the challenge.

After holding England to 12 points last week, despite the English enjoying 34 tackles inside the red zone to Tonga's 18, they repeated the dose against Lebanon on Friday night.

Tonga down Lebanon in World Cup Tonga's win over Lebanon kicked off what's expected to be a lopsided weekend in the Rugby League World Cup but there's still something to be gained amid the blow-outs.

The Cedars came in with an offload-heavy game plan and had some success moving the ball up the field. By the end, they had 29 tackles inside the attacking 20 to Tonga's 30, but that was where they stalled.

Some of it was due to a lack of creativity but there were plenty of last-gasp Tongan efforts to deny Lebanese players who looked tryline bound, and it means Tonga carry a strong form line into Sunday's blockbuster against Samoa.

2. Samoa running riot over PNG is a sign of the times

Rarely will you see two halves of a single game more different than what Samoa and Papua New Guinea dished up in Port Moresby.

The Kumuls held the gloves up well through the opening 40, trailing just 14-6 at the break and could have been even closer had Robert Derby successfully grounded the ball for their second try.

But what followed was a procession: Samoa scored 50 unanswered points in the second half, as their size and athleticism totally overwhelmed PNG, who had just four sets in the entire stanza.

Of all the blowout results this weekend, this more than any other was a sign of the times. Rugby league's embrace of the set restart rule and the increased speed of the game makes it almost impossible for an underdog team to stay in the fight beyond a certain point and when things break they can break badly.

Samoa only had to make 36 tackles through the entire second and the Kumuls only got over halfway for two tackles.

They finished the game conceding six tries in 15 minutes against a side they had held their own against for the whole first half.

There were plenty of less-extreme examples of the same through this year's NRL season, most notably when a top eight side conceded the third-most points in a game ever, but it's been turned up to greater levels through this World Cup given the talent and fitness disparity and it stacks the deck even further against the underdogs.

3. France's woes continue in England smash-up

England ran out easy winners against a hapless France outfit. (Getty Images: Janelle St Pierre )

England beat the clock against their old rivals in Perth, running out 82-0 winners in a result that means France have conceded 160 points in as many minutes through their two matches.

It's hard to find any silver lining for Les Chanticleers and ahead of their tournament finale against Lebanon, the French game finds itself in a strange position.

The potential for growth or a return to the glory days when France were one of Test football's true powers is always the dream, and with two Super League clubs in Catalans Dragons and Toulouse — giving France more professional teams than New Zealand — they seemingly have the ingredients and infrastructure for improvement.

France just cannot seem to close the gap on their more illustrious rivals. (Getty Images: Paul Kane )

All but two of this year's squad were home-grown players and since 2020 they have won nine of the 16 Tests they have played, with all seven losses coming against England or Samoa.

Problem is, across those seven games they have been outscored by a cumulative total of 394-44, with this England loss the worst of them.

There's greater pathways to the top for French talent than ever before but they can't seem to close the gap between them and the big dogs.

If anything, the gap has become wider. Nine years ago, in the 2017 World Cup, they played England at the same ground and lost 36-6 a week after losing to Australia 52-6.

Those scorelines aren't exactly a good time, but they're not a point-a-minute for two straight weeks either.

The Southern Hemisphere racing ahead of the north is a wider issue for the sport, but France are the collateral damage and they don't have a contingent of heritage NRL players to paper over the cracks.

4. Christchurch puts its best foot forward

Despite the result, it was a healthy crowd in Christchurch. (Getty Images: Kai Schwoerer)

Despite Esom Ioka's first-half hat-trick that briefly gave the Cook Islands the lead, few would have ever expected the Aitu to trouble New Zealand for long in their match at Te Kaha in Christchurch.

That didn't stop a sell-out crowd of 26,800 coming through the gates, marking the fifth biggest Test attendance of the past century in New Zealand and the highest ever for a game outside of Auckland.

It was a strong week of crowds throughout the tournament — Tonga and Lebanon pulled in more than 25,000 and Australia topped 40,000 for the second week in a row despite taking on Fiji.

But with the NRL expansion race heating up as the league prepares to hand out a licence for a 20th team, Christchurch showing up in droves did their chances of winning the bid no harm at all.

5. Fiji take Australia to the brink

Australia are through to the semi-finals of the World Cup after their win over Fiji. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris )

Speaking of that Australian-Fiji crowd, the 41,108 punters who packed into Lang Park didn't just push the attendance past that of the 2017 World Cup final at the same venue, they were treated to easily the best clash of the weekend.

On the back of an inspired display by five-eighth Kurt Donoghoe and a hat-trick to Castleford winger Semi Valemei, Fiji pushed Australia all the way before a late Jacob Preston try wrapped up a 36-22 win for the green and golds.

Consider the previous margins between the two (42-8, 54-6 and 64-0 in their last three meetings) and it's a measure of how far the Bati have come and how this World Cup is more up for grabs than one might think.

A couple of contentious calls and some killer instinct in key moments got the Kangaroos home.

But on what they've shown through two weeks, Samoa, Tonga and New Zealand will all fancy their chances of springing an upset should they meet Australia, who have wrapped up a semi-final berth in surprisingly shaky fashion.

World.title: Antonelli is two points away from the F1 title, and can win it next week
World.content:
With his ninth grand prix win of the season on Monday morning (AEDT), Italian Kimi Antonelli put himself on the cusp of winning his maiden Formula 1 drivers' championship.

The 20-year-old Mercedes pilot has been a class above the rest in 2026, and could have sealed the championship with his victory in Texas on Monday, but other results meant he had to wait at least one more week before popping the champagne.

Next weekend's Mexican Grand Prix shapes up to be the coronation of Antonelli as an F1 champion. Here is how he can seal the world title.

Antonelli needs just two more points

Heading into Monday's United States Grand Prix, there were still five drivers who could mathematically catch Kimi Antonelli in the race for the title.

Kimi Antonelli is in just his second season of Formula 1. (Getty Images: LAT Images/Simon Galloway)

But Antonelli's win reduced his challengers to teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

Drivers' championship standings

1: 365 — Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes

2: 242 — George Russell, Mercedes (-123)

3: 241 — Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari (-124)

With just five grands prix left to run, there is a maximum of 125 points a driver can achieve by winning every race.

Antonelli has 365 points, 123 ahead of Russell and 124 over Hamilton.

The maximum total Russell and Hamilton can end the season with is 367 and 366 points, respectively.

That means Antonelli needs to win just one more point to eliminate Hamilton from the title race, and two points to eliminate Russell.

Antonelli can achieve that in Mexico City by finishing ninth or higher.
